## Wave 4c: R5 bus changes (W4.40 to W4.47)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md` §9.2,
§9.3, §5.9, §3.5.2, §3.5.6 (drain), §9.1.1 (slot values), §6.8 (the
`pkg/events` test changes). Verified against the worktree at `4b103429` (local
main `cdbdd870` plus the spec commit); every symbol below was checked there, and
line numbers are avoided because Waves 1 to 3 move them.

This wave separates per-pod handler slots from the consumer-wide
`MaxAckPending`, replaces natsbus's `Consume` with a slot-gated pull that
reclaims lapsed deliveries under a cap and drains on stop, makes `Subscribe`
bind (never create) its durable and its dead-letter watcher, turns the watchers
into topology objects, adds `StreamAdmin.ConsumerState` and the
`events.DeadLetterWatcher` backstop, gives membus the same behaviour, and adds
`busconn.KeepTopology` and `busconn.WatchDeadLetters`. Nothing here is wired
into a binary: `internal/cli/manager` (Wave 5) adds `KeepTopology` and
`WatchDeadLetters` as `k8s.LeaderOnly` runnables, `internal/cli/agent` sets
`Subscription.Drain` and applies `CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS`, and the
`pkg/agentdomain` task (R5 manager) raises the autoscaled consumers'
`MaxAckPending` to `Slots × AutoscaleReplicaCeiling` under its own guard.

### Ordering, ownership and what this wave consumes

- **Serial.** W4.40 to W4.47 run in order. All of them touch `pkg/events`,
  `pkg/events/natsbus`, `pkg/events/membus` or `pkg/events/contracttest`, which
  this wave owns for its duration.
- **W4.40 lands before any Wave 4a task that edits `pkg/events/topology.go`.**
  The R3 probe stream `CLUSTARR_WORK_PROBE` is a DiscardNew WorkQueue without
  schedules and its consumers carry `Slots: 4` (§6.5.1); both need W4.40's
  `ConsumerSpec.Slots` and the DiscardNew exemption in `Topology.Validate`. If
  the orchestrator lands Wave 4a's topology task first anyway, W4.40's Step 3
  says what to do with the consumers already there.
- **Consumes from Wave 1:** W1.3's `events.StreamAdmin.Missing`,
  `events.TopologyObject{Kind, Stream, Name}` with `String()` (`stream S`,
  `consumer S/C`, `kv B`, `object store O`), `events.TopologyConsumer`,
  `membus.(*Bus).Ensure` recording every topology consumer through
  `(*stream).bindDurable(name)`, and `(*stream).hasDurable`; W1.4's
  `pkg/busconn` (`EnsureTopology(ctx context.Context, bus events.Bus, t events.Topology) error`,
  the package-variable test style of `awaitPoll`) and the move of
  `pkg/k8s/bus_hooks_test.go` to `pkg/busconn/bus_hooks_test.go`.
  This wave does **not** add `Missing` again (W1.3's spec-defect note 1).
- **Produces for later waves:** `events.ConsumerSpec.Slots`,
  `events.AutoscaleReplicaCeiling`, `events.SubscriptionSpec`,
  `events.Subscription.{MaxAckPending, Drain}`, `events.AckDeadline`,
  `events.DefaultAckWait`, `events.{SlotsEnv, ParseSlotOverrides, SlotsFor}`,
  `events.{DeadLetterWatcherPrefix, DeadLetterWatcherName, DeadLetterWatcherSpec, DeadLetterWatcherAckWait, DeadLetterWatcherMaxAckPending}`,
  `events.ConsumerState` (with `Lag()`), `events.StreamAdmin.ConsumerState`,
  `events.ErrConsumerNotFound`, `events.DeadLetterWatcher`,
  `busconn.KeepTopology(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, bus events.Bus, t events.Topology) error`,
  `busconn.WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, bus events.Bus, t events.Topology) error`,
  and `contracttest.Bind`. These are the names the Wave 5 gate (W5.1)
  checks with `go doc`.
- **AudioGraft drift.** The graft run touches no bus: `cmd/squasharr-worker`'s
  `runGraft` is documented "no NATS", and `app/squash/grafttask`,
  `app/squash/worker/graft` and `app/squash/controller/audiograft` import no
  `pkg/events` (checked at `4b103429`). Nothing in this wave changes for it.
  The one squasharr path this wave touches is the transcode pool's `Pull`
  (`app/squash/worker/serve.go`, `events.TranscodeTaskConsumer(...).Subscription()`):
  W4.40 keeps its durable's `MaxAckPending` at 64 when `Subscription()` starts
  carrying one slot.

### Wave-specific rules

- **Gotchas this wave must keep (CLAUDE.md).**
  - *MAX_DELIVERIES needs a waiting pull.* nats-server raises the advisory only
    from `getNextMsg`, which runs only while a pull request waits. The pull loop
    therefore keeps a `Fetch` open whenever a slot is free, and keeps one
    `Fetch(1)` open at the lapsed cap even when every slot is held (W4.44).
    nats-server keeps a pull request a client abandoned in `o.waiting` until it
    expires (`processWaiting` prunes only expired ones,
    `server/consumer.go` v2.15.0), which is what lets a stopped pod's last pull
    raise the advisory for the backstop (W4.45).
  - *BackOff nak arithmetic.* `natsbus.nakDelay` is unchanged. Lapse timing uses
    `events.AckDeadline` (Backoff[n-1], else AckWait), never AckWait alone, for
    the same server rule (`server/consumer.go:678-682`).
  - *A test on membus alone proves nothing.* Every behaviour change ships as a
    `pkg/events/contracttest` case, run by `pkg/events/natsbus` against an
    embedded nats-server and by `pkg/events/membus`.
- **No go.mod edit.** nats.go v1.53.1 and nats-server v2.15.0 are already
  required. No `go get`, no `go mod tidy`.
- **No RBAC or API types change.** `make manifests` must leave `config/` and
  `charts/` byte-identical; W4.47 checks this.
- **Formatting.** After every edit run
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w <touched .go files>` and
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w <touched .go files>`.
- **Envtest.** `$ENVTEST` stands for
  `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$($(go env GOPATH)/bin/setup-envtest use 1.37.0 -i -p path)"`.
- **Runtime.** The natsbus contract suite starts one embedded server per
  subtest. A full `go test ./pkg/events/natsbus/` takes minutes; the targeted
  commands below use `-run 'TestBusContract/<Case>'`.
- **Commits** are path-scoped (`git commit -m … -- <paths>`); `git add` new files
  first; never `git stash`, never push. W4.42 edits test files other wave-4
  tasks may also own: commit them immediately after the edit.

```go
// consumer's per-pod handler count today, except the artwork renderer (the
// process draws two at a time, so 32 slots would make an HPA under-count its
// load) and segment analysis (the shipped --concurrency default).

 want := map[string]int{
  events.ConsumerCatalogRSSMatcher:     256,
  events.ConsumerCatalogSearchHigh:     8,
  events.ConsumerCatalogSearchNorm:     8,
  events.ConsumerCatalogGrab:           16,

  events.ConsumerCatalogArtworkFetch:   32,
  events.ConsumerCatalogArtworkRender:  4,
  events.ConsumerCatalogMarkers:        32,

  events.ConsumerSegmentarrAnalyze:     1,
  events.ConsumerCatalogSegmentsResult: 32,
  events.ConsumerCatalogHistory:        512,
  events.ConsumerCatalogRedownload:     16,
  events.ConsumerImportScan:            4,
  events.ConsumerImportList:            2,
  events.ConsumerImportFile:            4,
  events.ConsumerIndexRSS:              4,
  events.ConsumerCaptionFetchHigh:      16,
  events.ConsumerCaptionFetchNormal:    16,
  events.ConsumerSquasharrResults:      1,
  events.ConsumerDLQProjector:          64,
 }
 got := map[string]int{}
 for _, c := range events.Default().Consumers {

  }
  got[c.Name] = c.Slots
 }

  if _, ok := got[name]; ok {
   want[name] = n
  }
 }

}

// A pool worker runs one task at a time, but its durable's cap across every
// puller stays 64: Pull writes Subscription.MaxAckPending, so one slot must
// not shrink it.
func TestAPoolDurableKeepsItsCapThroughItsSubscription(t *testing.T) {
 c := events.TranscodeTaskConsumer("6f1c-uid", "cpu")
 assert.Equal(t, 1, c.Slots)
 assert.Equal(t, 64, c.MaxAckPending)
 sub := c.Subscription()
 assert.Equal(t, 1, sub.MaxInFlight)
 assert.Equal(t, 64, sub.MaxAckPending)
 assert.Equal(t, 64, events.SubscriptionSpec(sub).MaxAckPending)
}

func TestSubscriptionSpecInvertsSubscription(t *testing.T) {
 for _, c := range events.Default().Consumers {
  want := c
  want.Description = "" // a Subscription does not carry it
  assert.Equal(t, want, events.SubscriptionSpec(c.Subscription()), c.Name)
 }
 // The defaults both buses apply: one slot, and a cap of the slots.
 got := events.SubscriptionSpec(events.Subscription{Stream: "S", Durable: "d", Filters: []string{"a.>"}})
 assert.Equal(t, 1, got.Slots)
 assert.Equal(t, 1, got.MaxAckPending)
 got = events.SubscriptionSpec(events.Subscription{Stream: "S", Durable: "d", Filters: []string{"a.>"}, MaxInFlight: 3})
 assert.Equal(t, 3, got.MaxAckPending)
}

func TestAckDeadline(t *testing.T) {
 s := time.Second
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  name    string
  sub     events.Subscription
  attempt uint64
  want    time.Duration
 }{
  {"no backoff and no AckWait is JetStream's default", events.Subscription{}, 1, events.DefaultAckWait},
  {"no backoff: AckWait for every attempt", events.Subscription{AckWait: 45 * s}, 3, 45 * s},
  {"first delivery: Backoff[0], not AckWait", events.Subscription{AckWait: 120 * s, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * s, 2 * time.Minute}}, 1, 30 * s},
  {"attempt 0 reads as the first", events.Subscription{Backoff: []time.Duration{10 * s}}, 0, 10 * s},
  {"delivery n: Backoff[n-1]", events.Subscription{Backoff: []time.Duration{s, 5 * s, 30 * s}}, 2, 5 * s},
  {"past the end: the last entry", events.Subscription{Backoff: []time.Duration{s, 5 * s}}, 9, 5 * s},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   assert.Equal(t, tc.want, events.AckDeadline(tc.sub, tc.attempt))
  })
 }
}
```

```go
package events_test

import (
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

func withConsumer(c events.ConsumerSpec) events.Topology {
 top := events.Default()
 top.Consumers = append(top.Consumers, c)
 return top
}

// Validate holds a process's slots under the durable's cap across every
// process (spec §9.2): a cap below one pod's slots would leave slots no
// delivery can ever fill.
func TestValidateHoldsSlotsUnderTheCap(t *testing.T) {
 ok := events.ConsumerSpec{
  Name: "ct-slots", Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr,
  Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS}, MaxDeliver: 2,
  Slots: 2, MaxAckPending: 4,
 }
 require.NoError(t, withConsumer(ok).Validate())

 noSlots := ok
 noSlots.Slots = 0
 err := withConsumer(noSlots).Validate()
 require.Error(t, err)
 assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "ct-slots.Slots")

 lowCap := ok
 lowCap.MaxAckPending = 1
 err = withConsumer(lowCap).Validate()
 require.Error(t, err)
 assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "ct-slots.MaxAckPending")
}

// A DiscardNew work queue cannot allow schedules (nats-server refuses the
// pairing), so the schedules rule exempts every one of them, not only
// squasharr's: the probe stream is the second (spec §9.2, §6.5.1).
func TestValidateExemptsDiscardNewWorkQueuesFromSchedules(t *testing.T) {
 top := events.Default()
 top.Streams = append(top.Streams, events.StreamSpec{
  Name: "CLUSTARR_WORK_TEST", Subjects: []string{"clustarr.worktest.>"},
  Retention: events.RetentionWorkQueue, Storage: events.StorageFile,
  Discard: events.DiscardNew, MaxBytes: events.MiB,
 })
 require.NoError(t, top.Validate())

 top.Streams[len(top.Streams)-1].Discard = events.DiscardOld
 err := top.Validate()
 require.Error(t, err)
 assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), "CLUSTARR_WORK_TEST.AllowMsgSchedules")
}
```

```go
// TestPullWritesTheSubscriptionsCapNotItsSlots: a pool durable is created by
// Pull, and its cap across every puller is the topology's 64 although each
// pool worker has one slot (spec §9.3).
func TestPullWritesTheSubscriptionsCapNotItsSlots(t *testing.T) {
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
 defer cancel()
 bus, err := natsbus.New(connect(t))
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("natsbus.New: %v", err)
 }
 t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
 if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, contracttest.Topology()); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Ensure: %v", err)
 }
 spec := events.TranscodeTaskConsumer("prof-cap", "cpu")
 p, err := bus.Pull(ctx, spec.Subscription())
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Pull: %v", err)
 }
 defer p.Stop()
 c, err := bus.JetStream().Consumer(ctx, spec.Stream, spec.Name)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("consumer %s: %v", spec.Name, err)
 }
 if got := c.CachedInfo().Config.MaxAckPending; got != spec.MaxAckPending {
  t.Errorf("pool durable MaxAckPending = %d, want the topology's %d", got, spec.MaxAckPending)
 }
}
```

```go
// DefaultAckWait is JetStream's acknowledgement deadline for a consumer that
// sets neither AckWait nor Backoff (nats-server JsAckWaitDefault).
const DefaultAckWait = 30 * time.Second

// AckDeadline is how long delivery attempt of s (1-based; 0 reads as 1) has
// before the broker makes it again. With Backoff set, nats-server replaces
// AckWait with Backoff[0] and times delivery n out on Backoff[n-1], the last
// entry past the end (server/consumer.go:678-682, checkPending); without it,
// every delivery gets AckWait. An InProgress restarts the same clock. The
// natsbus lapse reaper and membus share this one rule (spec §9.2).
func AckDeadline(s Subscription, attempt uint64) time.Duration {
 if n := len(s.Backoff); n > 0 {
  i := 0
  if attempt > 1 {
   i = int(min(attempt-1, uint64(n-1)))
  }
  return s.Backoff[i]
 }
 if s.AckWait > 0 {
  return s.AckWait
 }
 return DefaultAckWait
}
```

```go
package events

import (
 "fmt"
 "strconv"
 "strings"
)

// SlotsEnv overrides consumers' per-pod slots for one Deployment, as
// "segmentarr-analyze=3,catalogarr-grab=8" (spec §9.2, §10.2.2).
const SlotsEnv = "CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS"

// ParseSlotOverrides reads SlotsEnv's value. An empty value overrides
// nothing; a malformed entry, a count below one or a durable named twice is
// an error naming SlotsEnv.
func ParseSlotOverrides(v string) (map[string]int, error) {
 out := map[string]int{}
 if strings.TrimSpace(v) == "" {
  return out, nil
 }
 for _, part := range strings.Split(v, ",") {
  part = strings.TrimSpace(part)
  name, count, ok := strings.Cut(part, "=")
  name = strings.TrimSpace(name)
  if !ok || name == "" {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("events: %s: %q is not <durable>=<slots>", SlotsEnv, part)
  }
  n, err := strconv.Atoi(strings.TrimSpace(count))
  if err != nil || n < 1 {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("events: %s: %q: slots must be a whole number of at least 1", SlotsEnv, part)
  }
  if _, dup := out[name]; dup {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("events: %s: %s is named twice", SlotsEnv, name)
  }
  out[name] = n
 }
 return out, nil
}

// SlotsFor is c's per-pod slots: the override for its name, else c.Slots.
func SlotsFor(c ConsumerSpec, overrides map[string]int) int {
 if n, ok := overrides[c.Name]; ok {
  return n
 }
 return c.Slots
}
```

```go
package events

import "time"

// DeadLetterWatcherPrefix begins every dead-letter watcher's durable name.
const DeadLetterWatcherPrefix = "clustarr-dlq-watch-"

// A dead-letter watcher's tuning, unchanged from the watcher natsbus created
// per subscription before the watchers became topology objects (spec §5.9).
// A failed copy is retried for as long as it takes (MaxDeliver -1): the
// message an advisory names is otherwise never dead-lettered. AckWait covers
// the MaxAckPending advisories one pull holds, each allowed the bus's 10 s
// dead-letter timeout and handled one at a time, twice over.
const (
 DeadLetterWatcherMaxAckPending = 4
 DeadLetterWatcherAckWait       = 80 * time.Second
)

// DeadLetterWatcherName is the durable on StreamAdvisories that dead-letters
// stream's durable's lapsed final deliveries. It names the stream as well as
// the durable, so two durables of one name on different streams do not share,
// and fight over, one watcher's filter. It takes strings because
// StreamAdmin.DeleteSubscription deletes a watcher by stream and durable alone.
func DeadLetterWatcherName(stream, durable string) string {
 return DeadLetterWatcherPrefix + stream + "-" + durable
}

// DeadLetterWatcherSpec is c's MAX_DELIVERIES watcher: a durable on
// StreamAdvisories filtered to c's advisory subject, which every process
// consuming c shares, and the manager too as a backstop (spec §5.9). The
// manager's EnsureTopology creates it; Subscribe binds it.
func DeadLetterWatcherSpec(c ConsumerSpec) ConsumerSpec {
 return ConsumerSpec{
  Name:          DeadLetterWatcherName(c.Stream, c.Name),
  Stream:        StreamAdvisories,
  Description:   "Dead-letters the lapsed final deliveries of " + c.Name + ".",
  Filters:       []string{MaxDeliveriesAdvisorySubject(c.Stream, c.Name)},
  AckWait:       DeadLetterWatcherAckWait,
  MaxDeliver:    -1,
  MaxAckPending: DeadLetterWatcherMaxAckPending,
  Slots:         DeadLetterWatcherMaxAckPending,
 }
}

// withDeadLetterWatchers returns cs followed by one watcher per consumer.
func withDeadLetterWatchers(cs []ConsumerSpec) []ConsumerSpec {
 out := make([]ConsumerSpec, 0, 2*len(cs))
 out = append(out, cs...)
 for _, c := range cs {
  out = append(out, DeadLetterWatcherSpec(c))
 }
 return out
}
```

```go
// binds here. Each sub must set MaxDeliver above len(Backoff), as every
// topology consumer must (Topology.Validate): a Subscription's zero
// MaxDeliver means unlimited, which only a dead-letter watcher may be. A sub
// named like one of base's consumers fails as a duplicate.
//
// base must be the topology the test already ensured (Ensure replaces the
// bus's remembered topology, and natsbus refuses a replica change on a
// running server), so a test on events.Default().ForSingleNode() passes that.
func Bind(ctx context.Context, t testing.TB, bus events.Bus, base events.Topology, subs ...events.Subscription) {
 t.Helper()
 top := base
 top.Consumers = append([]events.ConsumerSpec(nil), base.Consumers...)
 for _, s := range subs {
  if s.MaxDeliver <= len(s.Backoff) {
   t.Fatalf("contracttest.Bind: %s: set MaxDeliver above len(Backoff)=%d, got %d",
    s.Durable, len(s.Backoff), s.MaxDeliver)
  }
  c := events.SubscriptionSpec(s)
  top.Consumers = append(top.Consumers, c, events.DeadLetterWatcherSpec(c))
 }
 if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, top); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("contracttest.Bind: Ensure: %v", err)
 }
}

// admin is bus's StreamAdmin half.
func admin(t *testing.T, bus events.Bus) events.StreamAdmin {
 t.Helper()
 sa, ok := bus.(events.StreamAdmin)
 if !ok {
  t.Fatalf("%T does not implement events.StreamAdmin", bus)
 }
 return sa
}
```

```go
package contracttest

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "sync"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

func consumerState(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, sa events.StreamAdmin, sub events.Subscription) events.ConsumerState {
 t.Helper()
 st, err := sa.ConsumerState(ctx, sub.Stream, sub.Durable)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("ConsumerState %s/%s: %v", sub.Stream, sub.Durable, err)
 }
 return st
}

func publishFetch(ctx context.Context, t *testing.T, bus events.Bus, id string, opts ...events.PublishOption) {
 t.Helper()
 if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkFetchSubject(events.PriorityNormal, id, "en"),
  envelope(id, "subtitle.FetchTask.v1", id), opts...); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Publish %s: %v", id, err)
 }
}

// testConsumerState holds StreamAdmin.ConsumerState to JetStream's ConsumerInfo
// (spec §9.2): Pending is matching and undelivered, AckPending delivered and
// unsettled -- running, or waiting out a delayed nak -- and a scheduled
// publish counts in neither until it fires.
func testConsumerState(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-state",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 2, MaxAckPending: 2,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)

 const published = 5
 for i := range published {
  publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, fmt.Sprintf("state-%d", i))
 }
 if st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, sub); st.Pending != published || st.AckPending != 0 || st.MaxAckPending != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("before any Subscribe: %+v, want Pending %d, AckPending 0, MaxAckPending 2", st, published)
 }

 verdicts := make(chan error, published)
 var mu sync.Mutex
 running := 0
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(ctx context.Context, _ events.Message) error {
  mu.Lock()
  running++
  mu.Unlock()
  select {
  case err := <-verdicts:
   return err
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return ctx.Err()
  }
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 waitUntil(t, "two deliveries held", func() bool {
  st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, sub)
  return st.AckPending == 2 && st.Pending == published-2
 })

 // A delayed nak keeps its delivery ack-pending, so the cap still holds
 // and nothing else is delivered.
 verdicts <- events.Retry(time.Hour, errors.New("provider asked us to wait"))
 time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
 if st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, sub); st.AckPending != 2 || st.Pending != published-2 {
  t.Errorf("after a one-hour nak: %+v, want AckPending 2, Pending %d", st, published-2)
 }
 mu.Lock()
 if running != 2 {
  t.Errorf("%d handlers started with MaxAckPending 2 held by one running and one naked delivery, want 2", running)
 }
 mu.Unlock()

 // A schedule in the future is on a holding subject no filter matches.
 publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, "state-later", events.WithScheduleAt(time.Now().Add(time.Hour)))
 time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
 if st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, sub); st.Pending != published-2 {
  t.Errorf("a scheduled publish counted as Pending: %+v", st)
 }

 if _, err := sa.ConsumerState(ctx, sub.Stream, "ct-no-such-durable"); !errors.Is(err, events.ErrConsumerNotFound) {
  t.Errorf("ConsumerState of a missing durable = %v, want ErrConsumerNotFound", err)
 }
 if _, err := sa.ConsumerState(ctx, "CLUSTARR_NO_SUCH_STREAM", "x"); !errors.Is(err, events.ErrStreamNotFound) {
  t.Errorf("ConsumerState on a missing stream = %v, want ErrStreamNotFound", err)
 }
}

// testMaxAckPendingCapsEveryReplica: the durable's MaxAckPending bounds every
// subscription of it together (spec §9.3). membus had no consumer-wide cap.
func testMaxAckPendingCapsEveryReplica(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-cap",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 2, MaxAckPending: 2,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 release := make(chan struct{})
 var releaseOnce sync.Once
 unblock := func() { releaseOnce.Do(func() { close(release) }) }
 t.Cleanup(unblock)

 var mu sync.Mutex
 running, most, finished := 0, 0, 0
 h := func(ctx context.Context, _ events.Message) error {
  mu.Lock()
  running++
  most = max(most, running)
  mu.Unlock()
  select {
  case <-release:
  case <-ctx.Done():
  }
  mu.Lock()
  running--
  finished++
  mu.Unlock()
  return nil
 }
 for range 2 {
  stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, h)
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
  }
  defer stop()
 }
 const published = 6
 for i := range published {
  publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, fmt.Sprintf("cap-%d", i))
 }
 waitUntil(t, "the cap's two handlers", func() bool {
  mu.Lock()
  defer mu.Unlock()
  return running == 2
 })
 time.Sleep(time.Second)
 mu.Lock()
 if most != 2 {
  t.Errorf("%d handlers ran at once across two subscriptions of a durable capped at 2", most)
 }
 mu.Unlock()
 unblock()
 waitUntil(t, "every task handled", func() bool {
  mu.Lock()
  defer mu.Unlock()
  return finished == published
 })
}
```

```go
package events

import "time"

// ConsumerState is one durable's backlog as the broker reports it (spec §9.2).
type ConsumerState struct {
 // Pending is JetStream's NumPending: matching messages not yet delivered.
 // A message a schedule still holds is on a subject no filter matches and
 // counts nowhere.
 Pending uint64
 // AckPending is NumAckPending: delivered and not settled -- in a handler,
 // waiting out a delayed nak, or lapsed.
 AckPending uint64
 // MaxAckPending is the durable's cap across every process.
 MaxAckPending int
 // ObservedAt is when the broker gathered the numbers.
 ObservedAt time.Time
}

// Lag is the work the durable still has, delivered or not: the
// clustarr_consumer_lag metric (spec §9.0).
func (s ConsumerState) Lag() uint64 { return s.Pending + s.AckPending }
```

```go
// ConsumerState implements events.StreamAdmin: one CONSUMER.INFO request
// (nats.go jetstream/consumer.go fetchConsumerInfo), read from the handle's
// cached info.
func (b *Bus) ConsumerState(ctx context.Context, stream, durable string) (events.ConsumerState, error) {
 c, err := b.js.Consumer(ctx, stream, durable)
 if err != nil {
  return events.ConsumerState{}, lookupError(stream, durable, err)
 }
 info := c.CachedInfo()
 return events.ConsumerState{
  Pending:       info.NumPending,
  AckPending:    uint64(max(info.NumAckPending, 0)),
  MaxAckPending: info.Config.MaxAckPending,
  ObservedAt:    info.TimeStamp,
 }, nil
}

// lookupError maps a consumer lookup's failure onto the events sentinels. A
// missing stream comes back from CONSUMER.INFO as an *APIError with
// JSErrCodeStreamNotFound, which is matched by code as well as by errors.Is.
func lookupError(stream, durable string, err error) error {
 var apiErr *jetstream.APIError
 switch {
 case errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound),
  errors.As(err, &apiErr) && apiErr.ErrorCode == jetstream.JSErrCodeStreamNotFound:
  return fmt.Errorf("natsbus: stream %s: %w", stream, events.ErrStreamNotFound)
 case errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConsumerNotFound):
  return fmt.Errorf("natsbus: consumer %s on %s: %w", durable, stream, events.ErrConsumerNotFound)
 }
 return fmt.Errorf("natsbus: consumer %s on %s: %w", durable, stream, err)
}
```

     Add `consumerState`:

```go
// consumerState is durable's ConsumerState, false when durable is not bound.
func (s *stream) consumerState(durable string, now time.Time) (events.ConsumerState, bool) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 d, ok := s.durables[durable]
 if !ok {
  return events.ConsumerState{}, false
 }
 workQueue := s.spec.Retention == events.RetentionWorkQueue
 out := events.ConsumerState{MaxAckPending: d.maxAckPending, ObservedAt: now}
 for _, m := range s.msgs {
  if m.removed || !matchAny(d.filters, m.subject) {
   continue
  }
  if !m.deliverAt.IsZero() && now.Before(m.deliverAt) {
   continue
  }
  if workQueue && m.claim != "" && m.claim != durable {
   continue
  }
  switch cs, ok := m.state[durable]; {
  case !ok || cs.attempts == 0:
   out.Pending++
  case !cs.settled:
   out.AckPending++
  }
 }
 return out, true
}
```

```go
func (b *Bus) ConsumerState(_ context.Context, stream, durable string) (events.ConsumerState, error) {

 b.mu.Unlock()
 if st == nil {
  return events.ConsumerState{}, fmt.Errorf("membus: stream %s: %w", stream, events.ErrStreamNotFound)

  return events.ConsumerState{}, fmt.Errorf("membus: consumer %s on %s: %w", durable, stream, events.ErrConsumerNotFound)
 }
 return cs, nil
}
```

### Task W4.44: Slot-gated pull, lapse reclaim under the lapsed cap, drain, and re-binding

**Spec:** §9.3 ("Slot-gated pull", "Reclaim", "The bound", "Drain", membus
parity), §5.9 (re-binding a running subscription whose durable or stream
vanished), §3.5.6 (drain); contract cases `SubscriptionHoldsNoMoreThanItsSlots`,
`ReplicasShareMaxAckPendingBeyondOneSlotCount`, `LapsedHandlerFreesItsSlot`,
`LapsedHandlersDoNotMultiplyConcurrency`, `DrainLetsRunningHandlersFinish`,
`SubscribeRebindsAVanishedDurable`

**The lapse rule this task implements** (it differs from §9.3's wording; see
the defects at the end): a running delivery past `deadline + 1s` is marked
lapsed, freeing its slot, **only while fewer than `slots` are lapsed**; a
handler starts whenever `live < slots`; and once `lapsed == slots` the loop
keeps one `Fetch(1)` open even when every slot is held, parking what arrives,
so JetStream always has a pull on which to raise MAX_DELIVERIES. Handlers
running in one pod therefore never exceed `2 × slots` (`live <= slots`,
`lapsed <= slots`), the bound §9.3 states, and one hung handler on a one-slot
subscription does not stop the next task.

```go
package contracttest

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "sync"
 "sync/atomic"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

// gate is a handler body that holds until released or, unless deaf, until
// its context ends.
type gate struct {
 mu                      sync.Mutex
 running, most, finished int
 release                 chan struct{}
 once                    sync.Once
}

func newGate(t *testing.T) *gate {
 g := &gate{release: make(chan struct{})}
 t.Cleanup(g.open)
 return g
}

func (g *gate) open() { g.once.Do(func() { close(g.release) }) }

func (g *gate) handler(ctx context.Context, _ events.Message) error {
 g.mu.Lock()
 g.running++
 g.most = max(g.most, g.running)
 g.mu.Unlock()
 select {
 case <-g.release:
 case <-ctx.Done():
 }
 g.mu.Lock()
 g.running--
 g.finished++
 g.mu.Unlock()
 return nil
}

func (g *gate) read() (running, most, finished int) {
 g.mu.Lock()
 defer g.mu.Unlock()
 return g.running, g.most, g.finished
}

// testHoldsNoMoreThanItsSlots: a subscription takes only as many deliveries
// as it has slots, however high the durable's cap, which is for every replica
// together (spec §9.3). natsbus's Consume pulled again as soon as its
// non-blocking callback returned and parked the rest: 5 held for one slot.
func testHoldsNoMoreThanItsSlots(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-slots",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 1, MaxAckPending: 8,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 g := newGate(t)
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, g.handler)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 for i := range 5 {
  publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, fmt.Sprintf("slots-%d", i))
 }
 waitUntil(t, "the one slot's handler", func() bool { r, _, _ := g.read(); return r == 1 })
 time.Sleep(2 * time.Second)
 if st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, sub); st.AckPending != 1 || st.Pending != 4 {
  t.Errorf("with one slot held: %+v, want AckPending 1 and Pending 4", st)
 }
}

// testReplicasShareTheCap: two replicas of two slots each run four handlers
// under a cap of four. natsbus once let one replica's Consume take the whole
// cap and park half of it, so two ran.
func testReplicasShareTheCap(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-share",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 2, MaxAckPending: 4,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 g := newGate(t)
 for range 2 {
  stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, g.handler)
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
  }
  defer stop()
 }
 for i := range 8 {
  publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, fmt.Sprintf("share-%d", i))
 }
 waitUntil(t, "four handlers across two subscriptions", func() bool { r, _, _ := g.read(); return r == 4 })
 time.Sleep(500 * time.Millisecond)
 if _, most, _ := g.read(); most != 4 {
  t.Errorf("at most %d ran at once, want 4", most)
 }
}

// testLapsedHandlerFreesItsSlot: a handler hung past the broker's deadline
// gives its slot back, so the next task runs (spec §9.3). The hung message
// hangs only on its first delivery: its redelivery is what JetStream hands
// the freed slot first, and it must not take the slot for good.
func testLapsedHandlerFreesItsSlot(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 const deadline = 2 * time.Second
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr, Durable: "ct-lapse-slot",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS},
  AckWait: deadline, MaxDeliver: 5, Backoff: []time.Duration{deadline},
  MaxInFlight: 1, MaxAckPending: 8,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 release := make(chan struct{})
 var once sync.Once
 hung := make(chan struct{}, 1)
 handled := make(chan time.Time, 1)
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  switch {
  case m.Envelope().ID == "lapse-hung" && m.Attempt() == 1:
   hung <- struct{}{}
   <-release // deaf to its context, as a handler stuck in a syscall is
  case m.Envelope().ID == "lapse-next":
   select {
   case handled <- time.Now():
   default:
   }
  }
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 t.Cleanup(stop)
 t.Cleanup(func() { once.Do(func() { close(release) }) }) // runs before stop
 if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-lapse-hung"), envelope("lapse-hung", "index.RssTask.v1", 0)); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
 }
 select {
 case <-hung:
 case <-time.After(Timeout):
  t.Fatal("the hung task was never delivered")
 }
 start := time.Now()
 if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-lapse-next"), envelope("lapse-next", "index.RssTask.v1", 1)); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
 }
 select {
 case at := <-handled:
  if got := at.Sub(start); got > 3*deadline {
   t.Errorf("the next task ran %v after it was published, want within 3x the %v deadline", got, deadline)
  }
 case <-time.After(3 * deadline):
  t.Fatalf("the next task waited more than 3x the %v deadline behind a hung handler: its slot was never reclaimed", deadline)
 }
}

// testLapsesAreBounded: handlers that are slow, not hung, lapse at the
// broker's deadline like hung ones. A reclaim without the lapsed cap would
// fetch a replacement for every lapse, bounded only by MaxAckPending; with
// it a pod runs at most twice its slots (spec §9.3, "The bound").
func testLapsesAreBounded(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setupFor(t, newBus, 90*time.Second)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr, Durable: "ct-lapse-bound",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS},
  AckWait: time.Second, MaxDeliver: 20, Backoff: []time.Duration{time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 2, MaxAckPending: 16,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 var mu sync.Mutex
 running, most := 0, 0
 done := map[string]bool{}
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  mu.Lock()
  running++
  most = max(most, running)
  mu.Unlock()
  time.Sleep(3 * time.Second) // slow past every deadline, and deaf to its context
  mu.Lock()
  running--
  done[m.Envelope().ID] = true
  mu.Unlock()
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 const published = 8
 for i := range published {
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject(fmt.Sprintf("idx-bound-%d", i)),
   envelope(fmt.Sprintf("bound-%d", i), "index.RssTask.v1", i)); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish %d: %v", i, err)
  }
 }
 for until := time.Now().Add(75 * time.Second); ; time.Sleep(100 * time.Millisecond) {
  mu.Lock()
  n := len(done)
  mu.Unlock()
  if n == published {
   break
  }
  if time.Now().After(until) {
   t.Fatalf("%d of %d slow tasks finished", n, published)
  }
 }
 mu.Lock()
 defer mu.Unlock()
 if most > 2*sub.MaxInFlight {
  t.Errorf("%d handlers ran at once with %d slots; lapsed handlers may add at most as many again", most, sub.MaxInFlight)
 }
 if most <= sub.MaxInFlight {
  t.Errorf("at most %d ran at once: no lapse ever freed a slot", most)
 }
}

// testDrain: once a subscription stops, a running handler keeps its context
// for up to Drain and its acknowledgement reaches the broker (spec §3.5.6,
// §9.3). Without Drain the context ends at once, as before.
func testDrain(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  durable string
  drain   time.Duration
  wantErr error
 }{
  {"ct-drain", 2 * time.Second, nil},
  {"ct-no-drain", 0, context.Canceled},
 } {
  sub := events.Subscription{
   Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr, Durable: tc.durable,
   Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS},
   AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
   MaxInFlight: 1, Drain: tc.drain,
  }
  Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
  subCtx, cancelSub := context.WithCancel(ctx)
  started, stopped := make(chan struct{}), make(chan struct{})
  result := make(chan error, 1)
  var calls atomic.Int32
  stop, err := bus.Subscribe(subCtx, sub, func(hctx context.Context, _ events.Message) error {
   if calls.Add(1) == 1 {
    close(started)
   }
   <-stopped
   time.Sleep(300 * time.Millisecond)
   result <- hctx.Err()
   return nil
  })
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscribe %s: %v", tc.durable, err)
  }
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-"+tc.durable), envelope(tc.durable, "index.RssTask.v1", 0)); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
  }
  select {
  case <-started:
  case <-time.After(Timeout):
   t.Fatalf("%s: never delivered", tc.durable)
  }
  cancelSub()
  close(stopped)
  select {
  case err := <-result:
   if !errors.Is(err, tc.wantErr) && err != tc.wantErr {
    t.Errorf("%s: the handler's context 300ms after the subscription stopped = %v, want %v", tc.durable, err, tc.wantErr)
   }
  case <-time.After(Timeout):
   t.Fatalf("%s: the handler never returned", tc.durable)
  }
  stop()
  waitUntil(t, tc.durable+"'s acknowledgement", func() bool {
   subjects, err := sa.Subjects(ctx, sub.Stream, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-"+tc.durable))
   return err == nil && len(subjects) == 0
  })
  if n := calls.Load(); n != 1 {
   t.Errorf("%s: handled %d times, want once", tc.durable, n)
  }
 }
}

// testRebind: a running subscription whose durable is deleted and created
// again -- what a NATS restart does to a memory-backed stream until the
// manager re-ensures (spec §5.9) -- resumes on its own.
func testRebind(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-rebind",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 1,
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 got := newCollector()
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  got.add(m)
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, "rebind-1")
 got.waitFor(t, 1, "the first task")
 if err := sa.DeleteSubscription(ctx, sub.Stream, sub.Durable); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("DeleteSubscription: %v", err)
 }
 time.Sleep(time.Second)
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub) // the manager re-creates it
 publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, "rebind-2")
 got.waitFor(t, 2, "a task after the durable was re-created")
}
```

```go
// TestSubscribeRebindsAfterItsStreamIsDeleted is the NATS-restart case the
// contract suite cannot stage (StreamAdmin deletes durables, not streams): a
// single-node restart wipes a memory-backed stream and its consumers, the
// manager re-ensures, and a running subscription resumes on its own (spec §5.9).
func TestSubscribeRebindsAfterItsStreamIsDeleted(t *testing.T) {
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 60*time.Second)
 defer cancel()
 bus, err := natsbus.New(connect(t))
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("natsbus.New: %v", err)
 }
 t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
 top := contracttest.Topology()
 if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, top); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Ensure: %v", err)
 }
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "nb-rebind-stream",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 1,
 }
 contracttest.Bind(ctx, t, bus, top, sub)
 got := make(chan string, 4)
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  got <- m.Envelope().ID
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 publish := func(id string) {
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkFetchSubject(events.PriorityNormal, id, "en"),
   &events.Envelope{ID: id, Data: []byte(`{}`)}); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish %s: %v", id, err)
  }
 }
 wait := func(id string) {
  select {
  case g := <-got:
   if g != id {
    t.Fatalf("handled %s, want %s", g, id)
   }
  case <-time.After(contracttest.Timeout):
   t.Fatalf("%s was never handled", id)
  }
 }
 publish("before")
 wait("before")
 if err := bus.JetStream().DeleteStream(ctx, events.StreamWorkCaptionarr); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("delete stream: %v", err)
 }
 time.Sleep(time.Second)
 contracttest.Bind(ctx, t, bus, top, sub)
 publish("after")
 wait("after")
}
```

```go
package natsbus

import (
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

// TestLapsedDeliveriesNeverExceedTheSlots drives the reaper's bookkeeping
// without a server: a lapse frees a slot only while fewer than slots are
// lapsed, and at the lapsed cap the loop still asks for one message, so
// JetStream has a pull on which to raise MAX_DELIVERIES (spec §9.3).
func TestLapsedDeliveriesNeverExceedTheSlots(t *testing.T) {
 s := &subscription{
  sub:     events.Subscription{Durable: "d", Backoff: []time.Duration{time.Second}},
  slots:   2,
  running: map[*delivery]struct{}{},
  wake:    make(chan struct{}, 1),
 }
 now := time.Now()
 overdue := func() *delivery {
  d := &delivery{seq: uint64(len(s.running) + 1), attempt: 1, deadline: now.Add(-2 * time.Second)}
  s.running[d] = struct{}{}
  s.live++
  return d
 }
 first, _ := overdue(), overdue()
 if n := s.next(); n != 0 {
  t.Fatalf("every slot live: next() = %d, want 0", n)
 }
 s.reap(now)
 if s.live != 0 || s.lapsed != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("after the first reap: live %d lapsed %d, want 0 and 2", s.live, s.lapsed)
 }
 if n := s.next(); n != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("two lapsed, none live: next() = %d, want 2", n)
 }
 overdue()
 overdue()
 s.reap(now)
 if s.live != 2 || s.lapsed != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("at the lapsed cap: live %d lapsed %d, want 2 and 2 (four handlers, twice the slots)", s.live, s.lapsed)
 }
 if n := s.next(); n != 1 {
  t.Fatalf("at the lapsed cap with every slot held: next() = %d, want 1 (a pull stays open)", n)
 }
 s.finish(first)
 s.reap(now)
 if s.live != 1 || s.lapsed != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("after a lapsed handler returned: live %d lapsed %d, want 1 and 2", s.live, s.lapsed)
 }
}
```

```go
// subscription's lapse deadline with it.
func (m *message) InProgress(context.Context) error {
```

```go
package natsbus

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "time"

 "github.com/nats-io/nats.go"
 "github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/logging"
)

// How a subscription waits for a durable it binds: the manager creates it
// (spec §5.9), so one that is missing -- not created yet, or wiped by a NATS
// restart -- is polled for until ctx ends, with a warning once a minute.
const (
 bindPoll      = 5 * time.Second
 bindWarnEvery = time.Minute
)

// bindConsumer looks durable up on stream and waits while it is missing. It
// never creates or updates it. The error is ctx's.
func (b *Bus) bindConsumer(ctx context.Context, stream, durable string) (jetstream.Consumer, error) {
 var warned time.Time
 for {
  c, err := b.js.Consumer(ctx, stream, durable)
  if err == nil {
   return c, nil
  }
  if ctx.Err() != nil {
   return nil, ctx.Err()
  }
  if time.Since(warned) >= bindWarnEvery {
   logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("bus: waiting for a durable the manager creates",
    "stream", stream, "durable", durable, "error", lookupError(stream, durable, err))
   warned = time.Now()
  }
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return nil, ctx.Err()
  case <-time.After(bindPoll):
  }
 }
}

// consumerGone reports a Fetch failure that means the durable or its stream
// no longer exists, so the loop must look it up again rather than retry the
// handle. nats.go v1.53.1 reports a consumer deleted under a waiting pull as
// ErrConsumerDeleted (409), a pull on a consumer that does not exist as
// nats.ErrNoResponders (503, jetstream/message.go checkMsg), and a server
// that restarted under a pull as ErrNoHeartbeat.
func consumerGone(err error) bool {
 return errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConsumerDeleted) ||
  errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrConsumerNotFound) ||
  errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) ||
  errors.Is(err, nats.ErrNoResponders) ||
  errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrNoHeartbeat)
}

// benignFetchError is a Fetch that ended without messages: it expired, or
// its context ended.
func benignFetchError(err error) bool {
 return errors.Is(err, nats.ErrTimeout) || errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrNoMessages) ||
  errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) || errors.Is(err, context.Canceled)
}
```

     (CLAUDE.md's MAX_DELIVERIES gotcha). The code:

```go
package natsbus

import (
 "context"
 "sync"
 "time"

 "github.com/nats-io/nats.go/jetstream"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/logging"
)

const (
 fetchWait      = 30 * time.Second
 fetchHeartbeat = 5 * time.Second
 fetchRetry     = time.Second
 reapEvery      = 250 * time.Millisecond
 // lapseGrace is how far past the broker's deadline a delivery runs
 // before its slot is reclaimed: the broker timed it from its own
 // delivery, a little before dispatch.
 lapseGrace = time.Second
)

// delivery is one running handler's message.
type delivery struct {
 seq, attempt uint64
 deadline     time.Time // the broker's redelivery deadline; InProgress moves it
 lapsed       bool
}

// parkedMsg is a delivery waiting for a slot.
type parkedMsg struct {
 msg          jetstream.Msg
 seq, attempt uint64
}

type subscription struct {
 bus   *Bus
 sub   events.Subscription
 slots int
 run   func(ctx context.Context, m jetstream.Msg, onProgress func())
 watch jetstream.ConsumeContext // the dead-letter watcher; W4.45 makes it a loop

 loopCtx        context.Context
 stopLoop       context.CancelFunc
 handlerCtx     context.Context
 cancelHandlers context.CancelFunc
 hard           chan struct{} // closed by halt: no drain
 hardOnce       sync.Once
 drained        chan struct{}

 mu       sync.Mutex
 stopping bool
 running  map[*delivery]struct{}
 live     int // running deliveries not lapsed: they hold the slots
 lapsed   int // running deliveries past their deadline: at most slots
 parked   []parkedMsg
 wake     chan struct{} // capacity 1
 handlers sync.WaitGroup
 loops    sync.WaitGroup
}

func newSubscription(ctx context.Context, b *Bus, sub events.Subscription,
 run func(context.Context, jetstream.Msg, func()),
) *subscription {
 s := &subscription{
  bus: b, sub: sub, slots: max(sub.MaxInFlight, 1), run: run,
  hard: make(chan struct{}), drained: make(chan struct{}),
  running: map[*delivery]struct{}{}, wake: make(chan struct{}, 1),
 }
 s.loopCtx, s.stopLoop = context.WithCancel(ctx)
 // Handlers outlive the loop by up to sub.Drain, so their context is not
 // the subscription's, though it keeps its values.
 s.handlerCtx, s.cancelHandlers = context.WithCancel(context.WithoutCancel(ctx))
 return s
}

func (s *subscription) start() {
 s.loops.Add(2)
 go s.pullLoop()
 go s.reapLoop()
 go s.drainOnStop()
}

// next starts what parked deliveries it can and says how many messages to
// fetch: the free slots; one at the lapsed cap even with every slot held, so
// a pull always waits for JetStream to raise MAX_DELIVERIES on; else none.
func (s *subscription) next() int {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 s.startParkedLocked()
 switch {
 case s.live < s.slots:
  return s.slots - s.live
 case s.lapsed >= s.slots:
  return 1
 default:
  return 0
 }
}

func (s *subscription) pullLoop() {
 defer s.loops.Done()
 ctx := s.loopCtx
 var cons jetstream.Consumer
 for ctx.Err() == nil {
  if cons == nil {
   c, err := s.bus.bindConsumer(ctx, s.sub.Stream, s.sub.Durable)
   if err != nil {
    return
   }
   cons = c
  }
  n := s.next()
  if n == 0 {
   select {
   case <-ctx.Done():
    return
   case <-s.wake:
   }
   continue
  }
  err := s.fetch(ctx, cons, n)
  switch {
  case err == nil, ctx.Err() != nil, benignFetchError(err):
  case consumerGone(err):
   logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("bus: durable gone; waiting for the manager to re-create it",
    "stream", s.sub.Stream, "durable", s.sub.Durable, "error", err)
   cons = nil
  default:
   logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("bus: fetch failed; retrying",
    "durable", s.sub.Durable, "error", err)
   select {
   case <-ctx.Done():
    return
   case <-time.After(fetchRetry):
   }
  }
 }
}

// fetch asks for n messages and dispatches each as it arrives. Its request
// waits up to fetchWait at the broker; one this process abandons stays there
// until then, which is how a stopped pod's last pull still lets JetStream
// raise MAX_DELIVERIES.
func (s *subscription) fetch(ctx context.Context, cons jetstream.Consumer, n int) error {
 fctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, fetchWait)
 defer cancel()
 batch, err := cons.Fetch(n, jetstream.FetchContext(fctx), jetstream.FetchHeartbeat(fetchHeartbeat))
 if err != nil {
  return err
 }
 for m := range batch.Messages() {
  s.dispatch(m)
 }
 return batch.Error()
}

// dispatch starts a handler for m when a slot is free and parks it otherwise.
// A fresh delivery starts even while an earlier delivery of the same message
// runs: JetStream has given up on that one.
func (s *subscription) dispatch(m jetstream.Msg) {
 var seq, attempt uint64 = 0, 1
 if md, err := m.Metadata(); err == nil {
  seq = md.Sequence.Stream
  attempt = max(md.NumDelivered, 1)
 }
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 if s.stopping {
  return // left unsettled: JetStream makes it again after its deadline
 }
 if s.live < s.slots {
  s.startLocked(m, seq, attempt)
  return
 }
 p := parkedMsg{msg: m, seq: seq, attempt: attempt}
 if seq != 0 {
  for i := range s.parked {
   if s.parked[i].seq == seq {
    s.parked[i] = p // a later delivery of a message already waiting
    return
   }
  }
 }
 s.parked = append(s.parked, p)
}

// startParkedLocked starts parked deliveries, oldest first, while a slot is
// free, skipping any whose message still has a handler running.
func (s *subscription) startParkedLocked() {
 for i := 0; i < len(s.parked) && s.live < s.slots && !s.stopping; {
  p := s.parked[i]
  if p.seq != 0 && s.seqRunningLocked(p.seq) {
   i++
   continue
  }
  s.parked = append(s.parked[:i], s.parked[i+1:]...)
  s.startLocked(p.msg, p.seq, p.attempt)
 }
}

func (s *subscription) seqRunningLocked(seq uint64) bool {
 for d := range s.running {
  if d.seq == seq {
   return true
  }
 }
 return false
}

func (s *subscription) startLocked(m jetstream.Msg, seq, attempt uint64) {
 d := &delivery{seq: seq, attempt: attempt, deadline: time.Now().Add(events.AckDeadline(s.sub, attempt))}
 s.running[d] = struct{}{}
 s.live++
 s.handlers.Add(1)
 go func() {
  defer s.handlers.Done()
  s.run(s.handlerCtx, m, func() { s.progress(d) })
  s.finish(d)
 }()
}

// finish returns d's slot, or its place under the lapsed cap, and hands a
// free slot to the oldest startable parked delivery.
func (s *subscription) finish(d *delivery) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 delete(s.running, d)
 if d.lapsed {
  s.lapsed--
 } else {
  s.live--
 }
 s.startParkedLocked()
 s.signalLocked()
}

// progress moves d's deadline on an InProgress. A lapsed delivery stays
// lapsed: JetStream may already have made it again.
func (s *subscription) progress(d *delivery) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 if !d.lapsed {
  d.deadline = time.Now().Add(events.AckDeadline(s.sub, d.attempt))
 }
}

// reap marks running deliveries past their deadline lapsed, freeing their
// slots, while fewer than slots are lapsed (spec §9.3, "The bound").
func (s *subscription) reap(now time.Time) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 changed := false
 for d := range s.running {
  if d.lapsed || s.lapsed >= s.slots || !now.After(d.deadline.Add(lapseGrace)) {
   continue
  }
  d.lapsed = true
  s.live--
  s.lapsed++
  changed = true
 }
 if changed {
  s.startParkedLocked()
  s.signalLocked()
 }
}

func (s *subscription) reapLoop() {
 defer s.loops.Done()
 t := time.NewTicker(reapEvery)
 defer t.Stop()
 for {
  select {
  case <-s.loopCtx.Done():
   return
  case now := <-t.C:
   s.reap(now)
  }
 }
}

func (s *subscription) signalLocked() {
 select {
 case s.wake <- struct{}{}:
 default:
 }
}

// drainOnStop waits for the subscription to stop, lets running handlers keep
// their context for up to sub.Drain unless halted, then cancels it.
func (s *subscription) drainOnStop() {
 select {
 case <-s.loopCtx.Done():
 case <-s.hard:
 }
 s.mu.Lock()
 s.stopping = true
 s.parked = nil
 s.mu.Unlock()
 if d := s.sub.Drain; d > 0 {
  idle := make(chan struct{})
  go func() { s.handlers.Wait(); close(idle) }()
  t := time.NewTimer(d)
  select {
  case <-idle:
  case <-t.C:
  case <-s.hard:
  }
  t.Stop()
 }
 s.cancelHandlers()
 close(s.drained)
}

// stop ends the subscription: no more fetches, running handlers keep their
// context for up to sub.Drain, and it returns once every handler and loop has.
func (s *subscription) stop() {
 s.stopLoop()
 if s.watch != nil {
  s.watch.Stop()
 }
 <-s.drained
 s.handlers.Wait()
 s.loops.Wait()
}

// halt is Close's stop: handlers' context ends at once, and nothing waits.
func (s *subscription) halt() {
 s.hardOnce.Do(func() { close(s.hard) })
 s.stopLoop()
 if s.watch != nil {
  s.watch.Stop()
 }
}
```

```go
// attemptOf is durable's delivery count of m.
func (s *stream) attemptOf(m *memMsg, durable string) uint64 {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 return m.stateFor(durable).attempts
}

// overdue reports whether durable's delivery attempt of m is past its
// acknowledgement deadline, or has been made again since.
func (s *stream) overdue(m *memMsg, durable string, attempt uint64, now time.Time) bool {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 cs, ok := m.state[durable]
 if !ok || cs.settled {
  return false
 }
 return cs.attempts != attempt || (!cs.ackDeadline.IsZero() && !now.Before(cs.ackDeadline))
}
```

  1. `pkg/events/membus/membus.go`: add the slot book-keeping natsbus has:

```go
// memSub is one Subscribe call's handler slots. A message is claimed only
// into a free slot, as natsbus fetches only for free slots, and a delivery
// past its acknowledgement deadline gives its slot back while fewer than
// slots are lapsed (spec §9.3).
type memSub struct {
 slots   int
 mu      sync.Mutex
 live    int
 lapsed  int
 running map[*memDelivery]struct{}
}

type memDelivery struct {
 msg     *memMsg
 attempt uint64
 lapsed  bool
}

func (s *memSub) acquire() bool {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 if s.live >= s.slots {
  return false
 }
 s.live++
 return true
}

func (s *memSub) unacquire() { s.mu.Lock(); s.live--; s.mu.Unlock() }

func (s *memSub) track(m *memMsg, attempt uint64) *memDelivery {
 d := &memDelivery{msg: m, attempt: attempt}
 s.mu.Lock()
 s.running[d] = struct{}{}
 s.mu.Unlock()
 return d
}

func (s *memSub) finish(d *memDelivery) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 delete(s.running, d)
 if d.lapsed {
  s.lapsed--
 } else {
  s.live--
 }
}

func (s *memSub) reclaim(st *stream, durable string, now time.Time) {
 s.mu.Lock()
 defer s.mu.Unlock()
 for d := range s.running {
  if d.lapsed || s.lapsed >= s.slots || !st.overdue(d.msg, durable, d.attempt, now) {
   continue
  }
  d.lapsed = true
  s.live--
  s.lapsed++
 }
}
```

```go
 }, nil
```

```go
// consume claims into free slots until ctx ends (false) or the bus closes
// (true). Lapsed final deliveries are swept on every pass, with or without a
// free slot: JetStream gives up on them whatever the client is doing.
func (b *Bus) consume(ctx, hctx context.Context, st *stream, sub events.Subscription, h events.Handler,
 ms *memSub, handlers *sync.WaitGroup, ackWait func(uint64) time.Duration,
) bool {
 for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return false
  case <-b.done:
   return true
  default:
  }
  now := b.clock.Now()
  b.deadLetterLapsed(ctx, st, sub, ackWait)
  ms.reclaim(st, sub.Durable, now)
  if ms.acquire() {
   if m := st.claim(sub.Durable, sub.Filters, now, ackWait, sub.MaxDeliver); m != nil {
    d := ms.track(m, st.attemptOf(m, sub.Durable))
    handlers.Add(1)
    go func() {
     defer handlers.Done()
     defer ms.finish(d)
     b.deliver(hctx, st, sub, h, m, ackWait)
    }()
    continue
   }
   ms.unacquire()
  }
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return false
  case <-b.done:
   return true
  case <-b.clock.After(pollInterval):
  }
 }
}

// awaitIdle waits up to d for every handler to return.
func (b *Bus) awaitIdle(handlers *sync.WaitGroup, d time.Duration) {
 idle := make(chan struct{})
 go func() { handlers.Wait(); close(idle) }()
 select {
 case <-idle:
 case <-b.clock.After(d):
 case <-b.done:
 }
}
```

### Task W4.45: Bind-only `Subscribe` and the `DeadLetterWatcher` backstop

**Spec:** §5.9 (`natsbus.Subscribe` binds and never creates, for its durable and
its watcher; `events.DeadLetterWatcher`; `Pull` keeps creating; membus mirrors
the binding), §9.3 (contract cases `SubscribeBindsAndNeverWritesConsumerConfig`,
`SubscribeWaitsForAMissingDurable`, `ALapsedFinalDeliveryIsDeadLetteredWithABindOnlySubscribe`),
§5.15 (`TestOnlyTheManagerEnsuresTopology`'s contract half)

**Files:**

- Modify: `pkg/events/bus.go` (`DeadLetterWatcher`; `Subscriber` and `StreamAdmin.Subscriptions` docs)
- Modify: `pkg/events/natsbus/natsbus.go` (`Subscribe` binds; the watcher is a loop)
- Modify: `pkg/events/natsbus/deadletter.go` (`runWatcher`, `WatchDeadLetters`; `watchMaxDeliveries` removed)
- Modify: `pkg/events/natsbus/pull.go` (creates its watcher, then runs `runWatcher`)
- Modify: `pkg/events/natsbus/subscription.go` (`watch` field becomes a loop)
- Modify: `pkg/events/membus/membus.go` (`Subscribe` waits for its durable; `WatchDeadLetters`)
- Modify: `pkg/events/membus/stream.go` (`claim` refuses an unbound durable)
- Test: Create `pkg/events/contracttest/bindonly.go`, `pkg/events/natsbus/consumer_writes_test.go`; Modify `pkg/events/contracttest/contracttest.go` (registration)

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: W4.41 (topology watchers), W4.42 (`Bind`; every test binds), W4.44 (`bindConsumer`, `consumerGone`, `benignFetchError`, `subscription`).
- Produces: `type events.DeadLetterWatcher interface { WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, sub events.Subscription) (stop func(), err error) }`,
  implemented by `*natsbus.Bus` and `*membus.Bus`; `Subscribe` on both buses
  returns at once, binds its durable (and on natsbus its watcher) when they
  exist, and never writes consumer config.

```go
package contracttest

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "slices"
 "sync"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

// testBindsNeverWrites: only the manager's EnsureTopology writes a static
// durable's config, so an older agent cannot revert a newer topology (spec
// §5.9). A Subscribe asking for other settings changes nothing, and creates
// no watcher the topology lacks.
func testBindsNeverWrites(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 ensured := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-bindonly",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 2, MaxAckPending: 8,
 }
 spec := events.SubscriptionSpec(ensured)
 top := Topology()
 top.Consumers = append(top.Consumers, spec) // no watcher, on purpose
 if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, top); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Ensure: %v", err)
 }
 asked := ensured
 asked.MaxInFlight, asked.MaxAckPending = 1, 1
 asked.AckWait, asked.Backoff = 5*time.Second, []time.Duration{5 * time.Second}
 got := newCollector()
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, asked, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  got.add(m)
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, "bindonly-1")
 got.waitFor(t, 1, "a task on the bound durable")
 if st := consumerState(ctx, t, sa, ensured); st.MaxAckPending != 8 {
  t.Errorf("MaxAckPending after Subscribe = %d, want the topology's 8", st.MaxAckPending)
 }
 time.Sleep(time.Second)
 watcher := events.TopologyObject{
  Kind: events.TopologyConsumer, Stream: events.StreamAdvisories,
  Name: events.DeadLetterWatcherName(ensured.Stream, ensured.Durable),
 }.String()
 withWatcher := top
 withWatcher.Consumers = append(slices.Clone(top.Consumers), events.DeadLetterWatcherSpec(spec))
 missing, err := sa.Missing(ctx, withWatcher)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Missing: %v", err)
 }
 if !slices.Equal(missing, []string{watcher}) {
  t.Errorf("Missing = %v, want only %s: Subscribe must not create its watcher", missing, watcher)
 }
}

// testWaitsForMissingDurable: a subscriber that starts before the manager
// idles instead of failing or creating, and starts once the durable exists.
func testWaitsForMissingDurable(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 sa := admin(t, bus)
 sub := events.Subscription{
  Stream: events.StreamWorkCaptionarr, Durable: "ct-wait",
  Filters: []string{events.FilterCaptionFetch},
  AckWait: 30 * time.Second, MaxDeliver: 3, Backoff: []time.Duration{30 * time.Second},
  MaxInFlight: 1,
 }
 got := newCollector()
 stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(_ context.Context, m events.Message) error {
  got.add(m)
  return nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Subscribe on a durable not created yet = %v, want it to wait", err)
 }
 defer stop()
 publishFetch(ctx, t, bus, "wait-1")
 time.Sleep(time.Second)
 if n := got.len(); n != 0 {
  t.Fatalf("handled %d tasks with no durable", n)
 }
 for _, c := range [][2]string{
  {sub.Stream, sub.Durable},
  {events.StreamAdvisories, events.DeadLetterWatcherName(sub.Stream, sub.Durable)},
 } {
  names, err := sa.Subscriptions(ctx, c[0])
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscriptions %s: %v", c[0], err)
  }
  if slices.Contains(names, c[1]) {
   t.Errorf("Subscribe created %s on %s", c[1], c[0])
  }
 }
 Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
 got.waitFor(t, 1, "the task once the manager created the durable")
}

// testBindOnlyDeadLetters: with Subscribe bind-only, a hung handler's final
// delivery is still dead-lettered, and removed from its work queue, by the
// subscription's own watcher -- and, once the subscription has stopped, by
// WatchDeadLetters alone, the manager's backstop (spec §5.9).
func testBindOnlyDeadLetters(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 t.Run("WhileSubscribed", func(t *testing.T) {
  ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
  dlq := subscribeDLQ(ctx, t, bus)
  sa := admin(t, bus)
  sub := events.Subscription{
   Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr, Durable: "ct-bindonly-dlq",
   Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS},
   AckWait: 500 * time.Millisecond, MaxDeliver: 2,
   Backoff: []time.Duration{500 * time.Millisecond}, MaxInFlight: 1,
  }
  Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
  release := make(chan struct{})
  var once sync.Once
  stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(context.Context, events.Message) error {
   <-release
   return errors.New("hung")
  })
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
  }
  t.Cleanup(stop)
  t.Cleanup(func() { once.Do(func() { close(release) }) })
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-bindonly"), envelope("bindonly-lapse", "index.RssTask.v1", 0)); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
  }
  dlq.waitFor(t, 1, "the dead-letter copy")
  waitUntil(t, "the lapsed message removed from its work queue", func() bool {
   s, err := sa.Subjects(ctx, sub.Stream, events.FilterIndexRSS)
   return err == nil && len(s) == 0
  })
 })
 t.Run("ByTheBackstopAfterTheSubscriptionStopped", func(t *testing.T) {
  ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
  dlq := subscribeDLQ(ctx, t, bus)
  sa := admin(t, bus)
  const deadline = 2 * time.Second
  // MaxInFlight above MaxDeliver: after the final delivery a slot is
  // still free, so the subscription has a pull waiting when it stops --
  // the pull a draining pod leaves behind, on which JetStream raises the
  // advisory with nobody subscribed.
  sub := events.Subscription{
   Stream: events.StreamWorkIndexarr, Durable: "ct-backstop",
   Filters: []string{events.FilterIndexRSS},
   AckWait: deadline, MaxDeliver: 2, Backoff: []time.Duration{deadline},
   MaxInFlight: 3,
  }
  Bind(ctx, t, bus, Topology(), sub)
  release := make(chan struct{})
  var once sync.Once
  var mu sync.Mutex
  attempts := 0
  stop, err := bus.Subscribe(ctx, sub, func(context.Context, events.Message) error {
   mu.Lock()
   attempts++
   mu.Unlock()
   <-release // deaf: the subscription's stop must not settle it
   return errors.New("hung")
  })
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Subscribe: %v", err)
  }
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.WorkRSSSubject("idx-backstop"), envelope("backstop-lapse", "index.RssTask.v1", 0)); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
  }
  waitUntil(t, "the final delivery", func() bool { mu.Lock(); defer mu.Unlock(); return attempts >= 2 })
  stopped := make(chan struct{})
  go func() { stop(); close(stopped) }()
  t.Cleanup(func() { once.Do(func() { close(release) }); <-stopped })

  w, ok := bus.(events.DeadLetterWatcher)
  if !ok {
   t.Fatalf("%T does not implement events.DeadLetterWatcher", bus)
  }
  stopWatch, err := w.WatchDeadLetters(ctx, sub)
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("WatchDeadLetters: %v", err)
  }
  defer stopWatch()
  dlq.waitFor(t, 1, "the backstop's copy of a lapse no subscription watched")
  waitUntil(t, "the lapsed message removed from its work queue", func() bool {
   s, err := sa.Subjects(ctx, sub.Stream, events.FilterIndexRSS)
   return err == nil && len(s) == 0
  })
 })
}
```

```go
// DeadLetterWatcher dead-letters a durable's lapsed final deliveries without
// consuming the durable. The manager runs one per static consumer
// (busconn.WatchDeadLetters) as a backstop, so a lapse a draining pod leaves
// behind is copied even while the durable's domain is at zero replicas (spec
// §5.9). natsbus binds the durable's watcher on StreamAdvisories, which the
// pods consuming the durable share; membus sweeps the durable for lapsed
// final deliveries.
type DeadLetterWatcher interface {
 WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, sub Subscription) (stop func(), err error)
}
```

     `Subscriber.Subscribe`'s doc becomes: "Subscribe binds to the durable s
     names, which the topology declares and the manager's EnsureTopology
     creates, and delivers to h. It never creates or updates consumer config:
     s.MaxInFlight is only this process's slots. A missing durable, or one
     that disappears later, is waited for. The stop function stops fetching,
     lets running handlers keep their context for up to s.Drain, then cancels
     it and waits; it does not delete the durable." `StreamAdmin.Subscriptions`'
     doc: "every durable Ensure declared or a Pull created, and no

```go
var _ events.DeadLetterWatcher = (*Bus)(nil)

// runWatcher dead-letters what sub's watcher on StreamAdvisories reports, one
// advisory at a time, until ctx ends. It binds the watcher, waiting while it
// is missing, and binds it again if it disappears, exactly as the pull loop
// binds a durable; an advisory whose copy fails is naked onto watchRetry.
func (b *Bus) runWatcher(ctx context.Context, sub events.Subscription) {
 name := events.DeadLetterWatcherName(sub.Stream, sub.Durable)
 base := context.WithoutCancel(ctx)
 var cons jetstream.Consumer
 for ctx.Err() == nil {
  if cons == nil {
   c, err := b.bindConsumer(ctx, events.StreamAdvisories, name)
   if err != nil {
    return
   }
   cons = c
  }
  err := b.watchOnce(ctx, base, cons, sub)
  switch {
  case err == nil, ctx.Err() != nil, benignFetchError(err):
  case consumerGone(err):
   cons = nil
  default:
   logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("bus: dead-letter watcher fetch failed; retrying",
    "watcher", name, "error", err)
   select {
   case <-ctx.Done():
    return
   case <-time.After(fetchRetry):
   }
  }
 }
}

func (b *Bus) watchOnce(ctx, base context.Context, cons jetstream.Consumer, sub events.Subscription) error {
 fctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, fetchWait)
 defer cancel()
 batch, err := cons.Fetch(events.DeadLetterWatcherMaxAckPending,
  jetstream.FetchContext(fctx), jetstream.FetchHeartbeat(fetchHeartbeat))
 if err != nil {
  return err
 }
 for m := range batch.Messages() {
  if b.deadLetterLapsed(base, sub, m.Data()) {
   _ = m.Ack()
   continue
  }
  attempt := uint64(1)
  if md, err := m.Metadata(); err == nil && md.NumDelivered > 0 {
   attempt = md.NumDelivered
  }
  _ = m.NakWithDelay(watchRetry[min(attempt, uint64(len(watchRetry)))-1])
 }
 return batch.Error()
}

// WatchDeadLetters implements events.DeadLetterWatcher. It binds sub's
// watcher, which EnsureTopology created, and never creates it; Close stops it.
func (b *Bus) WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, sub events.Subscription) (func(), error) {
 if err := sub.Validate(); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 b.mu.Lock()
 closed := b.closed
 b.mu.Unlock()
 if closed {
  return nil, events.ErrClosed
 }
 wctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 unhook := context.AfterFunc(b.serveCtx, cancel)
 done := make(chan struct{})
 go func() {
  defer close(done)
  b.runWatcher(wctx, sub)
 }()
 return func() {
  unhook()
  cancel()
  <-done
 }, nil
}
```

```go
// boundStream is sub's stream once sub's durable is bound on it, else nil.
func (b *Bus) boundStream(sub events.Subscription) *stream {

 st := b.streams[sub.Stream]
```

     Add `WatchDeadLetters`:

```go
var _ events.DeadLetterWatcher = (*Bus)(nil)

// WatchDeadLetters implements events.DeadLetterWatcher by sweeping sub's
// durable for lapsed final deliveries, the copy natsbus makes from the
// MAX_DELIVERIES advisory, until stop or Close.
func (b *Bus) WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, sub events.Subscription) (func(), error) {
 if err := sub.Validate(); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 if b.isClosed() {
  return nil, events.ErrClosed
 }
 wctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 done := make(chan struct{})
 ackWait := func(attempt uint64) time.Duration { return events.AckDeadline(sub, attempt) }
 b.wg.Add(1)
 go func() {
  defer b.wg.Done()
  defer close(done)
  for {
   if st := b.boundStream(sub); st != nil {
    b.deadLetterLapsed(wctx, st, sub, ackWait)
   }
   select {
   case <-wctx.Done():
    return
   case <-b.done:
    return
   case <-b.clock.After(pollInterval):
   }
  }
 }()
 return func() { cancel(); <-done }, nil
}
```

```go
func TestKeepTopologyEnsuresAtTheLeaseAndReplacesWhatGoesMissing(t *testing.T) {
```

```go
package busconn

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"
 "time"

 "github.com/nats-io/nats.go"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/logging"
)

// keepInterval is how often KeepTopology asks what is missing.
var keepInterval = 60 * time.Second

// KeepTopology keeps t on the broker while ctx lives: the manager's
// leader-only runnable (spec §5.9). After the split only the manager creates
// topology, and on single-node NATS every stream and bucket ForSingleNode
// keeps in memory -- with its consumers -- is gone after a NATS restart. So
// it ensures t once at start, when the lease is won (converging anything an
// older leader changed meanwhile), again on every reconnect of nc, and every
// keepInterval while StreamAdmin.Missing reports anything. A failed ensure is
// logged and retried, never returned: the next reconnect or interval tries
// again. Running subscriptions re-bind on their own. nc may be nil (no
// reconnect hook, as for membus).
func KeepTopology(ctx context.Context, nc *nats.Conn, bus events.Bus, t events.Topology) error {
 admin, ok := bus.(events.StreamAdmin)
 if !ok {
  return fmt.Errorf("busconn: %T cannot report missing topology (no events.StreamAdmin)", bus)
 }
 log := logging.FromContext(ctx)
 reconnected := make(chan struct{}, 1)
 if nc != nil {
  prev := nc.Opts.ReconnectedCB
  nc.SetReconnectHandler(func(c *nats.Conn) {
   if prev != nil {
    prev(c)
   }
   select {
   case reconnected <- struct{}{}:
   default:
   }
  })
  defer nc.SetReconnectHandler(prev)
 }
 ensure := func(why string) {
  if err := EnsureTopology(ctx, bus, t); err != nil {
   if ctx.Err() == nil {
    log.Error("bus: ensuring the topology failed; will retry", "why", why, "error", err)
   }
   return
  }
  log.Info("bus: topology ensured", "why", why)
 }
 ensure("lease acquired")
 tick := time.NewTicker(keepInterval)
 defer tick.Stop()
 for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return nil
  case <-reconnected:
   ensure("NATS reconnected")
  case <-tick.C:
   gone, err := admin.Missing(ctx, t)
   switch {
   case err != nil:
    if ctx.Err() == nil {
     log.Warn("bus: could not ask what topology is missing", "error", err)
    }
   case len(gone) > 0:
    log.Warn("bus: topology objects missing; re-creating them", "missing", gone)
    ensure("objects missing")
   }
  }
 }
}
```

  1. Create `pkg/busconn/deadletters.go` (GPL header):

```go
package busconn

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
)

// WatchDeadLetters watches every static consumer of t for lapsed final
// deliveries until ctx ends: the manager's leader-only backstop (spec §5.9).
// A lapsed final delivery stays ack-pending until JetStream raises its
// MAX_DELIVERIES advisory on a waiting pull, which a draining pod's last pull
// can do after the pod is gone; in a domain at zero replicas nothing else
// would copy it until the next wake. The dead-letter watchers themselves
// (on StreamAdvisories) are not watched.
func WatchDeadLetters(ctx context.Context, bus events.Bus, t events.Topology) error {
 w, ok := bus.(events.DeadLetterWatcher)
 if !ok {
  return fmt.Errorf("busconn: %T is not an events.DeadLetterWatcher", bus)
 }
 var stops []func()
 defer func() {
  for _, stop := range stops {
   stop()
  }
 }()
 for _, c := range t.Consumers {
  if c.Stream == events.StreamAdvisories {
   continue
  }
  stop, err := w.WatchDeadLetters(ctx, c.Subscription())
  if err != nil {
   return fmt.Errorf("busconn: watch the dead letters of %s: %w", c.Name, err)
  }
  stops = append(stops, stop)
 }
 <-ctx.Done()
 return nil
}
```

  1. `pkg/busconn/busconn.go`, `EnsureTopology`'s doc (carried from pkg/k8s
     by W1.4, still saying "every replica of every service calls this") is
     rewritten: "EnsureTopology creates or updates every stream, consumer,
     dead-letter watcher, bucket and object store in t. Only the manager calls
     it, once before it starts and then through KeepTopology (spec §5.9); every
     other process waits for the topology with AwaitTopology and binds, so an
     older agent can never revert a newer topology."

## Wave 4d: autoscaling, the manager side (W4.60 to W4.75)

Spec: `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md` §9.0,
§9.1.1, §9.2 (`pkg/agentdomain`), §9.4, §9.5, §9.6, §9.8, §9.9, §3.4.1 (the four
autoscale flags), §3.4.3 (the autoscale row), §3.5.3 ("The recycle sweep becomes
queued work"), §4.2.1 (`app/autoscale`), §5.3.6 (`clustarr-autoscale`), §13
OD27-OD36 and OD46. §11.1 step 7, plus the recycle half of step 4's import work
that OD36 moves here. Verified against the worktree at `4b103429` (local main
`cdbdd870` plus the spec commit).

What this wave builds: the domain table (`pkg/agentdomain`) and the
`MaxAckPending` raise it guards; the HPA reconciler (`app/autoscale/controller`:
`MatchingNodes`, `RenderHPA`, `Reconciler`, field manager `clustarr-autoscale`);
the hand-rolled External Metrics API (`app/autoscale/extmetrics`: `Handler`,
`FrontProxyAuth`, the TLS `Server` that is a `*manager.Server`, `CertManager`
with the caBundle injection, `QueueGauge`, `NamespaceGuard`);
`app/autoscale.Register`; and the recycle sweep as a manager-published task on
`importarr-recycle` (OD36, every 6 h). Nothing here wires `app/autoscale` into a
binary: `internal/cli/manager` (Wave 5, W5.7) calls `autoscale.Register`.

The AudioGraft work that landed after the spec (`--graft-task`, the AudioGraft
controller, `--graft-concurrency`) is not touched by this wave: the autoscale
reconciler selects only Deployments labelled `autoscale.clustarr.io/domain`, never
the transcode pool Jobs or the graft Job (both controller-rendered, §9.1.1
"engines, transcode pools: no"), and this wave edits no file under `app/squash`
or `cmd/squasharr-worker`. The interim RBAC placement below adds
`./app/autoscale/...` to squasharr's role, which also carries the AudioGraft
controller's markers; the change is additive and leaves those rules as they are.

```python
#!/usr/bin/env python3
# Paste config/rbac/<role>_role.yaml's rules between the chart's BEGIN/END
# sentinels, as charts/clustarr/templates/rbac.yaml's header says to.
import sys
role = sys.argv[1]
src = open(f"config/rbac/{role}_role.yaml").read()
rules = src[src.index("rules:\n") + len("rules:\n"):]
path = "charts/clustarr/templates/rbac.yaml"
chart = open(path).read()
begin = f"# BEGIN generated from config/rbac/{role}_role.yaml -- do not edit by hand.\n"
end = f"# END generated from config/rbac/{role}_role.yaml."
i = chart.index(begin) + len(begin)
j = chart.index(end)
open(path, "w").write(chart[:i] + rules + chart[j:])
```

```go
// RecycleSweepTask asks the import domain to sweep every recycle bin once
// (fileimport.RecycleSweeper.SweepOnce). Subject:
// clustarr.work.importarr.recycle.sweep, consumed by ConsumerImportRecycle
// ("importarr-recycle"). The manager's recyclesweep.Scheduler publishes one
// per 6-hour UTC slot (spec 2026-10-06 §3.5.3, OD36).
//
// It names no object: a bin shared by several RootFolders is swept with the
// longest retention any of them asks for, which one task over every bin
// knows and a per-RootFolder task would not.
type RecycleSweepTask struct {
 // Period is the start of the 6-hour UTC slot the sweep was queued for.
 // The handler does not read it; a dead letter carries it so an operator
 // can tell which sweep failed.
 Period time.Time `json:"period"`
}

// Schema implements Payload.
func (RecycleSweepTask) Schema() string { return "importarr.RecycleSweepTask.v1" }
```
