```go
// nats_test.go. Every clustarr Deployment dials NATS (manager, agents, ui,
// markers alike), so every one must carry NATS_URL, and one installer names one
// endpoint. Keyed on the installers' own labels until the installers wave keys
// it on binpath commands (§10.3.3).
func TestEveryClustarrDeploymentCarriesNATSURL(t *testing.T) {
 check := func(t *testing.T, installer string, deps []appsv1.Deployment) {
  urls := map[string]string{}
  for _, d := range deps {
   var url string
   for _, e := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Env {
    if e.Name == "NATS_URL" {
     url = e.Value
    }
   }
   require.NotEmptyf(t, url, "%s: Deployment %q sets no NATS_URL; it would dial %q, which no installer creates",
    installer, d.Name, "nats://clustarr-nats:4222")
   urls[d.Name] = url
  }
  require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(urls), 7, "%s: too few clustarr Deployments checked", installer)
  var ui string
  for name := range urls {
   if strings.HasSuffix(name, "ui") {
    ui = name
   }
  }
  require.NotEmpty(t, ui, "%s: the ui Deployment was not checked", installer)
  for name, url := range urls {
   require.Equalf(t, urls[ui], url, "%s: Deployment %q dials a different NATS from the ui", installer, name)
  }
 }
 t.Run("kustomize", func(t *testing.T) {
  paths, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(installtest.RepoRoot(t), "config/manager/*.yaml"))
  require.NoError(t, err)
  var all []appsv1.Deployment
  for _, p := range paths {
   all = append(all, installtest.DeploymentsIn(t, p)...)
  }
  check(t, "config/manager", all)
 })
 t.Run("chart", func(t *testing.T) {
  var ours []appsv1.Deployment
  for _, d := range installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t)).Deployments {
   if d.Spec.Template.Labels["app.kubernetes.io/name"] == "clustarr" {
    ours = append(ours, d)
   }
  }
  check(t, "charts/clustarr", ours)
 })
}
```

```go
// engine_identity_test.go. The Deployment that renders engines is the one
// carrying the engine image variable (today grabarr's CLUSTARR_ENGINE_IMAGE,
// after the installers wave the manager's CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE).
func engineRenderer(t *testing.T, r installtest.Rendered) (appsv1.Deployment, map[string]string) {
 t.Helper()
 for _, d := range r.Deployments {
  env := map[string]string{}
  for _, e := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Env {
   if e.ValueFrom == nil {
    env[e.Name] = e.Value
   }
  }
  if _, ok := env["CLUSTARR_ENGINE_IMAGE"]; ok {
   return d, env
  }
  if _, ok := env["CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE"]; ok {
   return d, env
  }
 }
 t.Fatal("no Deployment carries the engine image")
 return appsv1.Deployment{}, nil
}

func renders(t *testing.T) map[string]installtest.Rendered {
 return map[string]installtest.Rendered{
  "helm template clustarr":   installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t)),
  "helm template media":      installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.Run(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), installtest.FindTool(t, "helm"), "template", "media", "charts/clustarr")),
  "kustomize config/default": installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default")),
 }
}

func TestManagerStampsAClaimTheInstallerCreates(t *testing.T) {
 for name, r := range renders(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   dep, env := engineRenderer(t, r)
   claim := cmp.Or(env["CLUSTARR_DATA_CLAIM"], downloadclient.DefaultDataClaimName)
   require.True(t, r.Claims[claim], "engines would mount PVC %q, which %s does not create", claim, name)
   var mounted string
   for _, v := range dep.Spec.Template.Spec.Volumes {
    if v.Name == "data" && v.PersistentVolumeClaim != nil {
     mounted = v.PersistentVolumeClaim.ClaimName
    }
   }
   require.Equal(t, mounted, claim, "the engines would mount a different /data than the controller that sizes it")
  })

func TestEnginesRunAsAnAccountTheInstallerBinds(t *testing.T) {
 want := installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), "grabarr_engine_role.yaml").Rules))
 for name, r := range renders(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   _, env := engineRenderer(t, r)
   account := cmp.Or(env["CLUSTARR_ENGINE_SERVICE_ACCOUNT"], downloadclient.DefaultEngineServiceAccount)
   require.True(t, r.ServiceAccounts[account],
    "engine pods would run as ServiceAccount %q, which %s does not create", account, name)
   var boundTo []string
   for _, b := range r.Bindings {
    for _, s := range b.Subjects {
     if s.Kind == "ServiceAccount" && s.Name == account {
      boundTo = append(boundTo, b.RoleRef.Name)
     }
    }
   }
   require.Len(t, boundTo, 1, "engine ServiceAccount %q is bound to %v, not exactly the engine ClusterRole", account, boundTo)
   role, ok := r.Roles[boundTo[0]]
   require.True(t, ok, "ClusterRole %q is not rendered by %s", boundTo[0], name)
   require.Equal(t, want, installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(role.Rules)),
    "the ClusterRole engine pods run under is not the generated engine role")
  })
 }
}
```

```go
// Only the manager creates or updates topology (§5.9): busconn.EnsureTopology,
// busconn.KeepTopology and busconn.WatchDeadLetters are called, package-
// qualified, only from internal/cli/manager. pkg/busconn's own KeepTopology
// calls EnsureTopology unqualified, inside the package, which is the one
// other caller §5.15 allows.
func TestOnlyTheManagerEnsuresTopology(t *testing.T) {
 var managerCalls int
 for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
  busconnAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/busconn", "busconn")
  k8sAlias := importAlias(f, mod+"pkg/k8s", "k8s")
  ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
   call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
   if !ok {
    return true
   }
   for _, name := range []string{"EnsureTopology", "KeepTopology", "WatchDeadLetters"} {
    if !isSelector(call.Fun, busconnAlias, name) && !isSelector(call.Fun, k8sAlias, name) {
     continue
    }
    if strings.HasPrefix(path, "internal/cli/manager/") {
     managerCalls++
     continue
    }
    t.Errorf("%s calls %s: only the manager writes topology, so an older agent can never revert a newer one (§5.9)", path, name)
   }
   return true
  })
 }
 require.GreaterOrEqual(t, managerCalls, 3, "internal/cli/manager ensures, keeps and watches")
}
```

`test/starttest/indexes.go`:

```go
// RegisterIndexes registers each declared index on idx once, as
// internal/cli/agent does, for a test that builds its manager by hand. It
// lives here, under test/, because only internal/cli/agent may call
// IndexField in code a binary links (TestTheAgentIsTheOnlyIndexRegistrar).
// A (kind, name) declared by two slices is registered once.
func RegisterIndexes(ctx context.Context, idx client.FieldIndexer, ix ...[]k8s.FieldIndex) error {
 type key struct {
  kind reflect.Type
  name string
 }
 seen := map[key]bool{}
 for _, set := range ix {
  for _, fi := range set {
   k := key{reflect.TypeOf(fi.Object), fi.Name}
   if seen[k] {
    continue
   }
   seen[k] = true
   if err := idx.IndexField(ctx, fi.Object, fi.Name, fi.Extract); err != nil {
    return fmt.Errorf("starttest: field index %q on %T: %w", fi.Name, fi.Object, err)
   }
  }
 }
 return nil
}
```

### Task W5.19: `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome`
> **Amended by ADR-0019:** see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-agents-report-over-nats.md, "Amendments", W5.19.

> Runs after W5.17 and before the gate W5.18: it needs the five binaries and the eight domain packages as roots, and no `cmd/clustarr` or `app/<svc>` root left to link everything.

**Spec:** §5.15 (`TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome`, R7), §5.2 (the "After" column), §5.3.2 (the session store's `s.Manager`, attributed to its constructor's caller), §5.3.6 (`clustarr-autoscale`)
**Files:**

- Create: `test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go`
**Interfaces:**
- Consumes: W5.14's `depguard.Load(t, pkg, env...) Graph` with `Has` and `Chain`; W5.15's `productionFiles(t, dirs...) map[string]*ast.File` and `isSelector`/`importAlias` (`test/guards/astutil_test.go`); W4.20's `clients.NewSessionStore(c, bus, mgr)`; every `k8s.Manager*` constant (`k8s.FieldManagers()`), including Wave 4d's `k8s.ManagerAutoscale`.
- Produces: the guard only.

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test.** `test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go` (package `guards`):

```go
// homeRoots are §5.15's home roots, package-granular on purpose: each agent
// domain has its own registration package so a writer's home is the domain
// that links it, not the one agent binary that links every domain.
var homeRoots = map[string]string{
 "manager": mod + "cmd/manager", "ui": mod + "cmd/ui", "markers": mod + "cmd/markers", "transcode": mod + "cmd/transcode",
 "catalog": mod + "app/catalog/agent/catalog", "events": mod + "app/catalog/agent/events",
 "metadata": mod + "app/catalog/agent/metadata", "import": mod + "app/import/agent", "index": mod + "app/indexer/agent",
 "caption": mod + "app/caption/agent", "torrent-engine": mod + "app/grab/agent/torrent", "usenet-engine": mod + "app/grab/agent/usenet",
}

// wantHomes is §5.2's "After" column.
var wantHomes = map[k8s.FieldManager][]string{
 k8s.ManagerCatalogarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrSeries: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrFanout: {"manager"},
 k8s.ManagerCatalogarrClassify: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrWorker: {"catalog"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrGrab: {"catalog", "events"},
 k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMetadata: {"metadata"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrArtwork: {"catalog"}, k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMarkers: {"metadata"},
 k8s.ManagerImportarr: {"import", "manager"}, k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker: {"import", "manager"},
 k8s.ManagerIndexarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerIndexarrWorker: {"index"},
 k8s.ManagerGrabarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerGrabarrEngine: {"torrent-engine", "usenet-engine"},
 k8s.ManagerSquasharr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerSquasharrPool: {"manager"},
 k8s.ManagerCaptionarr: {"manager"}, k8s.ManagerCaptionarrWorker: {"caption"},
 k8s.ManagerDLQProjector: {"events"}, k8s.ManagerUI: {"ui"}, k8s.ManagerAutoscale: {"manager"},
}

// multiHome are the names §5.15 allows in more than one home.
var multiHome = map[k8s.FieldManager]bool{
 k8s.ManagerCatalogarrGrab: true, k8s.ManagerImportarr: true, k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker: true, k8s.ManagerGrabarrEngine: true,
}

// linkedNotWritten lists a home that links a writer package it never calls
// (the package-level graph over-approximates), with the reason. Empty until
// the scan shows a case; each entry needs a sentence a reviewer can check.
var linkedNotWritten = map[k8s.FieldManager]map[string]string{}

// aliases are the non-pkg/k8s names for a manager (§5.15's list).
var aliases = map[string]k8s.FieldManager{
 "rescan.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker, "fileimport.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker,
 "importlist.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker, "mediafilespec.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerImportarrWorker,
 "fetch.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerCaptionarrWorker, "catalogstatus.GatewayManager": k8s.ManagerCatalogarrMetadata,
 "catalogstatus.RendererManager": k8s.ManagerCatalogarrArtwork, "actions.FieldManager": k8s.ManagerUI,
}

// fixedManagerWrappers are status-package writers that take no manager
// argument because they always write one.
var fixedManagerWrappers = map[string]k8s.FieldManager{
 mod + "app/squash/status.PatchCAS": k8s.ManagerSquasharr,
}

// writeFuncs are the calls whose arguments name the writing manager.
var writeFuncs = map[string]bool{
 "PatchStatus": true, "PatchStatusCAS": true, "Apply": true, "FieldOwner": true,
 "Patch": true, "PatchCAS": true, "PatchOverlay": true, "PatchRequest": true, "PatchProfile": true, "PatchProvider": true,
 "NewSessionStore": true, // §5.3.2: the store writes as the manager its constructor's caller names
}

func TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome(t *testing.T) {
 byName := map[string]k8s.FieldManager{}
 for _, m := range k8s.FieldManagers() {
  byName["k8s.Manager"+managerSuffix(m)] = m
 }
 // writers: manager -> the packages holding a write naming it.
 writers := map[k8s.FieldManager]map[string]bool{}
 for path, f := range productionFiles(t) {
  dir := filepath.Dir(path)
  if dir == "pkg/k8s" || regexp.MustCompile(`^app/[a-z]+/status$`).MatchString(dir) {
   continue // declaration-only (§5.15)
  }
  pkg := mod + dir
  imports := importsOf(f) // alias -> import path
  ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
   call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
   if !ok {
    return true
   }
   name, qual := calleeName(call.Fun)
   if !writeFuncs[name] {
    return true
   }
   found := false
   for _, arg := range call.Args {
    if m, ok := managerOf(arg, byName, aliases); ok {
     addWriter(writers, m, pkg)
     found = true
    }
   }
   if !found {
    if m, ok := fixedManagerWrappers[imports[qual]+"."+name]; ok {
     addWriter(writers, m, pkg)
    }
   }
   return true
  })
 }

 graphs := map[string]depguard.Graph{}
 for home, root := range homeRoots {
  env := []string{"GOOS=linux", "GOARCH=amd64", "CGO_ENABLED=0"}
  if strings.HasPrefix(root, mod+"app/") && home != "ui" {
   env[2] = "CGO_ENABLED=1" // the agent's build mode (§3.9)
  }
  graphs[home] = depguard.Load(t, root, env...)
 }
 for _, m := range k8s.FieldManagers() {
  want, ok := wantHomes[m]
  require.True(t, ok, "%s has no row in §5.2's After column: add it to wantHomes", m)
  got := map[string]bool{}
  for pkg := range writers[m] {
   for home, g := range graphs {
    if g.Has(pkg) && linkedNotWritten[m][home] == "" {
     got[home] = true
    }
   }
  }
  homes := slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(got))
  assert.Equal(t, want, homes, "%s is written from %v (writer packages %v); §5.2 says %v", m, homes, slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(writers[m])), want)
  if !multiHome[m] {
   assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(homes), 1, "%s is reachable from two homes: one field manager per process (R7)", m)
  }
 }
}
```

  plus four small helpers in the same file: `managerSuffix(m k8s.FieldManager) string` (the constant's
  identifier suffix, from a table built by parsing `pkg/k8s/fieldmanager.go`'s `ManagerX FieldManager = "…"`
  lines, so the guard never restates the names); `calleeName(fun ast.Expr) (name, qualifier string)` (a
  selector's `Sel` and its `X` identifier, or a bare identifier); `managerOf(arg ast.Expr, byName, aliases)
  (k8s.FieldManager, bool)` (a `k8s.ManagerX` selector, a known alias selector or bare `FieldManager` in the
  alias's own package, and the same wrapped in `string(…)` or followed by `.String()`); `importsOf(f)`
  (alias → import path, the default alias being the path's last element); and `addWriter`.

- [ ] **Step 2: Run it and watch it fail, then falsify.**
  Run: `go test ./test/guards/ -run TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome -v`
  Expected: PASS if Waves 3-5 placed every writer where §5.2 says. Then falsify, in a scratch

  `wantHomes`); an over-approximation goes into `linkedNotWritten` with its reason.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** The test is the implementation; nothing in production changes.

- [ ] **Step 4: Run and pass.**

  Expected: `ok`.

- [ ] **Step 5: Commit.**

```bash

git commit -m "test(guards): TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome -- every write's field manager is reachable only from the homes spec §5.2 gives it, by package-granular roots (the five binaries and the eight domain packages) (spec 2026-10-06 §5.15, R7)" -- test/guards/fieldmanager_test.go
```

## Fold waves F0-F9: ADR-0016, the MediaFile remediation loop

**Spec:** loop spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-mediafile-remediation-loop-design.md`) §8.6 and §8.7, and the sections each wave cites; ADR-0016 (`docs/adr/0016-per-file-work-is-mediafile-status.md`); the owner's rulings (`.superpowers/unify/rulings.md`, "ADR-0016 -- owner answers": all three kinds fold, every MediaFile watcher merges into the loop, the fold lands after `cmd/manager` exists, D3 is taken as the loop spec reads it, and public pushes and live-cluster actions wait for the owner).

These waves implement ADR-0016. SubtitleRequest, TranscodeJob and AudioGraft fold into MediaFile `status.subtitles`, `status.transcode` and `status.graft`, which one remediation loop in the manager (`app/remediation`, controller `mediafile`, with file and item keys) plans and writes under `catalogarr`, while every per-file worker answers through a compare-and-swap record in a Durable KV bucket (`pkg/records`) and transcode and graft admission moves into a ledger (`app/squash/admission`, `transcode-admission`).

**Where they run.** F0-F8 run after W5.18 and W5.19 and before W6.1; with Waves 6-10 they are release N. F9 runs after W10.8 and is release N+1 (loop spec §8.2, §8.6, §9 D1). Every fold wave edits the loop, so the tasks run serially, F0.1 to F8.12, then F9.1 to F9.5; each wave's preamble gives its order and what it takes from earlier tasks. Nothing between W4.13 and F8.12 is deployed (loop spec §8.2 rule 3). The Global Constraints bind every task here, ADR-0016's rules among them.

| Wave | Tasks | Depends on | Gate adds |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| F0: prerequisites | F0.1-F0.3 | W5.18, W5.19 | `TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile` with its allow-list |
| F1: records core | F1.1-F1.5 | F0 | `pkg/records` suite; natsbus and membus Watch contract; records-bucket `Validate` rule; KV key contract |
| F2: API | F2.1-F2.4 | F1 | `TestMediaFileStringsAreBounded`, `TestMediaFileAtEveryCapFitsTheBudget`, `TestMediaFileStatusPhasesAreSelectable` |
| F3: loop core, probe, naming, rename, markers | F3.1-F3.6 | F2 | allow-list loses `rename`; `catalogarr-markers` writes gone; disjointness test inverted |
| F4: item keys | F4.1-F4.4 | F3 | allow-list loses the six item reconcilers |
| F5: subtitles | F5.1-F5.5 | F4 | allow-list loses `subtitleprofile`, `subtitlerequest`; `captionarr-worker` retired |
| F6: transcode and admission | F6.1-F6.7 | F5, MP4 phase-1 gate on main | allow-list loses `transcodeprofile`, `transcodejob`; ledger rebuild tests |
| F7: graft | F7.1-F7.5 | F6 | allow-list empty; the records and v1 guards (F7.4) |

## Deviations from loop spec §8.6, each with its reason

1. **`RecordKey`, `RecordSubKey` and `ParseKVKeyToken` land in F1.1, not F1.2.** `records.Requester.Withdraw(ctx, key, rev, seq)` (§4.7's signature) must write `withdrawn{seq}` over an *absent* record, and that record's header needs the UID (and sub-key) the key encodes, so `pkg/records` parses the key. F1.2 keeps the real-server key contract.
2. **F1.4 amends W4.12's tests instead of keeping them unchanged.** §4.9 opens the waker with `WatchUpdatesOnly`; W4.12's `TestTheProbeRecordsSourceEnqueuesResultsOnly` asserts that a record answered *before* the source started is enqueued (a replay), and `TestTheProbeRecordsSourceReopensAClosedWatch` drives `watchProbeRecords` and `probeWatchRetry`, which `recordsource` replaces. The first loses its pre-start row (the informer's initial list wakes that file, §4.9); the second is replaced by `TestSourceResumesFromRevisionAfterAClose` and `TestSourceSurvivesABucketRecreatedUnderIt`, named in the commit.
3. **F1.1 rewrites the W4.3/W4.4/W4.6/W4.11/W4.12/W4.13 `schema.ProbeRecord` composite literals and three literal-Seq assertions.** Go forbids promoted fields in a composite literal, so embedding `RecordHeader` breaks every literal naming `MediaFile`, `Seq`, `State`, `RequestedAt`, `Failure` or `Transient`; and `NextSeq`'s time floor (§4.6, §4.12) makes a first request's Seq the clock's millisecond, not 1. The edits are mechanical; the protocol tests keep every row.
4. **`Ensure`'s report is read through `events.RetiredReporter`, not returned by `Ensure`.** `Bus.Ensure(ctx, Topology) error` has dozens of callers and fakes; both buses keep the first report per retired durable for the Migrator (F8.3).

## Names the later fold files assumed, against what F1 builds

The fold files were written in parallel. Wave F6's "Names this wave takes from earlier fold tasks"
assumed F1's API from the loop spec's prose; F1 builds it that way except where §4.8 needs more:

| Assumed (Wave F6) | Built here | Why |
| --- | --- | --- |
| `records.Record` with `Header() *schema.RecordHeader` | same | |
| `records.NewRequester[R](kv events.KV, s Spec[R])`; `Get(ctx, key) (R, uint64, bool, error)`; `Request(ctx, key, rev, rec, opts ...records.Option) (uint64, error)`; `Withdraw(ctx, key, rev, seq, opts...) (uint64, error)`; `records.IncorporatedThrough(seq) records.Option` | same | §4.7's signatures |
| `records.NewAnswerer[R](kv, s, writer, writerVersion string)` | same | |
| `Answerer.Claim(ctx, key, rec R) (uint64, bool, error)` | `Claim(ctx, key string, seq int64, reclaim bool) (records.Verdict, error)` | §4.8 has three outcomes a bool cannot carry: write, nak with `NotYetDelay` (record absent or older), drop; and only the worker knows whether its lease is live (`reclaim`) |
| `Answerer.Answer(ctx, key, rec R) error` | `Answer(ctx, key string, ans R) (records.Verdict, error)` | the worker acks on `Dropped` and logs at Warn on `DroppedFact` (§4.8's last row) |
| `records.State{Requested,Withdrawn,Claimed,Answered,Failed}` | `records.StateRequested` … `StateFailed`, plus `StateDeferred` | |
| `events.RecordKey` from F1.2 | from F1.1 | deviation 1 |
| `recordsource.New(bus, bucket, toKey) source.TypedSource[remediation.Key]` | `New[K comparable](bus Bus, bucket string, toKey func(schema.Ref) (K, bool), opts ...Option[K]) *Source[K]` | the three-argument call compiles unchanged with `K = remediation.Key` (defect D5) |

| `(*Requester[R]).Get(ctx, key) (records.Current[R], error)` | F3 | `(R, uint64, bool, error)`, as F5 and F6 assumed; there is no exported `Current` |
| `(*Answerer[R]).Defer(ctx, key, seq, until, writer string) (bool, error)`; `Answer(ctx, key, seq, writer, fill func(cur Current[R]) R) (bool, error)` | F3 | `Defer(ctx, key, seq, until) (Verdict, error)`, `Answer(ctx, key, ans R) (Verdict, error)`; the writer is the `NewAnswerer` argument, and the answer is the worker's own record (§4.8 has the Answer re-read the record itself) |
| `(*Pacer).Reserve(remediation, key string, now time.Time)` | F3 | `Reserve(class, key string)`, the clock given to `NewPacer`, as F5 assumed |
| `recordsource.WithDecode(func(value []byte) (schema.Ref, string, bool)) Option` | F3 | `recordsource.WithDecoder[K](recordsource.Decoder)`, generic in the key type |
| `records.ErrDropped` from `Answer` | F5 | `Answer` returns `records.Dropped` (or `DroppedFact`) with a nil error; the caption worker counts and publishes only on `records.Wrote` |

### Task F0.3: `TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile` and its allow-list

**Spec:** loop spec §8.6 "F0.3", §3.20 (`TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile`), §3.18 (every current
watcher and the task that dissolves it); ADR-0016 ("One remediation loop … is the only writer of
MediaFile status"); owner ruling "every MediaFile watcher merges into the loop".

**Files:**

- Create: `test/guards/mediafilewatch_test.go`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: W5.15's `productionFiles(t *testing.T, dirs ...string) map[string]*ast.File`,
  `importAlias(f *ast.File, path, def string) string`, `isSelector(e ast.Expr, pkg, name string) bool`
  (`test/guards/astutil_test.go`); W5.14's `const mod`; F0.1 (the 13 watchers located).
- Produces: `TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile`; the package variables `loopHomes` and
  `mediaFileWatchers` that F3.1, F3.3, F4.2, F4.3, F5.3, F6.6 and F7.3 edit.

The guard scans calls, not types (as `TestUINeverWrites` does): the builder's `For`, `Owns`,
`Watches` and `WatchesMetadata` with a MediaFile object first, `source.Kind`/`source.TypedKind`
with it second, and a cache's `GetInformer` with it second. A `source.Channel` fed from MediaFile
events (§3.20's `ledger.profileWake`, `subtitleProfileWake`) is not syntactically attributable
here; F5.3 and F6.3, which create those two channels, add that half (defect D13).

- [ ] **Step 1: Write the test.** `test/guards/mediafilewatch_test.go`:

```go
package guards

import (
 "go/ast"
 "go/token"
 "maps"
 "path/filepath"
 "slices"
 "sort"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// loopHomes are the packages the remediation loop lives in (ADR-0016): the
// only places a controller may watch MediaFile. app/catalog/controller/mediafile
// is the loop until F3.1 dissolves its Reconciler into app/remediation; F3.1
// deletes that row, so a watch re-added there fails.
var loopHomes = map[string]string{
 "app/catalog/controller/mediafile": "the loop until F3.1 (F3.1 deletes this row)",
 "app/remediation":                  "the loop from F3.1",
}

// mediaFileWatchers is the allow-list: every other package that watches
// MediaFile at F0.3, tagged with the fold task that removes its watch and this
// row (loop spec §3.18, §8.6). A row whose package no longer watches fails, so
// the task that removes a watch removes its row; F8.12 runs with it empty.
var mediaFileWatchers = map[string]string{
 "app/import/controller/rename":           "F3.3",
 "app/catalog/controller/movie":           "F4.2",
 "app/catalog/controller/episode":         "F4.2",
 "app/catalog/controller/album":           "F4.3",
 "app/catalog/controller/book":            "F4.3",
 "app/catalog/controller/audiobook":       "F4.3",
 "app/catalog/controller/issue":           "F4.3",
 "app/caption/controller/subtitleprofile": "F5.3",
 "app/caption/controller/subtitlerequest": "F5.3",
 "app/squash/controller/transcodeprofile": "F6.6",
 "app/squash/controller/transcodejob":     "F6.6",
 "app/squash/controller/audiograft":       "F7.3",
}

// builderWatches take the watched object as their first argument.
var builderWatches = map[string]bool{"For": true, "Owns": true, "Watches": true, "WatchesMetadata": true}

// TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile: one loop is the only writer of MediaFile
// status, so it is the only controller woken by a MediaFile (ADR-0016, loop
// spec §3.20). Every other watch is a row of mediaFileWatchers until its fold
// task dissolves it into the loop's sources.
func TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile(t *testing.T) {
 sites := mediaFileWatchSites(productionFiles(t))
 var inLoop int
 for dir, at := range sites {
  if _, ok := loopHomes[dir]; ok {
   inLoop += len(at)
   continue
  }
  _, allowed := mediaFileWatchers[dir]
  assert.True(t, allowed, "%s watches MediaFile (%v): only the remediation loop may (ADR-0016); fold the watch into the loop's sources (loop spec §3.3, §3.18)", dir, at)
 }
 require.Positive(t, inLoop, "the loop itself watches MediaFile; finding no watch there means the scan is broken")
 for _, dir := range slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(mediaFileWatchers)) {
  assert.NotEmpty(t, sites[dir], "%s no longer watches MediaFile: delete its allow-list row (tagged %s)", dir, mediaFileWatchers[dir])
 }
}

// mediaFileWatchSites maps a module-relative package directory to the
// "file: Call" of every MediaFile watch in it.
func mediaFileWatchSites(files map[string]*ast.File) map[string][]string {
 out := map[string][]string{}
 for path, f := range files {
  catalog := importAlias(f, mod+"api/catalog/v1alpha1", "v1alpha1")
  if catalog == "" {
   continue
  }
  src := importAlias(f, "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/source", "source")
  dir := filepath.ToSlash(filepath.Dir(path))
  ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
   call, ok := n.(*ast.CallExpr)
   if !ok {
    return true
   }
   sel, ok := call.Fun.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
   if !ok {
    return true
   }
   var objs []ast.Expr
   switch name := sel.Sel.Name; {
   case builderWatches[name] && len(call.Args) > 0:
    objs = call.Args[:1]
   case (isSelector(call.Fun, src, "Kind") || isSelector(call.Fun, src, "TypedKind")) && len(call.Args) > 1:
    objs = call.Args[1:2]
   case name == "GetInformer" && len(call.Args) > 1:
    objs = call.Args[1:2]
   }
   for _, o := range objs {
    if isMediaFile(o, catalog) {
     out[dir] = append(out[dir], filepath.Base(path)+": "+sel.Sel.Name)
    }
   }
   return true
  })
 }
 for dir := range out {
  sort.Strings(out[dir])
 }
 return out
}

// isMediaFile reports whether e is &<catalog>.MediaFile{}, <catalog>.MediaFile{}
// or new(<catalog>.MediaFile).
func isMediaFile(e ast.Expr, catalog string) bool {
 if u, ok := e.(*ast.UnaryExpr); ok && u.Op == token.AND {
  e = u.X
 }
 if c, ok := e.(*ast.CallExpr); ok {
  if id, ok := c.Fun.(*ast.Ident); ok && id.Name == "new" && len(c.Args) == 1 {
   return isSelector(c.Args[0], catalog, "MediaFile")
  }
  return false
 }
 if cl, ok := e.(*ast.CompositeLit); ok {
  return isSelector(cl.Type, catalog, "MediaFile")
 }
 return false
}
```

```go
package schema_test

import (
 "encoding/json"
 "os"
 "path/filepath"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
)

// TestProbeRecordWireFormatIsUnchanged: embedding RecordHeader flat keeps every
// key W4.3 gave the probe record, with its type and meaning, and a record
// written before the fold decodes to the same values (loop spec §4.2, §4.12).
// It compares JSON objects, not bytes: the embedded header moves its keys to
// the front of the encoding, which no reader depends on.
func TestProbeRecordWireFormatIsUnchanged(t *testing.T) {
 at := time.Date(2026, 10, 6, 20, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  golden string
  rec    schema.ProbeRecord
 }{
  {"probe-record.golden.json", schema.ProbeRecord{
   RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{
    MediaFile: schema.Ref{Namespace: "media", Name: "heat-abc", UID: "u1"},
    Seq:       2, State: schema.ProbeFailed, RequestedAt: at,
    Failure: "stuck in the demuxer", Transient: true,
   },
   Path: "/data/media/movies/Heat (1995)/Heat (1995).mkv", ProbeHash: "h1",
   ProbeVersion: 3, RequestedVersion: 3, Lane: "high", ProbedAt: at.Add(time.Second),
   MediaInfo: &commonv1.MediaInfo{Container: "mkv", VideoCodec: "hevc"},
   Abandoned: true, AbandonedCount: 2, Source: schema.ProbeSourceProbe, Prober: "importarr-worker-7c9",
  }},
  {"probe-record-seed.golden.json", schema.ProbeRecord{
   RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{State: schema.ProbeProbed}, Source: schema.ProbeSourceImport,
  }},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.golden, func(t *testing.T) {
   want, err := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join("..", "..", "..", "test", "data", "schema", tc.golden))
   require.NoError(t, err)
   got, err := json.Marshal(tc.rec)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.JSONEq(t, string(want), string(got), "the probe record's keys changed")
   var back schema.ProbeRecord
   require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(want, &back))
   assert.Equal(t, tc.rec, back, "a record written before the fold decodes to the same values")
  })
 }
}

func TestEveryRecordHeaderKeyIsOptionalButTheProbes(t *testing.T) {
 b, err := json.Marshal(schema.RecordHeader{})
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.JSONEq(t, `{"mediaFile":{"name":""},"seq":0,"state":""}`, string(b),
  "a key the probe record never had is omitted when unset")
 h := &schema.RecordHeader{}
 assert.Same(t, h, h.Header())
 assert.Equal(t, schema.MaxRecordFailure, schema.MaxProbeFailure)
}
```

```go
// Records keys (loop spec §4.4): the UID's token, plus a sub-key token for a
// subtitle language; neither token can forge the "." between them.
func TestRecordKeysAreUIDTokens(t *testing.T) {
 assert.Equal(t, events.KVKeyToken("4b0c5a7e-2f1d"), events.RecordKey("4b0c5a7e-2f1d"))
 assert.Equal(t, events.ProbeKey("u1"), events.RecordKey("u1"), "the probe's key is a records key")
 assert.Equal(t, "u1.en-3aforced", events.RecordSubKey("u1", "en:forced"))
 assert.NotEqual(t, events.RecordSubKey("a.b", "c"), events.RecordSubKey("a", "b.c"))
 assert.True(t, events.SubjectMatches(events.RecordKey("u1")+".*", events.RecordSubKey("u1", "en")),
  "a Watch wildcard matches one sub-key token")
 assert.True(t, events.ValidKVKey(events.RecordSubKey("", "")))
}

// ParseKVKeyToken inverts KVKeyToken and refuses anything KVKeyToken never
// emits; the segments sweeper and records' Withdraw read UIDs back with it.
func TestParseKVKeyTokenInvertsKVKeyToken(t *testing.T) {
 corpus := []string{"", "-", "--", "-0", "-00", "\x00", "a:b", "en:forced", "Amélie", "a.b",
  "4b0c5a7e-2f1d-4c8e-9a3b-6d7e8f901234", "with space", "\xff", "Wall·E (2008)"}
 r := rand.New(rand.NewPCG(1, 2))
 for range 5000 {
  b := make([]byte, r.IntN(24))
  for i := range b {
   b[i] = byte(r.IntN(256))
  }
  corpus = append(corpus, string(b))
 }
 for _, s := range corpus {
  got, err := events.ParseKVKeyToken(events.KVKeyToken(s))
  require.NoError(t, err, "%q", s)
  require.Equal(t, s, got)
 }
 for _, bad := range []string{"", "-", "a-", "a-0", "-0x", "-zz", "-41", "-2d", "-3A", "a.b", "a b"} {
  _, err := events.ParseKVKeyToken(bad)
  assert.Error(t, err, "%q is no token KVKeyToken emits", bad)
 }
}
```

```go
package records_test

import (
 "context"
 "encoding/json"
 "sync"
 "sync/atomic"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/membus"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/records"
)

// rec is a record of a test remediation: its inputs, its result, and whether
// the answer changed the file on disk (a fact, as a transcode swap is).
type rec struct {
 schema.RecordHeader
 Inputs  string `json:"inputs,omitempty"`
 Result  string `json:"result,omitempty"`
 Swapped bool   `json:"swapped,omitempty"`
}

const (
 bucket     = "clustarr-records-test"
 testSchema = "records.test.v1"
)

var (
 file = schema.Ref{Namespace: "media", Name: "heat-abc", UID: "uid-heat"}
 key  = events.RecordKey(file.UID)
)

func spec() records.Spec[*rec] {
 return records.Spec[*rec]{
  Remediation: "test", Bucket: bucket, Schema: testSchema, MaxValue: 4 << 10,
  New:      func() *rec { return new(rec) },
  Answered: records.TerminalAnswered,
  Fact:     func(r *rec) bool { return r.State == records.StateAnswered && r.Swapped },
 }
}

func newBus(t *testing.T) *membus.Bus {
 t.Helper()
 bus := membus.New(nil)
 top := events.Default().ForSingleNode()
 top.Buckets = append(top.Buckets, events.BucketSpec{
  Name: bucket, History: 1, Storage: events.StorageMemory, Replicas: 1, LimitMarkerTTL: 5 * time.Minute,
 })
 require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(t.Context(), top))
 t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
 return bus
}

func at(seq int64, state string) *rec {
 return &rec{RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{MediaFile: file, Seq: seq, State: state}, Inputs: "in"}
}

// seed puts r under key as another writer would, and returns its revision.
func seed(t *testing.T, bus events.Bus, r *rec) uint64 {
 t.Helper()
 cp := *r
 cp.Schema = testSchema
 b, err := json.Marshal(&cp)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 rev, err := bus.KV(bucket).Put(t.Context(), key, b)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 return rev
}

type current struct {
 rec *rec
 rev uint64
 ok  bool
}

func read(t *testing.T, bus events.Bus) current {
 t.Helper()
 r, rev, ok, err := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec()).Get(t.Context(), key)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 return current{r, rev, ok}
}

type clock struct {
 mu sync.Mutex
 t  time.Time
}

func newClock() *clock { return &clock{t: time.Date(2026, 10, 6, 20, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)} }

func (c *clock) Now() time.Time {
 c.mu.Lock()
 defer c.mu.Unlock()
 return c.t
}

func (c *clock) Add(d time.Duration) {
 c.mu.Lock()
 c.t = c.t.Add(d)
 c.mu.Unlock()
}

// interleavedKV runs after once, right after the first Get through it returns:
// a second writer landing between a worker's read and its compare-and-swap.
type interleavedKV struct {
 events.KV
 after func()
 once  sync.Once
 gets  atomic.Int32
}

func (k *interleavedKV) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (events.Entry, error) {
 e, err := k.KV.Get(ctx, key)
 k.gets.Add(1)
 k.once.Do(k.after)
 return e, err
}
```

```go
package records_test

import (
 "encoding/json"
 "strings"
 "testing"
 "time"
 "unicode/utf8"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/records"
)

// Split §6.5.2's "prev.Seq + 1, 1 when absent" restarts at 1 once the 7-day TTL
// retires a record; a task that waited longer in its queue would then outrank
// a newer request. NextSeq never goes backwards (loop spec §4.6).
func TestNextSeqIsMonotoneAcrossExpiry(t *testing.T) {
 now := time.Date(2026, 10, 6, 20, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC)
 first := records.NextSeq(0, 0, now)
 assert.Equal(t, now.UnixMilli(), first, "the clock's millisecond floors a first request")
 assert.Greater(t, records.NextSeq(0, first, now), first, "the record expired; status still holds the Seq")
 assert.Greater(t, records.NextSeq(0, first, now.Add(-time.Hour)), first, "a clock stepped back never reissues a Seq")
 assert.Greater(t, records.NextSeq(0, 0, now.Add(8*24*time.Hour)), first, "both expired: the floor still moves on")
 assert.EqualValues(t, 8, records.NextSeq(7, 3, time.UnixMilli(5)))
 assert.Equal(t, 7*24*time.Hour, records.FactWindow(6*24*time.Hour, 2*24*time.Hour), "never past the bucket's TTL")
 assert.Equal(t, 3*time.Hour, records.FactWindow(2*time.Hour, time.Hour))
 assert.Less(t, records.RepublishWindow, time.Hour, "inside the work streams' one-hour Duplicates window")
}

func TestOversizedRecordIsRefused(t *testing.T) {
 bus := newBus(t)
 q := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec())
 big := at(1, "")
 big.Inputs = strings.Repeat("x", 5<<10)
 _, err := q.Request(t.Context(), key, 0, big)
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, records.ErrTooLarge)
 assert.False(t, read(t, bus).ok, "nothing was written")

 a := records.NewAnswerer(bus.KV(bucket), spec(), "worker-0", "test")
 ans := at(1, records.StateAnswered)
 ans.Result = strings.Repeat("y", 5<<10)
 _, err = a.Answer(t.Context(), key, ans)
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, records.ErrTooLarge)

 // A failure is clipped to 1024 bytes on a rune boundary, so a failed
 // answer always fits (§4.5 "Writers clamp first").
 failed := at(1, records.StateFailed)
 failed.Failure = strings.Repeat("é", 2000)
 v, err := a.Answer(t.Context(), key, failed)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.Equal(t, records.Wrote, v)
 got := read(t, bus).rec.Failure
 assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(got), records.MaxFailure)
 assert.True(t, utf8.ValidString(got))
}

// Records are input to the loop, never instructions: an undecodable value, a
// value of another remediation's schema, and another file's record under this
// key all read as absent, at their revision, and each counts a decode error.
func TestUndecodableRecordReadsAbsent(t *testing.T) {
 mustJSON := func(r *rec) []byte {
  b, err := json.Marshal(r)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  return b
 }
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  name string
  raw  []byte
 }{
  {"not JSON", []byte("{not json")},
  {"another remediation's schema", mustJSON(&rec{RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{
   Schema: "records.other.v1", MediaFile: file, Seq: 1, State: records.StateRequested,
  }})},
  {"another file's record under this key", mustJSON(&rec{RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{
   Schema: testSchema, MediaFile: schema.Ref{Namespace: "media", Name: "other", UID: "uid-other"}, Seq: 1, State: records.StateRequested,
  }})},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   bus := newBus(t)
   rev, err := bus.KV(bucket).Put(t.Context(), key, tc.raw)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   var counted []string
   sp := spec()
   sp.Errors = func(op string) { counted = append(counted, op) }
   q := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), sp)
   r, gotRev, ok, err := q.Get(t.Context(), key)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.False(t, ok)
   assert.Nil(t, r)
   assert.Equal(t, rev, gotRev, "a write replaces it at its revision")
   assert.Equal(t, []string{"decode"}, counted)
   _, err = q.Request(t.Context(), key, gotRev, at(1, ""))
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.True(t, read(t, bus).ok)
  })
 }
}
```

```go
package records_test

import (
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/records"
)

func TestRequestIsACompareAndSwapAtTheReadRevision(t *testing.T) {
 bus := newBus(t)
 q := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec())
 rev, err := q.Request(t.Context(), key, 0, at(1, ""))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 got := read(t, bus)
 require.True(t, got.ok)
 assert.Equal(t, rev, got.rev)
 assert.Equal(t, records.StateRequested, got.rec.State)
 assert.False(t, got.rec.RequestedAt.IsZero())
 assert.Equal(t, testSchema, got.rec.Schema)

 _, err = q.Request(t.Context(), key, 0, at(2, ""))
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, records.ErrRaced, "a request from a stale read must lose")
 _, err = q.Request(t.Context(), key, rev, at(1, ""))
 require.Error(t, err, "a Seq not above the record's is refused")
 assert.NotErrorIs(t, err, records.ErrRaced)
 _, err = q.Request(t.Context(), key, rev, at(2, ""))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.EqualValues(t, 2, read(t, bus).rec.Seq)
}

// TestWithdrawRules is loop spec §4.7's table for Withdraw(seq 4).
func TestWithdrawRules(t *testing.T) {
 const S = 4
 fact := func(seq int64) *rec { r := at(seq, records.StateAnswered); r.Swapped = true; return r }
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  name  string
  cur   *rec
  opts  []records.Option
  wrote bool
  err   error
 }{
  {"absent", nil, nil, true, nil},
  {"requested below", at(3, records.StateRequested), nil, true, nil},
  {"answered below", at(3, records.StateAnswered), nil, true, nil},
  {"an unincorporated fact below", fact(3), nil, false, records.ErrUnincorporatedFact},
  {"an incorporated fact below", fact(3), []records.Option{records.IncorporatedThrough(3)}, true, nil},
  {"requested at S", at(S, records.StateRequested), nil, true, nil},
  {"claimed at S", at(S, records.StateClaimed), nil, true, nil},
  {"deferred at S", at(S, records.StateDeferred), nil, true, nil},
  {"withdrawn at S: done", at(S, records.StateWithdrawn), nil, false, nil},
  {"answered at S: incorporated instead", at(S, records.StateAnswered), nil, false, nil},
  {"failed at S: incorporated instead", at(S, records.StateFailed), nil, false, nil},
  {"a fact at S: incorporated instead", fact(S), nil, false, nil},
  {"above S: a newer request owns the key", at(5, records.StateRequested), nil, false, nil},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   bus := newBus(t)
   var rev uint64
   if tc.cur != nil {
    rev = seed(t, bus, tc.cur)
   }
   q := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec())
   next, err := q.Withdraw(t.Context(), key, rev, S, tc.opts...)
   if tc.err != nil {
    require.ErrorIs(t, err, tc.err)
   } else {
    require.NoError(t, err)
   }
   assert.Equal(t, tc.wrote, next != 0)
   after := read(t, bus)
   switch {
   case tc.wrote:
    require.True(t, after.ok)
    assert.EqualValues(t, S, after.rec.Seq)
    assert.Equal(t, records.StateWithdrawn, after.rec.State)
    assert.Equal(t, file.UID, after.rec.MediaFile.UID, "the header names the file even over an absent record")
   case tc.cur == nil:
    assert.False(t, after.ok)
   default:
    assert.Equal(t, tc.cur.Seq, after.rec.Seq)
    assert.Equal(t, tc.cur.State, after.rec.State)
   }
  })
 }
}

// Facts are never overwritten (loop spec §4.7): a transcode that already
// swapped the file is recorded even after a withdrawal, and only the caller
// that has incorporated it may replace it.
func TestRequestNeverOverwritesAnUnincorporatedFact(t *testing.T) {
 bus := newBus(t)
 f := at(4, records.StateAnswered)
 f.Swapped = true
 rev := seed(t, bus, f)
 q := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec())
 for _, opts := range [][]records.Option{nil, {records.IncorporatedThrough(3)}} {
  _, err := q.Request(t.Context(), key, rev, at(5, ""), opts...)
  require.ErrorIs(t, err, records.ErrUnincorporatedFact)
  assert.EqualValues(t, 4, read(t, bus).rec.Seq)
 }
 _, err := q.Request(t.Context(), key, rev, at(5, ""), records.IncorporatedThrough(4))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.EqualValues(t, 5, read(t, bus).rec.Seq)

 plain := newBus(t)
 rev = seed(t, plain, at(4, records.StateAnswered))
 _, err = records.NewRequester(plain.KV(bucket), spec()).Request(t.Context(), key, rev, at(5, ""))
 require.NoError(t, err, "an answer that is no fact is replaced without a word")
}
```

```go
package records_test

// TestAnswerRules is loop spec §4.8's table for a task at Seq 4: what
// Superseded says before work, what Claim (live lease, and a redelivery with
// none) and Defer do, and what Answer does with a plain answer and a fact.
func TestAnswerRules(t *testing.T) {
 const S = 4
 c := newClock()
 deferred := func(until time.Time) *rec { r := at(S, records.StateDeferred); r.DeferredUntil = &until; return r }
 W, N, D, F := records.Wrote, records.NotYet, records.Dropped, records.DroppedFact
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  name                                    string
  cur                                     *rec
  superseded                              bool
  claim, reclaim, deferV, answer, factAns records.Verdict
 }{
  {"absent: expired, or the bucket was lost", nil, false, N, N, N, W, W},
  {"requested below S", at(3, records.StateRequested), false, N, N, N, W, W},
  {"answered below S", at(3, records.StateAnswered), false, N, N, N, W, W},
  {"requested at S", at(S, records.StateRequested), false, W, W, W, W, W},
  {"claimed at S", at(S, records.StateClaimed), false, D, W, D, W, W},
  {"deferred at S, not yet due", deferred(c.Now().Add(time.Hour)), false, D, D, D, W, W},
  {"deferred at S, past DeferredUntil", deferred(c.Now().Add(-time.Minute)), false, W, W, W, W, W},
  {"answered at S", at(S, records.StateAnswered), true, D, D, D, D, D},
  {"failed at S", at(S, records.StateFailed), true, D, D, D, D, D},
  {"withdrawn at S", at(S, records.StateWithdrawn), true, D, D, D, D, W},
  {"above S", at(5, records.StateRequested), true, D, D, D, D, F},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   fresh := func(t *testing.T) (*membus.Bus, *records.Answerer[*rec]) {
    bus := newBus(t)
    if tc.cur != nil {
     seed(t, bus, tc.cur)
    }
    sp := spec()
    sp.Now = c.Now
    return bus, records.NewAnswerer(bus.KV(bucket), sp, "worker-0", "v-test")
   }
   unchanged := func(t *testing.T, bus *membus.Bus) {
    t.Helper()
    after := read(t, bus)
    if tc.cur == nil {
     assert.False(t, after.ok)
     return
    }
    assert.Equal(t, tc.cur.Seq, after.rec.Seq)
    assert.Equal(t, tc.cur.State, after.rec.State)
   }
   check := func(t *testing.T, name string, want records.Verdict, op func(context.Context, *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error), state string) {
    t.Helper()
    bus, a := fresh(t)
    v, err := op(t.Context(), a)
    require.NoError(t, err, name)
    assert.Equal(t, want, v, name)
    if v != records.Wrote {
     unchanged(t, bus)
     return
    }
    after := read(t, bus)
    require.True(t, after.ok, name)
    assert.EqualValues(t, S, after.rec.Seq, name)
    assert.Equal(t, state, after.rec.State, name)
    assert.Equal(t, "worker-0", after.rec.Writer, name)
    assert.Equal(t, "v-test", after.rec.WriterVersion, name)
    assert.Equal(t, "in", after.rec.Inputs, "%s keeps the task's inputs", name)
   }

   _, a := fresh(t)
   got, err := a.Superseded(t.Context(), key, S)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.Equal(t, tc.superseded, got, "Superseded")

   check(t, "Claim", tc.claim, func(ctx context.Context, a *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error) {
    return a.Claim(ctx, key, S, false)
   }, records.StateClaimed)
   check(t, "Claim of a redelivery with no live lease", tc.reclaim, func(ctx context.Context, a *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error) {
    return a.Claim(ctx, key, S, true)
   }, records.StateClaimed)
   check(t, "Defer", tc.deferV, func(ctx context.Context, a *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error) {
    return a.Defer(ctx, key, S, c.Now().Add(10*time.Minute))
   }, records.StateDeferred)
   check(t, "Answer", tc.answer, func(ctx context.Context, a *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error) {
    ans := at(S, records.StateAnswered)
    ans.Result = "done"
    return a.Answer(ctx, key, ans)
   }, records.StateAnswered)
   check(t, "Answer with a fact", tc.factAns, func(ctx context.Context, a *records.Answerer[*rec]) (records.Verdict, error) {
    ans := at(S, records.StateAnswered)
    ans.Result, ans.Swapped = "swapped", true
    return a.Answer(ctx, key, ans)
   }, records.StateAnswered)
  })
 }
}

// TestAnswerReReadsBeforeItsCAS: a worker read a requested record, then lost
// its compare-and-swap to the loop's newer request. Answer reads again and
// drops its answer (the lost-update rule), and a fact is dropped with the
// verdict the worker logs at Warn instead of overwriting the new request.
func TestAnswerReReadsBeforeItsCAS(t *testing.T) {
 for _, fact := range []bool{false, true} {
  t.Run(fmt.Sprint("fact=", fact), func(t *testing.T) {
   bus := newBus(t)
   seed(t, bus, at(4, records.StateRequested))
   loop := records.NewRequester(bus.KV(bucket), spec())
   kv := &interleavedKV{KV: bus.KV(bucket)}
   kv.after = func() {
    _, rev, _, err := loop.Get(context.Background(), key)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    _, err = loop.Request(context.Background(), key, rev, at(5, ""))
    require.NoError(t, err)
   }
   a := records.NewAnswerer[*rec](kv, spec(), "worker-0", "v-test")
   ans := at(4, records.StateAnswered)
   ans.Swapped = fact
   v, err := a.Answer(t.Context(), key, ans)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   want := records.Dropped
   if fact {
    want = records.DroppedFact
   }
   assert.Equal(t, want, v)
   got := read(t, bus)
   assert.EqualValues(t, 5, got.rec.Seq)
   assert.Equal(t, records.StateRequested, got.rec.State)
   assert.EqualValues(t, 2, kv.gets.Load(), "Answer read again after its compare-and-swap missed")
  })
 }
}
```

  **1g.** `pkg/records/pacer_test.go`:

```go
package records_test

import (
 "fmt"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/records"
)

// TestThePacerReservesOneSlotPerKey (loop spec §4.7): a key holds one slot
// however often its pass requeues, a consumed reservation frees the key, a
// reservation unconsumed 10 minutes past its slot lapses, and an unpaced
// class is always now. 1,000 due files at 600/min take 100 s of slots, not one
// reservation per pass.
func TestThePacerReservesOneSlotPerKey(t *testing.T) {
 c := newClock()
 t0 := c.Now()
 p := records.NewPacer(records.DefaultRates(), c.Now)
 const lane = records.PaceProbeLow
 slot := func(n int) time.Time { return t0.Add(time.Duration(n) * 100 * time.Millisecond) }

 a := p.Reserve(lane, "a")
 assert.Equal(t, slot(0), a)
 assert.Equal(t, a, p.Reserve(lane, "a"), "a requeued pass finds its own slot")
 b := p.Reserve(lane, "b")
 assert.Equal(t, slot(1), b)
 for i := range 1000 {
  k := fmt.Sprint(i)
  first := p.Reserve(lane, k)
  assert.Equal(t, slot(2+i), first)
  assert.Equal(t, first, p.Reserve(lane, k))
 }
 assert.Equal(t, slot(1002), p.Reserve(lane, "last"))

 p.Consume(lane, "a")
 assert.Equal(t, slot(1003), p.Reserve(lane, "a"), "a consumed key reserves anew")

 c.Add(b.Sub(t0) + records.ReservationLapse + time.Second)
 assert.Equal(t, c.Now(), p.Reserve(lane, "b"), "an unconsumed reservation lapses 10 minutes after its slot")

 assert.Equal(t, c.Now(), p.Reserve("transcode", "x"), "transcode and graft are bounded by the ledger, not paced")
 assert.Equal(t, map[string]int{records.PaceProbeLow: 600, records.PaceSubtitle: 120, records.PaceMarkers: 120}, records.DefaultRates())
}
```

```go
// TestRecordsLinksNoKubernetes: the credential-less transcode and markers

func TestRecordsLinksNoKubernetes(t *testing.T) {
 out, err := exec.Command("go", "list", "-f", `{{join .Imports "\n"}}`, ".").Output()
```

```go
package schema

import "time"

// MaxRecordFailure bounds RecordHeader.Failure, in bytes (loop spec §4.5).
const MaxRecordFailure = 1024

// RecordHeader is embedded, flat, in every records-bucket value (loop spec
// 2026-10-06 §4.5; pkg/records). Its keys are the probe record's own, so the
// probe record keeps its JSON: no existing key is renamed, and every key the
// header adds is omitted when unset.
type RecordHeader struct {
 // Schema is "records.<remediation>.v1"; absent on probe records.
 Schema string `json:"schema,omitempty"`
 // MediaFile is the file whose status incorporates the record.
 MediaFile Ref `json:"mediaFile"`
 // Sub is the unescaped second key token: a subtitle's langKey.
 Sub string `json:"sub,omitempty"`
 // Seq is the loop's sequence for the request (records.NextSeq).
 Seq int64 `json:"seq"`
 // State is one of records.State*; the probe keeps requested, probed and
 // failed.
 State string `json:"state"`
 // RequestedAt keeps the probe record's omitzero: a seed answers no
 // request and carries no time.
 RequestedAt   time.Time  `json:"requestedAt,omitzero"`
 ClaimedAt     *time.Time `json:"claimedAt,omitempty"`
 DeferredUntil *time.Time `json:"deferredUntil,omitempty"`
 AnsweredAt    *time.Time `json:"answeredAt,omitempty"`
 // Writer is the pod name of the last worker write, WriterVersion its
 // version.String(), for skew.
 Writer        string `json:"writer,omitempty"`
 WriterVersion string `json:"writerVersion,omitempty"`
 // Failure is at most MaxRecordFailure bytes.
 Failure   string `json:"failure,omitempty"`
 Transient bool   `json:"transient,omitempty"`
 // Failures counts consecutive failures for the same inputs.
 Failures int32 `json:"failures,omitempty"`
}

// Header gives pkg/records the header of any record that embeds it.
func (h *RecordHeader) Header() *RecordHeader { return h }
```

  **3c.** `pkg/events/kvkey.go`, after `KVKeyToken`:

```go
// RecordKey is a records bucket's key for one object: its UID through
// KVKeyToken (loop spec §4.4). It is ProbeKey's rule for every remediation.
func RecordKey(uid string) string { return KVKeyToken(uid) }

// RecordSubKey is the key of one of several records an object has in a
// bucket (a subtitle language): "<KVKeyToken(uid)>.<KVKeyToken(sub)>". Neither
// token can hold a ".", so the pair cannot be forged and a Watch wildcard
// matches one token.
func RecordSubKey(uid, sub string) string { return KVKeyToken(uid) + "." + KVKeyToken(sub) }

// ParseKVKeyToken inverts KVKeyToken. It refuses anything KVKeyToken never
// emits, the non-canonical escapes included ("-41" for "A", upper-case hex),
// so a key read back always names exactly one id.
func ParseKVKeyToken(tok string) (string, error) {
 if tok == "-0" {
  return "", nil
 }
 if tok == "" {
  return "", errors.New("events: an empty string is no KV key token")
 }
 var b []byte
 for i := 0; i < len(tok); i++ {
  c := tok[i]
  switch {
  case c >= 'a' && c <= 'z', c >= 'A' && c <= 'Z', c >= '0' && c <= '9':
   b = append(b, c)
  case c == '-' && i+1 < len(tok) && tok[i+1] == '-':
   b = append(b, '-')
   i++
  case c == '-' && i+2 < len(tok):
   v, err := hex.DecodeString(tok[i+1 : i+3])
   if err != nil {
    return "", fmt.Errorf("events: %q is no KV key token: %w", tok, err)
   }
   b = append(b, v[0])
   i += 2
  default:
   return "", fmt.Errorf("events: %q is no KV key token: byte %q at %d", tok, c, i)
  }
 }
 s := string(b)
 if KVKeyToken(s) != tok {
  return "", fmt.Errorf("events: %q is not KVKeyToken's encoding of %q", tok, s)
 }
 return s, nil
}
```

  (`kvkey.go` gains the imports `errors` and `fmt`.)

  **3d.** `pkg/records/records.go`:

```go
// Package records is the compare-and-swap record protocol every remediation
// reports through (loop spec 2026-10-06 §4; ADR-0016): one record per
// MediaFile UID (and sub-key) in a Durable KV bucket per remediation; the
// loop the only issuer of Seq, writing status, then the record, then the
// task; workers answering by compare-and-swap after a fresh re-read; nobody
// deleting a record, whose bucket TTL retires it. Requester is the loop's
// half, Answerer the workers'. It imports pkg/events, its schema and the
// standard library only (TestRecordsLinksNoKubernetes), so the
// credential-less transcode and markers binaries link it.
package records

import (
 "context"
 "encoding/json"
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "strings"
 "time"
 "unicode/utf8"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
)

// States of the records buckets the fold adds. The probe keeps its own
// (requested, probed, failed), and its Spec's Answered maps probed and failed
// to answered.
const (
 StateRequested = "requested" // the loop
 StateWithdrawn = "withdrawn" // the loop
 StateClaimed   = "claimed"   // a worker started (transcode, graft)
 StateDeferred  = "deferred"  // a worker postponed to DeferredUntil (markers)
 StateAnswered  = "answered"  // a worker's answer: a success or a remediation-level failure
 StateFailed    = "failed"    // no answer could be produced
)

const (
 // CASAttempts bounds how often a write re-reads and decides again.
 CASAttempts = 8
 // RepublishWindow is how long a requested, unclaimed record is
 // republished under its Msg-Id: inside the work streams' one-hour
 // Duplicates window, so a republish is absorbed (§4.7).
 RepublishWindow = 50 * time.Minute
 // MaxFactWindow caps FactWindow at the buckets' TTL.
 MaxFactWindow = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
 // NotYetDelay is how long a worker naks a task whose record is absent or
 // older: the loop's owed write recreates it within a pass (§4.8).
 NotYetDelay = 30 * time.Second
 // MaxFailure bounds RecordHeader.Failure; Answer clips to it.
 MaxFailure = schema.MaxRecordFailure
)

var (
 // ErrRaced is a compare-and-swap the loop lost: requeue and decide again
 // from a fresh read.
 ErrRaced = errors.New("records: the record changed since it was read")
 // ErrTooLarge is a record over its bucket's MaxValueSize.
 ErrTooLarge = errors.New("records: the record exceeds the bucket's value limit")
 // ErrUnincorporatedFact is a write that would replace an answer which
 // changed the file on disk before the caller incorporated it.
 ErrUnincorporatedFact = errors.New("records: the record holds a fact the caller has not incorporated")
)

// NextSeq is the Seq the loop issues for a new request: above the record's
// and the status's, and never below the clock's millisecond, so a Seq never
// restarts when the TTL retires a record (§4.6).
func NextSeq(recordSeq, statusSeq int64, now time.Time) int64 {
 return max(recordSeq+1, statusSeq+1, now.UnixMilli())
}

// FactWindow is how long the planner keeps reading a withdrawn dispatch's
// record for a fact (§4.10): the work's deadline plus its grace, at most the
// buckets' TTL.
func FactWindow(deadline, grace time.Duration) time.Duration {
 return min(deadline+grace, MaxFactWindow)
}

// Record is a records-bucket value: a pointer to a struct embedding
// schema.RecordHeader.
type Record interface {
 Header() *schema.RecordHeader
}

// Spec is one remediation's protocol.
type Spec[R Record] struct {
 // Remediation names it in errors and metrics: "probe", "transcode",
 // "graft", "subtitle", "markers".
 Remediation string
 // Bucket is the records bucket, for errors.
 Bucket string
 // Schema is RecordHeader.Schema on every value; "" for the probe.
 Schema string
 // MaxValue is the bucket's MaxValueSize; a larger write is ErrTooLarge.
 MaxValue int
 // New allocates an empty record. Required.
 New func() R
 // Answered reports a worker's terminal state; nil is TerminalAnswered.
 Answered func(state string) bool
 // Fact reports an answer recording a change already made on disk; nil
 // is none.
 Fact func(R) bool
 // Carry, when set, copies what a remediation carries forward from the
 // current record into the next before every write (the probe's
 // AbandonedCount, a failure counter).
 Carry func(cur R, ok bool, next R)
 // Errors, when set, counts a failed operation ("get", "request",
 // "withdraw", "decode", "claim", "answer"); the manager binds it to
 // clustarr_record_errors_total.
 Errors func(op string)
 // Now is the clock; nil is time.Now.
 Now func() time.Time
}

// TerminalAnswered is the Answered of every bucket the fold adds.
func TerminalAnswered(state string) bool { return state == StateAnswered || state == StateFailed }

// Option qualifies one write.
type Option func(*writeOptions)

type writeOptions struct{ incorporated int64 }

// IncorporatedThrough states the highest Seq whose answer the caller has
// incorporated: a fact at or below it may be replaced (§4.7).
func IncorporatedThrough(seq int64) Option {
 return func(o *writeOptions) { o.incorporated = seq }
}

type store[R Record] struct {
 spec Spec[R]
 kv   events.KV
}

func newStore[R Record](kv events.KV, spec Spec[R]) store[R] {
 if spec.New == nil {
  panic("records: Spec.New is required (" + spec.Remediation + ")")
 }
 if spec.Answered == nil {
  spec.Answered = TerminalAnswered
 }
 if spec.Now == nil {
  spec.Now = time.Now
 }
 return store[R]{spec: spec, kv: kv}
}

func (s store[R]) now() time.Time { return s.spec.Now().UTC() }

func (s store[R]) count(op string) {
 if s.spec.Errors != nil {
  s.spec.Errors(op)
 }
}

// get reads key: (record, revision, ok). An undecodable value, another
// Schema, or a header naming another UID or sub-key than the key reads as
// absent at its revision, so a write replaces it there.
func (s store[R]) get(ctx context.Context, key string) (R, uint64, bool, error) {
 var zero R
 e, err := s.kv.Get(ctx, key)
 if errors.Is(err, events.ErrKeyNotFound) {
  return zero, 0, false, nil
 }
 if err != nil {
  s.count("get")
  return zero, 0, false, fmt.Errorf("records: get %s/%s: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, err)
 }
 if e.Operation != events.KVPut || len(e.Value) == 0 {
  return zero, e.Revision, false, nil
 }
 rec := s.spec.New()
 if err := json.Unmarshal(e.Value, rec); err != nil {
  s.count("decode")
  return zero, e.Revision, false, nil
 }
 h := rec.Header()
 uid, sub, err := keyParts(key)
 if err != nil || h.Schema != s.spec.Schema || h.MediaFile.UID != uid || h.Sub != sub {
  s.count("decode")
  return zero, e.Revision, false, nil
 }
 return rec, e.Revision, true, nil
}

// at reads key and fails with ErrRaced unless it is still at rev.
func (s store[R]) at(ctx context.Context, key string, rev uint64) (R, bool, error) {
 cur, got, ok, err := s.get(ctx, key)
 if err != nil {
  return cur, false, err
 }
 if got != rev {
  var zero R
  return zero, false, fmt.Errorf("records: %s/%s is at revision %d, not %d: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, got, rev, ErrRaced)
 }
 return cur, ok, nil
}

// write creates key when rev is 0 and replaces it at rev otherwise.
func (s store[R]) write(ctx context.Context, key string, rev uint64, rec R, op string) (uint64, error) {
 h := rec.Header()
 uid, sub, err := keyParts(key)
 if err != nil || h.MediaFile.UID != uid || h.Sub != sub {
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: a %s record for %q/%q cannot be written under key %q", s.spec.Remediation, h.MediaFile.UID, h.Sub, key)
 }
 h.Schema = s.spec.Schema
 b, err := json.Marshal(rec)
 if err != nil {
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: encode %s/%s: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, err)
 }
 if s.spec.MaxValue > 0 && len(b) > s.spec.MaxValue {
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: %s/%s is %d bytes, over %d: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, len(b), s.spec.MaxValue, ErrTooLarge)
 }
 var next uint64
 if rev == 0 {
  next, err = s.kv.Create(ctx, key, b)
 } else {
  next, err = s.kv.Update(ctx, key, b, rev)
 }
 switch {
 case errors.Is(err, events.ErrKeyExists), errors.Is(err, events.ErrRevisionMismatch), errors.Is(err, events.ErrKeyNotFound):
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: write %s/%s: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, ErrRaced)
 case err != nil:
  s.count(op)
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: write %s/%s: %w", s.spec.Bucket, key, err)
 }
 return next, nil
}

// clone deep-copies r through its JSON, the only form every record shares.
func (s store[R]) clone(r R) (R, error) {
 b, err := json.Marshal(r)
 if err != nil {
  var zero R
  return zero, fmt.Errorf("records: copy a %s record: %w", s.spec.Remediation, err)
 }
 out := s.spec.New()
 if err := json.Unmarshal(b, out); err != nil {
  var zero R
  return zero, fmt.Errorf("records: copy a %s record: %w", s.spec.Remediation, err)
 }
 return out, nil
}

// refuseFact is ErrUnincorporatedFact when cur is an answered fact above what
// opts say the caller incorporated.
func (s store[R]) refuseFact(cur R, ok bool, opts []Option) error {
 if !ok || s.spec.Fact == nil {
  return nil
 }
 h := cur.Header()
 if !s.spec.Answered(h.State) || !s.spec.Fact(cur) {
  return nil
 }
 var o writeOptions
 for _, fn := range opts {
  fn(&o)
 }
 if h.Seq <= o.incorporated {
  return nil
 }
 return fmt.Errorf("records: %s %s seq %d: %w", s.spec.Bucket, h.MediaFile.UID, h.Seq, ErrUnincorporatedFact)
}

// keyParts reads the UID and sub-key back out of a records key.
func keyParts(key string) (uid, sub string, err error) {
 first, second, two := strings.Cut(key, ".")
 if uid, err = events.ParseKVKeyToken(first); err != nil {
  return "", "", err
 }
 if two {
  if sub, err = events.ParseKVKeyToken(second); err != nil {
   return "", "", err
  }
 }
 return uid, sub, nil
}

// clip cuts s to at most n bytes on a rune boundary.
func clip(s string, n int) string {
 if len(s) <= n {
  return s
 }
 for n > 0 && !utf8.RuneStart(s[n]) {
  n--
 }
 return s[:n]
}
```

```go
package records

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
)

// Requester is the loop's half (§4.5): it reads records, requests and
// withdraws. Only the remediation loop calls Request and Withdraw.
type Requester[R Record] struct{ s store[R] }

// NewRequester binds spec to kv, the remediation's records bucket.
func NewRequester[R Record](kv events.KV, spec Spec[R]) *Requester[R] {
 return &Requester[R]{s: newStore(kv, spec)}
}

// Get reads key: the record, its revision (0 when absent), and whether it
// decoded. An unreadable record is absent at its revision.
func (q *Requester[R]) Get(ctx context.Context, key string) (R, uint64, bool, error) {
 return q.s.get(ctx, key)
}

// Request writes rec as the requested record at rec.Header().Seq, over the
// record the caller read at rev (0: absent). rec's Seq must be above the
// record's. A record holding an answered fact the caller has not incorporated
// is never replaced (ErrUnincorporatedFact). A record no longer at rev is
// ErrRaced: the planner requeues and decides again. It returns the new
// revision.
func (q *Requester[R]) Request(ctx context.Context, key string, rev uint64, rec R, opts ...Option) (uint64, error) {
 cur, ok, err := q.s.at(ctx, key, rev)
 if err != nil {
  return 0, err
 }
 h := rec.Header()
 if ok && h.Seq <= cur.Header().Seq {
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: request %s/%s at seq %d, not above the record's %d", q.s.spec.Bucket, key, h.Seq, cur.Header().Seq)
 }
 if err := q.s.refuseFact(cur, ok, opts); err != nil {
  return 0, err
 }
 h.State = StateRequested
 if h.RequestedAt.IsZero() {
  h.RequestedAt = q.s.now()
 }
 h.ClaimedAt, h.DeferredUntil, h.AnsweredAt = nil, nil, nil
 h.Writer, h.WriterVersion, h.Failure, h.Transient = "", "", "", false
 if q.s.spec.Carry != nil {
  q.s.spec.Carry(cur, ok, rec)
 }
 return q.s.write(ctx, key, rev, rec, "request")
}

// Withdraw closes seq over the record read at rev, by §4.7's table:
// absent, or any state below seq, becomes withdrawn{seq} (an answered fact
// below seq the caller has not incorporated is ErrUnincorporatedFact);
// requested, claimed or deferred at seq becomes withdrawn{seq}; withdrawn,
// answered or failed at seq, and anything above seq, is left alone. It
// returns the new revision, 0 when it wrote nothing.
func (q *Requester[R]) Withdraw(ctx context.Context, key string, rev uint64, seq int64, opts ...Option) (uint64, error) {
 cur, ok, err := q.s.at(ctx, key, rev)
 if err != nil {
  return 0, err
 }
 var next R
 switch {
 case ok && cur.Header().Seq > seq:
  return 0, nil
 case ok && cur.Header().Seq == seq:
  if st := cur.Header().State; st == StateWithdrawn || q.s.spec.Answered(st) {
   return 0, nil
  }
  if next, err = q.s.clone(cur); err != nil {
   return 0, err
  }
 default:
  if ferr := q.s.refuseFact(cur, ok, opts); ferr != nil {
   return 0, ferr
  }
  uid, sub, perr := keyParts(key)
  if perr != nil {
   return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: withdraw %s/%s: %w", q.s.spec.Bucket, key, perr)
  }
  next = q.s.spec.New()
  nh := next.Header()
  nh.MediaFile, nh.Sub, nh.RequestedAt = schema.Ref{UID: uid}, sub, q.s.now()
  if ok {
   nh.MediaFile = cur.Header().MediaFile
  }
 }
 nh := next.Header()
 nh.Seq, nh.State = seq, StateWithdrawn
 nh.Writer, nh.WriterVersion = "", ""
 return q.s.write(ctx, key, rev, next, "withdraw")
}
```

```go
package records

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"
 "time"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
)

// Verdict is what a worker does after Claim, Defer or Answer (§4.8).
type Verdict int

const (
 // Wrote: the write landed.
 Wrote Verdict = iota + 1
 // NotYet: the record is absent or older than the task. Do not start; nak
 // with NotYetDelay, and ack on the task's last delivery.
 NotYet
 // Dropped: superseded, withdrawn or already answered. Ack; the first
 // answer stands.
 Dropped
 // DroppedFact: a fact over a newer request. Nothing was written; log it
 // at Warn with the task's Seq and inputs, since the loop recovers it from
 // disk (§5.9).
 DroppedFact
)

func (v Verdict) String() string {
 switch v {
 case Wrote:
  return "wrote"
 case NotYet:
  return "not-yet"
 case Dropped:
  return "dropped"
 case DroppedFact:
  return "dropped-fact"
 }
 return fmt.Sprintf("Verdict(%d)", int(v))
}

// Answerer is the workers' half (§4.5): Superseded, Claim, Defer, Answer, and
// Seed for the probe importer. Every write re-reads immediately before its
// compare-and-swap (the lost-update rule).
type Answerer[R Record] struct {
 s               store[R]
 writer, version string
}

// NewAnswerer binds spec to kv. writer and writerVersion (the pod name and
// version.String()) are stamped on every claim, deferral and answer; the
// probe passes "" for both, since its Prober carries the pod.
func NewAnswerer[R Record](kv events.KV, spec Spec[R], writer, writerVersion string) *Answerer[R] {
 return &Answerer[R]{s: newStore(kv, spec), writer: writer, version: writerVersion}
}

// Superseded reports whether a task at seq is already superseded, withdrawn
// or answered, so the worker acks it without working.
func (a *Answerer[R]) Superseded(ctx context.Context, key string, seq int64) (bool, error) {
 cur, _, ok, err := a.s.get(ctx, key)
 if err != nil {
  return false, err
 }
 return superseded(a.s.spec, cur, ok, seq), nil
}

func superseded[R Record](spec Spec[R], cur R, ok bool, seq int64) bool {
 if !ok {
  return false
 }
 h := cur.Header()
 switch {
 case h.Seq > seq:
  return true
 case h.Seq < seq:
  return false
 }
 return h.State == StateWithdrawn || spec.Answered(h.State)
}

// Claim marks seq claimed. It writes over requested at seq, over claimed at
// seq only when reclaim says this is a redelivery with no live lease, and
// over deferred at seq once DeferredUntil has passed.
func (a *Answerer[R]) Claim(ctx context.Context, key string, seq int64, reclaim bool) (Verdict, error) {
 now := a.s.now()
 return a.progress(ctx, key, seq, StateClaimed, "claim", func(h *schema.RecordHeader) bool {
  switch h.State {
  case StateClaimed:
   return reclaim
  case StateDeferred:
   return h.DeferredUntil == nil || !now.Before(*h.DeferredUntil)
  }
  return false
 }, func(h *schema.RecordHeader) { h.ClaimedAt, h.DeferredUntil = &now, nil })
}

// Defer postpones seq to until (markers): over requested at seq, or over
// deferred at seq once its DeferredUntil has passed.
func (a *Answerer[R]) Defer(ctx context.Context, key string, seq int64, until time.Time) (Verdict, error) {
 now, until := a.s.now(), until.UTC()
 return a.progress(ctx, key, seq, StateDeferred, "claim", func(h *schema.RecordHeader) bool {
  return h.State == StateDeferred && (h.DeferredUntil == nil || !now.Before(*h.DeferredUntil))
 }, func(h *schema.RecordHeader) { h.DeferredUntil = &until })
}

// progress is Claim's and Defer's loop: a record absent or below seq is
// NotYet (no write), one superseded is Dropped, one requested at seq or
// allowed by may is written in state, stamped.
func (a *Answerer[R]) progress(ctx context.Context, key string, seq int64, state, op string,
 may func(*schema.RecordHeader) bool, stamp func(*schema.RecordHeader),
) (Verdict, error) {
 for range CASAttempts {
  cur, rev, ok, err := a.s.get(ctx, key)
  if err != nil {
   return 0, err
  }
  if !ok || cur.Header().Seq < seq {
   return NotYet, nil
  }
  if superseded(a.s.spec, cur, ok, seq) {
   return Dropped, nil
  }
  if h := cur.Header(); h.State != StateRequested && !may(h) {
   return Dropped, nil
  }
  next, err := a.s.clone(cur)
  if err != nil {
   return 0, err
  }
  nh := next.Header()
  nh.State, nh.Writer, nh.WriterVersion = state, a.writer, a.version
  stamp(nh)
  _, err = a.s.write(ctx, key, rev, next, op)
  if err == nil {
   return Wrote, nil
  }
  if !errorsIsRaced(err) {
   return 0, err
  }
 }
 return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: %s %s/%s: %w", state, a.s.spec.Bucket, key, ErrRaced)
}

// Answer records ans, whose header carries the task's Seq and whose state is
// one Spec.Answered accepts, by §4.8's table: written over an absent or older
// record (the task's inputs with it), over requested, claimed or deferred at
// its Seq, and, for a fact only, over withdrawn at its Seq; Dropped over an
// answer at its Seq, over withdrawn at its Seq, and over a newer record;
// DroppedFact for a fact over a newer record. Failure is clipped to
// MaxFailure. Timestamps of the request it answers are carried.
func (a *Answerer[R]) Answer(ctx context.Context, key string, ans R) (Verdict, error) {
 ah := ans.Header()
 if !a.s.spec.Answered(ah.State) {
  return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: a %s answer cannot be %q", a.s.spec.Remediation, ah.State)
 }
 fact := a.s.spec.Fact != nil && a.s.spec.Fact(ans)
 seq := ah.Seq
 for range CASAttempts {
  cur, rev, ok, err := a.s.get(ctx, key)
  if err != nil {
   return 0, err
  }
  if ok {
   h := cur.Header()
   switch {
   case h.Seq > seq && fact:
    return DroppedFact, nil
   case h.Seq > seq:
    return Dropped, nil
   case h.Seq == seq && a.s.spec.Answered(h.State):
    return Dropped, nil
   case h.Seq == seq && h.State == StateWithdrawn && !fact:
    return Dropped, nil
   }
  }
  next, err := a.s.clone(ans)
  if err != nil {
   return 0, err
  }
  nh := next.Header()
  nh.Failure = clip(nh.Failure, MaxFailure)
  nh.Writer, nh.WriterVersion = a.writer, a.version
  if nh.AnsweredAt == nil {
   at := a.s.now()
   nh.AnsweredAt = &at
  }
  if ok && cur.Header().Seq == seq {
   if nh.RequestedAt.IsZero() {
    nh.RequestedAt = cur.Header().RequestedAt
   }
   if nh.ClaimedAt == nil {
    nh.ClaimedAt = cur.Header().ClaimedAt
   }
  }
  if a.s.spec.Carry != nil {
   a.s.spec.Carry(cur, ok, next)
  }
  _, err = a.s.write(ctx, key, rev, next, "answer")
  if err == nil {
   return Wrote, nil
  }
  if !errorsIsRaced(err) {
   return 0, err
  }
 }
 return 0, fmt.Errorf("records: answer %s/%s: %w", a.s.spec.Bucket, key, ErrRaced)
}

// Seed writes rec unsolicited (the probe importer, §4.12): at the current
// record's Seq (0 when absent), unless keep says the current record already
// answers for rec's inputs. It reports whether it wrote.
func (a *Answerer[R]) Seed(ctx context.Context, key string, rec R, keep func(cur R, ok bool) bool) (bool, error) {
 for range CASAttempts {
  cur, rev, ok, err := a.s.get(ctx, key)
  if err != nil {
   return false, err
  }
  if keep != nil && keep(cur, ok) {
   return false, nil
  }
  next, err := a.s.clone(rec)
  if err != nil {
   return false, err
  }
  nh := next.Header()
  nh.Seq = 0
  if ok {
   nh.Seq = cur.Header().Seq
  }
  nh.Failure = clip(nh.Failure, MaxFailure)
  nh.Writer, nh.WriterVersion = a.writer, a.version
  if a.s.spec.Carry != nil {
   a.s.spec.Carry(cur, ok, next)
  }
  _, err = a.s.write(ctx, key, rev, next, "answer")
  if err == nil {
   return true, nil
  }
  if !errorsIsRaced(err) {
   return false, err
  }
 }
 return false, fmt.Errorf("records: seed %s/%s: %w", a.s.spec.Bucket, key, ErrRaced)
}

func errorsIsRaced(err error) bool { return errors.Is(err, ErrRaced) }
```

```go
package records

import (
 "sync"
 "time"
)

// Pacer classes (§4.7). The probe high lane, transcode and graft are bounded
// by the import rate and the admission ledger, and are not paced.
const (
 PaceProbeLow = "probe/low"
 PaceSubtitle = "subtitle"
 PaceMarkers  = "markers"
 // ReservationLapse frees a reservation not consumed this long after its slot.
 ReservationLapse = 10 * time.Minute
)

// DefaultRates are §4.7's admission rates, per minute.
func DefaultRates() map[string]int {
 return map[string]int{PaceProbeLow: 600, PaceSubtitle: 120, PaceMarkers: 120}
}

// Pacer is the leader-local admission queue over new requests (not
// republishes), one per class: a key reserves one slot and keeps it until
// Consume or until it lapses, so a requeued pass never reserves again (§4.7;
// TestThePacerReservesOneSlotPerKey).
type Pacer struct {
 mu    sync.Mutex
 now   func() time.Time
 every map[string]time.Duration
 next  map[string]time.Time
 held  map[string]map[string]time.Time
 swept map[string]time.Time
}

// NewPacer paces each class at perMinute; a class absent or at zero is
// unpaced. A nil now is time.Now.
func NewPacer(perMinute map[string]int, now func() time.Time) *Pacer {
 if now == nil {
  now = time.Now
 }
 p := &Pacer{
  now: now, every: map[string]time.Duration{}, next: map[string]time.Time{},
  held: map[string]map[string]time.Time{}, swept: map[string]time.Time{},
 }
 for class, n := range perMinute {
  if n > 0 {
   p.every[class] = time.Minute / time.Duration(n)
   p.held[class] = map[string]time.Time{}
  }
 }
 return p
}

// Reserve returns key's slot in class: the slot it holds, or else the next
// free one, which it then holds. A planner whose slot is in the future returns
// Due = the slot plus up to 5 s of jitter, and checks its reservation before
// any I/O that serves only the dispatch. An unpaced class is always now.
func (p *Pacer) Reserve(class, key string) time.Time {
 p.mu.Lock()
 defer p.mu.Unlock()
 now := p.now()
 every, paced := p.every[class]
 if !paced {
  return now
 }
 p.sweepLocked(class, now)
 held := p.held[class]
 if slot, ok := held[key]; ok {
  if now.Before(slot.Add(ReservationLapse)) {
   return slot
  }
  delete(held, key)
 }
 slot := p.next[class]
 if slot.Before(now) {
  slot = now
 }
 p.next[class] = slot.Add(every)
 held[key] = slot
 return slot
}

// Consume releases key's reservation once its request's apply landed.
func (p *Pacer) Consume(class, key string) {
 p.mu.Lock()
 defer p.mu.Unlock()
 delete(p.held[class], key)
}

// sweepLocked drops lapsed reservations at most once a minute per class.
func (p *Pacer) sweepLocked(class string, now time.Time) {
 if now.Sub(p.swept[class]) < time.Minute {
  return
 }
 p.swept[class] = now
 for k, slot := range p.held[class] {
  if !now.Before(slot.Add(ReservationLapse)) {
   delete(p.held[class], k)
  }
 }
}
```
