```go
// ErrConflict is a compare-and-swap that lost to another writer: re-read and
// decide again. It is records.ErrRaced, so errors.Is holds under either name.
var ErrConflict = records.ErrRaced

// MaxValue is clustarr-probes' MaxValueSize (loop spec §4.3): a probe answer's
// MediaInfo runs to about 153 KB at the schema's worst case.
const MaxValue = 256 << 10

// Option configures a Store.
type Option func(*Store)

// WithErrors counts a failed records operation ("get", "decode", "request",
// "answer"); the manager binds it to clustarr_record_errors_total.
func WithErrors(count func(op string)) Option { return func(s *Store) { s.errs = count } }

// Store reads and writes probe records through pkg/records (loop spec §4.12).
type Store struct {
 bus  Bus
 errs func(op string)
 q    *records.Requester[*schema.ProbeRecord]
 a    *records.Answerer[*schema.ProbeRecord]
 // Now is the clock; nil is time.Now.
 Now func() time.Time
}

// New is the store over bus's clustarr-probes bucket.
func New(bus Bus, opts ...Option) *Store {
 s := &Store{bus: bus}
 for _, o := range opts {
  o(s)
 }
 spec := records.Spec[*schema.ProbeRecord]{
  Remediation: "probe", Bucket: events.BucketProbes, MaxValue: MaxValue,
  New:      func() *schema.ProbeRecord { return new(schema.ProbeRecord) },
  Answered: func(st string) bool { return st == schema.ProbeProbed || st == schema.ProbeFailed },
  Carry:    carryAbandoned,
  Errors:   s.errs,
  Now:      s.now,
 }
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketProbes)
 s.q = records.NewRequester(kv, spec)
 s.a = records.NewAnswerer(kv, spec, "", "")
 return s
}

func (s *Store) now() time.Time {
 if s.Now != nil {
  return s.Now().UTC()
 }
 return time.Now().UTC()
}

// Get reads uid's record.
func (s *Store) Get(ctx context.Context, uid string) (Current, error) {
 rec, rev, ok, err := s.q.Get(ctx, events.ProbeKey(uid))
 if err != nil {
  return Current{}, fmt.Errorf("probestore: get %s: %w", uid, err)
 }
 cur := Current{OK: ok, Revision: rev}
 if ok {
  cur.Record = *rec
 }
 return cur, nil
}

// Watch streams every record now in the bucket and then every change.
func (s *Store) Watch(ctx context.Context) (<-chan events.Entry, error) {
 return s.bus.KV(events.BucketProbes).Watch(ctx, ">")
}

// Request writes a requested record for want at prev's revision, with Seq
// records.NextSeq(prev's, 0, now) (loop spec §4.6, §4.12) and prev's
// AbandonedCount when prev describes the same path and hash. A lost
// compare-and-swap is ErrConflict. The caller then Publishes the task.
func (s *Store) Request(ctx context.Context, want Want, prev Current) (schema.ProbeRecord, error) {
 var prevSeq int64
 if prev.OK {
  prevSeq = prev.Record.Seq
 }
 now := s.now()
 rec := &schema.ProbeRecord{
  RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{MediaFile: want.MediaFile, Seq: records.NextSeq(prevSeq, 0, now), RequestedAt: now},
  Path:         want.Path, ProbeHash: want.ProbeHash, RequestedVersion: want.ProbeVersion, Lane: lane(want.Lane),
 }
 if _, err := s.q.Request(ctx, events.ProbeKey(want.MediaFile.UID), prev.Revision, rec); err != nil {
  return schema.ProbeRecord{}, err
 }
 return *rec, nil
}

// Superseded reports whether t's answer would be dropped.
func (s *Store) Superseded(ctx context.Context, t schema.ProbeTask) (bool, error) {
 return s.a.Superseded(ctx, events.ProbeKey(t.MediaFile.UID), t.Seq)
}

// Answer records ans, a probed or failed answer to t (§6.5.2's rule, which is
// records' §4.8 table for the probe's states). An answer over MaxValue is
// recorded as a failure instead.
func (s *Store) Answer(ctx context.Context, t schema.ProbeTask, ans schema.ProbeRecord) (bool, error) {
 if ans.State != schema.ProbeProbed && ans.State != schema.ProbeFailed {
  return false, fmt.Errorf("probestore: an answer is %q or %q, not %q", schema.ProbeProbed, schema.ProbeFailed, ans.State)
 }
 key := events.ProbeKey(t.MediaFile.UID)
 task := func(r *schema.ProbeRecord) *schema.ProbeRecord {
  r.MediaFile, r.Seq, r.RequestedVersion, r.Lane, r.Source = t.MediaFile, t.Seq, t.ProbeVersion, t.Lane, schema.ProbeSourceProbe
  return r
 }
 rec := ans
 v, err := s.a.Answer(ctx, key, task(&rec))
 if errors.Is(err, records.ErrTooLarge) {
  over := &schema.ProbeRecord{
   RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{State: schema.ProbeFailed, Failure: fmt.Sprintf("answer exceeds %d bytes", MaxValue)},
   Path:         ans.Path, ProbeHash: ans.ProbeHash, ProbeVersion: ans.ProbeVersion, ProbedAt: ans.ProbedAt, Prober: ans.Prober,
  }
  v, err = s.a.Answer(ctx, key, task(over))
 }
 if err != nil {
  return false, fmt.Errorf("probestore: answer for %s: %w", t.MediaFile, err)
 }
 return v == records.Wrote, nil
}

// Seed records a probe an importer ran: probed, answering no request
// (RequestedVersion 0, the current Seq), unless the record is already probed
// for the same path and hash at seed's version or newer.
func (s *Store) Seed(ctx context.Context, seed Seed) error {
 if seed.MediaFile.UID == "" || seed.MediaInfo == nil {
  return errors.New("probestore: a seed needs the MediaFile's UID and a MediaInfo")
 }
 rec := &schema.ProbeRecord{
  RecordHeader: schema.RecordHeader{MediaFile: seed.MediaFile, State: schema.ProbeProbed},
  Path:         seed.Path, ProbeHash: seed.ProbeHash, ProbeVersion: seed.ProbeVersion, ProbedAt: s.now(),
  MediaInfo: seed.MediaInfo, Source: schema.ProbeSourceImport, Prober: seed.Prober,
 }
 _, err := s.a.Seed(ctx, events.ProbeKey(seed.MediaFile.UID), rec, func(cur *schema.ProbeRecord, ok bool) bool {
  return ok && cur.State == schema.ProbeProbed && cur.Path == seed.Path &&
   cur.ProbeHash == seed.ProbeHash && cur.ProbeVersion >= seed.ProbeVersion
 })
 if err != nil {
  return fmt.Errorf("probestore: seed for %s: %w", seed.MediaFile, err)
 }
 return nil
}

// carryAbandoned is the probe's Carry: a request keeps the count of the same
// path and hash, an abandoned answer counts one more than it, any other
// answer resets it.
func carryAbandoned(cur *schema.ProbeRecord, ok bool, next *schema.ProbeRecord) {
 same := ok && cur.Path == next.Path && cur.ProbeHash == next.ProbeHash
 switch {
 case next.State == schema.ProbeRequested:
  next.AbandonedCount = 0
  if same {
   next.AbandonedCount = cur.AbandonedCount
  }
 case next.Abandoned:
  next.AbandonedCount = 1
  if same {
   next.AbandonedCount = cur.AbandonedCount + 1
  }
 default:
  next.AbandonedCount = 0
 }
}
```

```go
func TestRecordsBucketsAreDurableHistoryOneAndBounded(t *testing.T) {

  }

 for name, w := range want {
  b := findBucket(t, top, name)
  assert.True(t, b.Records, name)
  assert.True(t, b.Durable, "%s: a records bucket outlives a NATS restart", name)
  assert.EqualValues(t, 1, b.History, name)
  assert.Equal(t, w.ttl, b.TTL, name)
  assert.Equal(t, w.maxBytes, b.MaxBytes, name)
  assert.Equal(t, w.maxValue, b.MaxValueSize, name)
  assert.Equal(t, 5*time.Minute, b.LimitMarkerTTL, name)
  cfg := events.KeyValueConfig(b)
  assert.Equal(t, w.maxBytes, cfg.MaxBytes, "%s: Ensure creates it with its MaxBytes", name)
  assert.Equal(t, w.maxValue, cfg.MaxValueSize, "%s: and its MaxValueSize", name)
  single := findBucket(t, top.ForSingleNode(), name)
  assert.Equal(t, events.StorageFile, single.Storage, "%s stays on file on a single node", name)
  assert.Equal(t, 1, single.Replicas, name)

// Validate holds every Records bucket to §4.15's rule.
func TestValidateHoldsEveryRecordsBucketToTheRule(t *testing.T) {
 for _, tc := range []struct {
  name  string
  mut   func(*events.BucketSpec)
  field string
 }{
  {"not durable", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.Durable = false }, ".Durable"},
  {"history kept", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.History = 2 }, ".History"},
  {"unbounded", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.MaxBytes = 0 }, ".MaxBytes"},
  {"any value size", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.MaxValueSize = 0 }, ".MaxValueSize"},
  {"a TTL shorter than a request timeout", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.TTL = 24 * time.Hour }, ".TTL"},
  {"a TTL without limit markers", func(b *events.BucketSpec) { b.LimitMarkerTTL = 0 }, ".LimitMarkerTTL"},
 } {
  t.Run(tc.name, func(t *testing.T) {
   top := events.Default()
   for i := range top.Buckets {
    if top.Buckets[i].Name == events.BucketTranscodes {
     tc.mut(&top.Buckets[i])
    }
   }
   err := top.Validate()
   require.Error(t, err)
   assert.Contains(t, err.Error(), events.BucketTranscodes+tc.field)
  })
 }
 top := events.Default()
 for i := range top.Buckets {
  if top.Buckets[i].Name == events.BucketTranscodes {
   top.Buckets[i].TTL = 0
  }
 }
 require.NoError(t, top.Validate(), "TTL 0 keeps records forever, as clustarr-segments does")
}
```

  **1c.** `pkg/events/contracttest/contracttest.go`: in `RunBusContract`, after the

  `t.Run("RetiredConsumersAreDeletedAndPurged", func(t *testing.T) { testRetiredConsumers(t, newBus) })`, and:

```go
// testRetiredConsumers holds Topology.Retired (loop spec §4.15, §7.3.9):
// Ensure deletes a retired durable and purges its filter, reports the lag the
// durable still had (results nobody will apply), and stays idempotent. It
// builds its own durable on the DLQ stream, which every topology keeps, so it
// outlives the results durables the fold retires (F3.4, F6.6).
func testRetiredConsumers(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 const durable, filter = "contracttest-retired", "clustarr.dlq.contracttest.>"
 spec, ok := events.Default().Consumer(events.ConsumerDLQProjector)
 if !ok {
  t.Fatalf("%s is not in the default topology", events.ConsumerDLQProjector)
 }
 spec.Name, spec.Filters = durable, []string{filter}
 live := Topology()
 live.Consumers = []events.ConsumerSpec{spec}
 if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, live); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Ensure with the durable: %v", err)
 }
 for i := range 3 {
  id := fmt.Sprintf("result-%d", i)
  if _, err := bus.Publish(ctx, events.DLQSubject("contracttest", "retired", id), envelope(id, "contracttest.Result.v1", map[string]int{"n": i}), events.WithMsgID(id)); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Publish: %v", err)
  }
 }
 admin := bus.(events.StreamAdmin)
 st, err := admin.ConsumerState(ctx, events.StreamDLQ, durable)
 if err != nil || st.Lag() != 3 {
  t.Fatalf("ConsumerState before retiring = %+v, %v; want a lag of 3", st, err)
 }

 gone := events.RetiredConsumer{Stream: events.StreamDLQ, Durable: "contracttest-never-existed"}
 retiring := events.RetiredConsumer{Stream: events.StreamDLQ, Durable: durable, Purge: filter}
 retired := Topology()
 retired.Retired = []events.RetiredConsumer{retiring, gone}
 for range 2 {
  if err := bus.Ensure(ctx, retired); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Ensure retiring the durable (idempotent): %v", err)
  }
 }
 if _, err := admin.ConsumerState(ctx, events.StreamDLQ, durable); !errors.Is(err, events.ErrConsumerNotFound) {
  t.Errorf("the retired durable still exists: %v", err)
 }
 if subjects, err := admin.Subjects(ctx, events.StreamDLQ, filter); err != nil || len(subjects) != 0 {
  t.Errorf("Subjects under the retired filter = %v, %v; want none", subjects, err)
 }
 reports := bus.(events.RetiredReporter).RetiredReports()
 if len(reports) != 2 {
  t.Fatalf("RetiredReports = %+v; want one per retired durable", reports)
 }
 for _, r := range reports {
  switch r.Durable {
  case retiring.Durable:
   if !r.Existed || r.Lag != 3 {
    t.Errorf("report for %s = %+v; want Existed with a lag of 3 (the first Ensure's, kept)", r.Durable, r)
   }
  case gone.Durable:
   if r.Existed {
    t.Errorf("report for %s = %+v; want not Existed", r.Durable, r)
   }
  }
 }
}
```

```go
package natsbus_test

import (
 "bytes"

 "testing"

// TestKVMaxValueSize: a real server refuses a value over a records bucket's
// MaxValueSize, so an oversized answer can never evict or truncate a record
// (loop spec §4.3, §4.15). The in-memory bus has no such limit; pkg/records
// refuses first (ErrTooLarge).
func TestKVMaxValueSize(t *testing.T) {
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 30*time.Second)
 defer cancel()
 bus, err := natsbus.New(connect(t))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 defer func() { _ = bus.Close() }()
 require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(ctx, events.Default().ForSingleNode()))
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketGrafts)

 _, err = kv.Put(ctx, events.RecordKey("at-the-cap"), bytes.Repeat([]byte("x"), events.GraftsMaxValueSize))
 require.NoError(t, err, "a value at the cap is accepted")
 _, err = kv.Put(ctx, events.RecordKey("over-the-cap"), bytes.Repeat([]byte("x"), events.GraftsMaxValueSize+1))
 require.Error(t, err, "a value over MaxValueSize is refused by the server")
 _, err = kv.Get(ctx, events.RecordKey("over-the-cap"))
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, events.ErrKeyNotFound)
}
```

```go
package events

import (
 "cmp"
 "context"
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "slices"
 "time"
)

// The records buckets the remediation loop requests through (loop spec
// 2026-10-06 §4.3): one per remediation, keyed by RecordKey (subtitles by
// RecordSubKey), every write a compare-and-swap (pkg/records), nobody
// deleting a record. clustarr-probes (probe.go) and clustarr-segments
// (topology.go) are records buckets too.
const (
 BucketTranscodes = "clustarr-transcodes"
 BucketGrafts     = "clustarr-grafts"
 BucketSubtitles  = "clustarr-subtitles"
 BucketMarkers    = "clustarr-markers"
)

// Each records bucket's caps (§4.3). The reservations total 720 MiB, all on
// the file store (they are Durable), against config/nats' 20 GiB.
const (
 ProbesMaxBytes         = 256 * MiB
 ProbesMaxValueSize     = 256 * KiB
 TranscodesMaxBytes     = 128 * MiB
 TranscodesMaxValueSize = 32 * KiB
 GraftsMaxBytes         = 16 * MiB
 GraftsMaxValueSize     = 16 * KiB
 SubtitlesMaxBytes      = 128 * MiB
 SubtitlesMaxValueSize  = 8 * KiB
 MarkersMaxBytes        = 64 * MiB
 MarkersMaxValueSize    = 16 * KiB
 SegmentsMaxBytes       = 128 * MiB
 SegmentsMaxValueSize   = 16 * KiB
)

const (
 // RecordsTTL retires an inbox record nobody rewrote for a week; it
 // outlives every request timeout.
 RecordsTTL = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
 // RecordsMinTTL is the shortest TTL Validate accepts on a records bucket.
 RecordsMinTTL = 7 * 24 * time.Hour
)

func recordBuckets() []BucketSpec {
 r := func(name, desc string, maxBytes int64, maxValue int32) BucketSpec {
  return BucketSpec{
   Name: name, Description: desc, TTL: RecordsTTL, History: 1, Storage: StorageFile, Replicas: 3,
   LimitMarkerTTL: 5 * time.Minute, Durable: true, Records: true, MaxBytes: maxBytes, MaxValueSize: maxValue,
  }
 }
 return []BucketSpec{
  r(BucketTranscodes, "One transcode record per MediaFile UID: the loop's request, the pool worker's claim and answer.", TranscodesMaxBytes, TranscodesMaxValueSize),
  r(BucketGrafts, "One graft record per MediaFile UID: the loop's request, the graft Job's answer.", GraftsMaxBytes, GraftsMaxValueSize),
  r(BucketSubtitles, "One subtitle record per MediaFile UID and language key: the loop's request, the caption domain's answer.", SubtitlesMaxBytes, SubtitlesMaxValueSize),
  r(BucketMarkers, "One TheIntroDB markers record per MediaFile UID: the loop's request, the metadata domain's answer.", MarkersMaxBytes, MarkersMaxValueSize),
 }
}

// RetiredConsumer is a durable a release removed. Ensure deletes it, and its
// dead-letter watcher, and purges Purge (when set) from Stream, every time
// and idempotently, so a results stream nobody reads can never fill.
type RetiredConsumer struct {
 Stream  string
 Durable string
 Purge   string
}

// RetiredReport is what Ensure found of one retired durable.
type RetiredReport struct {
 RetiredConsumer
 // Existed is whether the durable was still on the broker.
 Existed bool
 // Lag is its Pending + AckPending then: results nobody will apply
 // (loop spec §7.3.9; the pre-deploy drain gate keeps it at zero).
 Lag uint64
 // At is when Ensure retired it.
 At time.Time
}

// RetiredReporter is a bus that remembers what its Ensure retired; the
// release-N Migrator (F8.3) counts an undrained one.
type RetiredReporter interface {
 RetiredReports() []RetiredReport
}

// Retire reads each retired durable's lag, deletes it (DeleteSubscription
// takes its dead-letter watcher too) and purges its filter. A durable or
// stream already gone is not an error.
func Retire(ctx context.Context, admin StreamAdmin, retired []RetiredConsumer, now time.Time) ([]RetiredReport, error) {
 var out []RetiredReport
 var errs []error
 for _, r := range retired {
  rep := RetiredReport{RetiredConsumer: r, At: now}
  st, err := admin.ConsumerState(ctx, r.Stream, r.Durable)
  switch {
  case err == nil:
   rep.Existed, rep.Lag = true, st.Lag()
  case errors.Is(err, ErrConsumerNotFound), errors.Is(err, ErrStreamNotFound):
  default:
   errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("events: retire %s/%s: %w", r.Stream, r.Durable, err))
   continue
  }
  if err := admin.DeleteSubscription(ctx, r.Stream, r.Durable); err != nil {
   errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("events: retire %s/%s: %w", r.Stream, r.Durable, err))
   continue
  }
  if r.Purge != "" {
   if err := admin.PurgeSubject(ctx, r.Stream, r.Purge); err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ErrStreamNotFound) {
    errs = append(errs, fmt.Errorf("events: retire %s/%s: purge %s: %w", r.Stream, r.Durable, r.Purge, err))
    continue
   }
  }
  out = append(out, rep)
 }
 return out, errors.Join(errs...)
}

// MergeRetired keeps, per retired durable, the first report that found it on
// the broker, else the latest.
func MergeRetired(seen map[string]RetiredReport, reports []RetiredReport) {
 for _, r := range reports {
  k := r.Stream + "/" + r.Durable
  if prev, ok := seen[k]; ok && prev.Existed {
   continue
  }
  seen[k] = r
 }
}

// SortedRetired lists seen by stream and durable.
func SortedRetired(seen map[string]RetiredReport) []RetiredReport {
 out := make([]RetiredReport, 0, len(seen))
 for _, r := range seen {
  out = append(out, r)
 }
 slices.SortFunc(out, func(a, b RetiredReport) int {
  return cmp.Or(cmp.Compare(a.Stream, b.Stream), cmp.Compare(a.Durable, b.Durable))
 })
 return out
}
```

```go
// Ensure creates or updates every stream, bucket and object store in t, then
// retires t.Retired (events.Retire).
func (b *Bus) Ensure(ctx context.Context, t events.Topology) error {
 if err := b.ensure(t); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 reports, err := events.Retire(ctx, b, t.Retired, b.clock.Now().UTC())
 b.mu.Lock()
 events.MergeRetired(b.retired, reports)
 b.mu.Unlock()
 return err
}

 b.mu.Lock()
 defer b.mu.Unlock()
 return events.SortedRetired(b.retired)
}
```

```go
// nextEntry waits for one watch delivery.
func nextEntry(t *testing.T, ch <-chan events.Entry) events.Entry {
 t.Helper()
 select {
 case e, ok := <-ch:
  if !ok {
   t.Fatal("the watch closed")
  }
  return e
 case <-time.After(Timeout):
  t.Fatal("timed out waiting for a watch delivery")
 }
 return events.Entry{}
}

// testKVWatchDeliversPastTheBuffer: a watcher opened over 200 keys that then
// falls 1,000 updates behind loses nothing, in revision order (membus dropped
// past 64 until F1.3; loop spec §4.15).
func testKVWatchDeliversPastTheBuffer(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 for i := range 200 {
  if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("pre-%04d", i), []byte("v")); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
  }
 }
 watchCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 defer cancel()
 ch, err := kv.Watch(watchCtx, ">")
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Watch: %v", err)
 }
 for i := range 1000 {
  if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, fmt.Sprintf("post-%04d", i), []byte("v")); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
  }
 }
 seen := map[string]bool{}
 var last uint64
 for len(seen) < 1200 {
  e := nextEntry(t, ch)
  if e.Revision <= last {
   t.Fatalf("revision %d after %d: out of order", e.Revision, last)
  }
  last = e.Revision
  seen[e.Key] = true
 }
}

func testKVWatchUpdatesOnly(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 for _, k := range []string{"a", "b"} {
  if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, k, []byte("before")); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
  }
 }
 watchCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 defer cancel()
 ch, err := kv.Watch(watchCtx, ">", events.WatchUpdatesOnly())
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Watch: %v", err)
 }
 if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, "c", []byte("after")); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
 }
 if e := nextEntry(t, ch); e.Key != "c" {
  t.Fatalf("first delivery = %q; an updates-only watch replays nothing", e.Key)
 }
}

func testKVWatchFromRevision(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 revs := map[string]uint64{}
 for _, k := range []string{"a", "b", "c"} {
  rev, err := kv.Put(ctx, k, []byte(k))
  if err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
  }
  revs[k] = rev
 }
 watchCtx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 defer cancel()
 ch, err := kv.Watch(watchCtx, ">", events.WatchFromRevision(revs["b"]))
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Watch: %v", err)
 }
 for _, want := range []string{"b", "c"} {
  if e := nextEntry(t, ch); e.Key != want || e.Revision != revs[want] {
   t.Fatalf("delivery = %q@%d; want %q@%d from revision %d", e.Key, e.Revision, want, revs[want], revs["b"])
  }
 }
 if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, "d", []byte("d")); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
 }
 if e := nextEntry(t, ch); e.Key != "d" {
  t.Fatalf("delivery = %q; want the update d", e.Key)
 }
}

func testKVKeys(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 keys, err := kv.Keys(ctx)
 if err != nil || len(keys) != 0 {
  t.Fatalf("Keys of an empty bucket = %v, %v; want none and no error", keys, err)
 }
 for _, k := range []string{"x-2", "x-1", "x-3"} {
  if _, err := kv.Put(ctx, k, []byte("v")); err != nil {
   t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
  }
 }
 if err := kv.Delete(ctx, "x-3"); err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Delete: %v", err)
 }
 keys, err = kv.Keys(ctx)
 if err != nil || !slices.Equal(keys, []string{"x-1", "x-2"}) {
  t.Fatalf("Keys = %v, %v; want [x-1 x-2], sorted, the deleted key gone", keys, err)
 }
}

// testKVStatus: a bucket's last revision and creation time, which the records
// waker seeds from and checks for a recreated bucket (loop spec §4.9).
func testKVStatus(t *testing.T, newBus func() events.Bus) {
 ctx, bus := setup(t, newBus)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 before, err := kv.Status(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Status: %v", err)
 }
 if before.Bucket != events.BucketTranscodes || before.Created.IsZero() {
  t.Fatalf("Status = %+v; want the bucket and its creation time", before)
 }
 rev, err := kv.Put(ctx, "k", []byte("v"))
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Put: %v", err)
 }
 after, err := kv.Status(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  t.Fatalf("Status: %v", err)
 }
 if after.LastRevision != rev || !after.Created.Equal(before.Created) {
  t.Fatalf("Status after a put = %+v; want LastRevision %d and Created unchanged %v", after, rev, before.Created)
 }
 if _, err := bus.KV("clustarr-no-such-bucket").Status(ctx); !errors.Is(err, events.ErrBucketNotFound) {
  t.Fatalf("Status of a missing bucket = %v; want ErrBucketNotFound", err)
 }
}
```

  **3a.** `pkg/events/bus.go`, after `ResolveKVOptions`:

```go
// WatchOptions is the resolved effect of a list of WatchOption values.
type WatchOptions struct {
 // UpdatesOnly skips the current values: only writes after the watch
 // opens are delivered. It wins over FromRevision.
 UpdatesOnly bool
 // FromRevision starts the watch at this revision instead of at each
 // key's current value; 0 is the current values.
 FromRevision uint64
}

// WatchOption modifies a KV.Watch.
type WatchOption func(*WatchOptions)

// WatchUpdatesOnly opens a watch at the bucket's end (jetstream.UpdatesOnly).
func WatchUpdatesOnly() WatchOption { return func(o *WatchOptions) { o.UpdatesOnly = true } }

// WatchFromRevision opens a watch at revision rev
// (jetstream.ResumeFromRevision): every live value written at or after it,
// in revision order, then every change.
func WatchFromRevision(rev uint64) WatchOption {
 return func(o *WatchOptions) { o.FromRevision = rev }
}

// ResolveWatchOptions folds opts into a WatchOptions value.
func ResolveWatchOptions(opts []WatchOption) WatchOptions {
 var o WatchOptions
 for _, fn := range opts {
  fn(&o)
 }
 return o
}

// KVStatus is a bucket's backing stream: its last revision, and when it was
// created. A bucket deleted and created again has a new Created, and its
// revisions start over.
type KVStatus struct {
 Bucket       string
 LastRevision uint64
 Created      time.Time
}
```

  The `KV` interface's `Watch` becomes, with `Keys` and `Status` after it:

```go
 // Watch streams the current value of every key matching pattern, in
 // revision order, then every subsequent change, never dropping one: a
 // slow reader neither loses an update nor blocks a writer.
 // WatchUpdatesOnly skips the current values; WatchFromRevision starts at
 // a revision. The channel is closed when ctx is cancelled or the bus
 // closes.
 Watch(ctx context.Context, pattern string, opts ...WatchOption) (<-chan Entry, error)

 // Keys lists every live key, sorted. An empty bucket is no keys and no
 // error.
 Keys(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error)

 // Status reads the bucket's last revision and creation time. A missing
 // bucket is ErrBucketNotFound.
 Status(ctx context.Context) (KVStatus, error)
```

  **3b.** `pkg/events/membus/kv.go`: delete `watchBuffer`; `watcher` becomes a queue with a pump:

```go
// watcher is one Watch: an unbounded queue a pump goroutine drains into out,
// in order, so a slow reader neither loses an update nor blocks a writer --
// natsbus's parity (natsbus/kv.go forwards with a blocking send behind
// nats.go's own buffer).
type watcher struct {
 pattern string
 out     chan events.Entry
 mu      sync.Mutex
 queue   []events.Entry
 wake    chan struct{}
 done    chan struct{}
 once    sync.Once
}

func newWatcher(pattern string) *watcher {
 return &watcher{pattern: pattern, out: make(chan events.Entry), wake: make(chan struct{}, 1), done: make(chan struct{})}
}

func (w *watcher) push(e events.Entry) {
 w.mu.Lock()
 w.queue = append(w.queue, e)
 w.mu.Unlock()
 select {
 case w.wake <- struct{}{}:
 default:
 }
}

// pump forwards the queue until the watcher closes, then closes out.
func (w *watcher) pump() {
 defer close(w.out)
 for {
  w.mu.Lock()
  if len(w.queue) == 0 {
   w.mu.Unlock()
   select {
   case <-w.wake:
    continue
   case <-w.done:
    return
   }
  }
  e := w.queue[0]
  w.queue[0] = events.Entry{}
  w.queue = w.queue[1:]
  w.mu.Unlock()
  select {
  case w.out <- e:
  case <-w.done:
   return
  }
 }
}

func (w *watcher) close() { w.once.Do(func() { close(w.done) }) }
```

  `bucket` gains `created time.Time` (doc: "when Ensure created it; KVStatus.Created"). `notifyLocked`'s
  `select { case w.ch <- e: … default: }` becomes `w.push(e)`. `Watch`:

```go
// Watch streams the current value of every matching key, in revision order,
// then every subsequent change (events.KV.Watch). Like JetStream it sends no
// end-of-initial-values marker, because events.Entry has no nil form.
func (k *kvHandle) Watch(ctx context.Context, pattern string, opts ...events.WatchOption) (<-chan events.Entry, error) {
 b, err := k.resolve()
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 o := events.ResolveWatchOptions(opts)
 w := newWatcher(pattern)
 now := k.bus.clock.Now()
 b.mu.Lock()
 if !o.UpdatesOnly {
  var initial []events.Entry
  for key := range b.vals {
   v, ok := b.liveLocked(key, now)
   if !ok || !events.SubjectMatches(pattern, key) || v.rev < o.FromRevision {
    continue
   }
   initial = append(initial, events.Entry{
    Bucket: b.spec.Name, Key: key, Value: append([]byte(nil), v.value...),
    Revision: v.rev, Created: v.created, Operation: events.KVPut,
   })
  }
  slices.SortFunc(initial, func(x, y events.Entry) int { return cmp.Compare(x.Revision, y.Revision) })
  for _, e := range initial {
   w.push(e)
  }
 }
 b.watchers = append(b.watchers, w)
 b.mu.Unlock()

 k.bus.wg.Add(2)
 go func() {
  defer k.bus.wg.Done()
  w.pump()
 }()
 go func() {
  defer k.bus.wg.Done()
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
  case <-k.bus.done:
  case <-w.done:
  }
  b.mu.Lock()
  kept := b.watchers[:0]
  for _, x := range b.watchers {
   if x != w {
    kept = append(kept, x)
   }
  }
  b.watchers = kept
  b.mu.Unlock()
  w.close()
 }()
 return w.out, nil
}

// Keys lists every live key, sorted.
func (k *kvHandle) Keys(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
 if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 b, err := k.resolve()
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 now := k.bus.clock.Now()
 b.mu.Lock()
 defer b.mu.Unlock()
 var out []string
 for key := range b.vals {
  if _, ok := b.liveLocked(key, now); ok {
   out = append(out, key)
  }
 }
 slices.Sort(out)
 return out, nil
}

// Status reads the bucket's last revision and creation time.
func (k *kvHandle) Status(ctx context.Context) (events.KVStatus, error) {
 if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
  return events.KVStatus{}, err
 }
 b, err := k.resolve()
 if err != nil {
  return events.KVStatus{}, err
 }
 b.mu.Lock()
 defer b.mu.Unlock()
 return events.KVStatus{Bucket: b.spec.Name, LastRevision: b.rev, Created: b.created}, nil
}
```

  **3c.** `pkg/events/natsbus/kv.go`:

```go
// Watch streams the current value of every key matching pattern and then
// every subsequent change. The JetStream end-of-initial-values marker is
// swallowed, because events.Entry has no nil form.
func (k *kvHandle) Watch(ctx context.Context, pattern string, opts ...events.WatchOption) (<-chan events.Entry, error) {
 kv, err := k.resolve(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 var wopts []jetstream.WatchOpt
 switch o := events.ResolveWatchOptions(opts); {
 case o.UpdatesOnly:
  wopts = append(wopts, jetstream.UpdatesOnly())
 case o.FromRevision > 0:
  wopts = append(wopts, jetstream.ResumeFromRevision(o.FromRevision))
 }
 w, err := kv.Watch(ctx, pattern, wopts...)
 // … the rest of W4-era Watch unchanged …
}

// Keys lists every live key, sorted (nats.go's Keys ignores deletes).
func (k *kvHandle) Keys(ctx context.Context) ([]string, error) {
 kv, err := k.resolve(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 keys, err := kv.Keys(ctx)
 if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrNoKeysFound) {
  return nil, nil
 }
 if err != nil {
  return nil, kvError("keys", k.name, ">", err)
 }
 return keys, nil
}

// Status reads the bucket's backing stream: its last sequence (the last
// revision) and creation time.
func (k *kvHandle) Status(ctx context.Context) (events.KVStatus, error) {
 kv, err := k.resolve(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  return events.KVStatus{}, err
 }
 st, err := kv.Status(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  if errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrStreamNotFound) || errors.Is(err, jetstream.ErrBucketNotFound) {
   return events.KVStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("natsbus: status %s: %w", k.name, events.ErrBucketNotFound)
  }
  return events.KVStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("natsbus: status %s: %w", k.name, err)
 }
 bs, ok := st.(*jetstream.KeyValueBucketStatus)
 if !ok {
  return events.KVStatus{}, fmt.Errorf("natsbus: status %s: %T carries no stream info", k.name, st)
 }
 info := bs.StreamInfo()
 return events.KVStatus{Bucket: k.name, LastRevision: info.State.LastSeq, Created: info.Created}, nil
}
```

```go
// realBus is natsbus on an embedded JetStream server with the shipped
// single-node topology: the waker's behaviour rests on JetStream's
// UpdatesOnly and ResumeFromRevision, which membus only mirrors.
func realBus(t *testing.T) (*natsbus.Bus, jetstream.JetStream) {
 t.Helper()
 dir, err := os.MkdirTemp(t.TempDir(), "jetstream")
 require.NoError(t, err)
 srv, err := natsserver.NewServer(&natsserver.Options{
  ServerName: "recordsource", Host: "127.0.0.1", Port: -1, JetStream: true, StoreDir: dir, NoLog: true, NoSigs: true,
 })
 require.NoError(t, err)
 go srv.Start()
 require.True(t, srv.ReadyForConnections(20*time.Second))
 t.Cleanup(srv.Shutdown)
 nc, err := nats.Connect(srv.ClientURL())
 require.NoError(t, err)
 t.Cleanup(nc.Close)
 bus, err := natsbus.New(nc)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
 require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(t.Context(), events.Default().ForSingleNode()))
 return bus, bus.JetStream()
}

 t.Cleanup(q.ShutDown)

}

func (q *recordingQueue) Add(k string) { q.AddWithOpts(priorityqueue.AddOpts{}, k) }

func (q *recordingQueue) AddWithOpts(o priorityqueue.AddOpts, ks ...string) {
 p := 0
 if o.Priority != nil {
  p = *o.Priority
 }
 q.mu.Lock()
 defer q.mu.Unlock()
 for _, k := range ks {
  q.got = append(q.got, added{k, p})
 }
}

 defer q.mu.Unlock()
 out := make([]string, 0, len(q.got))
 for _, a := range q.got {
  out = append(out, a.key)
 }
 return out
}

func (q *recordingQueue) priorityOf(k string) (int, bool) {
 q.mu.Lock()
 defer q.mu.Unlock()
 for _, a := range q.got {
  if a.key == k {
   return a.priority, true
  }
 }
 return 0, false
}

func shorten(t *testing.T) {
 t.Helper()
 oi, om, oc, od := reopenInitial, reopenMax, recreateCheck, openDeadline
 reopenInitial, reopenMax, recreateCheck, openDeadline = 100*time.Millisecond, 200*time.Millisecond, 50*time.Millisecond, 500*time.Millisecond
 t.Cleanup(func() { reopenInitial, reopenMax, recreateCheck, openDeadline = oi, om, oc, od })
}

// The waker enqueues the file of every worker write after it opened, and
// skips the loop's own writes (requested, withdrawn), deletes, garbage, and
// whatever was written before it opened: that is read by the pass the
// informer's initial list enqueues (loop spec §4.9).
func TestSourceSkipsTheLoopsOwnWrites(t *testing.T) {
 bus, _ := realBus(t)
 kv := bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 put(t, kv, "before", records.StateAnswered)
 q := newRecordingQueue(t)
 require.NoError(t, New(bus, events.BucketTranscodes, name).Start(t.Context(), q))

 put(t, kv, "requested", records.StateRequested)
 put(t, kv, "withdrawn", records.StateWithdrawn)
 put(t, kv, "claimed", records.StateClaimed)
 put(t, kv, "answered", records.StateAnswered)
 put(t, kv, "failed", records.StateFailed)
 _, err := kv.Put(t.Context(), events.RecordKey("garbage"), []byte("{not json"))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 require.NoError(t, kv.Delete(t.Context(), events.RecordKey("before")))

 require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(q.keys()) >= 3 }, 10*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)
 time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
 assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{"media/claimed", "media/answered", "media/failed"}, q.keys())
}

// closingBus lets a test close the watch under a live source, as nats.go does
// when its ordered consumer gives up, and records how each watch opened.
type closingBus struct {
 inner   Bus
 mu      sync.Mutex
 cancels []context.CancelFunc
 opened  []events.WatchOptions
}

func (b *closingBus) KV(bucket string) events.KV { return &closingKV{KV: b.inner.KV(bucket), b: b} }

func (b *closingBus) closeLatest() {
 b.mu.Lock()
 defer b.mu.Unlock()
 b.cancels[len(b.cancels)-1]()
}

func (b *closingBus) opens() []events.WatchOptions {
 b.mu.Lock()
 defer b.mu.Unlock()
 return append([]events.WatchOptions(nil), b.opened...)
}

type closingKV struct {
 events.KV
 b *closingBus
}

func (k *closingKV) Watch(ctx context.Context, pattern string, opts ...events.WatchOption) (<-chan events.Entry, error) {
 wctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 k.b.mu.Lock()
 k.b.cancels = append(k.b.cancels, cancel)
 k.b.opened = append(k.b.opened, events.ResolveWatchOptions(opts))
 k.b.mu.Unlock()
 return k.KV.Watch(wctx, pattern, opts...)
}

// A watch that closes while the source runs is opened again after a backoff
// from the revision after the last one seen: nothing written in the gap is
// lost, and nothing before it is delivered twice.
func TestSourceResumesFromRevisionAfterAClose(t *testing.T) {
 shorten(t)
 real, _ := realBus(t)
 bus := &closingBus{inner: real}
 kv := real.KV(events.BucketTranscodes)
 q := newRecordingQueue(t)
 require.NoError(t, New(bus, events.BucketTranscodes, name).Start(t.Context(), q))
 revA := put(t, kv, "a", records.StateAnswered)
 require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(q.keys()) == 1 }, 10*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)

 bus.closeLatest()
 put(t, kv, "b", records.StateAnswered)
 require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(q.keys()) == 2 }, 10*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)
 time.Sleep(200 * time.Millisecond)
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"media/a", "media/b"}, q.keys(), "b once, a not again")
 opens := bus.opens()
 require.GreaterOrEqual(t, len(opens), 2)
 assert.True(t, opens[0].UpdatesOnly, "the first open replays nothing")
 assert.Equal(t, revA+1, opens[1].FromRevision, "the reopen resumes after the last revision seen")
}

// A bucket deleted and created again under the source (a lost NATS volume, an
// operator's purge) is replayed at low priority, and every file whose status
// shows an outstanding request is woken, since its record went with the old
// bucket (loop spec §4.9, §5.15).
func TestSourceSurvivesABucketRecreatedUnderIt(t *testing.T) {
 shorten(t)
 bus, js := realBus(t)
 var woke atomic.Int32
 q := newRecordingQueue(t)
 src := New(bus, events.BucketTranscodes, name, OnRecreated[string](func(_ context.Context, enqueue func(string)) {
  woke.Add(1)
  enqueue("media/outstanding-in-status")
 }))
 require.NoError(t, src.Start(t.Context(), q))
 put(t, bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes), "old", records.StateAnswered)
 require.Eventually(t, func() bool { return len(q.keys()) == 1 }, 10*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)

 require.NoError(t, js.DeleteKeyValue(t.Context(), events.BucketTranscodes))
 require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(t.Context(), events.Default().ForSingleNode()))
 put(t, bus.KV(events.BucketTranscodes), "new", records.StateAnswered)

 require.Eventually(t, func() bool {
  _, outstanding := q.priorityOf("media/outstanding-in-status")
  _, fresh := q.priorityOf("media/new")
  return outstanding && fresh
 }, 15*time.Second, 20*time.Millisecond)
 assert.EqualValues(t, 1, woke.Load())
 p, _ := q.priorityOf("media/outstanding-in-status")
 assert.Equal(t, handler.LowPriority, p)
}

// Start fails, rather than leaving the loop deaf, when the bucket never
// appears within openDeadline; controller-runtime then fails the controller.
func TestStartFailsWhenTheBucketNeverAppears(t *testing.T) {
 shorten(t)
 bus := membus.New(nil)
 t.Cleanup(func() { _ = bus.Close() })
 require.NoError(t, bus.Ensure(t.Context(), events.Default().ForSingleNode()))
 err := New(bus, "clustarr-no-such-bucket", name).Start(t.Context(), newRecordingQueue(t))
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, events.ErrBucketNotFound)
}
```

  **3a.** `pkg/records/recordsource/recordsource.go`:

```go
// Package recordsource wakes the remediation loop from a records bucket
// (loop spec 2026-10-06 §4.9): a controller source, so leader-only, that
// watches one bucket from its current end, enqueues the file a worker's
// record names and skips the loop's own writes. It writes nothing and decides
// nothing; every pass reads its records itself, and a dropped wake costs
// latency, never correctness. It links controller-runtime, so only the
// manager uses it; workers write through pkg/records.
package recordsource

import (
 "context"
 "encoding/json"
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "time"

 "k8s.io/client-go/util/workqueue"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/controller/priorityqueue"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/handler"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events/schema"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/obs/logging"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/records"
)

// Timers; the tests shorten them.
var (
 // openDeadline bounds Start's first open, retried with backoff.
 openDeadline = 60 * time.Second
 // reopenInitial and reopenMax bound the reopen backoff, doubling.
 reopenInitial = time.Second
 reopenMax     = 30 * time.Second
 // recreateCheck is how often an open watch checks that its bucket is
 // still the one it opened: nats.go's ordered consumer can outlive a
 // stream deleted and created again without closing (defect D8).
 recreateCheck = 30 * time.Second
)

// Bus is what a source needs of the bus. Every events.Bus is one.
type Bus interface {
 KV(bucket string) events.KV
}

// Decoder reads which file a record names, and its state.
type Decoder func(value []byte) (file schema.Ref, state string, ok bool)

// HeaderDecoder reads schema.RecordHeader's mediaFile and state: every
// records bucket but clustarr-segments, whose v2 records name their file
// under another key (F3.4 passes its own Decoder).
func HeaderDecoder(value []byte) (schema.Ref, string, bool) {
 var h struct {
  MediaFile schema.Ref `json:"mediaFile"`
  State     string     `json:"state"`
 }
 if err := json.Unmarshal(value, &h); err != nil || h.MediaFile.Name == "" {
  return schema.Ref{}, "", false
 }
 return h.MediaFile, h.State, true
}

// Option configures a Source.
type Option[K comparable] func(*Source[K])

// WithDecoder replaces HeaderDecoder.
func WithDecoder[K comparable](d Decoder) Option[K] { return func(s *Source[K]) { s.decode = d } }

// OnRecreated is called when the bucket was deleted and created again under
// the source; enqueue adds at low priority. The loop enqueues, from its cache,
// every file whose status shows an outstanding request of this remediation.
func OnRecreated[K comparable](f func(ctx context.Context, enqueue func(K))) Option[K] {
 return func(s *Source[K]) { s.recreated = f }
}

// Source is one bucket's waker.
type Source[K comparable] struct {
 bus       Bus
 bucket    string
 toKey     func(schema.Ref) (K, bool)
 decode    Decoder
 recreated func(ctx context.Context, enqueue func(K))

 // lastRev and created belong to the run goroutine once Start returns.
 lastRev uint64
 created time.Time
}

// New is bucket's waker: toKey maps a record's file to the loop's key, false
// to skip it.
func New[K comparable](bus Bus, bucket string, toKey func(schema.Ref) (K, bool), opts ...Option[K]) *Source[K] {
 s := &Source[K]{bus: bus, bucket: bucket, toKey: toKey, decode: HeaderDecoder}
 for _, o := range opts {
  o(s)
 }
 return s
}

func (s *Source[K]) String() string { return "records source " + s.bucket }

type watch struct {
 ch     <-chan events.Entry
 cancel context.CancelFunc
 // replayThrough marks a recreated bucket's replay: entries at or below
 // it are enqueued at low priority.
 replayThrough uint64
}

// Start opens the watch from the bucket's end, synchronously, retrying with
// backoff for up to openDeadline: controller-runtime starts workers only once
// every source started and every cache synced, so a record written before
// this open is read by the pass the informer's initial list enqueues, and one
// written after is delivered (§4.9). A goroutine forwards until ctx ends.
func (s *Source[K]) Start(ctx context.Context, q workqueue.TypedRateLimitingInterface[K]) error {
 kv := s.bus.KV(s.bucket)
 deadline := time.Now().Add(openDeadline)
 wait := reopenInitial
 for {
  w, _, err := s.open(ctx, kv, true)
  if err == nil {
   go s.run(ctx, kv, w, q)
   return nil
  }
  if ctx.Err() != nil {
   return ctx.Err()
  }
  if time.Now().Add(wait).After(deadline) {
   return fmt.Errorf("recordsource: watch %s: %w", s.bucket, err)
  }
  logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("recordsource: could not open the records watch; retrying", "bucket", s.bucket, "error", err, "in", wait)
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return ctx.Err()
  case <-time.After(wait):
  }
  wait = min(wait*2, reopenMax)
 }
}

// open reads the bucket's status, then watches: from its end on the first
// open, from lastRev+1 on a reopen, and from the start of a bucket that was
// recreated (its creation time changed, or its last revision fell below
// lastRev), which it reports.
func (s *Source[K]) open(ctx context.Context, kv events.KV, first bool) (watch, bool, error) {
 st, err := kv.Status(ctx)
 if err != nil {
  return watch{}, false, err
 }
 var opts []events.WatchOption
 var w watch
 recreated := false
 switch {
 case first:
  s.created, s.lastRev = st.Created, max(s.lastRev, st.LastRevision)
  opts = append(opts, events.WatchUpdatesOnly())
 case !st.Created.Equal(s.created) || st.LastRevision < s.lastRev:
  recreated = true
  s.created, s.lastRev, w.replayThrough = st.Created, 0, st.LastRevision
 default:
  opts = append(opts, events.WatchFromRevision(s.lastRev+1))
 }
 wctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(ctx)
 ch, err := kv.Watch(wctx, ">", opts...)
 if err != nil {
  cancel()
  return watch{}, false, err
 }
 w.ch, w.cancel = ch, cancel
 return w, recreated, nil
}

func (s *Source[K]) run(ctx context.Context, kv events.KV, w watch, q workqueue.TypedRateLimitingInterface[K]) {
 log := logging.FromContext(ctx).With("bucket", s.bucket)
 tick := time.NewTicker(recreateCheck)
 defer tick.Stop()
 defer func() { w.cancel() }()
 for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return
  case e, ok := <-w.ch:
   if ok {
    s.handle(e, w.replayThrough, q)
    continue
   }
  case <-tick.C:
   st, err := kv.Status(ctx)
   if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, events.ErrBucketNotFound) {
    continue
   }
   if err == nil && st.Created.Equal(s.created) && st.LastRevision >= s.lastRev {
    continue
   }
  }
  w.cancel()
  next, ok := s.reopen(ctx, kv, q, log)
  if !ok {
   return
  }
  w = next
 }
}

// reopen opens the watch again after a backoff of reopenInitial doubling to
// reopenMax, until ctx ends.
func (s *Source[K]) reopen(ctx context.Context, kv events.KV, q workqueue.TypedRateLimitingInterface[K], log interface {
 Warn(msg string, args ...any)
}) (watch, bool) {
 wait := reopenInitial
 for {
  select {
  case <-ctx.Done():
   return watch{}, false
  case <-time.After(wait):
  }
  w, recreated, err := s.open(ctx, kv, false)
  if err != nil {
   wait = min(wait*2, reopenMax)
   log.Warn("recordsource: could not reopen the records watch; retrying", "error", err, "in", wait)
   continue
  }
  if recreated {
   log.Warn("recordsource: the records bucket was recreated; replaying it and waking every outstanding request")
   if s.recreated != nil {
    s.recreated(ctx, func(k K) { addLow(q, k) })
   }
  }
  return w, true
 }
}

// handle enqueues the file of a worker's write; the loop's own writes
// (requested, withdrawn), deletes, purges and undecodable values only move
// lastRev.
func (s *Source[K]) handle(e events.Entry, replayThrough uint64, q workqueue.TypedRateLimitingInterface[K]) {
 s.lastRev = max(s.lastRev, e.Revision)
 if e.Operation != events.KVPut {
  return
 }
 ref, state, ok := s.decode(e.Value)
 if !ok || state == records.StateRequested || state == records.StateWithdrawn {
  return
 }
 k, ok := s.toKey(ref)
 if !ok {
  return
 }
 if e.Revision <= replayThrough {
  addLow(q, k)
  return
 }
 q.Add(k)
}

// addLow enqueues k at controller-runtime's LowPriority when the queue is a
// priority queue (the default since v0.23), else plainly.
func addLow[K comparable](q workqueue.TypedRateLimitingInterface[K], k K) {
 if pq, ok := q.(priorityqueue.PriorityQueue[K]); ok {
  low := handler.LowPriority
  pq.AddWithOpts(priorityqueue.AddOpts{Priority: &low}, k)
  return
 }
 q.Add(k)
}
```

  (`logging.FromContext` returns a `*slog.Logger`, whose `Warn` satisfies the `reopen` parameter.)

  **3c.** `app/catalog/controller/mediafile/results.go`: replace W4.12's body below the imports with:

```go
// probeRecordsSource wakes the reconciler for every answered probe: S16 of
// the remediation loop to come (loop spec §3.18, §4.9), a records source over
// clustarr-probes that enqueues the MediaFile a probed or failed record names
// and skips requests, deletes and undecodable values. It writes nothing:
// Reconcile reads the record itself. Controller sources start only on the
// leader; a probe answered while no leader ran is read by the pass the
// informer's initial list enqueues.
func (r *Reconciler) probeRecordsSource() source.Source {
 return recordsource.New(r.Probes.Bus(), clustarrevents.BucketProbes, mediaFileRequest,
  recordsource.OnRecreated[reconcile.Request](r.wakePendingProbes))
}

func mediaFileRequest(ref schema.Ref) (reconcile.Request, bool) {
 if ref.Name == "" {
  return reconcile.Request{}, false
 }
 return reconcile.Request{NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{Namespace: ref.Namespace, Name: ref.Name}}, true
}

// wakePendingProbes enqueues every MediaFile whose status says a probe is
// pending (Probed False, ProbePending): its request went with a recreated
// bucket (loop spec §4.9, §5.15 "records bucket lost").
func (r *Reconciler) wakePendingProbes(ctx context.Context, enqueue func(reconcile.Request)) {
 var list catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileList
 if err := r.List(ctx, &list); err != nil {
  logging.FromContext(ctx).Warn("mediafile: could not list MediaFiles to wake their pending probes", "error", err)
  return
 }
 for i := range list.Items {
  mf := &list.Items[i]
  c := k8s.FindCondition(mf.Status.Conditions, catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionProbed)
  if c != nil && c.Status == metav1.ConditionFalse && c.Reason == catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileReasonProbePending {
   enqueue(reconcile.Request{NamespacedName: types.NamespacedName{Namespace: mf.Namespace, Name: mf.Name}})
  }
 }
}
```

wave adds no watch. Runs before F3.1.

**Order inside the wave:** serial, F2.1 → F2.4. F2.2 and F2.3 reuse F2.1's envtest helpers in
`pkg/crdcheck`, and F2.3 uses F2.2's `pkg/k8s` text helpers and API bounds.

**What this wave does.** It writes the MediaFile status API the fold leaves behind and nothing that
uses it: the blocks (`status.subtitles`, the expanded `status.transcode`, `status.graft`), the per-file
sequence (`status.lastSeq`, `Dispatch`), the sidecar `name`, `status.handledNonces` and the intent
annotations, the planner-error conditions, the selectable fields and print columns, the bounds on every
MediaFile string, the render boundary `mediafilestatus.Render` the loop (F3.1) will apply through, the
size budget and its guards, and the item-scoped graft home on Movie and Episode
(`status.audio.donor`, `status.audio.rejectedReleases`). Nothing is removed (§2.15): every reader and
writer of today's fields, the interim MediaFile reconciler's `knownStatus.statusAC` (W4.13) included,
keeps compiling and passing. Nothing in this wave is deployed (§8.2 rule 3, D1).

**Commands.** `$ENVTEST go test …` means
`KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$("$(go env GOPATH)/bin/setup-envtest" use 1.37.0 -p path)" go test …`. Check `-v`
output for `SKIP`: a suite that finishes in milliseconds skipped. `FMT <files>` means
`$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w <files> && $(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w <files>`.

**Deviations from the loop spec, each reported as a spec defect** (the loop spec is not edited by this
wave; F8.11 carries the amendments):

1. **`TranscodeState.Phase` is `json:"phase,omitempty"` in release N** (§2.5 writes `json:"phase"`). A
   typed marshal of a phase-less block -- the 171 live legacy blocks, and the interim reconciler's own
   `TranscodeState{Compliant, ProfileTag, LastResult}` until F6 -- would send `"phase":""`, which the
   enum refuses; under §3.7's JSON round trip (F3.1) every such file's status apply would be refused
   between F3.1 and F6. The loop always sets a phase, so §2.1 item 3's "always written" still holds.
   F9.2 makes it `json:"phase"` and `+required`.
2. **Two strings §2.11.2 leaves unbounded get `MaxLength=253`:** `commonv1.MediaRef.name` (spec
   `mediaRef.name`) and `TranscodeState.jobRef` (§2.5's code has no cap). Without them
   `TestMediaFileStringsAreBounded` cannot pass.
3. **The caps on shared `commonv1` types change ten CRDs, not three.** `MediaInfo` (TranscodeJob
   `status.result.mediaInfo`), `Quality.name` (Movie, Episode, Album, Audiobook, Issue, Download,
   Search) and `MediaRef` (Download, Search, AudioGraft) carry their new MaxLengths wherever they are
   embedded. §8.6's "the three legacy CRDs are unchanged" holds for SubtitleRequest only; F2.4 checks
   the actual list and that every change is additive.
4. **`MediaFileObjectBudgetBytes` is `832 << 10` in release N** (§2.11.3 says 768 KiB). Release N's
   sidecars list is a map keyed by a 4,096-byte `path`, so catalogarr's `managedFields` entry repeats
   every key (32 × about 4.2 KB = 131 KiB), which the spec's 660 KiB estimate leaves out; the modelled
   worst case is about 781 KiB (spec 86 KB, status 309 KB with `transcode.plan.dropped`'s 8 × 320,
   annotations 256 KiB, managedFields about 141 KB). F9.2 restores `768 << 10` with the atomic list.
   `MediaFileStatusBudgetBytes = 320 << 10` stands (modelled: 301 KiB).
5. **Importarr clamps the spec fields §2.11.2 caps.** A Download's `release.title`, `indexerName`, and the
   group and edition parsed from it are unbounded; an import whose MediaFile carried a 600-byte title
   would be refused at the apply. `fileimport` clamps them (`MaxReleaseTitleLength` and friends, held to
   the CRD by a mirror test). The rescan re-applies stored values unchanged (ratcheting admits them).
6. **The probe clamps every newly capped `MediaInfo` string, not only titles.** TranscodeJob's
   `status.result.mediaInfo` takes the same caps and has no renderer; the clamp lives in
   `pkg/mediainfo.toMediaInfo`, which the native prober reaches through `mediainfo.FromRaw` (W8.3), so no
   W8 task changes. `ProbeVersion` is not raised.
7. **A path or file name with an unapplyable rune is dropped, not rewritten** (§2.11.1 rule 3 says every
   string is sanitised; a sanitised path names a file that does not exist). It drops exactly as rule 1
   drops an over-long one.
8. **"Carried forward" (rule 5) is judged per top-level status field.** CRD validation ratcheting
   correlates map-list entries by key but not the items of an atomic list (`mediaInfo.audio` and every
   new list), so a leaf-level judgement could send an over-cap value inside a changed atomic list,
   which the apiserver refuses.
9. **An invalid nonce is recorded as `HandledNonce(v)`** (§2.9 says it is recorded but the fields are
   MaxLength 63, and a clamped record never equals the annotation, so it would be re-handled on every
   pass): `v` when valid, else `invalid-` and 16 hex digits of its SHA-256. F5 and F6 compare the
   annotation through it.
10. **All six intent constants live in `mediafile_annotations.go`** (§2.4 puts `AnnotationSubtitleSearch` in
    shared_types.go, §2.9 in mediafile_annotations.go), named `AnnotationSubtitleSearch` and
    `AnnotationTranscode{Retry,Cancel,Suspend,Priority,Hardware}` (§2.9 names no Go constants for the
    transcode five).
11. **`TestSubtitleLanguageStateMirrorsTheFetchVerdicts` (§2.11.4) moves to F5.1:** the verdicts are
    `schema.SubtitleRecord`'s, which F5.1 creates, and the two sets differ (`kept`, `throttled` and
    `dropped` have no state), so the test is a mapping check written with them.
12. **`mediafilestatus.Render`'s home and signature:** §2.11.1 names no package path and rule 5 needs the
    stored status. It is `app/remediation/mediafilestatus.Render(stored, draft *MediaFileStatus)
    (MediaFileStatus, []Drop)`; the Warning Event reason for a drop is `StatusEntryDropped`.
13. **The item renderer bounds the graft's item home too.** `AudioDonor.release` and `rejectedReleases`
    copy Download release titles into Movie and Episode status by server-side apply; §2.11 sanitises
    MediaFile only, and one C1 control in a title would block the item's apply. `rollup.AudioStateAC`
    sanitises and clamps them and drops a donor whose path it cannot carry.

---

```go
package v1alpha1_test

import (
 "encoding/json"
 "strings"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 catalogv1alpha1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/catalog/v1alpha1"
)

// TestMediaFileFoldNames pins the names other services and kubectl users
// type: the intent annotations, the field selectors and the condition
// vocabulary (loop spec §2.8-§2.10).
func TestMediaFileFoldNames(t *testing.T) {
 assert.Equal(t, "subtitle.clustarr.io/search", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationSubtitleSearch)
 assert.Equal(t, "transcode.clustarr.io/retry", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationTranscodeRetry)
 assert.Equal(t, "transcode.clustarr.io/cancel", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationTranscodeCancel)
 assert.Equal(t, "transcode.clustarr.io/suspend", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationTranscodeSuspend)
 assert.Equal(t, "transcode.clustarr.io/priority", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationTranscodePriority)
 assert.Equal(t, "transcode.clustarr.io/hardware", catalogv1alpha1.AnnotationTranscodeHardware)
 assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
  "subtitle.clustarr.io/search", "transcode.clustarr.io/retry", "transcode.clustarr.io/cancel",
  "transcode.clustarr.io/suspend", "transcode.clustarr.io/priority", "transcode.clustarr.io/hardware",
 }, catalogv1alpha1.IntentAnnotations())

 assert.Equal(t, "status.transcode.phase", catalogv1alpha1.FieldTranscodePhase)
 assert.Equal(t, "status.graft.phase", catalogv1alpha1.FieldGraftPhase)

 assert.Equal(t, []string{
  "ProbePlannerError", "NamingPlannerError", "TranscodePlannerError",
  "GraftPlannerError", "SubtitlesPlannerError", "MarkersPlannerError",
 }, []string{
  catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionProbePlannerError, catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionNamingPlannerError,
  catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionTranscodePlannerError, catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionGraftPlannerError,
  catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionSubtitlesPlannerError, catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileConditionMarkersPlannerError,
 })
 assert.Equal(t, "PlannerError", catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileReasonPlannerError)
 assert.Equal(t, "PlannerPanic", catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileReasonPlannerPanic)
}

// TestAPhaselessTranscodeBlockSendsNoPhase: the previous release's block
// (and the interim reconciler's, until F6) has no phase. Marshalled as a
// typed value it must not send phase:"", which the enum refuses -- the
// whole status apply with it (deviation 1).
func TestAPhaselessTranscodeBlockSendsNoPhase(t *testing.T) {
 raw, err := json.Marshal(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeState{
  Compliant: true, ProfileTag: "default@abc", LastResult: catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeResultSucceeded,
 })
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.JSONEq(t, `{"compliant":true,"profileTag":"default@abc","lastResult":"succeeded"}`, string(raw))

 // A NotWanted subtitles block is the ~72 bytes every probed file gains
 // (§2.11.3): phase and cutoffMet always, profile when set, nothing else.
 raw, err = json.Marshal(catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesStatus{Phase: catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesPhaseNotWanted, Profile: "english"})
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.JSONEq(t, `{"phase":"NotWanted","profile":"english","cutoffMet":false}`, string(raw))
}

func TestDispatchInFlight(t *testing.T) {
 var none *catalogv1alpha1.Dispatch
 assert.False(t, none.InFlight())
 assert.True(t, (&catalogv1alpha1.Dispatch{Seq: 5, AnsweredSeq: 4}).InFlight())
 assert.False(t, (&catalogv1alpha1.Dispatch{Seq: 5, AnsweredSeq: 5}).InFlight())
}

// TestHandledNonce: a valid nonce is recorded as itself; an invalid one of
// any length is recorded as a well-formed digest that fits the field's 63
// bytes and is the same on every pass, so it is handled once (deviation 9).
func TestHandledNonce(t *testing.T) {
 for _, v := range []string{"1759752000", "fold-7", "a", "A.b_c-d", strings.Repeat("a", 63)} {
  assert.True(t, catalogv1alpha1.ValidNonce(v), v)
  assert.Equal(t, v, catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(v), v)
 }
 for _, v := range []string{"", "-1", ".x", "has space", strings.Repeat("a", 64), "naïve", "a/b"} {
  assert.False(t, catalogv1alpha1.ValidNonce(v), v)
 }
 assert.Empty(t, catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(""), "no annotation, nothing to record")

 long := strings.Repeat("x", 4096)
 h := catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(long)
 assert.True(t, catalogv1alpha1.ValidNonce(h), "the record of an invalid nonce is itself well formed")
 assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(h), 63)
 assert.True(t, strings.HasPrefix(h, "invalid-"), h)
 assert.Equal(t, h, catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(long), "deterministic: the next pass sees it handled")
 assert.NotEqual(t, h, catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(long+"y"))
}
```

```go
package crdcheck

import (
 "encoding/json"
 "os"
 "slices"
 "sort"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
 apiextensionsv1 "k8s.io/apiextensions-apiserver/pkg/apis/apiextensions/v1"
 "sigs.k8s.io/yaml"

 catalogv1alpha1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/catalog/v1alpha1"
 transcodev1alpha1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/transcode/v1alpha1"
)

// enumAt is the sorted enum of the schema at path in a generated CRD.
func enumAt(t *testing.T, file string, path ...string) []string {
 t.Helper()
 s := crdSchemaAt(t, file, path...)
 out := make([]string, 0, len(s.Enum))
 for _, v := range s.Enum {
  var e string
  require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(v.Raw, &e))
  out = append(out, e)
 }
 sort.Strings(out)
 return out
}

// TestMediaFilePrintColumnsAndSelectableFields holds the MediaFile CRD to
// loop spec §2.10: six of the apiserver's eight selectable fields, the
// queue views kubectl filters on, and the thirteen print columns in order.
func TestMediaFilePrintColumnsAndSelectableFields(t *testing.T) {
 raw, err := os.ReadFile("../../config/crd/bases/catalog.clustarr.io_mediafiles.yaml")
 require.NoError(t, err)
 var crd apiextensionsv1.CustomResourceDefinition
 require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(raw, &crd))
 require.NotEmpty(t, crd.Spec.Versions)
 v := crd.Spec.Versions[0]

 fields := make([]string, 0, len(v.SelectableFields))
 for _, f := range v.SelectableFields {
  fields = append(fields, f.JSONPath)
 }
 assert.ElementsMatch(t, []string{
  ".spec.mediaRef.name", ".spec.mediaRef.kind", ".status.transcode.phase",
  ".status.subtitles.phase", ".status.graft.phase", ".status.naming.current",
 }, fields)
 assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(fields), 8, "the apiserver allows eight selectable fields")

 type column struct {
  Name, Path string
  Priority   int32
 }
 cols := make([]column, 0, len(v.AdditionalPrinterColumns))
 for _, c := range v.AdditionalPrinterColumns {
  cols = append(cols, column{c.Name, c.JSONPath, c.Priority})
 }
 assert.Equal(t, []column{
  {"Media", ".spec.mediaRef.name", 0},
  {"Kind", ".spec.mediaRef.kind", 0},
  {"Quality", ".spec.quality.name", 0},
  {"Ready", `.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Ready")].status`, 0},
  {"Transcode", ".status.transcode.phase", 0},
  {"Subtitles", ".status.subtitles.phase", 0},
  {"Graft", ".status.graft.phase", 1},
  {"Class", ".status.transcode.class", 1},
  {"Worker", ".status.transcode.workerPod", 1},
  {"Probed", `.status.conditions[?(@.type=="Probed")].status`, 1},
  {"Score", ".spec.formatScore", 1},
  {"Size", ".spec.sizeBytes", 1},
  {"Age", ".metadata.creationTimestamp", 0},
 }, cols)
}

// TestTranscodeHardwareMirrorsTheProfileEnum: the hardware annotation and a
// profile's spec.hardware land in status.transcode.hardware, and
// api/catalog cannot import api/transcode, so the enum is restated there
// and held here (loop spec §2.11.4).
func TestTranscodeHardwareMirrorsTheProfileEnum(t *testing.T) {
 profile := enumAt(t, "transcode.clustarr.io_transcodeprofiles.yaml", "spec", "hardware")
 require.Len(t, profile, 5)
 assert.Equal(t, profile, enumAt(t, "catalog.clustarr.io_mediafiles.yaml", "status", "transcode", "hardware"))
 for p, m := range map[transcodev1alpha1.Hardware]catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardware{
  transcodev1alpha1.HardwareCPU:    catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardwareCPU,
  transcodev1alpha1.HardwareNVIDIA: catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardwareNVIDIA,
  transcodev1alpha1.HardwareIntel:  catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardwareIntel,
  transcodev1alpha1.HardwareAuto:   catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardwareAuto,
  transcodev1alpha1.HardwareGPU:    catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeHardwareGPU,
 } {
  assert.Equal(t, string(p), string(m))
 }
}

// TestTranscodeClassIsConcreteHardware: a dispatch's class is the hardware
// it ran on, never a policy (auto, gpu).
func TestTranscodeClassIsConcreteHardware(t *testing.T) {
 hw := enumAt(t, "transcode.clustarr.io_transcodeprofiles.yaml", "spec", "hardware")
 want := slices.DeleteFunc(slices.Clone(hw), func(h string) bool { return h == "auto" || h == "gpu" })
 assert.Equal(t, want, enumAt(t, "catalog.clustarr.io_mediafiles.yaml", "status", "transcode", "class"))
}
```

```go
package crdcheck

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"
 "os"
 "sort"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
 metav1 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/apis/meta/v1"
 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/watch"
 metav1ac "k8s.io/client-go/applyconfigurations/meta/v1"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/client"
 "sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/envtest"

 catalogac "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/applyconfiguration/catalog/catalog/v1alpha1"
 catalogv1alpha1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/catalog/v1alpha1"
 commonv1 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/api/common/v1alpha1"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/k8s"
)

// newFoldEnv starts an apiserver with every CRD installed and returns a
// direct, watching client on the project scheme. It skips without the
// envtest binaries; `make test` sets KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS.
func newFoldEnv(t *testing.T) client.WithWatch {
 t.Helper()
 if os.Getenv("KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS") == "" {
  t.Skip("KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS is unset; run via `make test` to install the CRDs")
 }
 env := &envtest.Environment{CRDDirectoryPaths: []string{"../../config/crd/bases"}, ErrorIfCRDPathMissing: true}
 cfg, err := env.Start()
 require.NoError(t, err, "start envtest")
 t.Cleanup(func() { require.NoError(t, env.Stop()) })
 c, err := client.NewWithWatch(cfg, client.Options{Scheme: k8s.MustNewScheme()})
 require.NoError(t, err)
 return c
}

// newFoldMediaFile creates a MediaFile named name in default, backing an
// item of kind.
func newFoldMediaFile(t *testing.T, c client.Client, name string, kind commonv1.MediaKind) {
 t.Helper()
 require.NoError(t, c.Create(context.Background(), &catalogv1alpha1.MediaFile{
  ObjectMeta: metav1.ObjectMeta{Name: name, Namespace: "default"},
  Spec: catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileSpec{
   MediaRef: commonv1.MediaRef{Kind: kind, Name: name + "-item"},
   Path:     "/data/media/" + name + ".mkv",
   Quality:  commonv1.Quality{Name: "Bluray-1080p"},
  },
 }))
}

// applyFoldStatus applies st to name's status as the loop will: one
// server-side apply under catalogarr.
func applyFoldStatus(t *testing.T, c client.Client, name string, st *catalogac.MediaFileStatusApplyConfiguration) error {
 t.Helper()
 _, err := k8s.PatchStatus(context.Background(), c, k8s.ManagerCatalogarr, catalogac.MediaFile(name, "default").WithStatus(st))
 return err
}

func nextEvent(t *testing.T, w watch.Interface) watch.Event {
 t.Helper()
 select {
 case ev, ok := <-w.ResultChan():
  require.True(t, ok, "the watch closed")
  return ev
 case <-time.After(10 * time.Second):
  t.Fatal("no watch event within 10s")
 }
 return watch.Event{}
}

// TestMediaFileStatusPhasesAreSelectable: the status phases are field
// selectors (loop spec §2.10), list and watch both filter on them, a file
// with no block reads "", and a file leaving a filtered watch's selection
// arrives as DELETED -- what admission's rebuild and the queue views rely on.
func TestMediaFileStatusPhasesAreSelectable(t *testing.T) {
 c := newFoldEnv(t)
 ctx := context.Background()
 now := metav1.NewTime(time.Date(2026, 10, 6, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
 for _, n := range []string{"failed-blocked", "planned-satisfied", "no-blocks"} {
  newFoldMediaFile(t, c, n, commonv1.MediaKindEpisode)
 }
 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "failed-blocked", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodePhaseFailed).
   WithReason("RetriesExhausted").WithBlocked(true)).
  WithSubtitles(catalogac.SubtitlesStatus().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesPhaseBlocked).
   WithReason("NoProfile").WithCutoffMet(false))))
 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "planned-satisfied", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodePhasePlanned).
   WithReason("WaitingForSlot").WithPlannedAt(now)).
  WithSubtitles(catalogac.SubtitlesStatus().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesPhaseSatisfied).WithCutoffMet(true)).
  WithGraft(catalogac.GraftState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.GraftPhaseWaiting).WithReason("WaitingForTranscode"))))

 names := func(sel client.MatchingFields) []string {
  var l catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileList
  require.NoError(t, c.List(ctx, &l, client.InNamespace("default"), sel))
  out := make([]string, 0, len(l.Items))
  for _, m := range l.Items {
   out = append(out, m.Name)
  }
  sort.Strings(out)
  return out
 }
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"failed-blocked"}, names(client.MatchingFields{catalogv1alpha1.FieldTranscodePhase: "Failed"}))
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"planned-satisfied"}, names(client.MatchingFields{catalogv1alpha1.FieldTranscodePhase: "Planned"}))
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"planned-satisfied"}, names(client.MatchingFields{catalogv1alpha1.FieldGraftPhase: "Waiting"}))
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"failed-blocked"}, names(client.MatchingFields{
  "spec.mediaRef.kind": "episode", "status.subtitles.phase": "Blocked",
 }))
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"no-blocks"}, names(client.MatchingFields{catalogv1alpha1.FieldTranscodePhase: ""}),
  "a file with no block reads \"\" under a field selector (§2.1 item 3)")

 w, err := c.Watch(ctx, &catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileList{}, client.InNamespace("default"),
  client.MatchingFields{"status.subtitles.phase": string(catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesPhaseBlocked)})
 require.NoError(t, err)
 t.Cleanup(w.Stop)
 ev := nextEvent(t, w)
 require.Equal(t, watch.Added, ev.Type)
 require.Equal(t, "failed-blocked", ev.Object.(*catalogv1alpha1.MediaFile).Name)

 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "failed-blocked", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodePhaseFailed).
   WithReason("RetriesExhausted").WithBlocked(true)).
  WithSubtitles(catalogac.SubtitlesStatus().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.SubtitlesPhaseSatisfied).WithCutoffMet(true))))
 ev = nextEvent(t, w)
 assert.Equal(t, watch.Deleted, ev.Type, "a file leaving the selection is DELETED to a filtered watch")
 assert.Equal(t, "failed-blocked", ev.Object.(*catalogv1alpha1.MediaFile).Name)
}

// TestTheSchemaAcceptsThePreviousReleasesMediaFileApply holds §2.16's table
// at the schema: after release N wrote a phased transcode block and a
// sidecar with both halves, the previous release's apply under the same
// field manager -- transcode {compliant, profileTag, lastResult} with no
// phase, sidecars re-sent with their path alone, as main's
// mediafile_controller.go knownStatus renders them -- is accepted, and
// releases what it did not send. It also holds the fold's caps (12
// conditions, 32 sidecars) and lastResult's lost default.
func TestTheSchemaAcceptsThePreviousReleasesMediaFileApply(t *testing.T) {
 c := newFoldEnv(t)
 ctx := context.Background()
 newFoldMediaFile(t, c, "heat", commonv1.MediaKindMovie)
 at := metav1.NewTime(time.Date(2026, 10, 6, 12, 0, 0, 0, time.UTC))
 srt := "/data/media/movies/Heat (1995)/Heat (1995).en.srt"

 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithLastSeq(at.UnixMilli()).
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodePhaseSucceeded).
   WithProfile("default").WithProfileHash("abc123").WithProbeHash("h1").
   WithCompliant(true).WithProfileTag("default@abc123").
   WithDispatch(catalogac.Dispatch().WithSeq(at.UnixMilli()).WithAnsweredSeq(at.UnixMilli()).WithDispatchedAt(at))).
  WithSidecars(catalogac.Sidecar().WithPath(srt).WithName("Heat (1995).en.srt").WithLanguage("en"))),
  "release N's own steady state")

 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithCompliant(true).WithProfileTag("default@abc123").
   WithLastResult(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeResultSucceeded)).
  WithSidecars(catalogac.Sidecar().WithPath(srt).WithLanguage("en"))),
  "release N's schema must accept the previous release's apply, or a rollback freezes every file N touched")

 var got catalogv1alpha1.MediaFile
 require.NoError(t, c.Get(ctx, client.ObjectKey{Namespace: "default", Name: "heat"}, &got))
 require.NotNil(t, got.Status.Transcode)
 assert.Empty(t, got.Status.Transcode.Phase, "the previous release released the phase it never sends")
 assert.Equal(t, catalogv1alpha1.TranscodeResultSucceeded, got.Status.Transcode.LastResult)
 require.Len(t, got.Status.Sidecars, 1)
 assert.Equal(t, srt, got.Status.Sidecars[0].Path)
 assert.Empty(t, got.Status.Sidecars[0].Name)

 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().
  WithTranscode(catalogac.TranscodeState().WithPhase(catalogv1alpha1.TranscodePhaseSkipped).WithReason("Transcoded"))))
 require.NoError(t, c.Get(ctx, client.ObjectKey{Namespace: "default", Name: "heat"}, &got))
 assert.Empty(t, got.Status.Transcode.LastResult, "lastResult lost its +kubebuilder:default in release N (§2.1 item 5)")

 conds := make([]*metav1ac.ConditionApplyConfiguration, 13)
 for i := range conds {
  conds[i] = metav1ac.Condition().WithType(fmt.Sprintf("Type%02d", i)).WithStatus(metav1.ConditionTrue).
   WithReason("Test").WithMessage("m").WithLastTransitionTime(at)
 }
 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().WithConditions(conds[:12]...)))
 require.ErrorContains(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().WithConditions(conds...)), "12")

 sidecars := make([]*catalogac.SidecarApplyConfiguration, 33)
 for i := range sidecars {
  sidecars[i] = catalogac.Sidecar().WithPath(fmt.Sprintf("/data/media/movies/Heat (1995)/Heat (1995).%02d.srt", i))
 }
 require.NoError(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().WithSidecars(sidecars[:32]...)))
 require.ErrorContains(t, applyFoldStatus(t, c, "heat", catalogac.MediaFileStatus().WithSidecars(sidecars...)), "32")
}
```
