  2. Replace `images/Dockerfile.native`'s content with:

```dockerfile
# syntax=docker/dockerfile:1.7
#
# ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native -- the agent, markers and transcode
# binaries on FFmpeg 9's libraries, FROM scratch (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1.3,
# R1, R2). Targets:
#
#   native        every agent domain (the download engines included), markers,
#                 every transcode pool (cpu, nvidia, intel) and the graft
#                 Jobs; amd64 and arm64 (Intel's VAAPI driver and QSV runtimes
#                 on amd64 only)
#   native-debug  the same plus a static busybox, for kubectl exec
#
#   make docker-build-native     # both, with the pinned build contexts
#
# No ENTRYPOINT: the image holds three binaries, so every container names its
# own (pkg/binpath; TestEveryContainerNamesItsBinary), and one that names none
# fails at once instead of starting the wrong program.
#
# There is no CUDA target (docs/adr/0015-no-cuda-image.md). An nvidia pool
# runs `native`: the NVIDIA container runtime injects the driver's libraries
# (libcuda, libnvidia-encode, libnvcuvid) into a pod that asks for them with
# runtimeClassName, an nvidia.com/gpu request and
# NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=video,compute,utility
# (app/squash/controller/pool.applyHardware).
#
# There is no ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2 executable in the image: every binary
# runs FFmpeg through ffgo in-process, and (from §11.1 step 12) par2 through
# par2go. stage.sh refuses all three, so a copy cannot creep back in.
#
# FFmpeg is BtbN's 9.0 shared GPL build (FFMPEG_RELEASE/FFMPEG_VERSION pin
# one, checked by its SHA-256): NVENC/NVDEC and the CUDA filters, VAAPI
# through libva (dlopen'ed), and the libvpl dispatcher. Its libraries, the
# ffgo shim compiled against the same tarball's headers from the fork's own
# shim/ffshim.c, and ONNX Runtime live in /usr/lib, which the dynamic linker
# searches without an ld.so.cache. hack/native-assets.sh reads the FFmpeg and
# ONNX Runtime pins from this file's ARG defaults, so tests load what ships.

ARG GO_VERSION=1.27
ARG FFMPEG_BRANCH=9.0

# Empty unless `--build-context ffgo=<dir>` / `par2go=<dir>` replaces them
# (spec §7.6, §10.1.5): go.mod replaces both modules with local directories
# until their tags are published. The COPY targets are go.mod's directories
# as /src/.. sees them.
FROM scratch AS ffgo
FROM scratch AS par2go

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# build: agent (cgo, R13), markers and transcode (purego), and the ffgo
# shim's source. Built on the target platform: the agent needs cgo.
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM golang:${GO_VERSION}-bookworm AS build
ARG VERSION=dev
ARG FFGO_COMMIT=""
WORKDIR /src
ENV GOFLAGS=-trimpath
COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/
COPY --from=par2go / /par2go-1bd94eb/
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod \
    --mount=type=cache,target=/root/.cache/go-build \
    set -eux; \
    ld="-s -w -X github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/version.Version=${VERSION}"; \
    CGO_ENABLED=1 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/agent ./cmd/agent; \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/markers ./cmd/markers; \
    CGO_ENABLED=0 go build -ldflags "${ld}" -o /out/transcode ./cmd/transcode; \
    mkdir -p /out/ffgo /out/licenses/clustarr /out/licenses/ffgo; \
    ffgo="$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)"; \
    cp -r "${ffgo}/shim" /out/ffgo/; \
    cp "${ffgo}/LICENSE" /out/licenses/ffgo/LICENSE; \
    printf 'ffgo %s\nSource: https://github.com/mediactl/ffgo (a fork of https://github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)\n' \
      "${FFGO_COMMIT:-$(go list -m -f '{{if .Replace}}{{.Replace.Path}} {{.Replace.Version}}{{else}}{{.Version}}{{end}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)}" \
      > /out/licenses/ffgo/SOURCE; \
    cp LICENSE /out/licenses/clustarr/LICENSE

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ffmpeg: BtbN's shared build into /usr, and the shim against its headers
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS ffmpeg
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG FFMPEG_BRANCH
# One dated BtbN build, checked by its published SHA-256, so CI, the release
# and hack/native-assets.sh use the same FFmpeg. FFMPEG_URL (with
# FFMPEG_SHA256) overrides.
ARG FFMPEG_RELEASE=autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08
ARG FFMPEG_VERSION=n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64=01a9764d0b5364b66cfeb4617557c64321b0e232e172ec73f0a701c5f7694326
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64=706ccdbc8b0537646345532713a9b6750c0a6258cc001ec1c0379754f0ae730a
ARG FFMPEG_URL=""
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256=""
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl xz-utils gcc libc6-dev \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=build /out/ffgo/shim /src/shim
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) a=linux64; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) a=linuxarm64; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    url="https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/${FFMPEG_RELEASE}/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}-${a}-gpl-shared-${FFMPEG_BRANCH}.tar.xz"; \
    if [ -n "${FFMPEG_URL}" ]; then url="${FFMPEG_URL}"; sum="${FFMPEG_SHA256}"; fi; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/ff.tar.xz "${url}"; \
    if [ -n "${sum}" ]; then echo "${sum}  /tmp/ff.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -; fi; \
    mkdir -p /opt/ffmpeg; \
    tar -xJf /tmp/ff.tar.xz --strip-components=1 -C /opt/ffmpeg; \
    mkdir -p /out/usr/lib /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg; \
    cp -a /opt/ffmpeg/lib/lib*.so* /out/usr/lib/; \
    cp /opt/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt; \
    printf 'FFmpeg %s, built by BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds (GPL, shared): %s\nSource: https://github.com/FFmpeg/FFmpeg (the commit after the last "g" in the version)\nBuild scripts: https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds\n' \
      "$(LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ffmpeg/lib /opt/ffmpeg/bin/ffmpeg -hide_banner -version 2>/dev/null | head -n1 || echo "${FFMPEG_VERSION}")" "${url}" \
      > /out/usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE; \
    gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVDEVICE=1 -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVFILTER=1 \
      -I/opt/ffmpeg/include -o /out/usr/lib/libffshim.so /src/shim/ffshim.c \
      -L/opt/ffmpeg/lib -lavutil -lavcodec -lavformat -lavdevice -lavfilter

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# ort: ONNX Runtime's shared library, for markers' text detector
# (pkg/segments/textdet through onnxruntime-purego, C API 23 = ORT 1.23)
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS ort
ARG TARGETARCH
ARG ORT_VERSION=1.23.2
ARG ORT_SHA256_AMD64=1fa4dcaef22f6f7d5cd81b28c2800414350c10116f5fdd46a2160082551c5f9b
ARG ORT_SHA256_ARM64=7c63c73560ed76b1fac6cff8204ffe34fe180e70d6582b5332ec094810241e5c
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends ca-certificates curl \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in \
      amd64) a=x64; sum="${ORT_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; \
      arm64) a=aarch64; sum="${ORT_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; \
      *) echo "unsupported TARGETARCH=${TARGETARCH}" >&2; exit 1 ;; \
    esac; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/ort.tgz "https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/download/v${ORT_VERSION}/onnxruntime-linux-${a}-${ORT_VERSION}.tgz"; \
    echo "${sum}  /tmp/ort.tgz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    mkdir -p /tmp/ort /out/usr/lib /out/usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime; \
    tar -xzf /tmp/ort.tgz --strip-components=1 -C /tmp/ort; \
    install -m 0644 "/tmp/ort/lib/libonnxruntime.so.${ORT_VERSION}" /out/usr/lib/libonnxruntime.so; \
    install -m 0644 /tmp/ort/LICENSE /tmp/ort/ThirdPartyNotices.txt /out/usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime/

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# staging: lddtree everything the binaries load into /staging
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# Staged from Debian 13: BtbN's FFmpeg 9 calls libva 2.21's vaMapBuffer2, and
# Debian 12's libva 2.17 lacks it. glibc and libstdc++ run binaries built
# against older versions, as the agent (bookworm, cgo) and BtbN's are.
FROM debian:trixie-slim AS staging-base
RUN apt-get update \
 && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends pax-utils ca-certificates gcc binutils \
 && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
COPY --from=ffmpeg /out/ /
COPY --from=ort /out/ /
COPY --from=build /out/agent /out/markers /out/transcode /usr/bin/
COPY --from=build /out/licenses/ /usr/share/licenses/
COPY images/distroless/stage.sh /stage.sh

# Intel (amd64 only): Debian 13's VAAPI driver (the non-free iHD build: the
# free one has no HEVC 10-bit encode on Kaby Lake through Comet Lake) and
# libva 2.22, and both QSV runtimes -- libmfx-gen for Gen12 and newer, and
# Media SDK's libmfxhw64 for Broadwell..Ice Lake, which Debian 13 dropped, so
# it alone comes from Debian 12. All of it is dlopen'ed, so it is named for
# lddtree. On arm64 there is no Intel GPU to drive.
#
# Then the C++-symbol check (spec §7.6 item 2): ONNX Runtime is C++, and
# FFmpeg's libraries must never export a C++ symbol beside it.
FROM staging-base AS staging
ARG TARGETARCH
RUN set -eux; \
    if [ "${TARGETARCH}" = amd64 ]; then \
      sed -i 's/^Components: main$/Components: main non-free/' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; \
      grep -q '^Components: main non-free$' /etc/apt/sources.list.d/debian.sources; \
      printf 'Types: deb\nURIs: http://deb.debian.org/debian\nSuites: bookworm\nComponents: main\nSigned-By: /usr/share/keyrings/debian-archive-keyring.gpg\n' \
        > /etc/apt/sources.list.d/bookworm.sources; \
      printf 'Package: *\nPin: release n=bookworm\nPin-Priority: 100\n' > /etc/apt/preferences.d/bookworm; \
      apt-get update; \
      apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends intel-media-va-driver-non-free libmfx-gen1.2 libva2 libva-drm2 libmfx1/bookworm; \
      rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*; \
      d=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu; \
      export EXTRA_DLOPEN="$d/dri/iHD_drv_video.so $d/libva.so.2 $d/libva-drm.so.2 $d/libmfx-gen.so.1.2 $(ls $d/libmfx-gen/*.so) $d/libmfxhw64.so.1 $(ls $d/mfx/*.so)"; \
    fi; \
    /stage.sh /staging; \
    if nm -D --defined-only /staging/usr/lib/libav*.so.* /staging/usr/lib/libsw*.so.* | grep -q ' _Z'; then \
      echo 'FFmpeg exports C++ symbols beside ONNX Runtime' >&2; exit 1; \
    fi

# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
# native: FROM scratch, plus what one architecture alone needs
# ---------------------------------------------------------------------------
FROM scratch AS native-base
LABEL org.opencontainers.image.source="https://github.com/mediactl/clustarr" \
      org.opencontainers.image.licenses="GPL-3.0-only" \
      org.opencontainers.image.title="clustarr-native"
COPY --from=staging /staging/ /
ENV FFGO_SHIM_DIR=/usr/lib \
    ORT_LIB_PATH=/usr/lib/libonnxruntime.so
VOLUME ["/data"]
USER 1000:1000

# libva logs every driver load at info level on stderr; errors only keeps
# FFmpeg's own error in a transcode's stderr tail. The driver path is where
# staging put iHD, under amd64's multiarch directory.
FROM native-base AS native-amd64
ENV LIBVA_MESSAGING_LEVEL=1 \
    LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH=/usr/lib/x86_64-linux-gnu/dri \
    LIBVA_DRIVER_NAME=iHD

# arm64 stages no libva and no driver (see staging), so it names none.
FROM native-base AS native-arm64

FROM native-${TARGETARCH} AS native

FROM native AS native-debug
COPY --from=busybox:1.37-musl /bin/ /bin/
COPY images/distroless/busybox-SOURCE /usr/share/licenses/busybox/SOURCE
```

```sh
# Stages into $1 exactly what the native image loads, for a FROM-scratch
# image (images/Dockerfile.native).
#
# lddtree follows each file's DT_NEEDED tree: the agent (a cgo build, so it
# brings libc, libm, libresolv, libstdc++ and libgcc_s), markers and
# transcode (purego binaries, so the dynamic linker and libc), the ffgo shim,
# ONNX Runtime and every FFmpeg library -- never an ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2
# executable, which nothing in the image runs (R2), and which the last step
# refuses. What no DT_NEEDED names, because it is dlopen'ed, is traced
# explicitly: glibc's NSS plugins here, and the caller's EXTRA_DLOPEN (the
# Intel runtime).
```

```sh
# exec'ing it.
for f in ffmpeg ffprobe par2; do
 if [ -n "$(find "$dst" -name "$f" \( -type f -o -type l \) | head -n1)" ]; then
```

  1. `images/distroless/README.md` (whole file):

````markdown
# The native image

`images/Dockerfile.native` builds `ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native` FROM
scratch (spec `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md`
§10.1.3): the `agent`, `markers` and `transcode` binaries on FFmpeg 9's
libraries. It replaced the `transcoder` image (this file's
`Dockerfile.transcoder` until then) and the debian-based `media` image, which
carried `ffmpeg`, `ffprobe` and `par2` executables; nothing runs an external
media program any more (R2).

| Target | Platforms | Runs | Size |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| `native` | amd64, arm64 | every agent domain, the download engines, markers, the transcode pools (`cpu`, `cuda`, `intel` on amd64) and the graft Jobs | the transcoder's 118 MB gzipped on amd64 plus the agent, markers and ONNX Runtime |
| `native-debug` | as `native` | | +1 MB (static busybox) |

Both are per-architecture: `native` is `native-amd64` or `native-arm64` over a
shared `native-base`, and only amd64, which stages libva and Intel's iHD
driver, sets `LIBVA_*`. There is no ENTRYPOINT: every container names its
binary (`/usr/bin/agent`, `/usr/bin/markers`, `/usr/bin/transcode`).

There is no CUDA image ([ADR-0015](../../docs/adr/0015-no-cuda-image.md)).
An nvidia pool runs `native`: the NVIDIA container runtime injects the
driver's libraries (`libcuda`, `libnvidia-encode`, `libnvcuvid`), which
FFmpeg `dlopen`s, into a pod that sets `runtimeClassName: nvidia`, requests
`nvidia.com/gpu` and sets `NVIDIA_DRIVER_CAPABILITIES=video,compute,utility`,
as the manager's pool template does. Do not add a CUDA target back without
reading the ADR.

What is in it, and why:

- `stage.sh` runs `lddtree --copy-to-tree` on the three binaries (the agent
  is a cgo build, R13, so it brings glibc and libstdc++), the ffgo shim,
  ONNX Runtime and every FFmpeg library. It fails the build if `ffmpeg`,
  `ffprobe` or `par2` is staged.
- `lddtree` cannot see what is `dlopen`ed, so that is named: glibc's NSS
  plugins and, on amd64, the VAAPI driver and the QSV runtimes.
- The CA bundle, `nsswitch.conf`, `passwd` and `group` for uid 1000, and
  `/data`, `/scratch` and `/tmp`.
- FFmpeg's libraries, the shim and ONNX Runtime live in `/usr/lib`, which the
  dynamic linker searches without an `ld.so.cache`; `FFGO_SHIM_DIR` and
  `ORT_LIB_PATH` point there.

```sh
make docker-build-native   # native and native-debug, with the pinned contexts (make contexts)
make docker-selfcheck      # hack/image-checks.sh, as CI and the release run it
```
````

```go
// imageCheckPatterns are the case patterns hack/image-checks.sh defines, as
// anchored regexps ("version:*" matches "version:agent").
func imageCheckPatterns(t *testing.T, root string) []*regexp.Regexp {
 t.Helper()
 script := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "hack/image-checks.sh"))
 var out []*regexp.Regexp
 for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\s+([a-z0-9:*|-]+)\)`).FindAllStringSubmatch(script, -1) {
  for _, alt := range strings.Split(m[1], "|") {
   if alt == "*" {
    continue // the unknown-check fallthrough, which refuses
   }
   out = append(out, regexp.MustCompile("^"+strings.ReplaceAll(regexp.QuoteMeta(alt), `\*`, ".+")+"$"))
  }
 }
 require.NotEmpty(t, out, "hack/image-checks.sh defines no checks")
 return out
}

// TestTheMakefileChecksImagesThroughOneScript: hack/image-checks.sh is the
// one definition of the image checks (spec §10.1.4), as hack/e2e.sh's
// `make e2e` is of the e2e go test line. The Makefile never runs an image
// itself, names only checks the script defines, and passes the pinned
// contexts to every build; hack/kind.sh loads the two images that exist.
func TestTheMakefileChecksImagesThroughOneScript(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 patterns := imageCheckPatterns(t, root)
 known := func(check string) bool {
  for _, p := range patterns {
   if p.MatchString(check) {
    return true
   }
  }
  return false
 }
 mk := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "Makefile"))
 var builds, checks int
 for _, line := range strings.Split(mk, "\n") {
  l := strings.TrimSpace(line)
  switch {
  case strings.HasPrefix(l, "docker build "):
   builds++
   assert.Contains(t, l, "$(LOCAL_CONTEXTS)", "every image build passes the pinned contexts: %s", l)
  case strings.HasPrefix(l, "docker run"), strings.Contains(l, "--self-check"):
   t.Errorf("the Makefile checks an image itself (%q): hack/image-checks.sh is the one definition", l)
  case strings.HasPrefix(l, "hack/image-checks.sh "):
   for _, c := range strings.Fields(l)[2:] {
    if strings.Contains(c, "$(") {
     continue
    }
    checks++
    assert.True(t, known(c), "the Makefile asks hack/image-checks.sh for %q, which it does not define", c)
   }
  }
 }
 m := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^NATIVE_CHECKS \?= (.+)$`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
 require.NotNil(t, m, "the Makefile has no NATIVE_CHECKS")
 for _, c := range strings.Fields(m[1]) {
  if !strings.Contains(c, "$(") {
   assert.True(t, known(c), "NATIVE_CHECKS names %q, which hack/image-checks.sh does not define", c)
  }
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 5, builds, "docker-build (2), docker-build-native (2), docker-build-fixtures (1)")
 assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, checks, 5)
 kind := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "hack/kind.sh"))
 assert.NotContains(t, kind, "MEDIA_IMG")
 assert.NotContains(t, kind, "TRANSCODER_IMG")
 assert.Contains(t, kind, `"${IMG}" "${NATIVE_IMG}"`)
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `hack/image-checks.sh` (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hack/image-checks.sh IMAGE CHECK... -- the one definition of the image
# checks (spec 2026-10-06 §10.1.4). The Makefile's docker-selfcheck, ci.yml
# and release.yml all call it; none restates a check.
#
#   version:<bin>                 /usr/bin/<bin> --version, read-only, no capabilities, uid 1000
#   self-check:transcode:<class>  transcode --self-check=<class>, as a pool pod runs it
#   self-check:agent              agent --self-check
#   self-check:markers            markers --self-check
#   self-check:par2-child         agent par2-repair --self-check
#   no-shell                      the image has no /bin/sh
#   notices                       (debug image) every licence notice exists and is non-empty
#   no-media-executables          (debug image) no ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2 file anywhere
set -euo pipefail
usage="usage: hack/image-checks.sh IMAGE CHECK..."
img=${1:?$usage}
shift
[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { echo "${usage}" >&2; exit 2; }
# The par2 integration (§11.1 step 12) adds par2cmdline-turbo's and par2go's notices.
notices=(
  /usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/LICENSE.txt
  /usr/share/licenses/ffmpeg/SOURCE
  /usr/share/licenses/clustarr/LICENSE
  /usr/share/licenses/ffgo/LICENSE
  /usr/share/licenses/ffgo/SOURCE
  /usr/share/licenses/onnxruntime/LICENSE
  /usr/share/doc/libc6/copyright
)
locked() { docker run --rm --read-only --cap-drop=ALL --user 1000:1000 "$@"; }
for check in "$@"; do
  echo "== ${img}: ${check}" >&2
  case "${check}" in
    version:*)
      locked --entrypoint "/usr/bin/${check#version:}" "${img}" --version ;;
    self-check:transcode:*)
      locked --entrypoint /usr/bin/transcode "${img}" --self-check="${check#self-check:transcode:}" >/dev/null ;;
    self-check:agent|self-check:markers)
      locked --entrypoint "/usr/bin/${check#self-check:}" "${img}" --self-check ;;
    self-check:par2-child)
      locked --entrypoint /usr/bin/agent "${img}" par2-repair --self-check ;;
    no-shell)
      if docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c true >/dev/null 2>&1; then
        echo "${img} has a shell" >&2; exit 1
      fi ;;
    notices)
      docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c \
        'set -e; for f in "$@"; do test -s "$f" || { echo "missing notice $f" >&2; exit 1; }; done; cat /usr/share/licenses/*/SOURCE' \
        sh "${notices[@]}" ;;
    no-media-executables)
      found=$(docker run --rm --entrypoint /bin/sh "${img}" -c 'find / -xdev \( -name ffmpeg -o -name ffprobe -o -name par2 \) -type f')
      [[ -z "${found}" ]] || { echo "${img} carries a media executable: ${found}" >&2; exit 1; } ;;
    *)
      echo "hack/image-checks.sh: unknown check ${check}" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done
echo "ok: ${img}" >&2
```

```bash
cmd_load() {
  need kind
  need docker
  cluster_exists || die "kind cluster '${CLUSTER_NAME}' does not exist; run 'hack/kind.sh up'"
  local img node_id
  for img in "${IMG}" "${NATIVE_IMG}"; do
    if ! docker image inspect "${img}" >/dev/null 2>&1; then
      log "image ${img} not found locally, skipping (run 'make docker-build')"
      continue
    fi
    # Loading unpacks gigabytes into the node's containerd store, which shares
    # a disk with etcd (CLAUDE.md, "loading an image into the node stalls
    # etcd"): load only an image whose content changed.
    node_id=$(docker exec "${CLUSTER_NAME}-control-plane" crictl inspecti -o go-template --template '{{.status.id}}' "${img}" 2>/dev/null || true)
    if [[ "${node_id}" == "$(docker image inspect -f '{{.Id}}' "${img}")" ]]; then
      log "${img} unchanged on the node, skipping"
      continue
    fi
    log "loading ${img}"
    kind load docker-image --name "${CLUSTER_NAME}" "${img}"
  done
}
```

```go
package guards

import (
 "os/exec"
 "path/filepath"
 "regexp"
 "runtime"
 "strings"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/test/installtest"
)

// dockerArgs is every `ARG NAME=default` of a Dockerfile.
func dockerArgs(df string) map[string]string {
 out := map[string]string{}
 for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^ARG ([A-Z0-9_]+)=(\S+)$`).FindAllStringSubmatch(df, -1) {
  if _, seen := out[m[1]]; !seen {
   out[m[1]] = m[2]
  }
 }
 return out
}

// TestNativeAssetsReadsItsPinsFromTheNativeDockerfile: the native tests must
// load the FFmpeg and ONNX Runtime the image ships, so hack/native-assets.sh
// reads them from images/Dockerfile.native's ARG defaults and restates none.
func TestNativeAssetsReadsItsPinsFromTheNativeDockerfile(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 out, err := exec.Command("bash", filepath.Join(root, "hack", "native-assets.sh"), "--print-pins").CombinedOutput()
 require.NoError(t, err, "%s", out)
 pins := map[string]string{}
 for _, line := range strings.Split(strings.TrimSpace(string(out)), "\n") {
  k, v, ok := strings.Cut(line, "=")
  require.True(t, ok, "pin line %q", line)
  pins[k] = v
 }
 arch := map[string]string{"amd64": "AMD64", "arm64": "ARM64"}[runtime.GOARCH]
 require.NotEmpty(t, arch, "GOARCH %s", runtime.GOARCH)
 args := dockerArgs(string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native")))
 for pin, arg := range map[string]string{
  "FFMPEG_RELEASE": "FFMPEG_RELEASE", "FFMPEG_VERSION": "FFMPEG_VERSION", "FFMPEG_BRANCH": "FFMPEG_BRANCH",
  "FFMPEG_SHA256": "FFMPEG_SHA256_" + arch, "ORT_VERSION": "ORT_VERSION", "ORT_SHA256": "ORT_SHA256_" + arch,
 } {
  require.NotEmpty(t, args[arg], "images/Dockerfile.native has no ARG %s default", arg)
  assert.Equal(t, args[arg], pins[pin], "%s", pin)
 }
 assert.Equal(t, "v1.5.0", pins["PAR2_CLI_VERSION"])
 script := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "hack/native-assets.sh"))
 for _, arg := range []string{"FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64", "FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64", "ORT_SHA256_AMD64", "ORT_SHA256_ARM64", "FFMPEG_RELEASE"} {
  assert.NotContains(t, script, args[arg], "hack/native-assets.sh restates %s; it must read it from the Dockerfile", arg)
 }
}

// TestTheTestTargetsLoadTheNativeAssets: make test and make test-race build
// the native assets and the chart's dependencies first and run with the
// assets' environment, under which a missing tool fails instead of skipping
// (spec §10.1.6, OD44). LD_LIBRARY_PATH is not optional: ffgo loads libav*
// at package init through it, before any test can set it.
func TestTheTestTargetsLoadTheNativeAssets(t *testing.T) {
 mk := string(readRepoFile(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), "Makefile"))
 for _, target := range []string{"test", "test-race"} {
  m := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^` + regexp.QuoteMeta(target) + `:([^#\n]*)`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
  require.NotNil(t, m, "no %s target", target)
  prereqs := strings.Fields(m[1])
  for _, p := range []string{"envtest", "pg-assets", "native-assets", "chart-deps"} {
   assert.Contains(t, prereqs, p, "%s's prerequisites", target)
  }
  recipe := regexp.MustCompile(`(?ms)^` + regexp.QuoteMeta(target) + `:[^\n]*\n((?:\t[^\n]*\n)+)`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
  require.NotNil(t, recipe, "%s's recipe", target)
  assert.Contains(t, recipe[1], "$(NATIVE_ENV)", "%s runs go test with the native assets' environment", target)
 }
 env := regexp.MustCompile(`(?ms)^NATIVE_ENV = (.*?)\n\n`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
 require.NotNil(t, env, "the Makefile has no NATIVE_ENV")
 for _, v := range []string{"LD_LIBRARY_PATH=", "CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS=", "FFGO_SHIM_DIR=", "ORT_LIB_PATH=",
  "PAR2GO_LIB=", "PAR2GO_REQUIRE=1", "PATH=", "CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1"} {
  assert.Contains(t, env[1], v)
 }
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `hack/native-assets.sh` (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hack/native-assets.sh DIR | --print-pins
#
# The native test assets, the analogue of `make pg-assets` (spec 2026-10-06
# §10.1.6). DIR/lib: FFmpeg 9's shared libraries and libffshim, ONNX Runtime
# and libpar2shim. DIR/bin: the test-only ffmpeg, ffprobe and par2
# executables the parity tests compare against and test/par2test.CreateSet
# runs. No image ships those executables.
#
# Pins: FFmpeg and ONNX Runtime from images/Dockerfile.native's ARG defaults,
# so the tests load what the image ships; libffshim from the ffgo module
# go.mod resolves (the shim/ffshim.c the Go side is built against);
# libpar2shim from `git archive $PAR2GO_REF` of $PAR2GO_DIR through par2go's
# own shim/build.sh; the par2 CLI from PAR2_CLI_VERSION below.
#
# Idempotent: DIR/.stamp records every input, and a matching stamp exits at
# once. The work happens under mktemp -d in $TMPDIR (scratch areas are
# shared between sessions), and DIR is swapped in with one rename.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
df="${repo}/images/Dockerfile.native"
PAR2_CLI_VERSION=v1.5.0
PAR2_CLI_SHA256_AMD64=5a9f64386813456693c2ea1fb7649436fe7544bbdf97fd73b3483dfcc8aca464
PAR2_CLI_SHA256_ARM64=3afb2f0b319fc4e6353c6d4261994757cbe3189f968a72420b4ba1d63f9c9a70
par2go_dir=${PAR2GO_DIR:-${repo}/../par2go}
par2go_ref=${PAR2GO_REF:-1bd94eb}

arg() {
  local v
  v=$(sed -nE "s/^ARG $1=(.+)$/\1/p" "${df}" | head -n1)
  [[ -n "${v}" ]] || { echo "native-assets: images/Dockerfile.native has no ARG $1 default" >&2; exit 1; }
  printf '%s' "${v}"
}
case "$(uname -m)" in
  x86_64) arch=AMD64 ff=linux64 ort=x64 p2=amd64 ;;
  aarch64) arch=ARM64 ff=linuxarm64 ort=aarch64 p2=arm64 ;;
  *) echo "native-assets: unsupported machine $(uname -m)" >&2; exit 1 ;;
esac
FFMPEG_RELEASE=$(arg FFMPEG_RELEASE)
FFMPEG_VERSION=$(arg FFMPEG_VERSION)
FFMPEG_BRANCH=$(arg FFMPEG_BRANCH)
FFMPEG_SHA256=$(arg "FFMPEG_SHA256_${arch}")
ORT_VERSION=$(arg ORT_VERSION)
ORT_SHA256=$(arg "ORT_SHA256_${arch}")
par2_sha="PAR2_CLI_SHA256_${arch}"
PAR2_CLI_SHA256=${!par2_sha}
pins=(FFMPEG_RELEASE FFMPEG_VERSION FFMPEG_BRANCH FFMPEG_SHA256 ORT_VERSION ORT_SHA256 PAR2_CLI_VERSION PAR2_CLI_SHA256)

if [[ "${1:-}" == --print-pins ]]; then
  for k in "${pins[@]}"; do printf '%s=%s\n' "${k}" "${!k}"; done
  exit 0
fi

dir=${1:?usage: hack/native-assets.sh DIR | --print-pins}
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${dir}")"
dir="$(cd "$(dirname "${dir}")" && pwd)/$(basename "${dir}")"
ffgo_dir=$(cd "${repo}" && go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)
par2go_commit=$(git -C "${par2go_dir}" rev-parse -q --verify "${par2go_ref}^{commit}") ||
  { echo "native-assets: ${par2go_dir} has no commit ${par2go_ref}" >&2; exit 1; }
stamp=$(
  for k in "${pins[@]}"; do printf '%s=%s\n' "${k}" "${!k}"; done
  printf 'par2go=%s\n' "${par2go_commit}"
  cat "${ffgo_dir}/shim/ffshim.c" "${ffgo_dir}/shim/ffshim.h" | sha256sum
  sha256sum < "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}"
)
stamp=$(printf '%s' "${stamp}" | sha256sum | cut -d' ' -f1)
if [[ -f "${dir}/.stamp" && "$(cat "${dir}/.stamp")" == "${stamp}" ]]; then
  echo "native-assets: ${dir} is current" >&2
  exit 0
fi

work=$(mktemp -d "${TMPDIR:-/tmp}/native-assets.XXXXXX")
trap 'rm -rf "${work}"' EXIT
out="${work}/out"
mkdir -p "${out}/lib" "${out}/bin"

echo "native-assets: FFmpeg ${FFMPEG_VERSION}" >&2
curl -fsSL -o "${work}/ff.tar.xz" \
  "https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/${FFMPEG_RELEASE}/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}-${ff}-gpl-shared-${FFMPEG_BRANCH}.tar.xz"
echo "${FFMPEG_SHA256}  ${work}/ff.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null
mkdir -p "${work}/ff"
tar -xJf "${work}/ff.tar.xz" --strip-components=1 -C "${work}/ff"
cp -a "${work}"/ff/lib/lib*.so* "${out}/lib/"
install -m 0755 "${work}/ff/bin/ffmpeg" "${work}/ff/bin/ffprobe" "${out}/bin/"

echo "native-assets: libffshim from ${ffgo_dir}/shim" >&2
gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -Wall -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVDEVICE=1 -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVFILTER=1 \
  -I"${work}/ff/include" -o "${out}/lib/libffshim.so" "${ffgo_dir}/shim/ffshim.c" \
  -L"${out}/lib" -lavutil -lavcodec -lavformat -lavdevice -lavfilter -Wl,-rpath,"${dir}/lib"

echo "native-assets: ONNX Runtime ${ORT_VERSION}" >&2
curl -fsSL -o "${work}/ort.tgz" \
  "https://github.com/microsoft/onnxruntime/releases/download/v${ORT_VERSION}/onnxruntime-linux-${ort}-${ORT_VERSION}.tgz"
echo "${ORT_SHA256}  ${work}/ort.tgz" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null
mkdir -p "${work}/ort"
tar -xzf "${work}/ort.tgz" --strip-components=1 -C "${work}/ort"
install -m 0644 "${work}/ort/lib/libonnxruntime.so.${ORT_VERSION}" "${out}/lib/libonnxruntime.so"

echo "native-assets: par2cmdline-turbo ${PAR2_CLI_VERSION} (a test-only CLI)" >&2
curl -fsSL -o "${work}/par2.zip" \
  "https://github.com/animetosho/par2cmdline-turbo/releases/download/${PAR2_CLI_VERSION}/par2cmdline-turbo-${PAR2_CLI_VERSION#v}-linux-${p2}.zip"
echo "${PAR2_CLI_SHA256}  ${work}/par2.zip" | sha256sum -c - >/dev/null
unzip -p "${work}/par2.zip" par2 > "${out}/bin/par2"
chmod 0755 "${out}/bin/par2"

echo "native-assets: libpar2shim from par2go ${par2go_ref} (${par2go_commit})" >&2
mkdir -p "${work}/par2go"
git -C "${par2go_dir}" archive "${par2go_commit}" | tar -x -C "${work}/par2go"
lib=$(CMAKE_BUILD_DIR="${work}/par2-cmake" OUT_DIR="${work}/par2-out" "${work}/par2go/shim/build.sh" | tail -n1)
[[ "$(basename "${lib}")" == libpar2shim.so ]] ||
  { echo "native-assets: par2go's shim/build.sh produced '${lib}', not libpar2shim.so" >&2; exit 1; }
install -m 0644 "${lib}" "${out}/lib/libpar2shim.so"

printf '%s\n' "${stamp}" > "${out}/.stamp"
next=$(mktemp -d "${dir}.new.XXXXXX")
cp -a "${out}/." "${next}/"
rm -rf "${dir}.old"
if [[ -e "${dir}" ]]; then mv "${dir}" "${dir}.old"; fi
mv "${next}" "${dir}"
rm -rf "${dir}.old"
echo "native-assets: ${dir}" >&2
```

  `Makefile`: after `PG_ASSETS ?= …` add

```make
# NATIVE_ASSETS holds what the native tests load and compare against
# (hack/native-assets.sh, spec §10.1.6): FFmpeg 9's libraries and libffshim,
# ONNX Runtime, libpar2shim, and the test-only ffmpeg, ffprobe and par2
# CLIs. ffgo finds libavutil, libavcodec and libavformat only through
# LD_LIBRARY_PATH and fixed system directories, at package init, so the
# variable must be in the test process's environment from the start;
# FFGO_SHIM_DIR locates only the shim. CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1 turns a
# missing tool (FFmpeg, the shims, ONNX Runtime, helm, kustomize,
# KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS) into a failure instead of a skip (OD44).
NATIVE_ASSETS ?= $(GOBIN)/native-assets
NATIVE_ENV = LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)/lib" \
 CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)" \
 FFGO_SHIM_DIR="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)/lib" \
 ORT_LIB_PATH="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)/lib/libonnxruntime.so" \
 PAR2GO_LIB="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)/lib/libpar2shim.so" \
 PAR2GO_REQUIRE=1 \
 PATH="$(NATIVE_ASSETS)/bin:$$PATH" \
 CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1

```

```go
package guards

import (
 "regexp"
 "strings"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/agentdomain"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/test/installtest"
)

// TestMakeBuildBuildsEachBinaryAsItsImageDoes: §3.9's build modes, held
// between the Makefile and the Dockerfiles, so a binary that works from
// bin/ cannot fail in its image for want of cgo (the agent's sqlite piece
// completion and go-libutp, R13) or link a loader the static image lacks.
func TestMakeBuildBuildsEachBinaryAsItsImageDoes(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 mk := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "Makefile"))
 recipe := regexp.MustCompile(`(?ms)^build:[^\n]*\n((?:\t[^\n]*\n)+)`).FindStringSubmatch(mk)
 require.NotNil(t, recipe, "no build target")
 built := map[string]string{}
 for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`CGO_ENABLED=(\d) go build -trimpath -ldflags "\$\(LDFLAGS\)" -o bin/(\w+) \./cmd/(\w+)`).FindAllStringSubmatch(recipe[1], -1) {
  require.Equal(t, m[2], m[3], "bin/%s is built from ./cmd/%s", m[2], m[3])
  built[m[2]] = m[1]
 }
 want := map[string]string{"manager": "0", "ui": "0", "agent": "1", "markers": "0", "transcode": "0"}
 assert.Equal(t, want, built, "make build: one line per binary, CGO_ENABLED as §3.9 says")

 native := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native"))
 inImage := map[string]string{}
 for _, m := range regexp.MustCompile(`CGO_ENABLED=(\d) go build [^\n]*-o /out/(\w+) \./cmd/\w+`).FindAllStringSubmatch(native, -1) {
  inImage[m[2]] = m[1]
 }
 _, clustarrBuild, ok := stageIn(string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.clustarr")), "build")
 require.True(t, ok)
 require.Contains(t, clustarrBuild, "CGO_ENABLED=0")
 for _, b := range []string{"manager", "ui"} {
  inImage[b] = "0"
 }
 assert.Equal(t, want, inImage, "the images build each binary as make build does")
}

// TestDevRunStartsEveryProcess: `make run-dev` is what `clustarr all` was
// (§3.10): the manager, one agent per queue- or RPC-driven domain (the
// engines need a DownloadClient, markers runs in its pod), and the ui, each
// on its own probe port, with the native libraries' environment.
func TestDevRunStartsEveryProcess(t *testing.T) {
 script := string(readRepoFile(t, installtest.RepoRoot(t), "hack/dev-run.sh"))
 starts := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^"\$\{bin\}/(\w+)"(.*) &$`).FindAllStringSubmatch(script, -1)
 count := map[string]int{}
 domains := map[string]int{}
 ports := map[string]bool{}
 for _, s := range starts {
  count[s[1]]++
  if d := regexp.MustCompile(`--domain=(\S+)`).FindStringSubmatch(s[2]); d != nil {
   domains[d[1]]++
  }
  if p := regexp.MustCompile(`--health-probe-bind-address=(\S+)`).FindStringSubmatch(s[2]); p != nil {
   assert.False(t, ports[p[1]], "two processes probe on %s", p[1])
   ports[p[1]] = true
  }
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 1, count["manager"])
 assert.Equal(t, 1, count["ui"])
 for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
  if len(d.Consumers) == 0 || d.Name == agentdomain.Markers {
   continue
  }
  assert.Equal(t, 1, domains[d.Name], "hack/dev-run.sh runs --domain=%s once", d.Name)
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 6, count["agent"])
 for _, v := range []string{"LD_LIBRARY_PATH=", "FFGO_SHIM_DIR=", "ORT_LIB_PATH=", "PAR2GO_LIB="} {
  assert.Contains(t, script, "export "+v, "hack/dev-run.sh exports %s", strings.TrimSuffix(v, "="))
 }
 assert.Contains(t, script, "kill 0", "one Ctrl-C stops every process")
}
```

  `hack/dev-run.sh` (`chmod +x`):

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
# hack/dev-run.sh -- the processes `clustarr all` used to be (spec 2026-10-06
# §3.10): the manager, one agent per domain and the ui, against the current
# kube context's API server and a NATS at $NATS_URL (for kind:
# `kubectl -n clustarr-system port-forward svc/nats 4222` and
# NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:4222). Manager and agent code never share a
# process, as in the cluster. One Ctrl-C stops them all: they share this
# script's process group, and the trap signals the group.
#
# Run it through `make run-dev`, which builds bin/ and the native assets
# first. The import and caption agents exit at start without the native
# libraries' environment below.
set -euo pipefail
repo=$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)
: "${NATS_URL:?export NATS_URL (kubectl -n clustarr-system port-forward svc/nats 4222; NATS_URL=nats://127.0.0.1:4222)}"
export NATS_URL
export POD_NAMESPACE="${POD_NAMESPACE:-clustarr-system}"
assets="${NATIVE_ASSETS:-$(go env GOPATH)/bin/native-assets}"
export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="${assets}/lib${LD_LIBRARY_PATH:+:${LD_LIBRARY_PATH}}"
export FFGO_SHIM_DIR="${assets}/lib"
export ORT_LIB_PATH="${assets}/lib/libonnxruntime.so"
export PAR2GO_LIB="${assets}/lib/libpar2shim.so"
native_img="${NATIVE_IMG:-ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native:dev}"
data_dir="${DATA_DIR:-${repo}/.data}"
index="${XDG_CACHE_HOME:-${HOME}/.cache}/clustarr/releases.db"
mkdir -p "$(dirname "${index}")" "${data_dir}"
bin="${repo}/bin"

trap 'trap - INT TERM EXIT; kill 0 2>/dev/null; wait' INT TERM EXIT

"${bin}/manager" --leader-elect=false --nats-single-node --native-image="${native_img}" --autoscale=false --external-metrics-bind-address=0 --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8081 --data-dir="${data_dir}" &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=catalog --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8082 &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=events --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8083 &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=metadata --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8084 &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=import --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8085 --data-dir="${data_dir}" &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=index --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8086 --index-path="${index}" --facade-bind-address=:9696 &
"${bin}/agent" --domain=caption --metrics-bind-address=0 --health-probe-bind-address=:8087 --data-dir="${data_dir}" &
"${bin}/ui" --auth-mode=anonymous --bind-address=:8080 &

# The first process to exit ends the session; the trap stops the rest.
wait -n
```

```go
// packages its identity's process links, built as its binary is (§3.9). A
// role's grants are for the code its home runs, so the paths the Makefile
// hands controller-gen are checked against what the home links.

 cgo  bool
 pkgs []string

// linkedNotRun names a marker package an identity's process links but whose
// grants it never needs, with the reason. Each entry must stay true: the
// package linked and uncovered.
var linkedNotRun = map[string]map[string]string{

  "app/catalog/controller/wantedcron": "the search worker calls wantedcron.ListCandidates, whose reads app/catalog/worker/search's own markers grant; the wanted-sweep Runnable runs in the manager",
 },

// markerPackages is every app/ package (repo-relative) with a
// +kubebuilder:rbac marker in a non-test file.
func markerPackages(t *testing.T, root string) map[string]bool {
 t.Helper()
 out := map[string]bool{}
 err := filepath.WalkDir(filepath.Join(root, "app"), func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
  if err != nil || d.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".go") || strings.HasSuffix(path, "_test.go") {
   return err
  }
  b, err := os.ReadFile(path)
  if err != nil {
   return err
  }
  if bytes.Contains(b, []byte("+kubebuilder:rbac:")) {
   rel, err := filepath.Rel(root, filepath.Dir(path))
   if err != nil {
    return err
   }
   out[filepath.ToSlash(rel)] = true
  }
  return nil
 })
 require.NoError(t, err)
 require.NotEmpty(t, out, "no app/ package carries a +kubebuilder:rbac marker; this guard is not looking where it thinks")
 return out
}

// linkedPackages is every module package (repo-relative) the packages link.
func linkedPackages(t *testing.T, root string, cgo bool, pkgs ...string) map[string]bool {
 t.Helper()
 cmd := exec.Command("go", append([]string{"list", "-deps", "-f", "{{if not .Standard}}{{.ImportPath}}{{end}}"}, pkgs...)...)
 cmd.Dir = root
 cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "CGO_ENABLED="+map[bool]string{true: "1", false: "0"}[cgo])
 out, err := cmd.Output()
 require.NoError(t, err, "go list -deps %v", pkgs)
 got := map[string]bool{}
 for _, p := range strings.Fields(string(out)) {
  if rel, ok := strings.CutPrefix(p, "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/"); ok {
   got[rel] = true
  }
 }
 return got
}

// TestEachRoleCoversTheMarkedPackagesItsHomeLinks (§10.3.2): no role holds
// grants for code its process does not run (a marker package in its
// RBAC_PATHS its home never links), and no process runs code whose grants
// its role lacks (a marker package its home links that its RBAC_PATHS miss),
// unless linkedNotRun says why the grants are not needed. envtest enforces no
// RBAC, so without this a missing grant is a Forbidden on a real cluster.
func TestEachRoleCoversTheMarkedPackagesItsHomeLinks(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 marked := markerPackages(t, root)
 roles := map[string]installtest.RBACRole{}
 for _, r := range installtest.RBACRoles(t, root) {
  roles[r.Name] = r
  _, homed := roleHomes[r.Name]
  assert.True(t, homed || legacyRoles[r.Name], "RBAC_ROLES names %s, which has no home here", r.Name)
 }
 for name, home := range roleHomes {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   r, ok := roles[name]
   require.True(t, ok, "RBAC_ROLES has no %s role (spec §4.6)", name)
   linked := linkedPackages(t, root, home.cgo, home.pkgs...)
   covered := func(dir string) bool {
    for _, p := range r.Paths {
     if installtest.PatternCovers(p, dir) {
      return true
     }
    }
    return false
   }
   for dir := range marked {
    switch {
    case covered(dir) && !linked[dir]:
     t.Errorf("RBAC_PATHS_%s covers %s, which %v never links: the role holds grants for code its process does not run", name, dir, home.pkgs)
    case !covered(dir) && linked[dir]:
     if reason := linkedNotRun[name][dir]; reason == "" {
      t.Errorf("%v links %s, whose +kubebuilder:rbac markers RBAC_PATHS_%s does not cover: add the path, or a linkedNotRun entry saying why its grants are not needed", home.pkgs, dir, name)
     }
    }
   }
   for dir := range linkedNotRun[name] {
    assert.True(t, linked[dir] && marked[dir] && !covered(dir), "stale linkedNotRun[%s][%s]", name, dir)
   }
  })
 }
}

// TestConfigRBACHoldsOnlyKnownRoleFiles: `make manifests` never deletes, so a
// retired role's generated file would linger in config/rbac (and in a
// kustomization that still lists it) after RBAC_ROLES drops it.
func TestConfigRBACHoldsOnlyKnownRoleFiles(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 want := map[string]bool{"ui_role.yaml": true, "leader_election_role.yaml": true}
 for _, r := range installtest.RBACRoles(t, root) {
  want[r.File()] = true
 }
 files, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "config", "rbac", "*_role.yaml"))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 got := map[string]bool{}
 for _, f := range files {
  got[filepath.Base(f)] = true
 }
 assert.Equal(t, want, got, "config/rbac/*_role.yaml must be RBAC_ROLES' generated files plus ui_role.yaml and leader_election_role.yaml")
}

// TestFoldedAgentsWriteNoPerFileWork (ADR-0016; loop spec §4.14): per-file
// work is MediaFile status, written by the manager's remediation loop under
// catalogarr, and the three folded kinds are the manager's alone. The two
// agents that wrote it before the fold -- the caption fetch worker
// (SubtitleRequest status) and the metadata domain (catalogarr-markers on
// mediafiles/status) -- keep no write verb on a per-file resource. Item
// status (movies/status and the like, under catalogarr-metadata) is not
// per-file work and stays the metadata domain's.
func TestFoldedAgentsWriteNoPerFileWork(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 perFile := regexp.MustCompile(`^(catalog\.clustarr\.io/mediafiles|subtitle\.clustarr\.io/subtitlerequests|transcode\.clustarr\.io/(transcodejobs|audiografts))(/[a-z]+)?:(create|update|patch|delete|deletecollection|\*)$`)
 for _, f := range []string{"agent_caption_role.yaml", "agent_metadata_role.yaml"} {
  for _, g := range installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, root, f).Rules)) {
   assert.False(t, perFile.MatchString(g), "%s grants %s: per-file work is MediaFile status, written by the manager's loop (ADR-0016)", f, g)
  }
 }
}

// TestNoAgentRoleGrantsMediaFileStatus (loop spec §4.14, §4.15; ADR-0016):
// MediaFile status has one writer, the manager's remediation loop, and
// workers answer through records, so no identity but the manager holds any
// verb on mediafiles/status, a read included.
func TestNoAgentRoleGrantsMediaFileStatus(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 status := regexp.MustCompile(`^catalog\.clustarr\.io/mediafiles/status:`)
 for identity := range roleHomes {
  if identity == "manager" {
   continue
  }
  f := strings.ReplaceAll(identity, "-", "_") + "_role.yaml"
  for _, g := range installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, root, f).Rules)) {
   assert.False(t, status.MatchString(g), "%s grants %s: only the manager's loop writes MediaFile status (ADR-0016)", f, g)
  }
 }
}
```

```
{{/*
The shared workload shape: ServiceAccount + Service + Deployment.

Call with a dict:
  root               $
  component          "manager" | "agent-<domain>" -- also the ServiceAccount/Service name suffix
  image              "clustarr" | "native" -- key under .Values.image
  command            the binary (pkg/binpath); every container names one, no image has an ENTRYPOINT
  args               list of container args
  values             the workload's values block (resources, consumerSlots, scheduling)
  replicas           the fixed replica count
  autoscaled         true for a domain whose HPA the manager owns (pkg/agentdomain): with
                     autoscaling.enabled the Deployment carries autoscale.clustarr.io/domain
                     and no spec.replicas; a soft hostname spread applies either way
  domain             that label's value
  natsSingleNodeFlag append --nats-single-node when the JetStream topology is single-node
                     (the manager only: agents never ensure topology)
  leaderElect        append --leader-elect (the manager only)
  data               true to mount the RWX /data volume read-write, with UMASK 002
  index              true to mount the RWO index volume at /var/lib/clustarr/index
  strategy           a Deployment strategy map, or "" for the apps/v1 default
  grace              terminationGracePeriodSeconds (longest AckWait drained + 25 s, spec §3.5.6)
  gomemPercent       GOMEMLIMIT's share of resources.limits.memory (default 80)
  serviceType        the Service's type (default ClusterIP)
  extraPorts         list of (dict "name" "containerPort") before metrics and health
  extraServicePorts  list of (dict "name" "port" "targetPort") before metrics
  extraEnv / extraVolumeMounts / extraVolumes   lists, rendered as given
*/}}
{{- define "clustarr.workload" }}
{{- $root := .root }}
{{- $name := printf "%s-%s" (include "clustarr.fullname" $root) .component }}
{{- /* `and` stops at a false .autoscaled, so .Values.autoscaling is read
       only by a caller that asks for autoscaling. */}}
{{- $autoscaled := and .autoscaled $root.Values.autoscaling.enabled }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: ServiceAccount
metadata:
  name: {{ $name }}
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" $root | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: {{ .component }}
{{- with $root.Values.imagePullSecrets }}
imagePullSecrets:
  {{- toYaml . | nindent 2 }}
{{- end }}
---
apiVersion: v1
kind: Service
metadata:
  name: {{ $name }}
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" $root | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: {{ .component }}
spec:
  type: {{ default "ClusterIP" .serviceType }}
  selector:
    {{- include "clustarr.selectorLabels" (dict "root" $root "component" .component) | nindent 4 }}
  ports:
  {{- range .extraServicePorts }}
  - name: {{ .name }}
    port: {{ .port }}
    targetPort: {{ .targetPort }}
    protocol: TCP
  {{- end }}
  - name: metrics
    port: 8443
    targetPort: metrics
    protocol: TCP
---
apiVersion: apps/v1
kind: Deployment
metadata:
  name: {{ $name }}
  labels:
    {{- include "clustarr.labels" $root | nindent 4 }}
    app.kubernetes.io/component: {{ .component }}
    {{- if $autoscaled }}

    {{- end }}
spec:

  {{- with .strategy }}

      terminationGracePeriodSeconds: {{ .grace }}
      {{- with $root.Values.imagePullSecrets }}
      imagePullSecrets:
        {{- toYaml . | nindent 8 }}
      {{- end }}
```

  1. `test/installtest/workloads.go`:

```go
package installtest

import (
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
 appsv1 "k8s.io/api/apps/v1"
 corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
)

// Workloads returns r's Clustarr Deployments by app.kubernetes.io/component,
// skipping subchart and fixture workloads (nats-box, the e2e stubs).
func Workloads(r Rendered) map[string]appsv1.Deployment {
 out := map[string]appsv1.Deployment{}
 for _, d := range r.Deployments {
  if d.Labels["app.kubernetes.io/name"] != "clustarr" {
   continue
  }
  if c := d.Labels["app.kubernetes.io/component"]; c != "" {
   out[c] = d
  }
 }
 return out
}

// Container returns component's one container, failing when it is absent.
func Container(t testing.TB, r Rendered, component string) corev1.Container {
 t.Helper()
 d, ok := Workloads(r)[component]
 require.True(t, ok, "no Deployment for component %q", component)
 require.Len(t, d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers, 1, component)
 return d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
}

// SetEnvFrom sets c's environment in the test process as the kubelet
// would: literal values as written, metadata.name and metadata.namespace
// fieldRefs as podName and "clustarr-system", and anything read from a
// Secret or ConfigMap as "from-<NAME>". A command reads its flag defaults
// from the environment, so its parse of the rendered args must see it.
func SetEnvFrom(t *testing.T, c corev1.Container, podName string) {
 t.Helper()
 for _, e := range c.Env {
  v := e.Value
  if f := e.ValueFrom; f != nil {
   switch {
   case f.FieldRef != nil && f.FieldRef.FieldPath == "metadata.name":
    v = podName
   case f.FieldRef != nil && f.FieldRef.FieldPath == "metadata.namespace":
    v = "clustarr-system"
   default:
    v = "from-" + e.Name
   }
  }
  t.Setenv(e.Name, v)
 }
}
```

  1. `test/guards/topology_test.go`:

```go
package guards

import (
 "maps"
 "slices"
 "strings"
 "testing"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
 appsv1 "k8s.io/api/apps/v1"
 corev1 "k8s.io/api/core/v1"
 "k8s.io/apimachinery/pkg/util/intstr"

 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/agentdomain"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/binpath"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/pkg/events"
 "github.com/mediactl/clustarr/test/installtest"
)

// workloadRow is one row of spec §10.2.1's table, as both installers render it.
type workloadRow struct {
 image       string // repository, without the tag
 command     string // pkg/binpath
 replicas    int32  // 0: spec.replicas omitted, the manager's HPA owns it
 strategy    appsv1.DeploymentStrategyType
 grace       int64
 leaderElect bool
 domain      string // the agent's --domain; the autoscale label's value on autoscaled rows
 autoscaled  bool
 gomemPct    int64
}

const (
 clustarrRepo = "ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr"
 nativeRepo   = "ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native"
)

// workloadTable is spec §10.2.1. The download engines and the transcode pool and
// graft Jobs are absent: the manager renders them at runtime. The manager's grace
// is 85, not §3.5.6's 70: it drains catalogarr-segments-plan (AckWait 60 s), and
// TestGracePeriodsCoverAckWait holds every Deployment to its longest AckWait plus 25 s.
var workloadTable = map[string]workloadRow{
 "manager":        {image: clustarrRepo, command: binpath.Manager, replicas: 1, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 85, leaderElect: true, gomemPct: 80},
 "agent-catalog":  {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 145, domain: "catalog", autoscaled: true, gomemPct: 80},
 "agent-events":   {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 55, domain: "events", autoscaled: true, gomemPct: 80},
 "agent-metadata": {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, replicas: 1, strategy: appsv1.RecreateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 85, domain: "metadata", gomemPct: 80},
 "agent-import":   {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 85, domain: "import", autoscaled: true, gomemPct: 60},
 "agent-index":    {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, replicas: 1, strategy: appsv1.RecreateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 85, domain: "index", gomemPct: 80},
 "agent-caption":  {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Agent, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 115, domain: "caption", autoscaled: true, gomemPct: 60},
 "markers":        {image: nativeRepo, command: binpath.Markers, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 1825, domain: "markers", autoscaled: true, gomemPct: 50},
 "ui":             {image: clustarrRepo, command: binpath.UI, replicas: 1, strategy: appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType, grace: 30, gomemPct: 80},
}

// installers renders both default installs: the chart as release
// "clustarr" (fullname "clustarr") and kustomize's config/default.
func installers(t *testing.T) map[string]installtest.Rendered {
 t.Helper()
 return map[string]installtest.Rendered{
  "helm":      installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t)),
  "kustomize": installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default")),
 }
}

// repoOf strips the tag from an image reference.
func repoOf(image string) string {
 if i := strings.LastIndex(image, ":"); i > strings.LastIndex(image, "/") {
  return image[:i]
 }
 return image
}

func argIn(args []string, want string) bool { return slices.Contains(args, want) }

func containerEnv(c corev1.Container, name string) (string, bool) {
 for _, e := range c.Env {
  if e.Name == name {
   return e.Value, true
  }
 }
 return "", false
}

// TestInstallersRenderTheTopology holds both installers to spec §10.2.1:
// exactly its Deployments, each with its image, binary, replicas (or none,
// for the manager's HPA), strategy, grace period, lease and autoscale
// declaration. It replaces TestManagerManifestsMatchTheCLI's topology map;
// each binary's manifest_test.go parses the argv.
func TestInstallersRenderTheTopology(t *testing.T) {
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   got := installtest.Workloads(r)
   assert.Equal(t, slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(workloadTable)), slices.Sorted(maps.Keys(got)), "the Deployments of spec §10.2.1")
   for component, row := range workloadTable {
    d, ok := got[component]
    if !ok {
     continue
    }
    spec := d.Spec.Template.Spec
    require.Len(t, spec.Containers, 1, component)
    c := spec.Containers[0]
    assert.Equal(t, component, c.Name, "%s's container", component)
    assert.Equal(t, row.image, repoOf(c.Image), "%s's image", component)
    assert.Equal(t, []string{row.command}, c.Command, "%s names its binary: no image has an ENTRYPOINT", component)
    if row.replicas == 0 {
     assert.Nil(t, d.Spec.Replicas, "%s omits spec.replicas: the manager's HPA owns it", component)
    } else if assert.NotNil(t, d.Spec.Replicas, "%s sets spec.replicas", component) {
     assert.Equal(t, row.replicas, *d.Spec.Replicas, "%s's replicas", component)
    }
    strategy := d.Spec.Strategy.Type
    if strategy == "" {
     strategy = appsv1.RollingUpdateDeploymentStrategyType
    }
    assert.Equal(t, row.strategy, strategy, "%s's strategy", component)
    require.NotNil(t, spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds, component)
    assert.Equal(t, row.grace, *spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds, "%s's terminationGracePeriodSeconds", component)
    assert.Equal(t, row.leaderElect, argIn(c.Args, "--leader-elect"), "%s: only the manager passes --leader-elect", component)
    if row.command == binpath.Agent {
     assert.Contains(t, c.Args, "--domain="+row.domain, component)
    }
    if row.autoscaled {
     assert.Equal(t, row.domain, d.Labels[agentdomain.LabelDomain], "%s carries the autoscale label", component)
     require.Len(t, spec.TopologySpreadConstraints, 1, "%s spreads softly across nodes", component)
     assert.Equal(t, "kubernetes.io/hostname", spec.TopologySpreadConstraints[0].TopologyKey, component)
     assert.Equal(t, corev1.ScheduleAnyway, spec.TopologySpreadConstraints[0].WhenUnsatisfiable, component)
    } else {
     assert.NotContains(t, d.Labels, agentdomain.LabelDomain, component)
    }
   }
   if m, ok := got["manager"]; ok {
    ru := m.Spec.Strategy.RollingUpdate
    require.NotNil(t, ru, "the manager pins its rollout")
    assert.Equal(t, intstr.FromInt32(1), *ru.MaxSurge, "a new manager pod starts before the old one stops")
    assert.Equal(t, intstr.FromInt32(0), *ru.MaxUnavailable)
   }
  })
 }
}

// TestEveryAgentDeploymentRunsOneDomain (§10.3.2): every agent container
// passes exactly one --domain, each domain with consumers runs in exactly
// one Deployment named for it, and the artwork renderer is the catalog
// domain's and the artwork fetch the metadata domain's (R4; the installer
// half of the retired TestBothInstallersRunTheRendererOnTheCatalogarrDeployment).
func TestEveryAgentDeploymentRunsOneDomain(t *testing.T) {
 var want []string
 for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
  if len(d.Consumers) > 0 && d.Name != agentdomain.Markers {
   want = append(want, d.Name)
  }
 }
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   seen := map[string]int{}
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    c := d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
    if !slices.Equal(c.Command, []string{binpath.Agent}) {
     continue
    }
    var domains []string
    for _, a := range c.Args {
     if v, ok := strings.CutPrefix(a, "--domain="); ok {
      domains = append(domains, v)
     }
    }
    require.Len(t, domains, 1, "%s passes exactly one --domain (one domain per process, §3.5.1)", component)
    assert.Equal(t, "agent-"+domains[0], component)
    seen[domains[0]]++
   }
   for _, d := range want {
    assert.Equal(t, 1, seen[d], "--domain=%s runs in exactly one Deployment", d)
   }
   assert.Len(t, seen, len(want), "a Deployment runs a domain agentdomain does not list: %v", seen)
  })
 }
 catalog, ok := agentdomain.Lookup(agentdomain.Catalog)
 require.True(t, ok)
 assert.Contains(t, catalog.Consumers, events.ConsumerCatalogArtworkRender, "the renderer runs in the catalog domain")
 metadata, ok := agentdomain.Lookup(agentdomain.Metadata)
 require.True(t, ok)
 assert.Contains(t, metadata.Consumers, events.ConsumerCatalogArtworkFetch, "the fetch runs in the metadata domain")
}

// TestDataMountsMatchTheTopology: /data is mounted read-write, with UMASK
// 002, exactly by the manager (its filesystem reconcilers, §5.14),
// agent-import and agent-caption; read-only by markers; by nothing else.
func TestDataMountsMatchTheTopology(t *testing.T) {
 want := map[string]string{"manager": "rw", "agent-import": "rw", "agent-caption": "rw", "markers": "ro"}
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    spec := d.Spec.Template.Spec
    mode := ""
    for _, v := range spec.Volumes {
     if v.Name != "data" || v.PersistentVolumeClaim == nil {
      continue
     }
     assert.Equal(t, "clustarr-data", v.PersistentVolumeClaim.ClaimName, component)
     mode = "rw"
     for _, m := range spec.Containers[0].VolumeMounts {
      if m.Name == "data" {
       assert.Equal(t, "/data", m.MountPath, component)
       if m.ReadOnly {
        mode = "ro"
       }
      }
     }
    }
    assert.Equal(t, want[component], mode, "%s's /data mount", component)
    _, umask := containerEnv(spec.Containers[0], "UMASK")
    assert.Equal(t, want[component] == "rw", umask, "%s: UMASK=002 exactly where /data is written", component)
   }
  })
 }
}
```

```go
// TestGracePeriodsCoverAckWait (generalises TestWorkerGracePeriodsCoverAckWait):
// every Deployment's grace covers the longest AckWait among the durables it
// drains plus 25 s (§3.5.6), so a SIGTERMed pod finishes or releases what it
// holds before it is killed. AckWait is the handler budget, not the
// broker's BackOff[0] deadline.
func TestGracePeriodsCoverAckWait(t *testing.T) {
 top := events.Default()
 drains := map[string][]string{"manager": managerConsumers}
 for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
  if len(d.Consumers) > 0 {
   drains[deploymentOf(d)] = d.Consumers
  }
 }
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    var longest time.Duration
    for _, c := range drains[component] {
     spec, ok := top.Consumer(c)
     require.True(t, ok, "%s drains %s, which events.Default() does not declare", component, c)
     longest = max(longest, spec.AckWait)
    }
    if longest == 0 {
     continue
    }
    grace := d.Spec.Template.Spec.TerminationGracePeriodSeconds
    require.NotNil(t, grace, component)
    assert.GreaterOrEqual(t, time.Duration(*grace)*time.Second, longest+25*time.Second,
     "%s's terminationGracePeriodSeconds must cover its longest AckWait (%s) plus 25 s", component, longest)
   }
  })
 }
}

// TestAutoscaledDeploymentsAreDeclared (§10.2.2): a Deployment carries the
// autoscale label iff agentdomain marks its domain autoscaled, such a
// Deployment omits spec.replicas (an explicit 0 would never be woken) and
// every other sets it, CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS parses and names only that
// domain's consumers, and autoscaling.enabled=false falls back to fixed
// replicas and tells the manager.
func TestAutoscaledDeploymentsAreDeclared(t *testing.T) {
 autoscaled := map[string]agentdomain.Domain{}
 for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
  if d.Autoscaled {
   autoscaled[deploymentOf(d)] = d
  }
 }
 require.NotEmpty(t, autoscaled)
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    dom, want := autoscaled[component]
    label, has := d.Labels[agentdomain.LabelDomain]
    assert.Equal(t, want, has, "%s: the autoscale label iff its domain is autoscaled", component)
    if want {
     assert.Equal(t, dom.Name, label, component)
     assert.Nil(t, d.Spec.Replicas, "%s omits spec.replicas", component)
    } else {
     assert.NotNil(t, d.Spec.Replicas, "%s sets spec.replicas", component)
    }
    assertConsumerSlots(t, component, d, dom)
   }
  })
 }
 var sets []string
 for _, d := range agentdomain.Domains() {
  if !d.Autoscaled || len(d.Consumers) == 0 {
   continue
  }
  key := "agents." + d.Name
  if d.Name == agentdomain.Markers {
   key = "markers"
  }
  sets = append(sets, "--set", key+".consumerSlots."+d.Consumers[0]+"=3")
 }
 for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, sets...))) {
  dom, ok := autoscaled[component]
  if !ok {
   continue
  }
  v, set := containerEnv(d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0], events.SlotsEnv)
  require.True(t, set, "%s renders no %s from consumerSlots", component, events.SlotsEnv)
  assert.Equal(t, dom.Consumers[0]+"=3", v, component)
  assertConsumerSlots(t, component, d, dom)
 }
 off := installtest.Workloads(installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, "--set", "autoscaling.enabled=false")))
 for component, d := range off {
  assert.NotContains(t, d.Labels, agentdomain.LabelDomain, "%s with autoscaling off", component)
  assert.NotNil(t, d.Spec.Replicas, "%s sets replicas with autoscaling off", component)
 }
 assert.Contains(t, off["manager"].Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0].Args, "--autoscale=false")
}

func assertConsumerSlots(t *testing.T, component string, d appsv1.Deployment, dom agentdomain.Domain) {
 t.Helper()
 v, ok := containerEnv(d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0], events.SlotsEnv)
 if !ok {
  return
 }
 slots, err := events.ParseSlotOverrides(v)
 require.NoError(t, err, "%s: %s=%q", component, events.SlotsEnv, v)
 for c := range slots {
  assert.Contains(t, dom.Consumers, c, "%s: %s names %s, not a consumer of domain %q", component, events.SlotsEnv, c, dom.Name)
 }
}
```

```go
// TestNativeImageIsWhatTheManagerStampsOntoPoolsAndEngines (ADR-0015 kept):
// the chart's image.native and config/manager's CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE are
// the image Dockerfile.native builds, every pool (nvidia's included) and
// engine runs it, no Dockerfile builds a CUDA target and none sets
// NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES.
func TestNativeImageIsWhatTheManagerStampsOntoPoolsAndEngines(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 var values struct {
  Image map[string]any `json:"image"`
 }
 require.NoError(t, yaml.Unmarshal(readRepoFile(t, root, "charts/clustarr/values.yaml"), &values))
 native, ok := values.Image["native"].(map[string]any)
 require.True(t, ok, "values.yaml has no image.native")
 assert.Equal(t, "mediactl/clustarr/native", native["repository"])
 for _, k := range []string{"controller", "media", "transcoder", "transcoderCuda"} {
  assert.NotContains(t, values.Image, k, "image.%s is retired", k)
 }
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  c := installtest.Workloads(r)["manager"].Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
  img, ok := containerEnv(c, "CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE")
  require.True(t, ok, "%s: the manager stamps no native image", name)
  assert.Equal(t, nativeRepo, repoOf(img), name)
  for _, gone := range []string{"CLUSTARR_ENGINE_IMAGE", "CLUSTARR_WORKER_IMAGE", "CLUSTARR_WORKER_IMAGE_CUDA"} {
   _, has := containerEnv(c, gone)
   assert.False(t, has, "%s: %s is retired (--native-image)", name, gone)
  }
 }
 c := installtest.Container(t, installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, "--set", "image.native.tag=t1")), "manager")
 img, _ := containerEnv(c, "CLUSTARR_NATIVE_IMAGE")
 assert.Equal(t, "ghcr.io/mediactl/clustarr/native:t1", img, "the manager stamps image.native")

 dockerfiles, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "images", "Dockerfile*"))
 require.NoError(t, err)
 cuda := regexp.MustCompile(`(?im)^FROM\s+\S+\s+AS\s+(\S*cuda\S*)\s*$`)
 for _, f := range dockerfiles {
  b, err := os.ReadFile(f)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  if m := cuda.FindSubmatch(b); m != nil {
   t.Errorf("%s builds a %s target: there is no CUDA image (ADR 0015)", filepath.Base(f), m[1])
  }
  if regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^[^#]*NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES`).Match(b) {
   t.Errorf("%s sets NVIDIA_VISIBLE_DEVICES: the device plugin names a pod's GPU", filepath.Base(f))
  }
 }
 _, err = os.Stat(filepath.Join(root, "images", "Dockerfile.media-cuda"))
 assert.True(t, os.IsNotExist(err), "Dockerfile.media-cuda stays gone")
}

// shippedBinaries is what each image's Dockerfile copies into /usr/bin, by repository.
func shippedBinaries(t *testing.T, root string) map[string][]string {
 t.Helper()
 out := map[string][]string{}
 for repo, file := range map[string]string{clustarrRepo: "images/Dockerfile.clustarr", nativeRepo: "images/Dockerfile.native"} {
  m := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^COPY --from=build ((?:/out/\w+ )+)/usr/bin/$`).FindStringSubmatch(string(readRepoFile(t, root, file)))
  require.NotNil(t, m, "%s copies no binary into /usr/bin", file)
  for _, f := range strings.Fields(m[1]) {
   out[repo] = append(out[repo], "/usr/bin/"+strings.TrimPrefix(f, "/out/"))
  }
 }
 return out
}

// TestGOMEMLIMITIsItsShareOfTheLimit (§10.2.1, OD42): GOMEMLIMIT is
// round(limit x share) -- 60% for agent-import and agent-caption, 50% for
// markers, 80% elsewhere -- in both installers, and their defaults agree.
func TestGOMEMLIMITIsItsShareOfTheLimit(t *testing.T) {
 values := map[string]map[string]string{}
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  values[name] = map[string]string{}
  for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
   row, ok := workloadTable[component]
   require.True(t, ok, component)
   c := d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
   limit, ok := c.Resources.Limits[corev1.ResourceMemory]
   require.True(t, ok, "%s %s sets no memory limit", name, component)
   got, ok := containerEnv(c, "GOMEMLIMIT")
   require.True(t, ok, "%s %s sets no GOMEMLIMIT", name, component)
   assert.Equal(t, strconv.FormatInt((limit.Value()*row.gomemPct+50)/100, 10), got,
    "%s %s: GOMEMLIMIT is %d%% of %s", name, component, row.gomemPct, limit.String())
   values[name][component] = got
  }
 }
 assert.Equal(t, values["helm"], values["kustomize"], "the chart's default limits and config/manager's")
}
```

```go
// TestEveryClustarrContainerCarriesNATSURL: every binary dials NATS, so
// every container whose command is a pkg/binpath binary carries NATS_URL --
// without it the binary dials a default Service no installer creates, and
// nats.go's retry hides the failure -- and one installer names one endpoint.
func TestEveryClustarrContainerCarriesNATSURL(t *testing.T) {
 binaries := map[string]bool{binpath.Manager: true, binpath.UI: true, binpath.Agent: true, binpath.Markers: true, binpath.Transcode: true}
 for name, r := range installers(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   urls := map[string]string{}
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    c := d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
    if len(c.Command) != 1 || !binaries[c.Command[0]] {
     continue
    }
    url, ok := containerEnv(c, "NATS_URL")
    require.True(t, ok && url != "", "%s runs %s and sets no NATS_URL", component, c.Command[0])
    urls[component] = url
   }
   require.Len(t, urls, len(workloadTable), "every Deployment of §10.2.1 runs a pkg/binpath binary")
   for component, url := range urls {
    assert.Equal(t, urls["manager"], url, "%s dials a different NATS from the manager", component)
   }
  })
 }
}
```

```go
// TestMarkersHasNoCredentials: markers reads /data and talks NATS only, so
// neither its ServiceAccount nor its pod mounts a token and nothing binds
// the account; it runs /usr/bin/markers with /data read-only.
func TestMarkersHasNoCredentials(t *testing.T) {
 for name, out := range map[string][]byte{
  "helm":      installtest.RenderChart(t),
  "kustomize": installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default"),
 } {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   objs := installtest.Objects(t, out)
   var dep, sa *unstructured.Unstructured
   for _, o := range objs {
    if o.GetKind() == "Deployment" && strings.HasSuffix(o.GetName(), "markers") {
     dep = o
    }
   }
   require.NotNil(t, dep, "no markers Deployment")
   spec, _, _ := unstructured.NestedMap(dep.Object, "spec", "template", "spec")
   assert.Equal(t, false, spec["automountServiceAccountToken"], "the pod mounts no token")
   account, _ := spec["serviceAccountName"].(string)
   require.NotEmpty(t, account)
   for _, o := range objs {
    switch o.GetKind() {
    case "ServiceAccount":
     if o.GetName() == account {
      sa = o
     }
    case "RoleBinding", "ClusterRoleBinding":
     subjects, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(o.Object, "subjects")
     for _, s := range subjects {
      assert.NotEqual(t, account, s.(map[string]any)["name"], "%s %s binds markers' account", o.GetKind(), o.GetName())
     }
    }
   }
   require.NotNil(t, sa, "the markers ServiceAccount is rendered")
   automount, found, _ := unstructured.NestedBool(sa.Object, "automountServiceAccountToken")
   assert.True(t, found && !automount, "the markers ServiceAccount mounts no token")
   containers, _, _ := unstructured.NestedSlice(spec, "containers")
   require.Len(t, containers, 1)
   c := containers[0].(map[string]any)
   assert.Equal(t, []any{binpath.Markers}, c["command"])
   env := map[string]bool{}
   for _, e := range c["env"].([]any) {
    env[e.(map[string]any)["name"].(string)] = true
   }
   assert.True(t, env["NATS_URL"] && env["POD_NAME"], "NATS_URL and POD_NAME")
   for _, m := range c["volumeMounts"].([]any) {
    if mm := m.(map[string]any); mm["mountPath"] == "/data" {
     assert.Equal(t, true, mm["readOnly"], "/data is read-only")
    }
   }
  })
 }
}
```

```go
// identities is spec §10.2.4's set: one ServiceAccount, one role each.
var identities = []string{"manager", "agent-catalog", "agent-events", "agent-metadata", "agent-import",
 "agent-index", "agent-caption", "grabarr-engine", "ui"}

// TestEachServiceAccountHoldsExactlyItsOwnRole: every identity a pod runs as
// (each Deployment's account, plus the engine pods' grabarr-engine) is bound
// to exactly one ClusterRole whose grants are exactly its own generated
// role (or ui's hand-written one). The component is the identity: no
// Deployment borrows another's role any more.
func TestEachServiceAccountHoldsExactlyItsOwnRole(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 want := map[string][]string{"ui": installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, root, "ui_role.yaml").Rules))}
 for _, r := range installtest.RBACRoles(t, root) {
  want[r.Name] = installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(installtest.ReadRole(t, root, r.File()).Rules))
 }
 assert.ElementsMatch(t, identities, slices.Collect(maps.Keys(want)), "RBAC_ROLES plus ui is spec §10.2.4's identities")
 helm := installtest.FindTool(t, "helm")
 for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
  out    []byte
  prefix string
 }{
  "helm template clustarr":   {installtest.RenderChart(t), "clustarr-"},
  "helm template media":      {installtest.Run(t, root, helm, "template", "media", "charts/clustarr"), "media-clustarr-"},
  "kustomize config/default": {installtest.BuildKustomize(t, "config/default"), ""},
 } {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   r := installtest.DecodeRendered(t, tc.out)
   accounts := map[string]string{tc.prefix + "grabarr-engine": "grabarr-engine"}
   for component, d := range installtest.Workloads(r) {
    if component == "markers" {
     continue // no token, nothing bound: TestMarkersHasNoCredentials
    }
    accounts[d.Spec.Template.Spec.ServiceAccountName] = component
   }
   assert.Equal(t, slices.Sorted(slices.Values(identities)), slices.Sorted(maps.Values(accounts)), "the identities %s runs", name)
   for account, identity := range accounts {
    require.True(t, r.ServiceAccounts[account], "%s runs as ServiceAccount %q, which %s does not create", identity, account, name)
    var boundTo []string
    for _, b := range r.Bindings {
     for _, s := range b.Subjects {
      if s.Kind == rbacv1.ServiceAccountKind && s.Name == account {
       boundTo = append(boundTo, b.RoleRef.Name)
      }
     }
    }
    require.Len(t, boundTo, 1, "ServiceAccount %q is bound to %v, not exactly its own role", account, boundTo)
    role, ok := r.Roles[boundTo[0]]
    require.True(t, ok, "ClusterRole %q is not rendered by %s", boundTo[0], name)
    assert.Equal(t, want[identity], installtest.SortedGrants(installtest.GrantsOf(role.Rules)),
     "ServiceAccount %q holds ClusterRole %q, which is not %s's own", account, boundTo[0], identity)
   }
  })
 }
}

// TestCredentialLessWorkloadsHoldNoToken: the transcode pool and graft

 helm := installtest.FindTool(t, "helm")
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 for name, out := range map[string][]byte{

 } {

   for _, gone := range []string{"squasharr-worker", "segmentarr-worker", "transcode"} {
    assert.NotContains(t, n, gone, "%s renders %s", name, n)
   }
  }
 }
```

```go
func TestCardigannValuesReachTheManager(t *testing.T) {
 const dir = "/etc/clustarr/cardigann"
 for name, tc := range map[string]struct {
  args   []string
  env    map[string]string
  volume *corev1.VolumeSource
  mount  *corev1.VolumeMount
 }{
  "defaults":    {env: map[string]string{}},
  "bundled off": {args: []string{"--set", "manager.cardigann.bundled=false"}, env: map[string]string{"CLUSTARR_CARDIGANN_BUNDLED": "false"}},
  "configMap": {
   args:   []string{"--set", "manager.cardigann.definitions.configMap=cardigann-defs"},
   env:    map[string]string{"CLUSTARR_CARDIGANN_DEFINITIONS_DIR": dir},
   volume: &corev1.VolumeSource{ConfigMap: &corev1.ConfigMapVolumeSource{LocalObjectReference: corev1.LocalObjectReference{Name: "cardigann-defs"}}},
   mount:  &corev1.VolumeMount{Name: "cardigann", MountPath: dir, ReadOnly: true},
  },
  "existingClaim with subPath": {
   args:   []string{"--set", "manager.cardigann.definitions.existingClaim=cardigann-pvc", "--set", "manager.cardigann.definitions.subPath=v11"},
   env:    map[string]string{"CLUSTARR_CARDIGANN_DEFINITIONS_DIR": dir},
   volume: &corev1.VolumeSource{PersistentVolumeClaim: &corev1.PersistentVolumeClaimVolumeSource{ClaimName: "cardigann-pvc", ReadOnly: true}},
   mount:  &corev1.VolumeMount{Name: "cardigann", MountPath: dir, ReadOnly: true, SubPath: "v11"},
  },
 } {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   d := installtest.Workloads(installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, tc.args...)))["manager"]
   c := d.Spec.Template.Spec.Containers[0]
   got := map[string]string{}
   for _, e := range c.Env {
    if strings.HasPrefix(e.Name, "CLUSTARR_CARDIGANN_") {
     got[e.Name] = e.Value
    }
   }
   require.Equal(t, tc.env, got, "the cardigann env vars on the manager")
   var vol *corev1.Volume
   for i := range d.Spec.Template.Spec.Volumes {
    if d.Spec.Template.Spec.Volumes[i].Name == "cardigann" {
     vol = &d.Spec.Template.Spec.Volumes[i]
    }
   }
   var mount *corev1.VolumeMount
   for i := range c.VolumeMounts {
    if c.VolumeMounts[i].Name == "cardigann" {
     mount = &c.VolumeMounts[i]
    }
   }
   if tc.volume == nil {
    require.Nil(t, vol)
    require.Nil(t, mount)
    return
   }
   require.NotNil(t, vol)
   require.Equal(t, *tc.volume, vol.VolumeSource)
   require.NotNil(t, mount)
   require.Equal(t, *tc.mount, *mount)
  })
 }
 off := installtest.DecodeRendered(t, installtest.RenderChart(t, "--set", "manager.cardigann.bundled=false"))
 _, onAgent := containerEnv(installtest.Container(t, off, "agent-index"), "CLUSTARR_CARDIGANN_BUNDLED")
 assert.False(t, onAgent, "the index agent loads no Cardigann bundle (R8, R9)")
}

// TestChartRefusesTwoCardigannDefinitionSources: the manager loads one
// definitions directory, so a configMap and an existingClaim together fail
// the render instead of mounting one and ignoring the other.
func TestChartRefusesTwoCardigannDefinitionSources(t *testing.T) {
 cmd := exec.Command(installtest.FindTool(t, "helm"), "template", "clustarr", "charts/clustarr",
  "--set", "manager.cardigann.definitions.configMap=a",
  "--set", "manager.cardigann.definitions.existingClaim=b")
 cmd.Dir = installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 var stderr bytes.Buffer
 cmd.Stderr = &stderr
 require.Error(t, cmd.Run(), "a render with both definition sources must fail")
 require.Contains(t, stderr.String(), "manager.cardigann.definitions: set configMap or existingClaim, not both")
}
```

```go
package main

import (
```
