## Wave 6b: test media without the CLI (W6.18 to W6.24)

**Source:** main's `docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-06-unify-media-upgrade-guide.md` (commits `4377f49f`, `013b0eb8`): **U2**, the owner's decision of 2026-10-06 that no test may run the `ffmpeg` or `ffprobe` CLI, with fixture clips made on ffgo or committed, and every R2 parity check reading goldens recorded once from the exec implementation before it is deleted. Spec sections the decision amends: §4.5.6 (the guard), §6.7 (probe parity), §7.2.6/§7.2.10 (decode parity), §7.3.2 (extraction parity), §10.1.6-§10.1.8 (assets, CI, e2e fixtures).

**Order.** After W6.17 green and before W7.1: W6.18, then W6.19-W6.22 in any order (each owns its directories), then W6.23 (it needs every exec implementation still present: Wave 7 deletes the first), then W6.24.

**What stays until Wave 10.** `make native-assets` keeps the `ffmpeg` and `ffprobe` CLIs, because the exec implementations Waves 7-8 delete still run them (and W6.23's recorder calls those implementations, never the CLIs itself). W10.9 adds the guard, W10.10 takes the CLIs out of the assets and CI, W10.11 rebuilds the e2e fixtures without them.

**The conversion table** (W6.19-W6.22, and every U2 amendment later). `internal/testmedia` models the ffmpeg command line, so a conversion is mechanical and keeps every assertion:

| ffmpeg argument | `testmedia` |
| --- | --- |
| `-f lavfi -i <graph>` (video: `testsrc2=…`, `color=…`, a chain such as `…,setfield=tff`) | `Video{Source: "<graph>"}` |
| `-f lavfi -i <graph>` (audio: `sine=…`, `anullsrc=…`, `…,aformat=channel_layouts=5.1(side)`) | `Audio{Source: "<graph>"}` |
| `-i some.wav` that the test wrote in Go | `Audio{Samples: &testmedia.Samples{Rate: r, Mono: x}}` |
| `-c:v X`, `-c:a X`, `-c:s srt\|ass` | `Video.Encoder`, `Audio.Encoder`, `Subtitle.Codec` (`subrip`, `ass`) |
| `-pix_fmt P`, `-sample_fmt F`, `-ar R`, `-ac N`, `-b:a 320k` | `Video.PixFmt`, `Audio.SampleFmt`, `Audio.SampleRate`, `Audio.Layout`, `Audio.BitrateKbps` |
| `-bf`, `-g`, `-flags`, `-x264-params`, `-x265-params`, `-strict`, `-center_mixlev`, `-bits_per_raw_sample`, `-crf`, `-preset` | `Options` of that stream (`"bf": "3"`, `"x265-params": "…"`) |
| `-color_primaries`, `-color_trc`, `-colorspace`, `-color_range` | `Video.Color` |
| x265 `master-display`/`max-cll`, or HDR10 side data | `Video.HDR10` |
| `-frames:v N`, `-shortest`, `-t D` | `Video.Frames`, `Spec.Shortest`, `Spec.Duration` |
| `-itsoffset S` before an input | that stream's `Offset` |
| `-output_ts_offset S` | `Spec.StartOffset` |
| `-metadata k=v`, `-metadata:s:X:i k=v`, `-disposition:X:i d` | `Spec.Tags`, `Stream.Metadata`, `Stream.Disposition` |
| a subtitle input file (`-i x.srt`) | `Subtitle{Events: testmedia.ParseSRT(t, body)}` |
| `-attach f -metadata:s:t mimetype=m` | `Spec.Attachments` |
| an `;FFMETADATA1` chapters input | `Spec.Chapters` (with the file's `TIMEBASE`) |
| `-f <muxer>`, `-movflags …` | `Spec.Format`, `Spec.MuxerOptions` |
| cutting a file short (`head -c`, `truncate`) | `testmedia.Truncate(t, path, n)` |
| `ffprobe -show_format/-show_streams/-show_chapters … -of json` used to **inspect** a test's output | `testmedia.Inspect(t, path)` |
| `ffprobe -show_entries stream=profile,pix_fmt,color_*,sample_aspect_ratio,codec_tag_string,channel_layout,start_time`, `stream_side_data=side_data_type` | `Inspect`'s `StreamInfo.{Profile, PixFmt, Color, SampleAspectRatio, CodecTag, Layout, StartTime, SideData}` |
| `ffprobe -count_frames … nb_read_frames`, `-show_entries frame=pts`, `frame_side_data=side_data_type` | `len(testmedia.Frames(t, path, i))`, `FrameInfo.PTS`, `FrameInfo.SideData` |
| `ffprobe -show_entries packet=stream_index,pts_time,pos` | `testmedia.Packets(t, path)` |
| `ffmpeg -i x -af astats -f null -` (per-channel RMS) | `testmedia.ChannelRMS(t, path, i)` |
| `-filter_complex` over inputs the test wrote in Go (`adelay=ms`, `volume=v`, `amix`) | the samples computed in Go (prepend `ms` of zeros, scale, sum), then `Audio{Samples: …}` |
| `-i existing -map 0 -c copy -metadata[:s:X:i] k=v [-t D] out` (retag or cut a file) | `testmedia.Remux(t, existing, name, testmedia.Retag{Tags, StreamMetadata, Until})` |
| a lavfi stream muxed with streams `-c copy`'d from another test clip | one `Spec` that carries every stream itself |
| `-b:v R`, `-minrate`, `-maxrate`, `-bufsize` | the video stream's `Options` (`"b": R`, …) |
| `-vtag T` / `-tag:v T` | dropped: no converted assertion reads the codec tag (`fileimport/probe_envtest_test.go`'s `[XviD]` comes from `pkg/naming` mapping codec `mpeg4` to XviD); `StreamInfo.CodecTag` reads one back where a test asserts it |
| `exec.LookPath("ffmpeg")` and a "not FFmpeg 9" check that only gate clip making | `testmedia.Require(t)` |

A Dolby Vision RPU cannot be synthesised on ffgo either: those tests keep their named skip.

### Task W6.18: `internal/testmedia`, clips on ffgo

**Spec:** upgrade guide U2.1
**Files:**

- Create: `internal/testmedia/doc.go`, `internal/testmedia/spec.go`, `internal/testmedia/write.go`, `internal/testmedia/inspect.go`, `internal/testmedia/require.go`
- Test: `internal/testmedia/testmedia_test.go`, `internal/testmedia/deps_test.go`

**Interfaces:**

- Consumes: W0.29 (`Muxer.AddSubtitleStream`, `WriteSubtitle`), W0.30 (`AudioEncoderConfig2.Options`; lavfi sources, HDR10 side data, chapters and tags proven), ffgo's `NewDecoderWithOptions`, `NewVideoStreamEncoder`, `NewAudioEncoder`, `NewMuxer`, `(*Muxer).AddEncoderStream`, `AddAttachment`, `SetChapters`, `SetMetadata`, `avdevice.RegisterAll`.
- Produces (package `github.com/mediactl/clustarr/internal/testmedia`, imported only by tests and by `hack/record-goldens` and `test/fixtures/mkclips`):
  - `func Require(t testing.TB)`: skips unless FFmpeg 9's libraries and a versioned shim load; with `CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1` it fails instead.
  - `type Spec struct{ Format string; MuxerOptions map[string]string; Duration time.Duration; Shortest bool; StartOffset time.Duration; Video []Video; Audio []Audio; Subtitles []Subtitle; Attachments []Attachment; Chapters []Chapter; Tags map[string]string }`
  - `type Video struct{ Source, Encoder, PixFmt string; Options map[string]string; Color Color; HDR10 *HDR10; Frames int; Stream Stream }`
  - `type Audio struct{ Source string; Samples *Samples; Encoder, SampleFmt, Layout string; SampleRate, BitrateKbps int; Options map[string]string; Offset time.Duration; Stream Stream }`
  - `type Samples struct{ Rate int; Mono []float64 }`, `type Stream struct{ Language, Title string; Disposition []string; Metadata map[string]string }`
  - `type Subtitle struct{ Codec, Header string; Events []Event; Stream Stream }`, `type Event struct{ Start, End time.Duration; Text string }`
  - `type Attachment struct{ Name, MIMEType string; Data []byte }`, `type Chapter struct{ Start, End int64; TimeBase [2]int; Title string }`
  - `type Color struct{ Primaries, Transfer, Matrix, Range string }`, `type HDR10 struct{ MasteringDisplay [10]uint32; MaxCLL, MaxFALL uint16 }` (display primaries G, B, R, white point in 0.00002 units, then max and min luminance in 0.0001 cd/m², the x265 `master-display` order)
  - `func Write(path string, s Spec) error`, `func Make(t testing.TB, name string, s Spec) string` (Require, then Write into `t.TempDir()/name`), `func Truncate(t testing.TB, path string, keep int64) string`, `func ParseSRT(t testing.TB, body string) []Event`
  - `type Info struct{ Format string; Duration time.Duration; Tags map[string]string; Streams []StreamInfo; Chapters []Chapter }`, `type StreamInfo struct{ Index int; Type, Codec, Profile, PixFmt, Layout, CodecTag, SampleAspectRatio, Language, Title string; Disposition []string; Channels, SampleRate, Width, Height int; StartTime time.Duration; Color Color; SideData []string; Tags map[string]string }` (`Profile` as ffprobe prints it, W0.14; `Color` from F11d's `StreamInfo.Color`; `StartTime` F11e; `CodecTag` the fourcc from `avcodec.GetCodecParTag`, e.g. `hvc1`; `SampleAspectRatio` as `32:27`; `SideData` the stream side-data names ffprobe prints: `Mastering display metadata`, `Content light level metadata`, `DOVI configuration record`), `func Inspect(t testing.TB, path string) Info`
  - `type FrameInfo struct{ PTS int64; SideData []string }`, `func Frames(t testing.TB, path string, stream int) []FrameInfo`: every decoded frame of that stream, in order (ffprobe's `-count_frames` `nb_read_frames`, `frame=pts` and `frame_side_data`)
  - `type PacketInfo struct{ Stream int; PTS time.Duration; Pos int64 }`, `func Packets(t testing.TB, path string) []PacketInfo`: every packet in demux order (ffprobe's `packet=stream_index,pts_time,pos`)
  - `func ChannelRMS(t testing.TB, path string, stream int) []float64`: each channel's RMS level in dB over the whole stream, `-Inf` for silence, in channel order (`ffmpeg -af astats`'s `RMS level dB` per `Channel: n`)
  - `type Retag struct{ Tags map[string]string; StreamMetadata map[int]map[string]string; Until time.Duration }`, `func RemuxFile(src, dst string, r Retag) error`, `func Remux(t testing.TB, src, name string, r Retag) string`: every stream of `src` stream-copied into `dst` (`Remux`: `t.TempDir()/name`), its format tags and each stream's metadata merged with `r`'s, packets past a non-zero `Until` dropped (`ffmpeg -i src -map 0 -c copy -metadata … [-t D]`); `src` may be `pipe:0`

```go
// everything is helpers_test.go's everythingClip, as a Spec: H.264 video,
// English AC-3 5.1 (default), French AAC stereo "Commentary" (comment),
// English SubRip (forced), a font, two chapters, container title "Clip".
func everything(seconds int) testmedia.Spec {
 half := int64(seconds) * 500
 return testmedia.Spec{
  Duration: time.Duration(seconds) * time.Second, Shortest: true, Tags: map[string]string{"title": "Clip", "CLUSTARR_PROFILE": "p@h"},
  Video: []testmedia.Video{{Source: "testsrc2=size=160x90:rate=24", Encoder: "libx264", Options: map[string]string{"preset": "ultrafast"}}},
  Audio: []testmedia.Audio{
   {Source: "sine=frequency=440:sample_rate=48000", Encoder: "ac3", Layout: "5.1(side)", Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "eng", Disposition: []string{"default"}}},
   {Source: "sine=frequency=880:sample_rate=48000", Encoder: "aac", Layout: "stereo", Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "fre", Title: "Commentary", Disposition: []string{"comment"}}},
  },
  Subtitles:   []testmedia.Subtitle{{Codec: "subrip", Events: []testmedia.Event{{Start: 500 * time.Millisecond, End: 1500 * time.Millisecond, Text: "Hello"}}, Stream: testmedia.Stream{Language: "eng", Disposition: []string{"forced"}}}},
  Attachments: []testmedia.Attachment{{Name: "font.ttf", MIMEType: "application/x-truetype-font", Data: []byte("not really a font")}},
  Chapters:    []testmedia.Chapter{{Start: 0, End: half, TimeBase: [2]int{1, 1000}, Title: "One"}, {Start: half, End: 2 * half, TimeBase: [2]int{1, 1000}, Title: "Two"}},
 }
}

func TestAClipCarriesWhatItsSpecSays(t *testing.T) {
 path := testmedia.Make(t, "everything.mkv", everything(2))
 info := testmedia.Inspect(t, path)
 assert.Equal(t, "matroska,webm", info.Format)
 assert.InDelta(t, 2.0, info.Duration.Seconds(), 0.1)
 assert.Equal(t, "Clip", info.Tags["title"])
 assert.Equal(t, "p@h", info.Tags["CLUSTARR_PROFILE"])
 require.Len(t, info.Streams, 5)
 assert.Equal(t, "h264", info.Streams[0].Codec)
 assert.Equal(t, []any{"ac3", "eng", 6, []string{"default"}}, []any{info.Streams[1].Codec, info.Streams[1].Language, info.Streams[1].Channels, info.Streams[1].Disposition})
 assert.Equal(t, []any{"aac", "fre", "Commentary", 2}, []any{info.Streams[2].Codec, info.Streams[2].Language, info.Streams[2].Title, info.Streams[2].Channels})
 assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[2].Disposition, "comment")
 assert.Equal(t, []any{"subtitle", "subrip", "eng"}, []any{info.Streams[3].Type, info.Streams[3].Codec, info.Streams[3].Language})
 assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[3].Disposition, "forced")
 assert.Equal(t, "attachment", info.Streams[4].Type)
 require.Len(t, info.Chapters, 2)
 assert.Equal(t, "Two", info.Chapters[1].Title)
}

func TestHDR10AndTenBitHEVC(t *testing.T) {
 path := testmedia.Make(t, "hdr10.mkv", testmedia.Spec{Duration: time.Second, Video: []testmedia.Video{{
  Source: "testsrc2=size=160x90:rate=24", Encoder: "libx265", PixFmt: "yuv420p10le",
  Options: map[string]string{"x265-params": "log-level=error"},
  HDR10:   &testmedia.HDR10{MasteringDisplay: [10]uint32{13250, 34500, 7500, 3000, 34000, 16000, 15635, 16450, 10000000, 50}, MaxCLL: 1000, MaxFALL: 400},
 }}})
 info := testmedia.Inspect(t, path)
 require.Len(t, info.Streams, 1)
 assert.Equal(t, "hevc", info.Streams[0].Codec)
 assert.Equal(t, "smpte2084", info.Streams[0].Color.Transfer, "HDR10 implies BT.2020/PQ unless Color says otherwise")
 assert.Contains(t, info.Streams[0].SideData, "Mastering display metadata")
 assert.Contains(t, testmedia.Frames(t, path, 0)[0].SideData, "Mastering display metadata")
}

// The inspectors the converted tests assert through, in place of ffprobe's
// stream, frame and packet entries, ffmpeg's astats, and `-c copy` retags.
func TestTheInspectorsReadWhatTheConvertedTestsAssert(t *testing.T) {
 path := testmedia.Make(t, "everything.mkv", everything(2))
 info := testmedia.Inspect(t, path)
 assert.NotEmpty(t, info.Streams[0].Profile)
 assert.NotEmpty(t, info.Streams[0].PixFmt)
 assert.Equal(t, "5.1(side)", info.Streams[1].Layout)
 frames := testmedia.Frames(t, path, 0)
 require.Len(t, frames, 48, "2 s at 24 fps")
 for i := 1; i < len(frames); i++ {
  assert.Greater(t, frames[i].PTS, frames[i-1].PTS)
 }
 per := map[int]int{}
 for _, p := range testmedia.Packets(t, path) {
  per[p.Stream]++
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 48, per[0])
 assert.NotZero(t, per[1])
 assert.Len(t, testmedia.ChannelRMS(t, path, 1), 6)
 re := testmedia.Remux(t, path, "retag.mkv", testmedia.Retag{Tags: map[string]string{"CLUSTARR_PROFILE": "q@r"}, StreamMetadata: map[int]map[string]string{2: {"language": "ger"}}})
 got := testmedia.Inspect(t, re)
 assert.Equal(t, "q@r", got.Tags["CLUSTARR_PROFILE"])
 assert.Equal(t, "Clip", got.Tags["title"], "a retag keeps the tags it does not name")
 assert.Equal(t, "ger", got.Streams[2].Language)
 assert.Len(t, got.Streams, len(info.Streams))
}

func TestTruncateAndTheSameSpecWritesTheSameBytes(t *testing.T) {
 a := testmedia.Make(t, "a.mkv", everything(1))
 b := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "b.mkv")
 require.NoError(t, testmedia.Write(b, everything(1)))
 ba, err := os.ReadFile(a)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 bb, err := os.ReadFile(b)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.Equal(t, sha256.Sum256(ba), sha256.Sum256(bb), "bit-exact: the goldens' clips are reproducible on one FFmpeg build")
 cut := testmedia.Truncate(t, a, 4096)
 st, err := os.Stat(cut)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.Equal(t, int64(4096), st.Size())
}
```

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `require.go`:

```go
// Require skips t unless FFmpeg 9's libraries and a versioned libffshim
// load. With CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1 (CI) a missing library fails t, so a
// test that needs ffgo can never pass by skipping (upgrade guide U2.1).
func Require(t testing.TB) {
 t.Helper()
 miss := func(format string, args ...any) {
  if os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE") == "1" {
   t.Fatalf("testmedia: "+format, args...)
  }
  t.Skipf("testmedia: "+format, args...)
 }
 if err := ffgo.Init(); err != nil {
  miss("no FFmpeg libraries: %v", err)
 }
 if _, avc, _ := ffgo.Version(); avc>>16 != 63 {
  miss("libavcodec %d is not FFmpeg 9's 63", avc>>16)
 }
 if ffgo.ShimAPIVersion() < 1 {
  miss("libffshim has no API version (want the clustarr/unify-media fork's shim, FFSHIM_API_VERSION >= 1)")
 }
 if err := avdevice.RegisterAll(); err != nil { // lavfi sources
  miss("libavdevice: %v", err)
 }
}
```

  `write.go`, the core (one function per concern; the shapes are the contract):

```go
// Write makes the clip s describes at path, as the equivalent ffmpeg
// command would: every source is a lavfi graph read through ffgo's
// demuxer (Samples go through a WAV and amovie), every stream is encoded
// with its encoder and Options, and packets are interleaved by
// presentation time. Muxer and encoders run bit-exact (fflags and flags
// +bitexact, one thread each), so one FFmpeg build writes the same bytes.
func Write(path string, s Spec) error {
 // A lavfi source opens only after avdevice.RegisterAll (W0.30), which
 // Require does for tests; hack/record-goldens and test/fixtures/mkclips
 // call Write without Require.
 if err := registerDevices(); err != nil {
  return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: libavdevice: %w", err)
 }
 m, err := ffgo.NewMuxer(path, s.format(path))
 if err != nil {
  return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: %w", err)
 }
 defer m.Close()
 var srcs []*source // one per Video and Audio: a lavfi decoder, an encoder and its muxer stream
 for i := range s.Video {
  src, err := openVideo(m, s.Video[i], s.Duration)
  if err != nil {
   return err
  }
  srcs = append(srcs, src)
 }
 for i := range s.Audio {
  src, err := openAudio(m, s.Audio[i], s.Duration)
  if err != nil {
   return err
  }
  srcs = append(srcs, src)
 }
 subs := make([]*ffgo.MuxerStream, len(s.Subtitles))
 for i, sub := range s.Subtitles {
  if subs[i], err = m.AddSubtitleStream(&ffgo.SubtitleStreamConfig{Codec: sub.codec(), Header: []byte(sub.Header), Options: sub.Stream.options()}); err != nil {
   return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: subtitle %d: %w", i, err)
  }
 }
 for _, a := range s.Attachments {
  if err := m.AddAttachment(ffgo.Attachment{Filename: a.Name, MimeType: a.MIMEType, Data: a.Data}); err != nil {
   return fmt.Errorf("testmedia: attachment %s: %w", a.Name, err)
  }
 }
 if err := m.SetChapters(s.chapters()); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 if err := m.SetMetadata(ffgo.Metadata(s.Tags)); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 opts := map[string]string{"fflags": "+bitexact"}
 maps.Copy(opts, s.MuxerOptions)
 if err := m.WriteHeaderWithOptions(opts); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 for i, sub := range s.Subtitles {
  for n, ev := range sub.Events {
   if err := m.WriteSubtitle(subs[i], ffgo.SubtitleEvent{PTS: ev.Start.Microseconds(), Duration: (ev.End - ev.Start).Microseconds(), Data: sub.packet(n, ev)}); err != nil {
    return err
   }
  }
 }
 if err := interleave(m, srcs, s.Shortest, s.StartOffset); err != nil { // always encodes the source whose next frame is earliest
  return err
 }
 return m.WriteTrailer()
}
```

  `registerDevices` is a package-level `sync.Once` around `avdevice.RegisterAll()` that keeps
  its error (registering twice is harmless, so `Require` keeps its own call).
  `openVideo` opens `ffgo.NewDecoderWithOptions(v.Source + durationSuffix, &ffgo.DecoderOptions{Format: "lavfi"})`,
  adds `format=<PixFmt>` to the graph when `PixFmt` is set, builds `ffgo.NewVideoStreamEncoder` with
  `EncoderName: v.Encoder` (default `libx264`), the source's size and rate, `CodecOptions` =
  `{"threads": "1", "flags": "+bitexact"}` plus `v.Options`, `SideData` from `v.HDR10` (mastering
  display and content light, as W0.30's test builds them), and adds it with
  `m.AddEncoderStream(enc, ffgo.StreamOptions{… v.Stream, SideData: the same two blobs})`; each frame gets
  `SetColorSpec` from `v.Color` (BT.2020/PQ/BT.2020nc when `HDR10` is set and `Color` is zero). `openAudio`
  does the same with `ffgo.NewAudioEncoder(ffgo.AudioEncoderConfig2{EncoderName, SampleRate, Layout,
  BitRate, Options})`, appending `aformat=sample_fmts=<the encoder's format>:channel_layouts=<Layout>` to the
  graph; `Samples` writes a 16-bit WAV beside the clip and uses `amovie=<path>` as the source; `Offset` is
  added to every packet's timestamps (rescaled to the stream's time base), as `-itsoffset` does.
  `durationSuffix` appends `:d=<Duration>` only when the graph's first filter has no `d=`/`duration=`.
  `inspect.go` reads the file back with `ffgo.NewDecoder` (format name, duration, tags, each stream's type,
  codec name, language, title, disposition names, channels, sample rate, size and tags, and the chapters)
  and fails `t` on an error. `ParseSRT` parses SubRip cues; `Truncate` copies the first `keep` bytes. `Inspect` fills `CodecTag` from `avcodec.GetCodecParTag(s.CodecParameters())` and `SideData` from `ffgo.StreamSideData`; `Frames`, `Packets` and `ChannelRMS` read with the same decoder (`ReadPacket`; each decoded frame's `BestEffortTimestamp` (F5) and `Frame.SideData` for the HDR types; float PCM per channel). `RemuxFile` opens `src` with `ffgo.NewDecoder`, adds one `AddCopyStream` per stream with its metadata merged with `StreamMetadata[i]`, sets the source's format tags merged with `Tags`, copies packets until `Until`, and is bit-exact like `Write` (`fflags +bitexact`). All of it (`Packet.Pos`, `Frame.SideData`, `StreamSideData`, `GetCodecParTag`, `AddCopyStream`, `WritePacket`) is in the fork's base tag, ffgo `.11` and later: no fork addition.
  `doc.go`: "Package testmedia writes deterministic test clips on ffgo, the model of an ffmpeg command line,
  so no test runs the ffmpeg or ffprobe CLI (owner decision of 2026-10-06; upgrade guide U2). Tests,
  hack/record-goldens and test/fixtures/mkclips import it; no binary does (TestNoBinaryLinksTestmedia)."

```go
// The goldens are what the parity tests compare with after the exec
// implementations are gone, so they must be complete and intact: every
// clip in the manifest exists with its recorded hash, and every kind it
// names has a golden (upgrade guide U2.3).
func TestTheGoldensAreCompleteAndIntact(t *testing.T) {
 m := goldens.Manifest(t)
 require.NotEmpty(t, m)
 var total int64
 for _, c := range m {
  b, err := os.ReadFile(goldens.ClipPath(c.Name))
  require.NoError(t, err, c.Name)
  assert.Equal(t, c.SHA256, fmt.Sprintf("%x", sha256.Sum256(b)), "%s changed after it was recorded", c.Name)
  assert.LessOrEqual(t, len(b), 1<<20, "%s is over 1 MiB", c.Name)
  total += int64(len(b))
  for _, k := range c.Kinds {
   m, err := filepath.Glob(goldens.GoldenPath(k, c.Name)) // extract is one file per stream
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.NotEmpty(t, m, "%s has no %s golden", c.Name, k)
  }
 }
 assert.LessOrEqual(t, total, int64(16<<20), "the committed clips stay under 16 MiB")
 for _, k := range []string{"probe", "extract", "decode"} {
  assert.NotEmpty(t, goldens.Clips(t, k), "no clip carries %s goldens", k)
 }
}
```

§6 (probe on ffgo: §6.2, §6.3, §6.4, §6.7, §6.8), §7 (markers decode, embedded

**What these waves do.**

- **W7** (§11.1 step 10): `pkg/ffruntime` (the one runtime gate), `test/nativetest`,
  `pkg/segments` without the Kubernetes API types, the versioned fingerprint
  cache (OD48), and `pkg/segments/decode` rebuilt on ffgo, byte-for-byte against

- **W9** (§11.1 step 12): `pkg/par2child` (par2go in a re-exec'd child of the

- **W10** (§11.1 steps 13-14): the exec guard's allow-list down to

### Wave-specific rules

- **Order.** W7 → W8 → W9 → W10, each after the installers wave (§11.1 step 9).
  W8 and W9 additionally need `cmd/clustarr` deleted (W5.17): they put purego
  into packages `cmd/clustarr` linked. Inside a wave, tasks run in order unless
  a task says it may run in parallel.
- **The native test environment.** Every native test (FFmpeg, ffgo's shim, ORT,
  par2go) runs with the variables `make test` exports (§10.1.6); `t.Setenv` is
  too late, because ffgo maps FFmpeg at package init. Save once as
  `<scratchpad>/native-env.sh` (scratchpad: this session's scratchpad directory;
  not committed) and source it before every `go test` below that names it:

  ```bash
  export NATIVE_ASSETS="$(go env GOPATH)/bin/native-assets"
  export LD_LIBRARY_PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib" CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS="$NATIVE_ASSETS" \
         FFGO_SHIM_DIR="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib" ORT_LIB_PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib/libonnxruntime.so" \
         PAR2GO_LIB="$NATIVE_ASSETS/lib/libpar2shim.so" PATH="$NATIVE_ASSETS/bin:$PATH" \
         CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1
  ```

  `$NATIVE` below means `. <scratchpad>/native-env.sh &&`. Run `make native-assets`
  once first. A native test that reports SKIP under `$NATIVE` is a failure of the
  step, never a pass (the CLAUDE.md silent-skip gotcha).
- **Envtest.** `$ENVTEST` means
  `KUBEBUILDER_ASSETS="$($(go env GOPATH)/bin/setup-envtest use 1.37.0 -i -p path)"`.
  Envtest packages these waves touch (after the fold; loop spec §8.3): `app/remediation/...`,
  `app/catalog/controller/mediafile`, `app/import/worker/fileimport`,
  `app/import/worker/rescan`, `app/squash/worker`,
  `app/squash/transcodeplan`, `internal/cli/agent`.
- **Parity tests** carry `//go:build parity` and live under `test/`, which the
  exec guard does not scan (§4.5.6). Run them with `-tags parity` under
  `$NATIVE`, so the CLIs in `$NATIVE_ASSETS/bin` are BtbN's FFmpeg 9.0.2, the
  same build ffgo loads.
- **Formatting.** After every edit run
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/gofumpt -w <files>` and
  `$(go env GOPATH)/bin/goimports -local github.com/mediactl/clustarr -w <files>`.
  Every new `.go` file starts with `hack/boilerplate.go.txt` verbatim, a blank
  line, then `package`; the snippets below omit the header.
- **No go.mod edit, no `go get`, no `go mod tidy`** (step 0c owns the three edits).
- **No field manager, CRD field, stream, consumer or RBAC rule is added** in W7-W9
  (§8.6: par2 owns none; §7: decode and extraction write nothing). `make manifests`
  must leave `config/` and `charts/` unchanged; each wave gate checks.
- **Graft drift.** The graft run (`cmd/transcode --graft-task`,
  `app/squash/worker/graft`, `pkg/transcode/engine/graft.go`) decodes on ffgo
  in-process already; since the fold (F7.2, D9) its pod answers in `clustarr-grafts`
  and writes no termination message. W8.5 routes its FFmpeg log through `ffruntime` and loads
  FFmpeg through `ffruntime.Load` before a graft runs (`graftWithFFmpeg`); nothing else in these waves
  touches it. main's `142d0d4b` (an arm64 image with no libva environment)
  is carried by the installers wave as `native-base` plus `native-amd64` and
  `native-arm64` (W6.5); W9.7 puts `ENV PAR2GO_LIB` on `native-base`.
- **Commits** are path-scoped (`git commit -m '…' -- <paths>`); `git add` new files
  first; a `git mv` stages both paths, so the pathspec names both. Never
  `git stash`, never push.

`pkg/ffruntime/do_test.go` (package `ffruntime`, internal, for the seams):

```go
package ffruntime

import (
 "context"
 "errors"
 "testing"
 "time"

 "github.com/stretchr/testify/assert"
 "github.com/stretchr/testify/require"
)

// seams sets the grace and the wedge threshold for one test and resets the
// process-wide abandonment state around it. No test in this package is
// parallel: the state is the process's.
func seams(t *testing.T, g time.Duration, max int) {
 t.Helper()
 resetDo()
 oldGrace, oldMax := grace, maxAbandoned
 grace, maxAbandoned = g, max
 t.Cleanup(func() { grace, maxAbandoned = oldGrace, oldMax; resetDo() })
}

func TestDoReturnsTheBodysResult(t *testing.T) {
 seams(t, 50*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
 boom := errors.New("boom")
 assert.NoError(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return nil }))
 assert.ErrorIs(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return boom }), boom)
}

func TestDoNeverStartsAfterItsContextEnded(t *testing.T) {
 seams(t, 50*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
 ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
 cancel()
 ran := false
 err := Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { ran = true; return nil })
 assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
 assert.False(t, ran)
}

// A body that honours its context inside the grace is not abandoned.
func TestABodyThatStopsInsideTheGraceIsNotAbandoned(t *testing.T) {
 seams(t, time.Second, MaxAbandoned)
 ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
 go func() { time.Sleep(20 * time.Millisecond); cancel() }()
 err := Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error { <-ctx.Done(); return ctx.Err() })
 assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.Canceled)
 assert.NotErrorIs(t, err, ErrAbandoned)
 assert.Zero(t, Abandoned())
}

// The old process-group kill's replacement: a call blocked past its context
// returns after the grace, and is counted until it returns (spec §7.4).
func TestACancelledCallReturnsWithinTheGraceAndIsCountedUntilItReturns(t *testing.T) {
 seams(t, 100*time.Millisecond, MaxAbandoned)
 release := make(chan struct{})
 start := time.Now()
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 20*time.Millisecond)
 defer cancel()
 err := Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { <-release; return nil })
 assert.Less(t, time.Since(start), time.Second)
 assert.ErrorIs(t, err, ErrAbandoned)
 assert.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
 assert.Equal(t, 1, Abandoned())
 close(release)
 assert.Eventually(t, func() bool { return Abandoned() == 0 }, time.Second, 5*time.Millisecond,
  "a call that returns after being abandoned is no longer counted")
}

func TestMaxAbandonedWedgesTheProcess(t *testing.T) {
 seams(t, 10*time.Millisecond, 2)
 release := make(chan struct{})
 defer close(release)
 for range 2 {
  ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), time.Millisecond)
  require.ErrorIs(t, Do(ctx, func(context.Context) error { <-release; return nil }), ErrAbandoned)
  cancel()
 }
 select {
 case <-Wedged():
 case <-time.After(time.Second):
  t.Fatal("Wedged() did not close at MaxAbandoned outstanding calls")
 }
 assert.ErrorIs(t, Do(context.Background(), func(context.Context) error { return nil }), ErrWedged)
 assert.ErrorIs(t, Healthz(nil), ErrWedged)
}
```

```go
// Errors reach slog at Warn as "ffmpeg", at most a burst of 20 and then
// 10 a second; warnings and below never do (spec §7.4).
func TestErrorsReachSlogRateLimited(t *testing.T) {
 now := time.Unix(0, 0)
 r, buf := newRouterForTest(t, func() time.Time { return now })
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogWarning, "a warning\n")
 for range 100 {
  r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "an error\n")
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 20, strings.Count(buf.String(), "msg=ffmpeg"))
 assert.NotContains(t, buf.String(), "a warning")
 now = now.Add(time.Second)
 for range 100 {
  r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "an error\n")
 }
 assert.Equal(t, 30, strings.Count(buf.String(), "msg=ffmpeg"), "10 more after one second")
}

func TestCaptureSeesEveryLineUntilReleased(t *testing.T) {
 r, _ := newRouterForTest(t, time.Now)
 var got []string
 release := r.capture(func(_ ffgo.LogLevel, m string) { got = append(got, m) })
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogWarning, "w")
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "e")
 release()
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "after")
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"w", "e"}, got)
}

func TestMuteSilencesSlogButNotCaptures(t *testing.T) {
 r, buf := newRouterForTest(t, time.Now)
 var got int
 defer r.capture(func(ffgo.LogLevel, string) { got++ })()
 unmute := r.mute()
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "muted")
 unmute()
 r.dispatch(ffgo.LogError, "heard")
 assert.Equal(t, 2, got)
 assert.NotContains(t, buf.String(), "muted")
 assert.Contains(t, buf.String(), "heard")
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/doc.go`:

```go
// Package ffruntime is the one runtime gate every binary that links ffgo
// passes through (spec 2026-10-06 §7.4). Load maps FFmpeg 9 and the ffgo
// shim once and checks the shim's API; Require checks the demuxers,
// decoders, encoders and filters a caller needs; one process-wide log
// trampoline routes FFmpeg's log to slog (RouteLog), to a run's own sink
// (Capture) or nowhere (Mute); and Do bounds every in-process FFmpeg call by
// its context plus Grace, counting calls it had to abandon until they
// return, and reports the process wedged at MaxAbandoned outstanding calls.
//
// ffgo dlopens FFmpeg at package init (avutil/avutil.go's init), not at
// Load, so any binary linking this package has mapped FFmpeg before main.
// It imports the standard library and ffgo only (TestFFRuntimeImportsOnlyFFgo).
package ffruntime
```

`pkg/ffruntime/load.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
 "errors"
 "fmt"
 "os"
 "path/filepath"
 "strings"
 "sync"
 "time"

 "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo"
)

const (
 // AVCodecMajor is FFmpeg 9's libavcodec major.
 AVCodecMajor = 63
 // MinShimAPI is FFSHIM_API_VERSION of ffgo v0.0.0-clustarr.13: an older
 // shim reads FFmpeg 9's structs at FFmpeg 4-7's offsets (spec §7.1 fact 8).
 MinShimAPI = 1
 // Grace is how long Do waits for a call after its context ends: the old
 // subprocess WaitDelay.
 Grace = 5 * time.Second
 // MaxAbandoned outstanding abandoned calls wedge the process.
 MaxAbandoned = 4
)

// Report is what Load found; the library paths are the files the dynamic
// loader mapped (/proc/self/maps), not the names asked for.
type Report struct {
 FFmpegMajor int    `json:"ffmpegMajor"`
 ShimAPI     int    `json:"shimAPI"`
 AVUtil      string `json:"avutil,omitempty"`
 AVCodec     string `json:"avcodec,omitempty"`
 AVFormat    string `json:"avformat,omitempty"`
 ShimPath    string `json:"shimPath,omitempty"`
}

var (
 // ErrUnavailable wraps every reason FFmpeg cannot be used here.
 ErrUnavailable = errors.New("ffruntime: FFmpeg is unavailable")
 // ErrWedged refuses calls once MaxAbandoned are outstanding.
 ErrWedged = errors.New("ffruntime: FFmpeg calls are stuck; restart the process")
 // ErrAbandoned is a call that outlived its context plus Grace.
 ErrAbandoned = errors.New("ffruntime: an FFmpeg call outlived its context and was abandoned")
)

var ffmpegReleases = map[int]int{58: 4, 59: 5, 60: 6, 61: 7, 62: 8, 63: 9}

var (
 loadOnce   sync.Once
 loadReport Report
 loadErr    error
)

// Load loads FFmpeg and the shim once per process and keeps the first
// result: ffgo's own loader remembers a failure and cannot be retried.
func Load() (Report, error) {
 loadOnce.Do(func() { loadReport, loadErr = load(func() ([]byte, error) { return os.ReadFile("/proc/self/maps") }) })
 return loadReport, loadErr
}

func load(maps func() ([]byte, error)) (Report, error) {
 var r Report
 if err := ffgo.Init(); err != nil {
  return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: load the FFmpeg libraries (LD_LIBRARY_PATH): %w", ErrUnavailable, err)
 }
 _, avc, _ := ffgo.Version()
 major := int(avc >> 16)
 r.FFmpegMajor = ffmpegReleases[major]
 if major != AVCodecMajor {
  return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: libavcodec %d is not FFmpeg 9's (%d)", ErrUnavailable, major, AVCodecMajor)
 }
 d := ffgo.Diagnose()
 r.ShimPath = d.ShimPath
 if !d.ShimLoaded {
  return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: no ffgo shim built for FFmpeg 9 was loaded (FFGO_SHIM_DIR): %s", ErrUnavailable, d.ShimError)
 }
 r.ShimAPI = ffgo.ShimAPIVersion()
 if r.ShimAPI < MinShimAPI {
  return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: the ffgo shim %s has API %d; this build needs %d (rebuild libffshim.so from ffgo v0.0.0-clustarr.13)",
   ErrUnavailable, d.ShimPath, r.ShimAPI, MinShimAPI)
 }
 if b, err := maps(); err == nil {
  r.AVUtil, r.AVCodec, r.AVFormat = mapped(b, "libavutil.so"), mapped(b, "libavcodec.so"), mapped(b, "libavformat.so")
  if p := mapped(b, "libffshim.so"); p != "" {
   r.ShimPath = p
  }
 }
 // F13 makes the level effective under a callback: lines above it never
 // reach the trampoline, so a debug line costs no purego callback.
 if err := ffgo.SetLogLevel(ffgo.LogWarning); err != nil {
  return r, fmt.Errorf("%w: set FFmpeg's log level: %w", ErrUnavailable, err)
 }
 return r, nil
}

// mapped is the path of the first mapping whose file name begins with lib,
// so "libavcodec.so" matches libavcodec.so.63.1.100.
func mapped(maps []byte, lib string) string {
 for _, line := range strings.Split(string(maps), "\n") {
  f := strings.Fields(line)
  if len(f) < 6 {
   continue
  }
  if p := strings.Join(f[5:], " "); strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(p), lib) {
   return p
  }
 }
 return ""
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/require.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
 "fmt"
 "strings"

 "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avcodec"
 "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avfilter"
 "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avformat"
)

// Needs names what a caller asks of FFmpeg, by FFmpeg's names.
type Needs struct{ Demuxers, Muxers, Decoders, Encoders, Filters []string }

// Require loads FFmpeg (Load) and fails naming every missing piece of n.
func Require(n Needs) error {
 if _, err := Load(); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 var missing []string
 for _, d := range n.Demuxers {
  if avformat.FindInputFormat(d) == nil {
   missing = append(missing, "demuxer "+d)
  }
 }
 for _, m := range n.Muxers {
  // A muxer is found by allocating an output context for it, freed at
  // once (spec §7.4: avformat.AllocOutputContext2).
  var oc avformat.FormatContext
  if err := avformat.AllocOutputContext2(&oc, nil, m, ""); err != nil {
   missing = append(missing, "muxer "+m)
   continue
  }
  avformat.FreeContext(oc)
 }
 for _, d := range n.Decoders {
  if avcodec.FindDecoderByName(d) == nil {
   missing = append(missing, "decoder "+d)
  }
 }
 for _, e := range n.Encoders {
  if avcodec.FindEncoderByName(e) == nil {
   missing = append(missing, "encoder "+e)
  }
 }
 for _, f := range n.Filters {
  if avfilter.GetByName(f) == nil {
   missing = append(missing, "filter "+f)
  }
 }
 if len(missing) > 0 {
  return fmt.Errorf("%w: this FFmpeg lacks %s", ErrUnavailable, strings.Join(missing, ", "))
 }
 return nil
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/log.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
 "log/slog"
 "strings"
 "sync"
 "time"

 "github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo"
)

// logRouter is the one FFmpeg log callback a process installs (FFmpeg's
// log callback is process-wide; spec §7.4). Lines at LogError or worse go to
// slog at Warn as "ffmpeg", rate-limited unless muted; every line goes to
// each Capture sink.
type logRouter struct {
 mu        sync.Mutex
 installed bool
 logger    *slog.Logger
 muted     int
 sinks     map[int]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)
 next      int
 bucket    tokenBucket
}

func newLogRouter(now func() time.Time) *logRouter {
 return &logRouter{sinks: map[int]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string){}, bucket: tokenBucket{rate: 10, burst: 20, tokens: 20, now: now}}
}

var router = newLogRouter(time.Now)

// RouteLog sends FFmpeg's errors to l from now on.
func RouteLog(l *slog.Logger) {
 router.mu.Lock()
 router.logger = l
 router.mu.Unlock()
 router.install()
}

// Capture hands every FFmpeg line to sink until release is called.
func Capture(sink func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)) (release func()) {
 router.install()
 return router.capture(sink)
}

// Mute stops FFmpeg's errors reaching slog until release is called; Capture
// sinks still see them.
func Mute() (release func()) {
 router.install()
 return router.mute()
}

func (r *logRouter) install() {
 r.mu.Lock()
 defer r.mu.Unlock()
 if r.installed {
  return
 }
 if err := ffgo.SetLogCallback(r.dispatch); err == nil {
  r.installed = true
 }
}

func (r *logRouter) capture(sink func(ffgo.LogLevel, string)) func() {
 r.mu.Lock()
 id := r.next
 r.next++
 r.sinks[id] = sink
 r.mu.Unlock()
 var once sync.Once
 return func() { once.Do(func() { r.mu.Lock(); delete(r.sinks, id); r.mu.Unlock() }) }
}

func (r *logRouter) mute() func() {
 r.mu.Lock()
 r.muted++
 r.mu.Unlock()
 var once sync.Once
 return func() { once.Do(func() { r.mu.Lock(); r.muted--; r.mu.Unlock() }) }
}

func (r *logRouter) dispatch(level ffgo.LogLevel, msg string) {
 r.mu.Lock()
 sinks := make([]func(ffgo.LogLevel, string), 0, len(r.sinks))
 for _, s := range r.sinks {
  sinks = append(sinks, s)
 }
 logger := r.logger
 toSlog := logger != nil && r.muted == 0 && level <= ffgo.LogError && r.bucket.allow()
 r.mu.Unlock()
 for _, s := range sinks {
  s(level, msg)
 }
 if toSlog {
  logger.Warn("ffmpeg", "level", level.String(), "message", strings.TrimRight(msg, "\n"))
 }
}

// tokenBucket is a burst-then-rate limiter; the caller holds the router's lock.
type tokenBucket struct {
 rate, burst float64
 tokens      float64
 last        time.Time
 now         func() time.Time
}

func (b *tokenBucket) allow() bool {
 t := b.now()
 if !b.last.IsZero() {
  b.tokens = min(b.burst, b.tokens+t.Sub(b.last).Seconds()*b.rate)
 }
 b.last = t
 if b.tokens < 1 {
  return false
 }
 b.tokens--
 return true
}
```

`pkg/ffruntime/do.go`:

```go
package ffruntime

import (
 "context"
 "fmt"
 "net/http"
 "sync"
 "time"
)

var (
 doMu         sync.Mutex
 outstanding  int
 wedged       = make(chan struct{})
 wedgedOnce   = new(sync.Once)
 grace        = Grace
 maxAbandoned = MaxAbandoned
)

// Do runs f on its own goroutine. When ctx ends and f has not returned
// within Grace, Do returns an error wrapping ErrAbandoned and ctx.Err() and
// leaves f running; Abandoned counts it until it returns. At MaxAbandoned
// outstanding calls Wedged closes and Do refuses every call with ErrWedged.
// A caller records an abandoned result as non-transient (spec §6.6).
func Do(ctx context.Context, f func(context.Context) error) error {
 select {
 case <-Wedged():
  return ErrWedged
 default:
 }
 if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 done := make(chan error, 1)
 go func() { done <- f(ctx) }()
 select {
 case err := <-done:
  return err
 case <-ctx.Done():
 }
 t := time.NewTimer(grace)
 defer t.Stop()
 select {
 case err := <-done:
  return err
 case <-t.C:
 }
 abandon(done)
 return fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrAbandoned, ctx.Err())
}

func abandon(done <-chan error) {
 doMu.Lock()
 outstanding++
 if outstanding >= maxAbandoned {
  w, once := wedged, wedgedOnce
  once.Do(func() { close(w) })
 }
 doMu.Unlock()
 go func() {
  <-done
  doMu.Lock()
  outstanding--
  doMu.Unlock()
 }()
}

// Abandoned is how many abandoned calls are still running.
func Abandoned() int {
 doMu.Lock()
 defer doMu.Unlock()
 return outstanding
}

// Wedged closes once MaxAbandoned calls are outstanding; it never reopens.
func Wedged() <-chan struct{} {
 doMu.Lock()
 defer doMu.Unlock()
 return wedged
}

// Healthz is the process-level healthz check "ffgo" (spec §3.3): an error
// once wedged, so the kubelet restarts a pod a restart can cure.
func Healthz(*http.Request) error {
 select {
 case <-Wedged():
  return ErrWedged
 default:
  return nil
 }
}

// resetDo is for this package's tests only.
func resetDo() {
 doMu.Lock()
 defer doMu.Unlock()
 outstanding, wedged, wedgedOnce = 0, make(chan struct{}), new(sync.Once)
}
```

```go
// Package nativetest is how a test asks for the native runtime -- FFmpeg 9
// with the ffgo shim, ONNX Runtime, par2go, the parity CLIs -- and either
// skips, naming what is missing, or fails when the run says the tools must be
// there (CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1, set by make test and CI; PAR2GO_REQUIRE=1
// for par2go). Spec 2026-10-06 §10.3.1, §13 OD44. Imported only by tests.
package nativetest

// Require skips t when err is not nil, or fails it when the tool is required.
func Require(t testing.TB, what string, err error) {
 t.Helper()
 if err == nil {
  return
 }
 msg := fmt.Sprintf("%s is unavailable: %v (run `make native-assets` and test through make, which sets LD_LIBRARY_PATH, FFGO_SHIM_DIR, ORT_LIB_PATH and PAR2GO_LIB)", what, err)
 if required(what) {
  t.Fatal(msg)
 }
 t.Skip(msg)
}

func required(what string) bool {
 // CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1 (CI; upgrade guide U2.1) makes a missing FFmpeg a
 // failure here too, as testmedia.Require does: one switch for every ffgo gate.
 return os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS") == "1" || (what == "par2go" && os.Getenv("PAR2GO_REQUIRE") == "1") ||
  (strings.HasPrefix(what, "FFmpeg") && os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE") == "1")
}

// FFmpeg loads FFmpeg through ffruntime and checks needs. Under
// CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1 the loaded libavcodec must be the pinned build in
// $CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS/lib: a host's system FFmpeg 9 cannot be told apart
// from it by version, and the parity oracles run the pinned build.
func FFmpeg(t testing.TB, needs ffruntime.Needs) ffruntime.Report {
 t.Helper()
 rep, err := ffruntime.Load()
 if err == nil {
  err = ffruntime.Require(needs)
 }
 if err == nil {
  err = pinned(rep.AVCodec)
 }
 Require(t, "FFmpeg 9 with the ffgo shim", err)
 return rep
}

func pinned(avcodec string) error {
 if os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS") != "1" {
  return nil
 }
 dir := os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS")
 if dir == "" {
  return errors.New("$CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS is unset: run the native tests through make")
 }
 if lib := filepath.Join(dir, "lib") + "/"; !strings.HasPrefix(avcodec, lib) {
  return fmt.Errorf("libavcodec was mapped from %s, not the pinned build under %s (LD_LIBRARY_PATH must be set before the test process starts)", avcodec, lib)
 }
 return nil
}

// Tool is name's path on PATH.
func Tool(t testing.TB, name string) string {
 t.Helper()
 p, err := exec.LookPath(name)
 Require(t, name, err)
 return p
}

// SameFFmpeg requires cli (ffmpeg or ffprobe) to be built on the libavcodec
// major.minor ffgo loaded, so a parity comparison compares decoders, not
// FFmpeg releases (spec §7.2.10 "Gate").
func SameFFmpeg(t testing.TB, cli string) {
 t.Helper()
 FFmpeg(t, ffruntime.Needs{})
 out, err := exec.Command(cli, "-hide_banner", "-version").CombinedOutput()
 if err == nil {
  major, minor, ok := libavcodecVersion(string(out))
  _, avc, _ := ffgo.Version()
  switch {
  case !ok:
   err = fmt.Errorf("%s -version printed no libavcodec line", cli)
  case uint32(major) != avc>>16 || uint32(minor) != (avc>>8)&0xff:
   err = fmt.Errorf("%s is libavcodec %d.%d, ffgo loaded %d.%d", cli, major, minor, avc>>16, (avc>>8)&0xff)
  }
 }
 Require(t, cli+" on ffgo's FFmpeg", err)
}

var avcodecLine = regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\s*libavcodec\s+(\d+)\.\s*(\d+)\.`)

func libavcodecVersion(out string) (major, minor int, ok bool) {
 m := avcodecLine.FindStringSubmatch(out)
 if m == nil {
  return 0, 0, false
 }
 major, _ = strconv.Atoi(m[1])
 minor, _ = strconv.Atoi(m[2])
 return major, minor, true
}
```

  (imports: `errors`, `fmt`, `os`, `os/exec`, `path/filepath`, `regexp`,
  `strconv`, `strings`, `testing`, ffgo, `pkg/ffruntime`.)

`pkg/ffruntime/ffmetrics/ffmetrics.go`:

```go
// Package ffmetrics exports pkg/ffruntime's abandoned-call count. It is
// separate so pkg/ffruntime stays standard library plus ffgo.
package ffmetrics

// Register adds clustarr_ffgo_abandoned_calls to r. A registry that already
// has it is not an error (an envtest registers several domains in one process).
func Register(r prometheus.Registerer) error {
 err := r.Register(prometheus.NewGaugeFunc(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
  Name: "clustarr_ffgo_abandoned_calls",
  Help: "In-process FFmpeg calls that outlived their context and are still running; at ffruntime.MaxAbandoned the process reports itself wedged.",
 }, func() float64 { return float64(ffruntime.Abandoned()) }))
 var are prometheus.AlreadyRegisteredError
 if errors.As(err, &are) {
  return nil
 }
 return err
}
```

```go
package segmentplan

// analysisErrorTTL is how long an analysis Error stands before the file is
// due again.
const analysisErrorTTL = 24 * time.Hour

// Due reports whether mf wants a segment analysis: a movie or episode file
// with a probe, never analyzed, analyzed for another probe or by an older
// analyzer, or whose analysis failed a day or more ago. A NotFound or Found
// at the current version and probe is never due again: the same bytes give
// the same answer. (Moved from pkg/segments, which no longer links the API.)
func Due(mf *catalogv1alpha1.MediaFile, now time.Time) bool {
 switch mf.Spec.MediaRef.Kind {
 case commonv1.MediaKindMovie, commonv1.MediaKindEpisode:
 default:
  return false
 }
 if mf.Status.MediaInfo == nil || mf.Status.ProbeHash == "" {
  return false
 }
 if mf.Status.Markers == nil || mf.Status.Markers.Analysis == nil {
  return true
 }
 a := mf.Status.Markers.Analysis
 switch {
 case a.ForProbeHash != mf.Status.ProbeHash, a.Version < segments.AnalyzerVersion:
  return true
 case a.Result == catalogv1alpha1.MarkersError:
  return now.Sub(a.AnalyzedAt.Time) >= analysisErrorTTL
 }
 return false
}
```

```go
// FingerprintVersion versions the clustarr-fingerprints cache keys. 1 stands
// for the unversioned keys the ffmpeg(1) decoder wrote; 2 is the in-process
// ffgo decoder (spec 2026-10-06 §7.2.7, OD48). Raise it whenever decode
// output can change: pkg/segments/decode, the fork's decode path, or the
// native image's libavcodec minor. Old objects age out under the store's
// 90-day MaxAge.
const FingerprintVersion int32 = 2

// FingerprintKey is a window's object name in the fingerprint cache.
func FingerprintKey(probeHash, which string) string {
 return probeHash + "." + which + ".v" + strconv.Itoa(int(FingerprintVersion))
}
```

```go
// Every window §7.2.10 names, both decoders, byte for byte.
func TestTheFFgoDecoderMatchesFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
 bin := nativetest.Tool(t, "ffmpeg")
 nativetest.SameFFmpeg(t, bin)
 ref, got := execDecoder{FFmpeg: bin}, decode.Decoder{}
 ctx := context.Background()
 for name, path := range fixtures(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   for _, at := range []float64{0, 12.5, 12.05} { // 0, mid-GOP, 50 ms after a keyframe (the 3/23 s edge)
    want, err := ref.Audio(ctx, path, 0, at, 10)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    have, err := got.Audio(ctx, path, 0, at, 10)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    compareAudio(t, fmt.Sprintf("audio@%.2f", at), want, have)
   }
   want, err := ref.Frames(ctx, path, 15)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   have, err := got.Frames(ctx, path, 15)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   compareFrames(t, "frames@15", want, have)
   for _, at := range []float64{1, 7.3, 12.05, 20.5, 29} {
    want, err := ref.Frame(ctx, path, at)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    have, err := got.Frame(ctx, path, at)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.True(t, bytes.Equal(want, have), "frame@%.2f differs", at)
   }
  })
 }
}

// compareAudio reports the differing sample count, max |diff| and the
// chromaprint Hamming distance of the two windows.
func compareAudio(t *testing.T, what string, want, have []int16) {
 t.Helper()
 if slices.Equal(want, have) {
  return
 }
 diff, maxd := 0, 0
 for i := range min(len(want), len(have)) {
  if d := int(want[i]) - int(have[i]); d != 0 {
   diff++
   maxd = max(maxd, abs(d))
  }
 }
 t.Errorf("%s: %d vs %d samples, %d differ, max |diff| %d, chromaprint Hamming %d bits",
  what, len(want), len(have), diff+abs(len(want)-len(have)), maxd, hamming(chromaprint.Fingerprint(want), chromaprint.Fingerprint(have)))
}

func compareFrames(t *testing.T, what string, want, have [][]byte) {
 t.Helper()
 if len(want) != len(have) {
  t.Errorf("%s: %d frames vs %d", what, len(want), len(have))
 }
 for i := range min(len(want), len(have)) {
  if !bytes.Equal(want[i], have[i]) {
   t.Errorf("%s: first differing frame %d of %d", what, i, len(want))
   return
  }
 }
}

func hamming(a, b []uint32) int {
 n := abs(len(a)-len(b)) * 32
 for i := range min(len(a), len(b)) {
  n += bits.OnesCount32(a[i] ^ b[i])
 }
 return n
}

func abs(x int) int { return max(x, -x) }
```

```go
// Was TestAHungFFmpegIsKilledWithItsGroup: a decode blocked past its
// context returns within the grace (ffruntime.Do), counted as abandoned.
func TestACancelledDecodeReturnsWithinTheGrace(t *testing.T) {
 ready(t)
 p := clip(t) // before the deadline: ffruntime.Do never starts a call whose context has ended
 release := make(chan struct{})
 restore := decode.SetBeforeRead(func(context.Context) { <-release })
 t.Cleanup(func() { // also on a failed require, so no later test inherits a blocking seam
  close(release)
  // Abandoned() reaching 0 orders the abandoned call's read of the seam
  // before restore's write (-race): Do decrements under its mutex after f returns.
  assert.Eventually(t, func() bool { return ffruntime.Abandoned() == 0 }, 10*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond)
  restore()
 })
 // 500 ms leaves room for the open and decoder setup under -race, which
 // decode reaches before its first beforeRead.
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 500*time.Millisecond)
 defer cancel()
 start := time.Now()
 _, err := decode.Decoder{}.Audio(ctx, p, 0, 0, 1)
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, ffruntime.ErrAbandoned)
 assert.Less(t, time.Since(start), ffruntime.Grace+2*time.Second)
}

// Was TestFramesDecodeKeyframesOnly: skip_frame=nokey decodes at most the
// keyframes from the seek point on (the clip has one a second).
func TestFramesDecodeKeyframesOnly(t *testing.T) {
 ready(t)
 n, restore := decode.CountDecodedFrames()
 defer restore()
 _, err := decode.Decoder{}.Frames(context.Background(), clip(t), 4)
 require.NoError(t, err)
 assert.LessOrEqual(t, n(), 7, "keyframes from 4 s to 10 s, plus the one before the seek point")
 assert.Positive(t, n())
}

// This process is the first to run concurrent ffgo decoders (spec §7.2.8).
func TestConcurrentDecodesAreRaceFree(t *testing.T) {
 ready(t)
 paths := []string{"../../../test/data/mediainfo/sample_hevc_10bit.mkv", "../../../test/data/mediainfo/sample_h264_8bit.mp4"}
 var wg sync.WaitGroup
 for g := range 4 {
  wg.Add(1)
  go func() {
   defer wg.Done()
   for i := range 10 {
    p := paths[(g+i)%2]
    _, err := decode.Decoder{Threads: 1}.Frame(context.Background(), p, 0.5)
    assert.NoError(t, err, p)
    _, err = decode.Decoder{Threads: 1}.Audio(context.Background(), p, 0, 0, 1)
    assert.NoError(t, err, p)
   }
  }()
 }
 wg.Wait()
}
```

```go
// audioTS is audio_ts_process: contiguous AAC frames at 48 kHz in a 1/1000
// stream keep sample-exact pts at 1/48000, and a gap resets the delta.
func TestAudioTSFollowsFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
 nativetest.FFmpeg(t, ffruntime.Needs{})
 s := newAudioTS()
 tb := ffgo.NewRational(1, 1000)
 assert.Equal(t, int64(0), s.next(0, tb, 48000, 1024))
 assert.Equal(t, int64(1024), s.next(21, tb, 48000, 1024), "21 ms is 1008 samples; the rescale delta keeps 1024")
 assert.Equal(t, int64(2048), s.next(43, tb, 48000, 1024))
 assert.Equal(t, int64(48000), s.next(1000, tb, 48000, 1024), "a gap resets the delta")
 assert.Equal(t, int64(49024), s.next(avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE, tb, 48000, 1024), "no pts takes the prediction")
}
```

  `decode.go`:

```go
// Decoder decodes in-process through ffgo; Threads is each decoder's thread
// count, 0 meaning FFmpeg's "auto" (ffmpeg(1)'s default).
type Decoder struct{ Threads int }

// Needs is what decoding asks of FFmpeg; cmd/markers requires it at start.
// libdav1d, not av1: FFmpeg's native AV1 decoder is hardware-only (§7.2.9).
var Needs = ffruntime.Needs{
 Demuxers: []string{"matroska", "mov", "mpegts", "avi"},
 Filters: []string{"buffer", "buffersink", "abuffer", "abuffersink", "trim", "atrim", "fps", "scale",
  "format", "aformat", "aresample"},
 Decoders: []string{"h264", "hevc", "libdav1d", "mpeg2video", "mpeg4", "aac", "ac3", "eac3", "dca",
  "truehd", "flac", "opus", "mp3"},
}

func (d Decoder) Audio(ctx context.Context, path string, stream int, fromS, durS float64) ([]int16, error) {
 var pcm []int16
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (err error) { pcm, err = d.audio(ctx, path, stream, fromS, durS); return err })
 return pcm, runtimeErr(err)
}

func (d Decoder) Frames(ctx context.Context, path string, fromS float64) ([][]byte, error) {
 var out [][]byte
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (err error) { out, err = d.frames(ctx, path, fromS); return err })
 return out, runtimeErr(err)
}

func (d Decoder) Frame(ctx context.Context, path string, atS float64) ([]byte, error) {
 var out []byte
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (err error) { out, err = d.frame(ctx, path, atS); return err })
 return out, runtimeErr(err)
}

// runtimeErr prefixes the gate's own errors; the bodies' already say "decode:".
func runtimeErr(err error) error {
 if err != nil && (errors.Is(err, ffruntime.ErrAbandoned) || errors.Is(err, ffruntime.ErrWedged) || !strings.HasPrefix(err.Error(), "decode:")) {
  return fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
 }
 return err
}

// ms is x in whole milliseconds as the CLI decoder printed it (secs()).
func ms(x float64) int64 {
 v, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(strconv.FormatFloat(max(x, 0), 'f', 3, 64), 64)
 return int64(math.Round(v * 1000))
}

// secs6 prints µs as an AV_OPT_TYPE_DURATION ("S.ffffff"): a bare integer
// would read as seconds (libavfilter/trim.c).
func secs6(us int64) string { return fmt.Sprintf("%d.%06d", us/1_000_000, us%1_000_000) }
```

  `open.go` (steps 1-7 of §7.2.2):

```go
const maxOutput = 64 << 20

var errTooLarge = errors.New("decode: output over the cap")

var us = ffgo.NewRational(1, 1_000_000)

// beforeRead and onDecodedFrame are test seams (export_test.go).
var (
 beforeRead     = func(context.Context) {}
 onDecodedFrame = func() {}
)

// input is one opened file: its demuxer, the chosen stream, and the origin
// -ss gave its clock (µs: ms(x)*1000 + start_time).
type input struct {
 in     *ffgo.Decoder
 si     *ffgo.StreamInfo
 origin int64
}

func open(ctx context.Context, path string, pick func([]*ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffgo.StreamInfo, none string, atS float64) (*input, error) {
 in, err := ffgo.NewDecoderWithOptions(path, &ffgo.DecoderOptions{AVOptions: map[string]string{"scan_all_pmts": "1"}})
 if err != nil {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %s: %w", path, err)
 }
 si := pick(in.Streams())
 if si == nil {
  _ = in.Close()
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %s has %s", path, none)
 }
 origin := ms(atS)*1000 + in.StartTime().Microseconds()
 seekTS := origin
 if !in.SeekToPTS() && slices.ContainsFunc(in.Streams(), func(s *ffgo.StreamInfo) bool { return s.VideoDelay > 0 }) {
  seekTS -= 3 * 1_000_000 / 23 // fftools/ffmpeg_demux.c: B-frame delay without AVFMT_SEEK_TO_PTS
 }
 if err := in.SeekTimestamp(seekTS); err != nil { // a warning in ffmpeg(1)
  logging.FromContext(ctx).DebugContext(ctx, "decode: seek failed; decoding from the start", "path", path, "at", atS, "error", err)
 }
 if err := in.Discard(si.Index); err != nil { // after the seek, as ist_add does
  _ = in.Close()
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %s: %w", path, err)
 }
 return &input{in: in, si: si, origin: origin}, nil
}

func (src *input) close() { _ = src.in.Close() }

// nthAudio is -map 0:a:N.
func nthAudio(n int) func([]*ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffgo.StreamInfo {
 return func(ss []*ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffgo.StreamInfo {
  for _, s := range ss {
   if s.Type == ffgo.MediaTypeAudio {
    if n == 0 {
     return s
    }
    n--
   }
  }
  return nil
 }
}

// mainVideo ports map_auto_video (fftools/ffmpeg_mux_init.c): the largest
// picture, a default stream worth 5,000,000 more, an attached picture 1; the
// first strictly greater score wins.
func mainVideo(ss []*ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffgo.StreamInfo {
 var best *ffgo.StreamInfo
 bestScore := int64(0)
 for _, s := range ss {
  if s.Type != ffgo.MediaTypeVideo {
   continue
  }
  score := int64(s.Width) * int64(s.Height)
  if s.Disposition&ffgo.DispositionDefault != 0 {
   score += 5_000_000
  }
  if s.Disposition&ffgo.DispositionAttachedPic != 0 {
   score = 1
  }
  if score > bestScore {
   best, bestScore = s, score
  }
 }
 return best
}

// decoder opens the stream's decoder with ffmpeg(1)'s options (F1).
func (src *input) decoder(threads int, video, keyframesOnly bool) (*ffgo.StreamDecoder, error) {
 opts := map[string]string{"threads": "auto"}
 if threads > 0 {
  opts["threads"] = strconv.Itoa(threads)
 }
 if video {
  opts["flags"] = "+unaligned" // ffmpeg(1) crops unaligned after decode
 }
 if keyframesOnly {
  opts["skip_frame"] = "nokey" // AVDISCARD_NONKEY, not a packet key-flag filter
 }
 sd, err := src.in.NewStreamDecoder(src.si.Index, &ffgo.StreamDecoderConfig{Options: opts})
 if err != nil {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: open the %s decoder: %w", src.si.Codec, err)
 }
 return sd, nil
}

// decode feeds the stream's packets, shifted by -origin (ffmpeg(1)'s
// ts_offset), to sd and hands each frame to each until each says stop, the
// decoder is drained at end of file, or an error. Frames are borrowed until
// each returns.
func (src *input) decode(ctx context.Context, sd *ffgo.StreamDecoder, each func(ffgo.Frame) (stop bool, err error)) error {
 off := ffgo.RescaleQ(-src.origin, us, src.si.TimeBase)
 receive := func() (stop bool, err error) {
  for {
   if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
    return true, err
   }
   f, err := sd.Receive()
   if errors.Is(err, ffgo.ErrAgain) || errors.Is(err, io.EOF) {
    return false, nil
   }
   if err != nil {
    return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
   }
   onDecodedFrame()
   if stop, err := each(f); stop || err != nil {
    return true, err
   }
  }
 }
 for {
  if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   return err
  }
  beforeRead(ctx)
  p, err := src.in.ReadPacket()
  if err != nil {
   return fmt.Errorf("decode: read: %w", err)
  }
  if p == nil {
   break
  }
  if p.StreamIndex() != src.si.Index {
   _ = p.Free()
   continue
  }
  shift(p, off)
  for {
   err = sd.Send(p)
   if !errors.Is(err, ffgo.ErrAgain) {
    break
   }
   if stop, rerr := receive(); stop || rerr != nil {
    _ = p.Free()
    return rerr
   }
  }
  _ = p.Free() // a packet the decoder refuses is skipped, as ffmpeg(1) logs and goes on
  if stop, rerr := receive(); stop || rerr != nil {
   return rerr
  }
 }
 for errors.Is(sd.Send(nil), ffgo.ErrAgain) {
  if stop, rerr := receive(); stop || rerr != nil {
   return rerr
  }
 }
 _, err := receive()
 return err
}

func shift(p *ffgo.Packet, off int64) {
 if v := p.PTS(); v != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
  avcodec.SetPacketPTS(p.Raw(), v+off)
 }
 if v := p.DTS(); v != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
  avcodec.SetPacketDTS(p.Raw(), v+off)
 }
}
```

  `ts.go`: the port of `audio_samplerate_update` and `audio_ts_process`
  (FFmpeg n9.0.2 `fftools/ffmpeg_dec.c`), on F8's helpers:

```go
// audioTS gives each decoded audio frame the pts ffmpeg(1) filters it at
// (fftools/ffmpeg_dec.c audio_ts_process and audio_samplerate_update).
type audioTS struct {
 lastTB     ffgo.Rational // last_frame_tb
 lastPTS    int64         // last_frame_pts
 lastDurEst int64         // last_frame_duration_est
 lastRate   int           // last_frame_sample_rate
 delta      int64         // last_filter_in_rescale_delta
}

func newAudioTS() audioTS {
 return audioTS{lastTB: ffgo.NewRational(1, 1), lastPTS: avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE, delta: avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE}
}

func (s *audioTS) update(frameTB ffgo.Rational, rate int) ffgo.Rational {
 if rate == s.lastRate {
  return s.lastTB
 }
 prev := int64(s.lastTB.Den)
 g := gcd(prev, int64(rate))
 tb := ffgo.NewRational(1, 28224000) // LCM of 192000 and 44100, when exact is impossible
 if prev/g < math.MaxInt32/int64(rate) {
  tb = ffgo.NewRational(1, int32(prev/g*int64(rate)))
 }
 if frameTB.Num == 1 && frameTB.Den > tb.Den && frameTB.Den%tb.Den == 0 {
  tb = frameTB
 }
 if s.lastPTS != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
  s.lastPTS = ffgo.RescaleQ(s.lastPTS, s.lastTB, tb)
 }
 s.lastDurEst = ffgo.RescaleQ(s.lastDurEst, s.lastTB, tb)
 s.lastTB, s.lastRate = tb, rate
 return tb
}

// next is pts (in frameTB, or AV_NOPTS_VALUE) as ffmpeg(1) gives the frame
// to its filter graph, in 1/rate.
func (s *audioTS) next(pts int64, frameTB ffgo.Rational, rate, nbSamples int) int64 {
 tb := s.update(frameTB, rate)
 pred := int64(0)
 if s.lastPTS != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
  pred = s.lastPTS + s.lastDurEst
 }
 if pts == avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
  pts, frameTB = pred, tb
 } else if s.lastPTS != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE && pts > ffgo.RescaleQRnd(pred, tb, frameTB, ffgo.RoundUp) {
  s.delta = avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE // a gap: reset the conversion state
 }
 pts = ffgo.RescaleDelta(frameTB, pts, tb, nbSamples, &s.delta, tb)
 s.lastPTS = pts
 s.lastDurEst = ffgo.RescaleQ(int64(nbSamples), ffgo.NewRational(1, int32(rate)), tb)
 return ffgo.RescaleQ(pts, tb, ffgo.NewRational(1, int32(rate)))
}

func gcd(a, b int64) int64 {
 for b != 0 {
  a, b = b, a%b
 }
 return a
}
```

  `audio.go` (§7.2.3). atrim's end is detected from the input side instead of
  from a buffersink EOF, which ffgo's `FilterGraph.Filter` folds into "no more
  frames" (`filter_graph.go:517-518`): atrim ends output at
  `first_pts + duration`, where `first_pts` is the pts of the first sample it
  passes, so once a frame starting at or after that point has been pushed,
  atrim has emitted EOF and no later frame can change the output.

```go
// frameDownmixInfo is AV_FRAME_DATA_DOWNMIX_INFO (libavutil/frame.h).
const frameDownmixInfo ffgo.FrameSideDataType = 4

type audioKey struct {
 rate          int
 format        int32
 layout        string
 downmix       string
}

func (d Decoder) audio(ctx context.Context, path string, stream int, fromS, durS float64) ([]int16, error) {
 src, err := open(ctx, path, nthAudio(stream), fmt.Sprintf("no audio stream %d", stream), fromS)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer src.close()
 sd, err := src.decoder(d.Threads, false, false)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = sd.Close() }()
 durUS := ms(durS) * 1000
 filters := "atrim=starti=0:durationi=" + secs6(durUS) +
  ",aformat=sample_fmts=s16:sample_rates=" + strconv.Itoa(SampleRate) + ":channel_layouts=mono"
 var (
  g     *ffgo.FilterGraph
  key   audioKey
  ts    = newAudioTS()
  first = int64(-1)
  out   []int16
 )
 defer func() {
  if g != nil {
   _ = g.Close()
  }
 }()
 take := func(fs []*ffgo.Frame) error {
  for _, o := range fs {
   w := ffgo.WrapFrame(*o, ffgo.MediaTypeAudio)
   b := w.Data(0)[:2*w.NumSamples()]
   for i := 0; i+1 < len(b); i += 2 {
    out = append(out, int16(binary.LittleEndian.Uint16(b[i:])))
   }
   _ = o.Free()
  }
  if 2*len(out) > maxOutput {
   return errTooLarge
  }
  return nil
 }
 err = src.decode(ctx, sd, func(f ffgo.Frame) (bool, error) {
  rate := ffgo.WrapFrame(f, ffgo.MediaTypeAudio).SampleRate()
  f.SetPTS(ts.next(f.PTS(), src.si.TimeBase, rate, f.NumSamples()))
  dm, _ := f.SideData(frameDownmixInfo)
  k := audioKey{rate: rate, format: f.Format(), layout: f.ChannelLayout(), downmix: string(dm)}
  if g == nil || k != key { // -reinit_filter 1: drain the old graph, build the same chain anew
   if g != nil {
    fs, err := g.Flush()
    if err := errors.Join(err, take(fs)); err != nil {
     return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
    }
    _ = g.Close()
   }
   var err error
   g, err = ffgo.NewFilterGraph(ffgo.FilterGraphConfig{
    SampleRate: rate, Layout: k.layout, SampleFmt: ffgo.SampleFormat(k.format),
    TimeBase: ffgo.NewRational(1, int32(rate)), InputSideData: &f, Filters: filters,
   })
   if err != nil {
    return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: audio graph: %w", err)
   }
   key = k
  }
  pts, n := f.PTS(), int64(f.NumSamples())
  if first < 0 && pts+n > 0 {
   first = max(pts, 0)
  }
  fs, err := g.Filter(&f)
  if err := errors.Join(err, take(fs)); err != nil {
   return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
  }
  end := first + ffgo.RescaleQ(durUS, us, ffgo.NewRational(1, int32(rate)))
  return first >= 0 && pts >= end, nil // atrim has ended: nothing later is output
 })
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 if g != nil {
  fs, err := g.Flush() // aresample's delay
  if err := errors.Join(err, take(fs)); err != nil {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
  }
 }
 return out, nil
}
```

  `video.go` (§7.2.4, §7.2.5):

```go
type videoKey struct {
 w, h          int
 format        int32
 space, rng    int32
}

// videoGraph builds its chain lazily from the first frame, and again on a
// change of size, pixel format, colorspace or range (-reinit_filter 1).
type videoGraph struct {
 filters string
 tb, sar ffgo.Rational
 g       *ffgo.FilterGraph
 key     videoKey
}

func (v *videoGraph) push(f ffgo.Frame) ([]*ffgo.Frame, error) {
 w := ffgo.WrapFrame(f, ffgo.MediaTypeVideo)
 cs := f.ColorSpec()
 k := videoKey{w: w.Width(), h: w.Height(), format: f.Format(), space: int32(cs.Space), rng: int32(cs.Range)}
 var drained []*ffgo.Frame
 if v.g == nil || k != v.key {
  if v.g != nil {
   fs, err := v.g.Flush()
   if err != nil {
    return fs, err
   }
   drained = fs
   _ = v.g.Close()
  }
  g, err := ffgo.NewFilterGraph(ffgo.FilterGraphConfig{
   Width: k.w, Height: k.h, PixelFmt: ffgo.PixelFormat(k.format), TimeBase: v.tb, SAR: v.sar,
   ColorSpace: cs.Space, ColorRange: cs.Range, InputSideData: &f, Filters: v.filters,
  })
  if err != nil {
   return drained, fmt.Errorf("decode: video graph: %w", err)
  }
  v.g, v.key = g, k
 }
 fs, err := v.g.Filter(&f)
 return append(drained, fs...), err
}

func (v *videoGraph) flush() ([]*ffgo.Frame, error) {
 if v.g == nil {
  return nil, nil
 }
 return v.g.Flush()
}

func (v *videoGraph) close() {
 if v.g != nil {
  _ = v.g.Close()
 }
}

// plane copies rows of w*bpp bytes from frame o's first plane.
func plane(o *ffgo.Frame, w, h, bpp int) []byte {
 fw := ffgo.WrapFrame(*o, ffgo.MediaTypeVideo)
 data, ls := fw.Data(0), fw.Linesize(0)
 out := make([]byte, 0, w*h*bpp)
 for y := range h {
  out = append(out, data[y*ls:y*ls+w*bpp]...)
 }
 return out
}

func (d Decoder) frames(ctx context.Context, path string, fromS float64) ([][]byte, error) {
 src, err := open(ctx, path, mainVideo, "no video stream", fromS)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer src.close()
 sd, err := src.decoder(d.Threads, true, true)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = sd.Close() }()
 vg := &videoGraph{filters: fmt.Sprintf("trim=starti=0,fps=fps=1:start_time=0,scale=%d:%d:flags=area,format=gray", GrayW, GrayH),
  tb: sd.TimeBase(), sar: src.si.SampleAspectRatio}
 defer vg.close()
 var out [][]byte
 take := func(fs []*ffgo.Frame) error {
  for _, o := range fs {
   out = append(out, plane(o, GrayW, GrayH, 1))
   _ = o.Free()
  }
  if len(out)*GrayW*GrayH > maxOutput {
   return errTooLarge
  }
  return nil
 }
 err = src.decode(ctx, sd, func(f ffgo.Frame) (bool, error) {
  f.SetPTS(f.BestEffortTimestamp())
  fs, err := vg.push(f)
  if err := errors.Join(err, take(fs)); err != nil {
   return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
  }
  return false, nil
 })
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 fs, err := vg.flush() // buffersrc closes at the last frame's pts+duration
 if err := errors.Join(err, take(fs)); err != nil {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
 }
 return out, nil
}

func (d Decoder) frame(ctx context.Context, path string, atS float64) ([]byte, error) {
 src, err := open(ctx, path, mainVideo, "no video stream", atS)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer src.close()
 sd, err := src.decoder(d.Threads, true, false)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = sd.Close() }()
 vg := &videoGraph{filters: fmt.Sprintf("trim=starti=0,scale=%d:%d:flags=area,format=pix_fmts=rgb24", RGBW, RGBH),
  tb: sd.TimeBase(), sar: src.si.SampleAspectRatio}
 defer vg.close()
 var out []byte
 first := func(fs []*ffgo.Frame) {
  for _, o := range fs {
   if out == nil {
    out = plane(o, RGBW, RGBH, 3)
   }
   _ = o.Free()
  }
 }
 err = src.decode(ctx, sd, func(f ffgo.Frame) (bool, error) {
  f.SetPTS(f.BestEffortTimestamp())
  fs, err := vg.push(f)
  first(fs)
  if err != nil {
   return true, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
  }
  return out != nil, nil // -frames:v 1
 })
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 if out == nil {
  fs, err := vg.flush()
  first(fs)
  if err != nil {
   return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: %w", err)
  }
 }
 if len(out) != RGBW*RGBH*3 {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("decode: frame at %.1fs of %s: %d bytes", atS, path, len(out))
 }
 return out, nil
}
```

```go
// guard wraps a task's decoder: after a call the runtime abandoned, every
// later call fails at once with the same error (spec §6.6).
type guard struct {
 Decoder
 mu        sync.Mutex
 abandoned error
}

var errSkipped = errors.New("not decoded: an earlier FFmpeg call in this task was abandoned")

func (g *guard) check() error {
 g.mu.Lock()
 defer g.mu.Unlock()
 if g.abandoned != nil {
  return fmt.Errorf("%w (%w)", errSkipped, g.abandoned)
 }
 return nil
}

func (g *guard) note(err error) error {
 if errors.Is(err, ffruntime.ErrAbandoned) || errors.Is(err, ffruntime.ErrWedged) {
  g.mu.Lock()
  if g.abandoned == nil {
   g.abandoned = err
  }
  g.mu.Unlock()
 }
 return err
}

func (g *guard) Audio(ctx context.Context, path string, stream int, fromS, durS float64) ([]int16, error) {
 if err := g.check(); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 pcm, err := g.Decoder.Audio(ctx, path, stream, fromS, durS)
 return pcm, g.note(err)
}
```

  plus the same for `Frames` and `Frame`. In `Handle`, right after the task
  decodes: `dec := &guard{Decoder: h.Decoder}` and pass `dec` where the task's
  code reads `h.Decoder` (thread it through `fingerprint`, `window` and `analyze`
  as a parameter, or set it on a per-task copy `hh := *h; hh.Decoder = dec`).
  At the end of `Handle`, after the loop that stores every file's record (F3.4's `h.store`):

```go
 if dec.abandoned != nil {
  return events.Discard("segments: an FFmpeg decode was abandoned; not redelivered into another stuck call", dec.abandoned)
 }
 return nil
```

  The error of a skipped file contains `abandoned`, which `clamp`s into its
  analysis result's `Message` and so into the stored record's `LastError.Message`.

```go
// decodeThreads is --decode-threads: an explicit value, else the cgroup's
// CPUs (GOMAXPROCS follows the quota) shared by the per-pod slots.
func decodeThreads(flag, slots, procs int) int {
 if flag > 0 {
  return flag
 }
 return max(1, procs/max(slots, 1))
}
```

  `cmd/markers/selfcheck.go`:

```go
type selfCheckReport struct {
 FFmpeg      ffruntime.Report `json:"ffmpeg"`
 ONNXRuntime string           `json:"onnxRuntime,omitempty"`
 Failures    []string         `json:"failures,omitempty"`
 OK          bool             `json:"ok"`
}

// selfCheck is `markers --self-check` (spec §3.7, §7.2.9, §10.1.1): FFmpeg 9
// with decode.Needs, and ONNX Runtime from $ORT_LIB_PATH, with no NATS and no
// pod environment. It prints the report as JSON and returns 0 or
// ExitMisconfigured. The detector is required here although markers runs
// without it: the image must carry it.
func selfCheck(w io.Writer, getenv func(string) string) int {
 var r selfCheckReport
 rep, err := ffruntime.Load()
 r.FFmpeg = rep
 if err == nil {
  err = ffruntime.Require(decode.Needs)
 }
 if err != nil {
  r.Failures = append(r.Failures, err.Error())
 }
 ort := getenv("ORT_LIB_PATH")
 if _, err := textdet.NewONNX(ort); err != nil {
  r.Failures = append(r.Failures, fmt.Sprintf("ONNX Runtime ($ORT_LIB_PATH=%q): %v", ort, err))
 } else {
  r.ONNXRuntime = ort
 }
 r.OK = len(r.Failures) == 0
 enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
 enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
 _ = enc.Encode(r)
 if !r.OK {
  return worker.ExitMisconfigured
 }
 return 0
}
```

  If `textdet.NewONNX` returns something that needs closing, close it after the check.

```go
// AudioProbeFromRaw reduces a probe to its first audio stream's AudioProbe:
// what both the in-process probe and the ffprobe oracle answer ProbeAudio
// with (spec 2026-10-06 §6.2).
func AudioProbeFromRaw(raw *Raw) (AudioProbe, error) {
 if raw == nil {
  return AudioProbe{}, ErrNoAudioStream
 }
 s := firstStream(raw.Streams, ffprobe.StreamAudio)
 if s == nil {
  return AudioProbe{}, ErrNoAudioStream
 }
 ap := AudioProbe{Codec: s.CodecName, BitrateKbps: roundKbps(s.BitRate)}
 if ap.BitrateKbps == 0 && raw.Format != nil {
  ap.BitrateKbps = roundKbps(raw.Format.BitRate)
 }
 if bits, err := strconv.Atoi(s.BitsPerRawSample); err == nil && bits > 0 {
  ap.SampleBits = bits
 } else if s.BitsPerSample > 0 {
  ap.SampleBits = s.BitsPerSample
 }
 return ap, nil
}

// AudioProbeFrom is AudioProbeFromRaw over ffprobe's decoded JSON.
func AudioProbeFrom(pd *ffprobe.ProbeData) (AudioProbe, error) {
 return AudioProbeFromRaw(&Raw{Format: pd.Format, Streams: pd.Streams})
}
```

```go
func testProber(t *testing.T) *Prober {
 t.Helper()
 nativetest.FFmpeg(t, Needs)
 p, err := New()
```

  `pkg/mediainfo/native/cancel_test.go` (package `native`):

```go
// A probe stuck in the kernel returns once its context ends and the grace
// passes, as the old subprocess's WaitDelay bounded it, and the stuck call is
// counted until it returns (spec §6.2 "Cancellation"). A FIFO nobody writes
// blocks the open in the kernel, where FFmpeg's interrupt callback cannot
// reach; opening its write end afterwards lets the stuck call finish.
func TestProbeHonoursItsContext(t *testing.T) {
 p := testProber(t)
 fifo := filepath.Join(t.TempDir(), "stalled.mkv")
 require.NoError(t, syscall.Mkfifo(fifo, 0o600))
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 100*time.Millisecond)
 defer cancel()
 start := time.Now()
 _, _, err := p.Probe(ctx, fifo)
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, mediainfo.ErrProbeAbandoned)
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, ffruntime.ErrAbandoned)
 assert.Less(t, time.Since(start), ffruntime.Grace+2*time.Second)
 assert.Equal(t, 1, ffruntime.Abandoned())
 w, err := os.OpenFile(fifo, os.O_WRONLY, 0) // meets the blocked open, then EOF
 require.NoError(t, err)
 require.NoError(t, w.Close())
 assert.Eventually(t, func() bool { return ffruntime.Abandoned() == 0 }, 5*time.Second, 10*time.Millisecond,
  "an abandoned call that returns is no longer counted")
}

// A probe the runtime abandons is ErrProbeAbandoned (non-transient for the
// probe worker), and enough of them fail the ffgo healthz (spec §6.6, §6.8
// TestAbandonedProbesFailHealth). Run in a child: the wedge is permanent for
// the process.
func TestAbandonedProbesFailHealth(t *testing.T) {
 if os.Getenv("NATIVE_ABANDON_CHILD") == "1" {
  p := testProber(t)
  readFirstFrame = func(*ffgo.Decoder, *ffgo.StreamInfo, *mediainfo.Raw) error { select {} }
  for range ffruntime.MaxAbandoned {
   ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Millisecond)
   _, _, err := p.Probe(ctx, "../../../test/data/mediainfo/sample_h264_8bit.mp4")
   cancel()
   if !errors.Is(err, mediainfo.ErrProbeAbandoned) {
    t.Fatalf("want ErrProbeAbandoned, got %v", err)
   }
  }
  if ffruntime.Healthz(nil) == nil {
   t.Fatal("the ffgo healthz check still passes after MaxAbandoned stuck probes")
  }
  return
 }
 testProber(t)
 cmd := exec.Command(os.Args[0], "-test.run=^TestAbandonedProbesFailHealth$", "-test.count=1")
 cmd.Env = append(os.Environ(), "NATIVE_ABANDON_CHILD=1")
 out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
 require.NoError(t, err, "%s", out)
}

// This process is the first to run concurrent ffgo probes (spec §6.8).
func TestNativeProbesInParallel(t *testing.T) {
 p := testProber(t)
 paths := []string{"../../../test/data/mediainfo/sample_hevc_10bit.mkv", "../../../test/data/mediainfo/sample_h264_8bit.mp4"}
 var wg sync.WaitGroup
 for g := range 8 {
  wg.Add(1)
  go func() {
   defer wg.Done()
   for i := range 5 {
    mi, _, err := p.Probe(context.Background(), paths[(g+i)%2])
    assert.NoError(t, err)
    assert.NotNil(t, mi)
   }
  }()
 }
 wg.Wait()
}

func TestProbeMissingFileReturnsWrappedError(t *testing.T) {
 p := testProber(t)
 _, _, err := p.Probe(context.Background(), "../../../test/data/mediainfo/does-not-exist.mkv")
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, fs.ErrNotExist)
 assert.ErrorContains(t, err, "mediainfo: probe")
}
```

```go
// field clustarr stores, read through ffgo (spec 2026-10-06 §6). Only
// app/import/agent and app/squash/worker/inprocess import it, so only
// cmd/agent and cmd/transcode link it; it touches no FFmpeg log callback
```
