  `pkg/mediainfo/native/prober.go`:

```go
// Needs names the demuxers the library's files use (spec §6.2).
var Needs = ffruntime.Needs{Demuxers: []string{"matroska", "mov", "mpegts", "avi", "flac", "mp3", "ogg", "wav"}}

// Prober probes in-process. New is the only way to get one: Disposition and
// ChannelLayout need the shim, so a Prober never exists without it.
type Prober struct{ _ [0]func() }

var _ mediainfo.Prober = (*Prober)(nil)

// New loads FFmpeg 9 and the shim (ffruntime.Load) and requires Needs.
func New() (*Prober, error) {
 if err := ffruntime.Require(Needs); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 return &Prober{}, nil
}

// Probe reads path: the container, its streams and chapters, and the first
// frame of v:0. It runs under ffruntime.Do, and FFmpeg's I/O under the
// context (ffgo.WithInterrupt).
func (p *Prober) Probe(ctx context.Context, path string) (*commonv1.MediaInfo, *mediainfo.Raw, error) {
 ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "mediainfo.native.Probe")
 defer span.End()
 var raw *mediainfo.Raw
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (err error) { raw, err = probeRaw(ctx, path, true); return err })
 if err != nil {
  err = probeErr(path, err)
  tracing.RecordError(span, err)
  return nil, nil, err
 }
 return mediainfo.FromRaw(raw), raw, nil
}

// ProbeAudio reads path's first audio stream: the header only, no frame.
func (p *Prober) ProbeAudio(ctx context.Context, path string) (mediainfo.AudioProbe, error) {
 ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "mediainfo.native.ProbeAudio")
 defer span.End()
 var ap mediainfo.AudioProbe
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) error {
  raw, err := probeRaw(ctx, path, false)
  if err == nil {
   ap, err = mediainfo.AudioProbeFromRaw(raw)
  }
  return err
 })
 if err != nil {
  err = probeErr(path, err)
  tracing.RecordError(span, err)
  return mediainfo.AudioProbe{}, err
 }
 return ap, nil
}

func probeErr(path string, err error) error {
 if errors.Is(err, ffruntime.ErrAbandoned) {
  return fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: probe %s: %w: %w", path, mediainfo.ErrProbeAbandoned, err)
 }
 return fmt.Errorf("mediainfo: probe %s: %w", path, err)
}
```

  `pkg/mediainfo/native/probe.go` (the moved file): `package native`; the old
  `func (Engine) Probe` body becomes `probeRaw`, opening the file as §6.2 says and
  taking v:0 (the first video stream by index, as `-select_streams v:0` does):

```go
// probeRaw builds the Raw ffprobe's JSON would decode to (spec §6.3); with
// frame it also merges v:0's first decoded frame, as the second ffprobe call did.
func probeRaw(ctx context.Context, path string, frame bool) (*mediainfo.Raw, error) {
 st, err := os.Stat(path)
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 d, err := ffgo.NewDecoder(path, ffgo.WithAVOptions(map[string]string{"scan_all_pmts": "1"}), ffgo.WithInterrupt(ctx.Done()))
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = d.Close() }()
 raw := &mediainfo.Raw{Format: &ffprobe.Format{
  Filename: path, FormatName: d.FormatName(), NBStreams: len(d.Streams()),
  DurationSeconds: d.Duration().Seconds(), Size: strconv.FormatInt(st.Size(), 10),
  BitRate: positive(d.BitRate()), TagList: tags(d.GetMetadata()),
 }}
 var v0 *ffgo.StreamInfo
 for _, s := range d.Streams() {
  raw.Streams = append(raw.Streams, stream(s))
  if s.Type == ffgo.MediaTypeVideo && v0 == nil {
   v0 = s
   if rec, ok, err := ffgo.StreamSideData(s.CodecParameters(), ffgo.PacketSideDOVIConf()); err == nil && ok {
    raw.Dovi = doviRecord(rec)
   }
  }
 }
 for i, c := range d.GetChapters() {
  raw.Chapters = append(raw.Chapters, &ffprobe.Chapter{
   ID: int64(i), StartTimeSeconds: c.Start.Seconds(), EndTimeSeconds: c.End.Seconds(),
   TagList: ffprobe.Tags{"title": c.Title},
  })
 }
 if frame && v0 != nil {
  if err := readFirstFrame(d, v0, raw); err != nil {
   raw.FrameErr = err
   if err := mediainfo.IncompleteHDR(raw); err != nil {
    return nil, err
   }
  }
 }
 return raw, nil
}

// stream is one stream as ffprobe's JSON decodes it. W8.4 completes it to
// every field §6.3 lists.
func stream(s *ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffprobe.Stream {
 ps := &ffprobe.Stream{
  Index: s.Index, CodecName: s.Codec, CodecType: codecType(s.Type), BitRate: positive(s.BitRate),
  TagList: tags(s.Metadata), Disposition: disposition(s.Disposition),
  Tags: ffprobe.StreamTags{
   Language: s.Metadata["language"], Title: s.Metadata["title"], Encoder: s.Metadata["encoder"],
   CreationTime: s.Metadata["creation_time"], Location: s.Metadata["location"],
  },
 }
 switch s.Type {
 case ffgo.MediaTypeVideo:
  ps.Width, ps.Height, ps.PixFmt = s.Width, s.Height, ffgo.PixelFormatName(s.PixelFmt)
  if s.FrameRate.Den > 0 {
   ps.RFrameRate = fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", s.FrameRate.Num, s.FrameRate.Den)
  }
  ps.SideDataList = staticHDRSideData(s)
 case ffgo.MediaTypeAudio:
  ps.Channels, ps.ChannelLayout, ps.SampleRate = s.Channels, s.ChannelLayout, strconv.Itoa(s.SampleRate)
 }
 return ps
}
```

  The rest of the moved file (`staticHDRSideData`, `readFirstFrame`,
  `firstFramePackets`, `firstFrame`, `masteringDisplay`, `doviRecord`,
  `codecType`, `disposition`, `tags`, `positive`, `colourNames`) is unchanged
  except: `firstFrame` opens the decoder with
  `d.NewStreamDecoder(v.Index, &ffgo.StreamDecoderConfig{Threads: 1})`; and
  `staticHDRSideData` is now set on every video stream (ffprobe prints each
  stream's side data, and `IncompleteHDR` reads the primary stream's). Its doc
  comment is rewritten: "probeRaw reads path as ffprobe does…" with no mention of
  the transcoder image.

  `app/squash/worker/inprocess/inprocess.go`:

```go
// Engine runs the standard's plans in-process; it probes through prober.
type Engine struct{ prober *native.Prober }

// New loads FFmpeg 9 and the shim (pkg/ffruntime, through native.New) and
// builds the in-process prober. The error names what is missing; the worker
// then runs no ffgo task.
func New() (Engine, error) {
 p, err := native.New()
 if err != nil {
  return Engine{}, err
 }
 return Engine{prober: p}, nil
}
```

  `app/squash/worker/inprocess/probe.go` (new, small):

```go
// Probe reads path through the in-process prober (pkg/mediainfo/native).
func (e Engine) Probe(ctx context.Context, path string) (*commonv1.MediaInfo, *mediainfo.Raw, error) {
 if e.prober == nil {
  return nil, nil, errors.New("inprocess: Engine{} has no prober: build it with New")
 }
 return e.prober.Probe(ctx, path)
}
```

```go
// validString is ffprobe's string validation: one U+FFFD per sequence
// av_utf8_decode (flags 0) rejects (spec §6.2).
func TestValidStringMatchesFFprobe(t *testing.T) {
 for _, tt := range []struct{ name, in, want string }{
  {"ascii", "Chapter 1", "Chapter 1"},
  {"utf-8", "Kapitel ü", "Kapitel ü"},
  {"latin-1 byte", "Kapitel \xfc", "Kapitel �"},
  {"stray continuation", "a\x80b", "a�b"},
  {"truncated sequence consumes one byte", "a\xe2\x82", "a��"},
  {"overlong '/'", "a\xc0\xafb", "a�b"},
  {"encoded surrogate", "a\xed\xa0\x80b", "a�b"},
  {"U+FFFE", "a\xef\xbf\xbeb", "a�b"},
  {"U+FFFF", "a\xef\xbf\xbfb", "a�b"},
  {"above U+10FFFF", "a\xf4\x90\x80\x80b", "a�b"},
  {"five-byte form", "a\xf8\x88\x80\x80\x80b", "a�b"},
  {"0xFE lead", "a\xfeb", "a�b"},
  {"control codes are kept", "a\x01b", "a\x01b"},
  {"stops at NUL as C does", "ab\x00cd", "ab"},
 } {
  t.Run(tt.name, func(t *testing.T) { assert.Equal(t, tt.want, validString(tt.in)) })
 }
}

// print_time: N/A (omitted) at AV_NOPTS_VALUE, else "%f" of ts*num/den.
func TestFFprobeTime(t *testing.T) {
 tb := ffgo.NewRational(1, 1_000_000_000)
 assert.Equal(t, "9300.000000", ffprobeTime(9_300_000_000_000, tb), "past int64 microseconds of a 1/1e9 base")
 assert.Empty(t, ffprobeTime(avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE, tb))
```

  `pkg/mediainfo/native/parity_test.go` (package `native`, internal, so it reuses
  `probeFixtures`; no build tag; skips without ffprobe unless `CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`):

```go
// TestNativeProbeMatchesFFprobe is §6.7's rule: for every fixture ffprobe
// probes, the native MediaInfo is deep-equal to the oracle's with nothing
// blanked, and so are the Raw leaves FromProbe and IncompleteHDR read,
// ProbeAudio, and the standard's plan.
func TestNativeProbeMatchesFFprobe(t *testing.T) {
 nativetest.SameFFmpeg(t, nativetest.Tool(t, "ffprobe"))
 p, err := New()
 require.NoError(t, err)
 oracle := ffprobeexec.Prober{}
 ctx := context.Background()
 for name, path := range parityFixtures(t) {
  t.Run(name, func(t *testing.T) {
   want, wantRaw, err := oracle.Probe(ctx, path)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   got, gotRaw, err := p.Probe(ctx, path)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.Equal(t, want, got, "MediaInfo")
   assert.Equal(t, rawLeaves(wantRaw), rawLeaves(gotRaw), "Raw leaves")
   wantA, wantErr := oracle.ProbeAudio(ctx, path)
   gotA, gotErr := p.ProbeAudio(ctx, path)
   assert.Equal(t, wantErr == nil, gotErr == nil, "ProbeAudio errors: %v / %v", wantErr, gotErr)
   assert.Equal(t, wantA, gotA, "ProbeAudio")
   if want.VideoCodec != "" {
    wantInfo, err := transcode.FromProbe(want, wantRaw)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    gotInfo, err := transcode.FromProbe(got, gotRaw)
    require.NoError(t, err)
    assert.Equal(t, wantInfo, gotInfo, "transcode.FromProbe")
    prof := standard.Profile{Name: "p", Hash: "h", Quality: 22, Container: transcode.ContainerMKV}
    hw := standard.Hardware{Tier: transcode.TierCPUx265}
    assert.Equal(t, standard.Plan(wantInfo, prof, hw).Hash(), standard.Plan(gotInfo, prof, hw).Hash(), "the standard's plan")
   }
  })
 }
}

type streamLeaves struct {
 Profile, RFrameRate, FieldOrder, ColorRange, ColorSpace, ColorTransfer, ColorPrimaries, Duration, SampleRate, BitRate, BitsPerRawSample, ChannelLayout string
 Level, BitsPerSample, Channels                                                                                                                         int
 Disposition                                                                                                                                            ffprobe.StreamDisposition
}

type leaves struct {
 Streams                                                    []streamLeaves
 Dovi                                                       *mediainfo.DoviRecord
 MasteringDisplay                                           *mediainfo.MasteringDisplay
 ContentLight                                               *mediainfo.ContentLight
 HasHDR10Plus                                               bool
 ColorPrimaries, ColorTransfer, ColorSpace, ColorRange      string
 FormatName, FormatBitRate, Size                            string
 Duration                                                   float64
 Chapters                                                   [][2]float64
}

func rawLeaves(r *mediainfo.Raw) leaves {
 l := leaves{Dovi: r.Dovi, MasteringDisplay: r.MasteringDisplay, ContentLight: r.ContentLight, HasHDR10Plus: r.HasHDR10Plus,
  ColorPrimaries: r.ColorPrimaries, ColorTransfer: r.ColorTransfer, ColorSpace: r.ColorSpace, ColorRange: r.ColorRange,
  FormatName: r.Format.FormatName, FormatBitRate: r.Format.BitRate, Size: r.Format.Size, Duration: r.Format.DurationSeconds}
 for _, s := range r.Streams {
  l.Streams = append(l.Streams, streamLeaves{Profile: s.Profile, RFrameRate: s.RFrameRate, FieldOrder: s.FieldOrder,
   ColorRange: s.ColorRange, ColorSpace: s.ColorSpace, ColorTransfer: s.ColorTransfer, ColorPrimaries: s.ColorPrimaries,
   Duration: s.Duration, SampleRate: s.SampleRate, BitRate: s.BitRate, BitsPerRawSample: s.BitsPerRawSample,
   ChannelLayout: s.ChannelLayout, Level: s.Level, BitsPerSample: s.BitsPerSample, Channels: s.Channels, Disposition: s.Disposition})
 }
 for _, c := range r.Chapters {
  l.Chapters = append(l.Chapters, [2]float64{c.StartTimeSeconds, c.EndTimeSeconds})
 }
 return l
}

// parityFixtures is probeFixtures (moved from inprocess in W8.3) plus
// §6.7's list, made by the pinned ffmpeg, plus the committed fixtures.
func parityFixtures(t *testing.T) map[string]string {
 t.Helper()
 bin := nativetest.Tool(t, "ffmpeg")
 dir := t.TempDir()
 write := func(name, body string) string {
  p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body), 0o644))
  return p
 }
 mk := func(name string, args ...string) string {
  out := filepath.Join(dir, name)
  a := append([]string{"-hide_banner", "-loglevel", "error", "-y"}, args...)
  b, err := exec.Command(bin, append(a, out)...).CombinedOutput()
  require.NoError(t, err, "%s: %s", name, b)
  return out
 }
 cat := func(parts ...[]string) []string { return slices.Concat(parts...) }
 v := []string{"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=d=2:s=320x180:r=24"}
 sine := func(f string) []string { return []string{"-f", "lavfi", "-i", "sine=d=2:sample_rate=48000" + f} }
 late := write("late.ffmeta", ";FFMETADATA1\n[CHAPTER]\nTIMEBASE=1/1000000000\nSTART=9300000000000\nEND=9400000000000\ntitle=Late\n")
 bad := write("bad.ffmeta", ";FFMETADATA1\n[CHAPTER]\nTIMEBASE=1/1000\nSTART=0\nEND=1000\ntitle="+strings.Repeat("\xe9", 140)+"\n")
 cover := mk("cover.png", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "color=c=red:s=16x16:d=1", "-frames:v", "1")
 fx := probeFixtures(t)
 fx["pcm in matroska"] = mk("pcm.mkv", cat(v, sine(""), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "pcm_s16le", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["chapters at 9300 s"] = mk("late.mkv", cat(v, []string{"-i", late, "-map", "0", "-map_chapters", "1", "-c:v", "libx264"})...)
 fx["field-coded h264 in mpeg-ts"] = mk("interlaced.ts", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=d=2:s=720x576:r=25",
  "-vf", "setfield=tff", "-c:v", "libx264", "-flags", "+ildct+ilme", "-x264-params", "tff=1", "-f", "mpegts")
 fx["dts 5.1"] = mk("dts.mkv", cat(v, sine(",aformat=channel_layouts=5.1"), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "dca", "-strict", "-2", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["e-ac-3 5.1 in mp4"] = mk("eac3.mp4", cat(v, sine(",aformat=channel_layouts=5.1"), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "eac3", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["truehd"] = mk("truehd.mkv", cat(v, sine(",aformat=channel_layouts=5.1(side)"), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "truehd", "-strict", "-2", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["vfr matroska"] = mk("vfr.mkv", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=d=4:s=320x180:r=30", "-vf", "select='not(mod(n\\,3))'", "-fps_mode", "vfr", "-c:v", "libx264")
 fx["mpeg-2 interlaced"] = mk("mpeg2i.mkv", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "testsrc2=d=2:s=720x576:r=25", "-vf", "setfield=tff", "-c:v", "mpeg2video", "-flags", "+ildct+ilme")
 fx["avi with mp3"] = mk("mp3.avi", cat(v, sine(""), []string{"-c:v", "mpeg4", "-c:a", "libmp3lame", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["mov pcm 24-bit"] = mk("pcm24.mov", cat(v, sine(""), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "pcm_s24le", "-shortest"})...)
 fx["flac 24-bit"] = mk("flac24.flac", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "sine=d=2:sample_rate=96000", "-c:a", "flac", "-sample_fmt", "s32", "-bits_per_raw_sample", "24")
 fx["alac 24-bit"] = mk("alac24.m4a", "-f", "lavfi", "-i", "sine=d=2:sample_rate=96000", "-c:a", "alac", "-sample_fmt", "s32p", "-bits_per_raw_sample", "24")
 fx["mp4 with the profile tag"] = mk("tagged.mp4", cat(v, []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-metadata", "CLUSTARR_PROFILE=p@h", "-movflags", "+use_metadata_tags"})...)
 fx["matroska with BPS tags"] = mk("bps.mkv", cat(v, sine(""), []string{"-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "aac", "-shortest",
  "-metadata:s:v:0", "BPS=1234567", "-metadata:s:v:0", "BPS-eng=1234567"})...)
 fx["mp4 with cover art"] = mk("cover.mp4", cat(v, []string{"-i", cover, "-map", "0", "-map", "1", "-c:v:0", "libx264",
  "-c:v:1", "mjpeg", "-disposition:v:1", "attached_pic"})...)
 fx["invalid utf-8 titles"] = mk("badutf8.mkv", cat(v, sine(""), []string{"-i", bad, "-map", "0", "-map", "1", "-map_chapters", "2",
  "-c:v", "libx264", "-c:a", "aac", "-shortest", "-metadata", "title=Caf\xe9",

 for _, f := range []string{"audio_flac_24bit.flac", "sample_h264_8bit.mp4", "sample_hevc_10bit.mkv"} {

// TestNativeProbeMatchesFFprobeOnACorpus is the cutover gate (§11.2 gate 2,
// OD16): every file under CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_DIR, read-only, native
// against ffprobe; with CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_MEDIAFILES (a `kubectl get
// mediafiles -o json` dump) also against the stored status.mediaInfo of every
// file whose stat hash still equals its probeHash. Every diff is reported.
func TestNativeProbeMatchesFFprobeOnACorpus(t *testing.T) {
 dir, dump := os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_DIR"), os.Getenv("CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_MEDIAFILES")
 if dir == "" && dump == "" {
  t.Skip("set CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_DIR and/or CLUSTARR_PROBE_PARITY_MEDIAFILES to run the corpus gate")
 }
 rep := nativetest.FFmpeg(t, Needs)
 t.Logf("FFmpeg: %+v", rep) // §11.2: each report's first line is ffruntime.Report
 p, err := New()
 require.NoError(t, err)
 ctx := context.Background()
 diffs, files := 0, 0
 if dir != "" {
  ffprobe := nativetest.Tool(t, "ffprobe")
  nativetest.SameFFmpeg(t, ffprobe)
  require.NoError(t, filepath.WalkDir(dir, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
   if err != nil || d.IsDir() || !isMedia(path) {
    return err
   }
   files++
   want, _, werr := ffprobeexec.Prober{}.Probe(ctx, path)
   if werr != nil {
    return nil // §6.7: only files ffprobe probes successfully
   }
   got, _, gerr := p.Probe(ctx, path)
   if gerr != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(want, got) {
    diffs++
    t.Errorf("%s: %v\n%s", path, gerr, cmp.Diff(want, got))
   }
   return nil
  }))
 }
 if dump != "" {
  var list catalogv1alpha1.MediaFileList
  b, err := os.ReadFile(dump)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  require.NoError(t, json.Unmarshal(b, &list))
  for _, mf := range list.Items {
   st, err := os.Stat(mf.Spec.Path)
   if err != nil || mf.Status.MediaInfo == nil || mediainfo.ProbeHash(mf.Spec.Path, st.Size(), st.ModTime()) != mf.Status.ProbeHash {
    continue
   }
   files++
   got, _, gerr := p.Probe(ctx, mf.Spec.Path)
   if gerr != nil || !reflect.DeepEqual(mf.Status.MediaInfo, got) {
    diffs++
    t.Errorf("%s (%s/%s): %v\n%s", mf.Spec.Path, mf.Namespace, mf.Name, gerr, cmp.Diff(mf.Status.MediaInfo, got))
   }
  }
 }
 t.Logf("%d files compared, %d differ", files, diffs)
}
```

```go
// codecName is codec_name as ffprobe prints it: a codec with no descriptor
// (ffgo's avcodec_get_name gives "none" or "unknown_codec") is omitted.
func codecName(c string) string {
 if c == "none" || c == "unknown_codec" {
  return ""
 }
 return c
}

// profile is ffprobe's rule: the profile's name, else its number unless it
// is AV_PROFILE_UNKNOWN, else omitted.
func profile(id ffgo.CodecID, p int) string {
 if n := ffgo.ProfileName(id, p); n != "" {
  return n
 }
 if p != ffgo.ProfileUnknown {
  return strconv.Itoa(p)
 }
 return ""
}

// ffprobeTime is print_time: "%f" of ts*av_q2d(tb), "" (N/A, which JSON
// omits) at AV_NOPTS_VALUE.
func ffprobeTime(ts int64, tb ffgo.Rational) string {
 if ts == avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE || tb.Den == 0 {
  return ""
 }
 return fmt.Sprintf("%f", float64(ts)*(float64(tb.Num)/float64(tb.Den)))
}

// ffprobeSeconds is ffprobeTime as go-ffprobe's `,string` float decodes it.
func ffprobeSeconds(ts int64, tb ffgo.Rational) float64 {
 v, _ := strconv.ParseFloat(ffprobeTime(ts, tb), 64)
 return v
}

// validString is fftools/textformat/avtextformat.c validate_string with
// string_validation=replace and U+FFFD: each sequence av_utf8_decode (flags
// 0) rejects becomes one U+FFFD. Like C, it stops at the first NUL.
func validString(s string) string {
 if i := strings.IndexByte(s, 0); i >= 0 {
  s = s[:i]
 }
 if utf8.ValidString(s) && !strings.ContainsAny(s, "￾￿") {
  return s // Go's validity is av_utf8_decode's except for the two noncharacters
 }
 var b strings.Builder
 for i := 0; i < len(s); {
  n, ok := utf8Decode(s[i:])
  if ok {
   b.WriteString(s[i : i+n])
  } else {
   b.WriteString("�")
  }
  i += n
 }
 return b.String()
}

// utf8Decode is libavutil/avstring.c av_utf8_decode with flags 0: how many
// bytes one call consumes, and whether they decode to an accepted code
// point. An incomplete sequence or a bad continuation consumes one byte.
func utf8Decode(s string) (n int, ok bool) {
 code := uint64(s[0])
 if code&0xc0 == 0x80 || code >= 0xfe {
  return 1, false
 }
 top := (code & 128) >> 1
 p, tail := 1, 0
 for code&top != 0 {
  tail++
  if p >= len(s) {
   return 1, false
  }
  tmp := int(s[p]) - 128
  p++
  if tmp>>6 != 0 {
   return 1, false
  }
  code = code<<6 + uint64(tmp)
  top <<= 5
 }
 code &= top<<1 - 1
 overlong := [6]uint64{0, 0x80, 0x800, 0x10000, 0x200000, 0x4000000}
 switch {
 case code < overlong[tail], code >= 1<<31,
  code > 0x10ffff, code >= 0xd800 && code <= 0xdfff, code == 0xfffe || code == 0xffff:
  return p, false
 }
 return p, true
}

// tags is an AVDictionary as ffprobe prints it: keys and values validated.
func tags(md ffgo.Metadata) ffprobe.Tags {
 if len(md) == 0 {
  return nil
 }
 out := make(ffprobe.Tags, len(md))
 for k, v := range md {
  out[validString(k)] = validString(v)
 }
 return out
}

// streamTags is go-ffprobe's StreamTags.setFrom over the validated tags.
func streamTags(t ffprobe.Tags) ffprobe.StreamTags {
 get := func(k string) string { v, _ := t.GetString(k); return v }
 rotate, _ := t.GetInt("rotate")
 return ffprobe.StreamTags{Rotate: int(rotate), CreationTime: get("creation_time"), Language: get("language"),
  Title: get("title"), Encoder: get("encoder"), Location: get("location")}
}
```

  (`tags` replaces the moved file's version; delete that one.)

  In `probe.go`, `stream` becomes the complete §6.3 mapping:

```go
func stream(s *ffgo.StreamInfo) *ffprobe.Stream {
 md := tags(s.Metadata)
 ps := &ffprobe.Stream{
  Index: s.Index, CodecName: codecName(s.Codec), CodecType: codecType(s.Type),
  Profile: profile(s.CodecID, s.Profile), BitRate: positive(s.BitRate),
  RFrameRate: fmt.Sprintf("%d/%d", s.RealFrameRate.Num, s.RealFrameRate.Den), // always printed, 0/0 included
  StartTime: ffprobeTime(s.StartTime, s.TimeBase), Duration: ffprobeTime(s.Duration, s.TimeBase),
  TagList: md, Tags: streamTags(md), Disposition: disposition(s.Disposition),
 }
 if s.BitsPerRawSample > 0 {
  ps.BitsPerRawSample = strconv.Itoa(s.BitsPerRawSample)
 }
 switch s.Type {
 case ffgo.MediaTypeVideo:
  ps.Width, ps.Height, ps.Level = s.Width, s.Height, s.Level
  if s.PixelFmt >= 0 {
   ps.PixFmt = ffgo.PixelFormatName(s.PixelFmt)
  }
  ps.FieldOrder = s.FieldOrder.String()
  ps.ColorPrimaries, ps.ColorTransfer, ps.ColorSpace, ps.ColorRange = colourNames(s.Color)
  ps.SideDataList = staticHDRSideData(s)
 case ffgo.MediaTypeAudio:
  ps.SampleRate, ps.Channels = strconv.Itoa(s.SampleRate), s.Channels
  if s.ChannelOrder != ffgo.ChannelOrderUnspec {
   ps.ChannelLayout = s.ChannelLayout
  }
  ps.BitsPerSample = ffgo.BitsPerSample(s.CodecID)
 }
 return ps
}
```

**Spec:** §7.4 (consumers table: `cmd/transcode`; "Logging"), §3.8 (start order), §6.7 (OD17), §6.8 (app/squash rows), §4.5.5 (`Require` `pkg/ffruntime`)

> **2cbbb2c1 note.** With `2cbbb2c1` on the branch, `inprocess.Engine.{PrepareGraft,EncodeGraft,CheckGraft}` (`inprocess/graft.go`) call FFmpeg as `Encode` does. Like `Encode` and `Measure`, none of them runs under `ffruntime.Do` (§7.4: `cmd/transcode` gates with `Load` and `Require` only; `Do` is for probe, decode and extraction, and an abandoned transcode call would count toward the wedge). `EncodeGraft` reaches FFmpeg through `engine.Run`, whose `logTail.install` becomes `ffruntime.Capture` here, so the graft's lines land in the task's one tail (§7.4 "Logging"). `PrepareGraft` and `CheckGraft` log through the trampoline `RouteLog` installs. `inprocess/graft.go` needs no edit; Step 4's `$ENVTEST $NATIVE go test ./app/squash/worker/` then runs `app/squash/worker/graft_envtest_test.go` (also `2cbbb2c1`'s) through the gate, and it must PASS, not SKIP. > instead of reading a termination log (Steps 1 and 3). Step 4's envtest runs

```go
// New loads FFmpeg 9 and the shim, requires class's encoders, muxers and
// filters (the image's self-check list) and builds the in-process prober
// (spec §7.4).
func New(class transcode.Hardware) (Engine, error) {
 if err := ffruntime.Require(needsFor(class)); err != nil {
  return Engine{}, err
 }
 p, err := native.New()
 if err != nil {
  return Engine{}, err
 }
 return Engine{prober: p}, nil
}

// needsFor is a pool class's self-check needs, as ffruntime.Needs.
func needsFor(class transcode.Hardware) ffruntime.Needs {
 c := selfcheck.ClassCPU
 switch class {
 case transcode.HardwareNVIDIA:
  c = selfcheck.ClassCUDA
 case transcode.HardwareIntel:
  c = selfcheck.ClassIntel
 }
 n := selfcheck.Needs[c]
 return ffruntime.Needs{Encoders: n.Encoders, Muxers: n.Muxers, Filters: n.Filters}
}
```

    (error path unchanged: `WorkerExitRetriable`), then `ffruntime.RouteLog(log)`;
- the graft's gate, a helper the pod calls where it called `graft.Run` (after `Claim`, before
    `Answer`; the answer is the helper's result):

```go
// graftWithFFmpeg runs one graft behind the runtime gate: an image that
// cannot load FFmpeg 9 and the shim answers ReasonError naming why, never a
// graft.Run that fails inside a C call (spec 2026-10-06 §7.4).
func graftWithFFmpeg(ctx context.Context, t grafttask.Task, dataDir string, log *slog.Logger) grafttask.Result {
 if _, err := ffruntime.Load(); err != nil {
  return grafttask.Failed(grafttask.ReasonError, "FFmpeg is unavailable in this image: %v", err)
 }
 ffruntime.RouteLog(log)
 return graft.Run(ctx, t, graft.Options{DataDir: dataDir})
}
```

```go
// newProber is the import domain's prober; a variable for one test.
var newProber = func() (mediainfo.Prober, error) { return native.New() }

// registerProbe builds the domain's one in-process prober (spec §6.6), adds
// the process-level healthz check "ffgo" (§3.3) and the abandoned-calls
// gauge, and routes FFmpeg's log. Without FFmpeg 9 and the shim the domain
// does not start: the native image always carries them.
func registerProbe(ctx context.Context, live *k8s.Checks) (mediainfo.Prober, error) {
 p, err := newProber()
 if err != nil {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("import: the in-process probe is unavailable: %w", err)
 }
 if err := live.Add("ffgo", ffruntime.Healthz); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 if err := ffmetrics.Register(ctrlmetrics.Registry); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 ffruntime.RouteLog(logging.FromContext(ctx))
 return p, nil
}
```

  (`ctrlmetrics` is `sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime/pkg/metrics`.) In `Register`,
  where W4.86 put the domain's one `prober := ffprobeexec.Prober{}` (passed to
  `newProbeWorker(bus, prober, dataPath)`, `fileimport.NewWorker(c, bus, prober)` and
  `rescan.NewWorker(c, bus, prober)`), replace it with the result of
  `registerProbe(ctx, live)`, where `live` is the `*k8s.Checks` the registration
  returns as `Registration.Live` (allocate it if the registration had none), and
  return its error before any worker subscribes. Drop the `ffprobeexec` import, and
  reword the comment there that names ffprobe or `ffprobeexec` to "It answers through
  the domain's one in-process prober (registerProbe, spec §6.6)." (If W4.86 left
  `newProbeWorker(bus events.Bus, dataRoot string)` building its own prober, give it
  the prober parameter here, `newProbeWorker(bus events.Bus, prober mediainfo.Prober, dataRoot string)`:
  the probe worker must answer through `registerProbe`'s prober, not a second one.)
  Any other production file the W8.1 gate listed is converted the same way: it
  takes the domain's prober as a parameter.

- [ ] **Step 3: Implement.** `native.go`:

```go
// Package native extracts a text subtitle stream as SRT in-process, as
// `ffmpeg -i P -map 0:N -c:s srt -f srt -` did: FFmpeg's decoder and srt
// encoder (which apply the stream's ASS styles), framed in Go as
// libavformat/srtenc.c writes it (spec 2026-10-06 §7.3). Only
// app/caption/agent imports it.
package native

const MaxOutputBytes = 8 << 20 // the remote providers' maxSubtitleBytes

var (
 ErrTooLarge = errors.New("subtitles: embedded: extracted subtitle exceeds 8 MiB")
 ErrNotText  = errors.New("subtitles: embedded: not a text subtitle stream")
)

// Needs is what extraction asks of FFmpeg.
var Needs = ffruntime.Needs{Encoders: []string{"srt"}, Decoders: []string{"subrip", "ass", "ssa", "webvtt", "mov_text"}}

var maxOutput = MaxOutputBytes

var (
 us = ffgo.NewRational(1, 1_000_000)
 ms = ffgo.NewRational(1, 1000)
)

// Extract is an embedded.ExtractFunc.
func Extract(ctx context.Context, path string, stream int) ([]byte, error) {
 var out []byte
 err := ffruntime.Do(ctx, func(ctx context.Context) (err error) { out, err = extract(ctx, path, stream); return err })
 if err != nil {
  return nil, fmt.Errorf("subtitles: embedded: extract stream %d of %s: %w", stream, path, err)
 }
 return out, nil
}

func extract(ctx context.Context, path string, stream int) ([]byte, error) {
 in, err := ffgo.NewDecoderWithOptions(path, &ffgo.DecoderOptions{AVOptions: map[string]string{"scan_all_pmts": "1"}})
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = in.Close() }()
 var si *ffgo.StreamInfo
 for _, s := range in.Streams() {
  if s.Index == stream {
   si = s
  }
 }
 if si == nil || si.Type != ffgo.MediaTypeSubtitle || !embedded.IsTextCodec(si.Codec) {
  return nil, ErrNotText
 }
 if err := in.Discard(stream); err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 tr, err := in.NewSubtitleTranscoder(stream, "srt")
 if err != nil {
  return nil, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = tr.Close() }()
 off := ffgo.RescaleQ(-in.StartTime().Microseconds(), us, si.TimeBase) // ffmpeg(1)'s ts_offset without -ss
 var buf bytes.Buffer
 index := 0
 write := func(ev ffgo.SubtitleEvent) error {
  s, d := ffgo.RescaleQ(ev.PTS, us, ms), ev.Duration/1000
  if d < 0 {
   return nil // "Insufficient timestamps"
  }
  index++
  fmt.Fprintf(&buf, "%d\n%s --> %s\n", index, srtTime(s), srtTime(s+d))
  buf.Write(ev.Data)
  buf.WriteString("\n\n")
  if buf.Len() > maxOutput {
   return ErrTooLarge
  }
  return nil
 }
 for {
  if err := ctx.Err(); err != nil {
   return nil, err
  }
  p, err := in.ReadPacket()
  if err != nil {
   return nil, err
  }
  if p == nil {
   break
  }
  if p.StreamIndex() != stream {
   _ = p.Free()
   continue
  }
  if v := p.PTS(); v != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
   avcodec.SetPacketPTS(p.Raw(), v+off)
  }
  if v := p.DTS(); v != avutil.AV_NOPTS_VALUE {
   avcodec.SetPacketDTS(p.Raw(), v+off)
  }
  ev, ok, err := tr.Transcode(p)
  _ = p.Free()
  switch {
  case errors.Is(err, ffgo.ErrSubtitleDecode): // ffmpeg(1) logs it and goes on
  case err != nil:
   return nil, err // "Subtitle encoding failed" is fatal
  case ok:
   if err := write(ev); err != nil {
    return nil, err
   }
  }
 }
 for {
  ev, ok, err := tr.Transcode(nil) // the decoder's flush
  if err != nil && !errors.Is(err, ffgo.ErrSubtitleDecode) {
   return nil, err
  }
  if !ok {
   break
  }
  if err := write(ev); err != nil {
   return nil, err
  }
 }
 return buf.Bytes(), nil
}

// srtTime is srtenc.c's "%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d", C truncating division.
func srtTime(v int64) string {
 return fmt.Sprintf("%02d:%02d:%02d,%03d", int32(v/3600000), int32(v/60000)%60, int32(v/1000)%60, int32(v%1000))
}
```

```go
// extractNeeds is what extraction asks of FFmpeg; a variable for one test.
var extractNeeds = embeddednative.Needs

// registerExtraction gives the provider builder the in-process extractor
// (spec §7.3.1), adds the process-level healthz check "ffgo" and the
// abandoned-calls gauge, and routes FFmpeg's log. Without FFmpeg 9 and the
// srt encoder the domain does not start.
func registerExtraction(ctx context.Context, b *build.Builder, live *k8s.Checks) error {
 if err := ffruntime.Require(extractNeeds); err != nil {
  return fmt.Errorf("caption: embedded subtitle extraction is unavailable: %w", err)
 }
 if err := live.Add("ffgo", ffruntime.Healthz); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 if err := ffmetrics.Register(ctrlmetrics.Registry); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 ffruntime.RouteLog(logging.FromContext(ctx))
 b.Extract = embeddednative.Extract
 return nil
}
```

  In the registration, replace `providers.Extract = execextract.New("")` with
  `if err := registerExtraction(ctx, providers, live); err != nil { return <zero Registration>, err }`
  (`live` as in W8.6). `git rm -r pkg/subtitles/providers/embedded/execextract`.
  An abandoned extraction returns an error wrapping `ffruntime.ErrAbandoned`
  from `Download`, which the fetch worker answers as a failed attempt in its
  `clustarr-subtitles` record (F5.2) and the subtitles planner records in the
  MediaFile's `status.subtitles` for that file and probe hash (no change: §6.6).

```go
type selfCheckReport struct {
 PieceCompletion string            `json:"pieceCompletion"`
 FFmpeg          *ffruntime.Report `json:"ffmpeg,omitempty"`
 Failures        []string          `json:"failures,omitempty"`
 OK              bool              `json:"ok"`
}

// runSelfCheck is `agent --self-check` (§10.1.1): the cgo piece completion
// (R13) and FFmpeg 9 with what the import and caption domains need, with no
// domain, cluster or NATS. W9.6 adds par2go.
func runSelfCheck(w io.Writer) error {
 return SelfCheckWith(w, mediainfonative.Needs, embeddednative.Needs)
}

// SelfCheckWith is runSelfCheck with the FFmpeg needs given, for tests.
func SelfCheckWith(w io.Writer, needs ...ffruntime.Needs) error {
 r := selfCheckReport{PieceCompletion: pieceCompletion}
 if pieceCompletion != "sqlite" {
  r.Failures = append(r.Failures, fmt.Sprintf("the torrent piece completion is %q, not sqlite: this agent was built without cgo (R13)", pieceCompletion))
 }
 rep, err := ffruntime.Load()
 r.FFmpeg = &rep
 for _, n := range needs {
  if err == nil {
   err = ffruntime.Require(n)
  }
 }
 if err != nil {
  r.Failures = append(r.Failures, err.Error())
 }
 r.OK = len(r.Failures) == 0
 enc := json.NewEncoder(w)
 enc.SetIndent("", "  ")
 if err := enc.Encode(r); err != nil {
  return err
 }
 if !r.OK {
  return fmt.Errorf("self-check: %s", strings.Join(r.Failures, "; "))
 }
 return nil
}
```

```bash
#!/usr/bin/env bash
set -u
cd /home/appkins/src/mediactl/clustarr-unify
fail=0
miss() { echo "MISSING: $*"; fail=1; }

  go doc github.com/mediactl/par2go "$s" >/dev/null 2>&1 || miss "par2go.$s"

grep -q 'cli.Main(agent.NewCommand)' cmd/agent/main.go || miss "cmd/agent/main.go (W5.9)"

grep -q 'AS par2$' images/Dockerfile.native && echo "NOTE: Dockerfile.native already has a par2 stage; W9.7 verifies it instead of adding it"
grep -q 'libpar2shim' hack/native-assets.sh || miss "hack/native-assets.sh building libpar2shim.so (W6.7)"
grep -q '_ "github.com/mediactl/par2go"' hack/deps/deps.go || miss "hack/deps's par2go entry (W0.26; W9.3 deletes it)"
pin=$(sed -n 's/^PAR2GO_REF ?= *//p' Makefile)
```

```go
// Package par2test makes PAR2 sets for tests with the par2 CLI that `make
// native-assets` installs for this purpose only: par2go has no creator by
// design (spec 2026-10-06 §8.8, OD26). It runs a program, so it lives under
// test/, outside the exec guard, and only tests import it.
package par2test

// CreateSet runs `par2 c -q -b<blocks> -r<pct> [-n<files>] -- <index> <files>` in dir.
func CreateSet(t testing.TB, dir, index string, files []string, blocks, redundancyPercent, recoveryFiles uint32) {
 t.Helper()
 bin := nativetest.Tool(t, "par2")
 args := []string{"c", "-q", fmt.Sprintf("-b%d", blocks), fmt.Sprintf("-r%d", redundancyPercent)}
 if recoveryFiles > 0 {
  args = append(args, fmt.Sprintf("-n%d", recoveryFiles))
 }
 args = append(append(args, "--", index), files...)
 cmd := exec.Command(bin, args...)
 cmd.Dir = dir
 out, err := cmd.CombinedOutput()
 require.NoErrorf(t, err, "par2 create: %s", out)
}
```

```go
// TestMain makes this test binary the child: `<bin> par2-repair …` is the
// real one (ChildMain), `<bin> par2-fake <mode>` a fake that needs no library.
func TestMain(m *testing.M) {
 par2child.RunIfChild()
 if len(os.Args) > 2 && os.Args[1] == "par2-fake" {
  os.Exit(fakeChild(os.Args[2]))
 }
 os.Exit(m.Run())
}

func fakeChild(mode string) int {
 var n uint32
 if err := binary.Read(os.Stdin, binary.BigEndian, &n); err != nil {
  return 3
 }
 var req par2child.Request
 if err := gob.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(os.Stdin, int64(n))).Decode(&req); err != nil {
  return 3
 }
 out := os.NewFile(3, "par2-result")
 write := func(r par2child.Result) int { _ = gob.NewEncoder(out).Encode(r); return 0 }
 switch mode {
 case "echo":
  return write(par2child.Result{Status: par2.Repaired, BlocksNeeded: 7, Log: req.Index + "|" + strings.Join(req.Extras, "|")})
 case "cooperative":
  _, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, os.Stdin) // the parent's cancel closes stdin
  return write(par2child.Result{ErrKind: par2child.ErrKindCancelled, Err: "cancelled"})
 case "stubborn":
  time.Sleep(time.Minute)
  return 0
 case "die":
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "boom: the child crashed")
  return 2
 case "env":
  return write(par2child.Result{Log: strings.Join(os.Environ(), "\n")})
 }
 return 3
}

func fake(mode string) par2child.Exec {
 return par2child.Exec{Path: os.Args[0], Args: []string{"par2-fake", mode}, Env: []string{}, Grace: 300 * time.Millisecond}
}
```

```go
func TestExecReturnsTheChildsResult(t *testing.T) {
 res, err := fake("echo").Run(context.Background(), par2child.Request{Op: par2child.OpRepair, Index: "/d/x.par2", Extras: []string{"/d/a", "/d/b"}})
 require.NoError(t, err)

 require.NoError(t, err)

}

func TestExecCancelsTheChildCooperatively(t *testing.T) {

 defer cancel()
 res, err := fake("cooperative").Run(ctx, par2child.Request{Op: par2child.OpRepair})
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)

 _, err := fake("stubborn").Run(ctx, par2child.Request{Op: par2child.OpRepair})
 require.ErrorIs(t, err, context.DeadlineExceeded)
```

```go
func set(t *testing.T, pct uint32) (dir string, data []byte) {

func repair(t *testing.T, dir string, extras ...string) (par2child.Result, error) {

func TestInProcessVerdicts(t *testing.T) {
 lib(t)
 t.Run("intact", func(t *testing.T) {
  dir, _ := set(t, 20)
  res, err := repair(t, dir)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  assert.Equal(t, par2.AllCorrect, res.Status)
 })
 t.Run("damaged", func(t *testing.T) {
  dir, data := set(t, 50)
  damaged := slices.Clone(data)
  copy(damaged[16<<10:], bytes.Repeat([]byte{0}, 4<<10))
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(filepath.Join(dir, "movie.mkv"), damaged, 0o644))
  res, err := repair(t, dir)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  assert.Equal(t, par2.Repaired, res.Status)
  got, _ := os.ReadFile(filepath.Join(dir, "movie.mkv"))
  assert.Equal(t, data, got)
 })
 t.Run("renamed", func(t *testing.T) {
  dir, _ := set(t, 20)
  require.NoError(t, os.Rename(filepath.Join(dir, "movie.mkv"), filepath.Join(dir, "z75QO.part070.rar")))
  res, err := repair(t, dir, filepath.Join(dir, "z75QO.part070.rar"))
  require.NoError(t, err)
  assert.Equal(t, par2.Repaired, res.Status)
  assert.FileExists(t, filepath.Join(dir, "movie.mkv"))
 })
 t.Run("impossible", func(t *testing.T) {
  dir, _ := set(t, 5)
  require.NoError(t, os.Truncate(filepath.Join(dir, "movie.mkv"), 32<<10))
  res, err := repair(t, dir)
  if err == nil {
   assert.Equal(t, par2.RepairNotPossible, res.Status)
  }
  assert.Positive(t, res.BlocksNeeded)
 })
```

```go
// TestTheOnlyExecIsTheRepairChild: exec.Command and exec.CommandContext
// appear only in exec.go, inside Exec.run; exec.LookPath nowhere (§8.9 guard 4).
func TestTheOnlyExecIsTheRepairChild(t *testing.T) {
 files, err := filepath.Glob("*.go")
 require.NoError(t, err)
 for _, p := range files {
  if strings.HasSuffix(p, "_test.go") {
   continue
  }
  f, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), p, nil, 0)
  require.NoError(t, err)
  ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
   fn, ok := n.(*ast.FuncDecl)
   if !ok {
    return true
   }
   ast.Inspect(fn, func(n ast.Node) bool {
    sel, ok := n.(*ast.SelectorExpr)
    if !ok {
     return true
    }
    if x, ok := sel.X.(*ast.Ident); ok && x.Name == "exec" {
     switch {
     case sel.Sel.Name == "LookPath":
      t.Errorf("%s: %s calls exec.LookPath: the child is always os.Executable()", p, fn.Name.Name)
     case strings.HasPrefix(sel.Sel.Name, "Command") && (p != "exec.go" || fn.Name.Name != "run"):
      t.Errorf("%s: %s calls exec.%s: the only exec is Exec.run's child", p, fn.Name.Name, sel.Sel.Name)
     }
    }
    return true
   })
   return false
  })
 }
}
```

  `types.go`:

```go
const (
 ChildCommand = "par2-repair" // `agent par2-repair`
 DefaultGrace = 30 * time.Second
 reapSlack    = 5 * time.Second
 maxResult    = 1 << 20
)

var ErrChildDied = errors.New("par2child: repair child exited without a result")

type Op uint8

const (
 OpRepair Op = 1
 OpProbe  Op = 2
)

type ErrKind uint8

const (
 ErrKindNone ErrKind = iota
 ErrKindUnavailable
 ErrKindInvalidOptions
 ErrKindInsufficientCriticalData
 ErrKindIO
 ErrKindMemory
 ErrKindRepairFailed
 ErrKindLogic
 ErrKindCancelled
 ErrKindOther
)

var sentinels = map[ErrKind]error{
 ErrKindUnavailable: par2.ErrUnavailable, ErrKindInvalidOptions: par2.ErrInvalidOptions,
 ErrKindInsufficientCriticalData: par2.ErrInsufficientCriticalData, ErrKindIO: par2.ErrIO,
 ErrKindMemory: par2.ErrMemory, ErrKindRepairFailed: par2.ErrRepairFailed, ErrKindLogic: par2.ErrLogic,
 ErrKindCancelled: context.Canceled,
}

// kindOf maps an error onto the kind that crosses gob.
func kindOf(err error) ErrKind {
 if err == nil {
  return ErrKindNone
 }
 if errors.Is(err, context.Canceled) || errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded) {
  return ErrKindCancelled
 }
 for k, s := range sentinels {
  if errors.Is(err, s) {
   return k
  }
 }
 return ErrKindOther
}

type Request struct {
 Op                   Op
 Index                string   // absolute path of the index volume
 Dir                  string   // absolute base directory; targets are written here
 Extras               []string // absolute paths scanned as candidate targets
 Threads, FileThreads int
 MemoryLimit          int64
}

type Result struct {
 Status       par2.Status
 BlocksNeeded int
 Headers      par2.Headers
 Log          string  // par2go's Log
 ErrKind      ErrKind // the sentinel, which cannot cross gob as an error
 Err          string  // its text
 Library      string  // the loaded library's path, for logs
}

// Error is nil, or an error wrapping the matching par2go sentinel.
func (r Result) Error() error {
 if r.ErrKind == ErrKindNone {
  return nil
 }
 if s, ok := sentinels[r.ErrKind]; ok {
  return fmt.Errorf("%w: %s", s, r.Err)
 }
 return fmt.Errorf("par2child: %s", r.Err)
}

type Runner interface {
 Run(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error)
 Probe(ctx context.Context) error
}
```

  `inprocess.go`:

```go
// InProcess runs par2go in this process: the child itself, and tests.
type InProcess struct{}

func (InProcess) Run(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error) {
 res, err := par2.Repair(ctx, req.Index, par2.Options{Dir: req.Dir, ExtraFiles: req.Extras,
  MemoryLimit: req.MemoryLimit, Threads: req.Threads, FileThreads: req.FileThreads})
 out := Result{Status: res.Status, BlocksNeeded: res.BlocksNeeded, Headers: res.Headers, Log: res.Log,
  ErrKind: kindOf(err), Library: Library()}
 if err != nil {
  out.Err = err.Error()
 }
 if ctx.Err() != nil {
  return out, fmt.Errorf("par2child: run interrupted: %w", ctx.Err())
 }
 return out, out.Error()
}

func (InProcess) Probe(context.Context) error { return par2.Available() }
```

  `maps.go`:

```go
// Library is the path of the libpar2shim.so this process mapped, "" before
// par2go has loaded it (par2go exports no accessor for it).
func Library() string {
 b, err := os.ReadFile("/proc/self/maps")
 if err != nil {
  return ""
 }
 for _, line := range strings.Split(string(b), "\n") {
  if f := strings.Fields(line); len(f) >= 6 {
   if p := strings.Join(f[5:], " "); strings.HasPrefix(filepath.Base(p), "libpar2shim.so") {
    return p
   }
  }
 }
 return ""
}
```

  `tail.go`: `tailWriter` from `pkg/download/usenet/repair.go:326-348`, renamed
  `tailBuffer` with a mutex (stdout and stderr write concurrently):

```go
type tailBuffer struct {
 mu  sync.Mutex
 buf []byte
 max int
}

func (w *tailBuffer) Write(p []byte) (int, error) {
 w.mu.Lock()
 defer w.mu.Unlock()
 w.buf = append(w.buf, p...)
 if over := len(w.buf) - w.max; over > 0 {
  w.buf = append(w.buf[:0], w.buf[over:]...)
 }
 return len(p), nil
}

func (w *tailBuffer) String() string {
 w.mu.Lock()
 defer w.mu.Unlock()
 return string(w.buf)
}
```

  `exec.go` (§8.4.3, the parent):

```go
// Exec runs par2go in a child of this binary.
type Exec struct {
 Path  string        // "" = os.Executable()
 Args  []string      // nil = []string{ChildCommand}
 Env   []string      // nil = childEnv()
 Grace time.Duration // 0 = DefaultGrace
}

var unreaped atomic.Int64

// Unreaped counts children whose deadline, grace and reap slack passed
// without them exiting (a read blocked in the kernel); the usenet engine
// exports it as clustarr_par2_unreaped_children.
func Unreaped() int { return int(unreaped.Load()) }

func (e Exec) Run(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error) { return e.run(ctx, req) }

// Probe loads par2go in a child, so the engine never dlopens it itself.
func (e Exec) Probe(ctx context.Context) error {
 res, err := e.run(ctx, Request{Op: OpProbe})
 if err != nil {
  return err
 }
 return res.Error()
}

func (e Exec) run(ctx context.Context, req Request) (Result, error) {
 path := e.Path
 if path == "" {
  p, err := os.Executable()
  if err != nil {
   return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: find this binary: %w", par2.ErrUnavailable, err)
  }
  path = p
 }
 args, env, grace := e.Args, e.Env, e.Grace
 if args == nil {
  args = []string{ChildCommand}
 }
 if env == nil {
  env = childEnv(os.Getenv)
 }
 if grace == 0 {
  grace = DefaultGrace
 }
 cmd := exec.CommandContext(ctx, path, args...)
 cmd.Env = env
 cmd.SysProcAttr = &syscall.SysProcAttr{Setpgid: true}
 stdin, err := cmd.StdinPipe()
 if err != nil {
  return Result{}, err
 }
 r, w, err := os.Pipe()
 if err != nil {
  return Result{}, err
 }
 defer func() { _ = r.Close() }()
 cmd.ExtraFiles = []*os.File{w} // fd 3 in the child
 tail := &tailBuffer{max: 64 << 10}
 cmd.Stdout, cmd.Stderr = tail, tail
 cmd.Cancel = func() error { return stdin.Close() } // the child cancels par2go when stdin closes
 cmd.WaitDelay = grace                              // then os/exec kills it
 if err := cmd.Start(); err != nil {
  _ = w.Close()
  if errors.Is(err, fs.ErrNotExist) || errors.Is(err, fs.ErrPermission) {
   return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: start %s: %w", par2.ErrUnavailable, path, err)
  }
  return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("par2child: start %s: %w", path, err)
 }
 _ = w.Close()
 var body bytes.Buffer
 if err := gob.NewEncoder(&body).Encode(req); err != nil {
  return Result{}, err
 }
 _ = binary.Write(stdin, binary.BigEndian, uint32(body.Len()))
 _, _ = stdin.Write(body.Bytes()) // stdin stays open: closing it is the cancel
 got := make(chan []byte, 1)
 go func() { b, _ := io.ReadAll(io.LimitReader(r, maxResult)); got <- b }()
 waited := make(chan error, 1)
 go func() { waited <- cmd.Wait() }() // Wait calls Process.Wait first, which a D-state child blocks
 var waitErr error
 select {
 case waitErr = <-waited:
 case <-ctx.Done():
  t := time.NewTimer(grace + reapSlack)
  defer t.Stop()
  select {
  case waitErr = <-waited:
  case <-t.C:
   unreaped.Add(1)
   go func() { <-waited; unreaped.Add(-1) }()
   return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w (still not reaped %s after its deadline; it is reaped when its I/O returns)",
    ErrChildDied, ctx.Err(), grace+reapSlack)
  }
 }
 var res Result
 decodeErr := gob.NewDecoder(bytes.NewReader(<-got)).Decode(&res)
 switch {
 case ctx.Err() != nil:
  return res, fmt.Errorf("par2child: %w", ctx.Err())
 case decodeErr != nil:
  return Result{}, fmt.Errorf("%w: %v: %s", ErrChildDied, waitErr, strings.TrimSpace(tail.String()))
 case res.ErrKind == ErrKindUnavailable:
  return res, res.Error()
 }
 return res, res.Error()
}

// childEnv is the child's whole environment (§8.4.3).
func childEnv(getenv func(string) string) []string {
 var env []string
 for _, k := range []string{"PAR2GO_LIB", "LD_LIBRARY_PATH", "TMPDIR", "GODEBUG", "GOMAXPROCS"} {
  if v := getenv(k); v != "" {
   env = append(env, k+"="+v)
  }
 }
 return env
}
```

  `child.go` (§8.4.3, the child; no flags, logging, tracing, NATS or Kubernetes):

```go
// ChildMain is `agent par2-repair`. It reads one gob Request (a big-endian
// uint32 length first) from stdin, runs it, writes the gob Result to fd 3
// and returns 0; 3 on a malformed request, 2 when par2go cannot load.
// Closing stdin cancels the run.
func ChildMain(args []string) int {
 if len(args) > 0 && args[0] == "--self-check" {
  if err := par2.Available(); err != nil {
   fmt.Fprintf(os.Stderr, "par2go is unavailable (PAR2GO_LIB=%q): %v\n", os.Getenv("PAR2GO_LIB"), err)
   return 1
  }
  fmt.Println("par2go", Library())
  return 0
 }
 _ = os.WriteFile("/proc/self/oom_score_adj", []byte("1000"), 0) // a cgroup OOM picks the child, best effort
 var n uint32
 if err := binary.Read(os.Stdin, binary.BigEndian, &n); err != nil || n > maxResult {
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "par2child: malformed request")
  return 3
 }
 var req Request
 if err := gob.NewDecoder(io.LimitReader(os.Stdin, int64(n))).Decode(&req); err != nil {
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "par2child: malformed request:", err)
  return 3
 }
 ctx, cancel := context.WithCancel(context.Background())
 defer cancel()
 go func() { _, _ = io.Copy(io.Discard, os.Stdin); cancel() }()
 out := os.NewFile(3, "par2-result")
 write := func(r Result) int {
  if err := gob.NewEncoder(out).Encode(r); err != nil {
   fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "par2child: write the result:", err)
   return 3
  }
  return 0
 }
 if err := par2.Available(); err != nil {
  _ = write(Result{ErrKind: ErrKindUnavailable, Err: err.Error()})
  return 2
 }
 switch req.Op {
 case OpProbe:
  return write(Result{Library: Library()})
 case OpRepair:
  res, _ := InProcess{}.Run(ctx, req)
  return write(res)
 }
 fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "par2child: unknown op", req.Op)
 return 3
}

// RunIfChild runs ChildMain and exits when this process was started as the
// repair child (os.Args[1] == ChildCommand). cmd/agent calls it first in
// main, and so does the TestMain of every test binary whose code can build a
// usenet engine: the child is os.Executable(), which in a test is the test
// binary, and without the dispatch it would run the package's tests again.
func RunIfChild() {
 if len(os.Args) > 1 && os.Args[1] == ChildCommand {
  os.Exit(ChildMain(os.Args[2:]))
 }
}
```

```go
// Repairer verifies a par2 set and repairs it in place.
type Repairer interface {
 // Available reports whether repair can run at all; false makes a set
 // that needs repair fail with ErrPar2Unavailable, a local fault.
 Available() bool
 // Repair verifies dir against indexFile (a name inside dir), scanning
 // every other regular file in dir as a candidate target, and repairs
 // when it can. A cancelled ctx returns an error wrapping ctx.Err().
 Repair(ctx context.Context, dir, indexFile string) (Par2Result, error)
}

// noRepairer is a client configured with no repairer.
type noRepairer struct{}

func (noRepairer) Available() bool { return false }
func (noRepairer) Repair(context.Context, string, string) (Par2Result, error) {
 return Par2Result{}, ErrPar2Unavailable
}

// ErrPar2Crashed is par2 ending without a verdict: out of memory, or a child
// that died without a result. It says nothing about the release, so it is a
// local fault, writeError, and never blocklists (§13 OD22).
var ErrPar2Crashed = errors.New("usenet: par2 ended without a verdict")
```

  `par2lib.go`:

```go
// LibraryRepairer repairs through par2go, in a child of this binary in the
// engine (par2child.Exec{}) and in-process in tests (spec §8.5.2).
type LibraryRepairer struct {
 Runner      par2child.Runner
 Threads     int   // 0 = par2go's default (GOMAXPROCS)
 MemoryLimit int64 // 0 = par2go's default (1/8 of the cgroup)
 mu          sync.Mutex
 ready       bool
}

// Available probes the library (in a child) once it succeeds; a failure
// probes again next call, which happens only when a job needs repair.
func (r *LibraryRepairer) Available() bool {
 r.mu.Lock()
 defer r.mu.Unlock()
 if r.ready {
  return true
 }
 ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(context.Background(), 10*time.Second)
 defer cancel()
 r.ready = r.Runner.Probe(ctx) == nil
 return r.ready
}

func (r *LibraryRepairer) Repair(ctx context.Context, dir, indexFile string) (Par2Result, error) {
 ctx, span := tracing.Start(ctx, "usenet.par2.repair")
 defer span.End()
 abs, err := filepath.Abs(dir)
 if err != nil {
  return Par2Result{}, err
 }
 res, err := r.Runner.Run(ctx, par2child.Request{Op: par2child.OpRepair, Index: filepath.Join(abs, indexFile), Dir: abs,
  Extras: par2Extras(abs, indexFile), Threads: r.Threads, MemoryLimit: r.MemoryLimit})
 span.SetAttributes(attribute.String("par2.status", res.Status.String()), attribute.Int("par2.blocks_needed", res.BlocksNeeded),
  attribute.Int("par2.recovery_blocks", res.Headers.RecoveryBlocks), attribute.Int("par2.missing_files", res.Headers.MissingFiles))
 logging.FromContext(ctx).DebugContext(ctx, "par2 finished", "index", indexFile, "status", res.Status, "error", err, "library", res.Library)
 if errors.Is(err, par2child.ErrChildDied) && ctx.Err() != nil {
  logging.FromContext(ctx).ErrorContext(ctx, "par2 child did not exit after its deadline", "dir", abs, "error", err)
 }
 out, verr := par2Verdict(res, err)
 if verr != nil {
  tracing.RecordError(span, verr)
 }
 return out, verr
}

// par2Verdict maps a library run onto today's verdicts (§8.5.3), with OD22.
func par2Verdict(res par2child.Result, err error) (Par2Result, error) {
 out := Par2Result{BlocksNeeded: res.BlocksNeeded, Output: tail(res.Log, 2048)}
 switch {
 case err == nil && res.Status == par2.AllCorrect:
  out.AllCorrect = true
  return out, nil
 case err == nil && res.Status == par2.Repaired:
  out.Repaired = true
  return out, nil
 case err == nil && res.Status == par2.RepairNotPossible:
  return out, fmt.Errorf("%w: %d more recovery blocks needed: %s", ErrRepairFailed, res.BlocksNeeded, out.Output)
 case err == nil:
  return out, fmt.Errorf("%w: par2 reported %s: %s", ErrRepairFailed, res.Status, out.Output)
 case errors.Is(err, context.Canceled), errors.Is(err, context.DeadlineExceeded):
  return out, err
 case errors.Is(err, par2.ErrUnavailable):
  return out, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrPar2Unavailable, err)
 case errors.Is(err, par2.ErrMemory), errors.Is(err, par2child.ErrChildDied):
  return out, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w", ErrPar2Crashed, err)
 case errors.Is(err, par2.ErrInvalidOptions):
  return out, fmt.Errorf("usenet: par2 refused its options: %w", err)
 }
 return out, fmt.Errorf("%w: %w: %s", ErrRepairFailed, err, out.Output)
}

// par2Extras is extraFiles as absolute paths, without empty files, as the
// CLI filters them (commandline.cpp: exists, inside basepath, non-empty).
func par2Extras(dir, indexFile string) []string {
 var out []string
 for _, name := range extraFiles(dir, indexFile) {
  p := filepath.Join(dir, name)
  if st, err := os.Stat(p); err == nil && st.Size() > 0 {
   out = append(out, p)
  }
 }
 return out
}
```

```go
 available bool
```

```go
// newRepairer is the engine's repairer: par2go in a child of this binary
// (§8.6). A variable for one test.
var newRepairer = func() usenetclient.Repairer { return &usenetclient.LibraryRepairer{Runner: par2child.Exec{}} }

// registerUnreaped exports par2child.Unreaped; a registry that has it already is fine.
func registerUnreaped(r prometheus.Registerer) error {
 err := r.Register(prometheus.NewGaugeFunc(prometheus.GaugeOpts{
  Name: "clustarr_par2_unreaped_children",
  Help: "par2 repair children still not reaped after their deadline and grace (a read blocked in the kernel).",
 }, func() float64 { return float64(par2child.Unreaped()) }))
 var are prometheus.AlreadyRegisteredError
 if errors.As(err, &are) {
  return nil
 }
 return err
}
```

### Task W9.7: The native image builds `libpar2shim.so` and checks the repair child

**Spec:** §8.7 (the `par2` stage, `stage.sh`, `ENV PAR2GO_LIB`, self-checks, notices), §8.9 guards 1 and 2, §8.8 (CI cache), §8.10 (licence notices), §10.1.4, §10.1.7

> **U1 amendment (overrides §8.7's build of the shim in the text below).** The `par2` stage
> downloads the published shim; it builds nothing:
>
> ```dockerfile
> # par2: par2go's published libpar2shim.so (upgrade guide U1), checked against
> # hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS, with par2cmdline-turbo's and par2go's notices.
> FROM debian:bookworm-slim AS par2
> ARG TARGETARCH
> ARG PAR2GO_VERSION=v0.1.0
> # par2cmdline-turbo as par2go's shim/build.sh pins it at PAR2GO_VERSION.
> ARG PAR2_COMMIT=4aa390514d0236c00810f2a74f4435b6fff5df37
> COPY hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS /tmp/par2go.sha256
> ADD https://github.com/mediactl/par2go/releases/download/${PAR2GO_VERSION}/libpar2shim-linux-${TARGETARCH}.so /tmp/
> ADD https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nzbgetcom/par2cmdline-turbo/${PAR2_COMMIT}/COPYING /tmp/par2-COPYING
> ADD https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nzbgetcom/par2cmdline-turbo/${PAR2_COMMIT}/AUTHORS /tmp/par2-AUTHORS
> COPY --from=build /go/pkg/mod/github.com/mediactl/par2go@${PAR2GO_VERSION}/LICENSE /tmp/par2go-LICENSE
> RUN set -eux; cd /tmp; \
>     grep " libpar2shim-linux-${TARGETARCH}.so\$" par2go.sha256 | sha256sum -c -; \
>     install -D -m 0755 "libpar2shim-linux-${TARGETARCH}.so" /out/usr/lib/libpar2shim.so; \
>     install -D -m 0644 par2go-LICENSE /out/usr/share/licenses/par2go/LICENSE; \
>     install -D -m 0644 par2-COPYING /out/usr/share/licenses/par2cmdline-turbo/COPYING; \
>     install -D -m 0644 par2-AUTHORS /out/usr/share/licenses/par2cmdline-turbo/AUTHORS; \
>     printf 'libpar2shim.so is par2go %s release asset libpar2shim-linux-%s.so, built from par2cmdline-turbo %s with par2go shim/patches. Source: https://github.com/mediactl/par2go/tree/%s and https://github.com/nzbgetcom/par2cmdline-turbo/tree/%s\n' \
>       "${PAR2GO_VERSION}" "${TARGETARCH}" "${PAR2_COMMIT}" "${PAR2GO_VERSION}" "${PAR2_COMMIT}" > /out/usr/share/licenses/par2cmdline-turbo/SOURCE
> ```
>
> (`build` is the native Dockerfile's Go build stage, whose `go mod download` puts par2go's
> module, pinned by go.sum, under `/go/pkg/mod`; use that stage's name and `GOMODCACHE` if they
> differ.) The Makefile's native build passes `--build-arg PAR2GO_VERSION=$(PAR2GO_VERSION)`.

```go
// §8.9 guard 1: no image ships a par2 executable, and stage.sh refuses one.
func TestNoImageShipsAPar2Executable(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 dockerfiles, err := filepath.Glob(filepath.Join(root, "images", "Dockerfile*"))
 require.NoError(t, err)

   t.Errorf("%s installs a par2 executable (%s): par2 is a library (ADR-0017)", filepath.Base(f), m)
  }
 }

// stage, built from par2go; only hack/native-assets.sh fetches a par2

 var fetchers []string

   }
   return nil
  }))
 }
 assert.Equal(t, []string{"hack/native-assets.sh"}, fetchers)
}

func TestEveryNativeImageCheckRunsThePar2Child(t *testing.T) {
```

```markdown
# ADR-0018: One manager runs every reconciler; workers run as one agent per domain; agents autoscale without KEDA

**Status:** Accepted, 2026-10-06 (supersedes ADR-0013)

## Context

ADR-0013 kept one controller Deployment per service until the system was
production ready, with the unified topology designed
(`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-09-24-unified-manager-design.md`) and deferred,
because one pod per component made a crash loop or a log stream attributable
without tooling. On 2026-10-06 the owner chose to adopt the unified topology
now, and to go further: every reconciler in one manager, every worker in one
agent binary run per domain, the segment and transcode workers renamed
`markers` and `transcode` on the in-process ffgo pattern, each binary linking
only what it needs, `cmd/clustarr` and `clustarr all` removed, and an
autoscaler that reaches zero without KEDA. The premise ADR-0013 rested on, that
per-service isolation was worth more than one cache and one lease during
development, is the owner's to weigh, and the owner weighed it the other way.
The design is `docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-manager-agent-split-design.md`.

## Decision

- **Five binaries, two images.** `cmd/manager` and `cmd/ui` (static, in the
  distroless `clustarr` image); `cmd/agent` (cgo, for the SQLite piece
  completion seeding torrents rely on), `cmd/markers` and `cmd/transcode` (in the
  FROM-scratch `native` image, with FFmpeg 9, the ffgo shim, ONNX Runtime and
  `libpar2shim.so`). No image sets an ENTRYPOINT; every container names its
  binary (`pkg/binpath`).
- **The manager** runs every controller and leader-only runnable of all six
  services under one lease (`manager.clustarr.io`) and one cache, registered by
  `app/<service>/manager`. It is the only process that ensures the NATS topology,
  and it re-ensures it after a NATS restart. It serves
  `external.metrics.k8s.io/v1beta1` itself and owns one HPA per autoscaled agent
  Deployment under the field manager `clustarr-autoscale`.
- **The agent** runs exactly one domain per process (`catalog`, `events`,
  `metadata`, `import`, `index`, `caption`, `torrent-engine`, `usenet-engine`),
  registered by `app/<service>/agent`, never leader-elected; its subscriptions
  bind durables and never create them.
- **Names stay.** Every field manager and every NATS stream, consumer and
  bucket name is unchanged; two new names exist (`clustarr-autoscale`, and the
  pinned default field owner `clustarr`).
- **Autoscaling.** One external metric, `clustarr_consumer_lag` (pending plus
  ack-pending per consumer); HPAs from 0 (1 for `events`) to the number of nodes
  the pod template can run on; the consumers whose downstream is throttled
  (search, grab, subtitle fetch) keep their consumer-wide cap, so `catalog` and
  `caption` scale 0..1. The installers render the APIService without a CA; the
  manager injects only `spec.caBundle`.
- **Guards.** Each binary has a `go list -deps` guard (`test/guards/deps_test.go`).

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the per-service Deployments (ADR-0013).** The owner declined it.
- **One binary with roles (`clustarr all`).** Every process would link
  everything: 94 MB static, and no way to keep FFmpeg's dynamic loader out of
  the distroless controller.
- **A combined-domain agent for development (`--domain all`).** It would bring
  `clustarr all` back under another name and cost field-index unions and
  probe-name rules; `make run-dev` starts one agent per domain instead (OD1).
- **KEDA, or prometheus-adapter.** An operator and its CRDs, or a Prometheus,
  for one metric the manager already holds; the owner asked for neither.
- **`k8s.io/apiserver` for the metrics API.** A large dependency for three
  routes; the hand-rolled server is security-sensitive and is tested for 401,
  403 and metric selection instead.

## Consequences

- One informer cache and one lease instead of six; a manager fault stops every
  reconciler at once, and the External Metrics API with it (HPAs hold).
- Agents at zero replicas cold-start on the first queued item.
- The index agent stays at one replica with `Recreate` under Postgres too, until
  indexers share a limiter (refines ADR-0010).
- Transcode pool pods pull the larger `native` image (refines ADR-0015, ADR-0009).
- A namespace deleted while the manager is down leaves the APIService behind;
  `docs/autoscaling.md` gives the manual recovery.

## Revisit triggers

- Indexers gain a shared KV limiter: the index agent and catalog search could scale out.
- The manager's cache outgrows its memory limit on a real library.
- A fault that needs per-service isolation to diagnose.
- `HPAScaleToZero` changes status in a supported Kubernetes release.
```

  `**Status:** Superseded by ADR-0018, 2026-10-06` (body untouched, README "Lifecycle" rule).

  `docs/adr/README.md`: the 0013 row's Status cell becomes
  `Superseded by ADR-0018, 2026-10-06`; add, after the 0016 row (W10.3 inserts 0017 between them), the row
  `| [0018](0018-manager-agents-and-ui.md) | One manager runs every reconciler; workers run as one agent per domain (cmd/agent), with the ui, markers and transcode as their own binaries; agents autoscale without KEDA (supersedes 0013) | Accepted, 2026-10-06 |`;
  under "Refinements that did not change a decision", add:

- `- **0015:** the transcoder image is now the \`native\` image, which also carries the agent and markers (2026-10-06, ADR-0018).`
- `- **0009:** pool Jobs run \`/usr/bin/transcode\` from the \`native\` image, component \`transcode\` (2026-10-06, ADR-0018).`

```markdown
# ADR-0017: No image ships or runs ffmpeg, ffprobe or par2; probing, decoding, subtitle extraction and par2 run as libraries

**Status:** Accepted, 2026-10-06 (supersedes the "PAR2 is an exec" decision
recorded in `hack/deps/deps.go` and `pkg/download/usenet/repair.go`)

## Context

Until 2026-10-06 four paths ran external programs: ffprobe (two calls per
probe, `pkg/mediainfo`), ffmpeg for segment decoding (`pkg/segments/decode`)
and for embedded subtitle extraction (the captionarr fetch worker), and
`par2 r` for usenet repair. The media image carried BtbN's unpinned "latest"
static ffmpeg and ffprobe and animetosho's par2 zip; the transcoder image
already ran FFmpeg 9 in-process through the ffgo fork (2026-10-01). The owner
asked for markers and transcode on the in-process pattern, for ffprobe to be
converted to ffgo, and for par2 to be par2cmdline-turbo used as a library;
converting embedded extraction followed, because the shared native image ships
no ffmpeg (OD8).

## Decision

- **Probe:** `pkg/mediainfo/native`, which prints what ffprobe printed for
  every stored field (`TestNativeProbeMatchesTheGoldens`, against the probe goldens
  recorded from ffprobe before its deletion, nothing blanked), so
  `mediainfo.ProbeVersion` stays 3. The manager never probes: the import
  domain answers probe tasks.
- **Decode:** `pkg/segments/decode` rebuilds the demux, seek, decode and filter
  graph `ffmpeg(1)` built, byte for byte; the fingerprint cache is versioned
  (`segments.FingerprintVersion` 2).
- **Embedded subtitles:** `pkg/subtitles/providers/embedded/native`, FFmpeg's
  decoders and srt encoder in-process.
- **One runtime gate:** `pkg/ffruntime` loads FFmpeg 9 and the shim once,
  checks the shim's API, routes FFmpeg's log, and bounds every call by its
  context plus a grace, wedging the process at four abandoned calls.
- **par2:** par2go (`github.com/mediactl/par2go`, `libpar2shim.so` through
  purego), run by the usenet engine in a short-lived child of the agent binary
  (`agent par2-repair`, `pkg/par2child`). `pkg/par2child/exec.go` is the only
  production code that starts a process, and its only target is
  `os.Executable()` (`TestNoProductionCodeStartsAProcess`).
- **No test runs ffmpeg or ffprobe either** (owner, 2026-10-06): clips come
  from `internal/testmedia` on ffgo, and parity is judged against
  `test/data/media-goldens`, recorded once from the exec implementations before
  their deletion (`TestNoGoFileRunsFFmpeg`). The par2 CLI that
  `test/par2test` makes sets with is the one test-only program
  `make native-assets` supplies.

## Alternatives considered

- **Keep the CLI execs.** Executables in the images, an unpinned build, and a
  process per call.
- **par2 in the engine process.** A worker-thread exception or `abort()` in
  par2-turbo would kill the engine and crash-loop it through re-attach; some
  phases cannot be cancelled; repair memory sits outside `GOMEMLIMIT`; par2go
  runs one job per process (OD21).
- **`akalin/gopar`.** Too slow, and reads a whole set into memory.
- **cgo bindings.** Would tie markers and transcode to FFmpeg's and par2's
  headers and toolchains; purego keeps them `CGO_ENABLED=0`.
- **A separate `cmd/par2` binary.** Another binary and image path for a child
  the agent can be.

## Consequences

- purego in the agent; the native image carries `.so` files (FFmpeg, the ffgo
  shim, ONNX Runtime, `libpar2shim.so`) and their notices (GPL-2.0-or-later for
  par2cmdline-turbo, combined under GPL-3.0, ADR-0002).
- `make native-assets` needs curl, xz, unzip and a C compiler (it compiles
  `libffshim.so` against the pinned FFmpeg; `libpar2shim.so` is par2go `v0.1.0`'s
  release asset, checked against `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS`); `make test` sets
  `CLUSTARR_REQUIRE_TOOLS=1`, so a missing native library fails rather than skips.
- FFmpeg's and par2's memory is outside `GOMEMLIMIT` (agents' and markers' limits
  leave room for it). A stuck FFmpeg call can be abandoned but not killed; the
  `ffgo` healthz check restarts a wedged pod.
- An out-of-memory par2 run or a repair child that died without a verdict is a
  local fault (`writeError`), not a blocklist (OD22); an engine stopped
  mid-repair no longer blocklists a good release.
- Every binary that links ffgo maps FFmpeg at package init, before `main`.

## Revisit triggers

- par2go or par2cmdline-turbo becoming exception-safe and cancellable in every
  phase: the child could go.
- ffgo's loader becoming lazy.
- A probe difference the fork cannot remove (OD16), which would force a
  `ProbeVersion` raise.
```

     - **What scales.** The table of §9.0's last bullet: HPAs for `agent-catalog`
       (0..1), `agent-events` (1..N), `agent-import` (0..N), `agent-caption`
       (0..1), `markers` (0..N); fixed replicas for the manager, `agent-metadata`,
       `agent-index`, `ui`, engines and transcode pools; why `catalog` and
       `caption` stop at 1 (their throttled consumers keep the consumer-wide
       `MaxAckPending`: indexarr's per-host limiter and the shared subtitle
       token bucket cannot feed more replicas, and extra search replicas turn a
       sweep's queue into `paced` skips; OD46).
     - **The metric.** `clustarr_consumer_lag{stream,consumer}` = `NumPending + NumAckPending`
       from JetStream `ConsumerInfo`; it counts delayed naks, so a domain in a
       backoff stays at 1 (OD27).
     - **The External Metrics API.** Served by the manager on `:6443` behind the
       `external-metrics` Service (`publishNotReadyAddresses: true`); front-proxy
       mTLS against `kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication` (401 without a
       verified cert or identity, 403 for a CN not allowed); the CA in the Secret
       named by `CLUSTARR_EXTERNAL_METRICS_SECRET`.
     - **Who owns what.** The installers render `v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io`
       without `caBundle` and the kube-system RoleBinding; the manager writes only
       `spec.caBundle`, as `clustarr-autoscale`, and owns one HPA per Deployment
       labelled `autoscale.clustarr.io/domain`; no installer renders an HPA.
     - **The HPA.** minReplicas 0 (1 for `events`, raised by
       `autoscale.clustarr.io/min-replicas`); maxReplicas from the nodes the pod
       template can run on and the consumers' caps; one External metric per
       consumer at its slots; scale-up immediate, scale-down after the longest
       AckWait or 5 minutes; `autoscale.clustarr.io/paused` stops the reconciler
       touching a Deployment's HPA.
     - **Slots.** `events.ConsumerSpec.Slots` per durable;
       `CLUSTARR_CONSUMER_SLOTS=segmentarr-analyze=3,catalogarr-grab=8` overrides
       them per Deployment (values `consumerSlots`), and is what the reconciler
       reads as the per-pod target.
     - **Turning it off.** `autoscaling.enabled: false` (Helm) renders fixed
       replicas, passes `--autoscale=false` and renders no APIService: use it
       where KEDA or prometheus-adapter already holds the group, which this
       chart does not support beside it.
     - **Failure modes.** §9.8's table, verbatim in substance, including the
       Events `ScaleToZeroUnavailable` and `NoMatchingNodes`.
     - **A namespace stuck Terminating.** If the release namespace was deleted while
       the manager was down, run `kubectl delete apiservice v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io`;

### Task W10.7: CLAUDE.md
> **Amended by ADR-0019:** see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-agents-report-over-nats.md, "Amendments", W10.7.
> **Amended by Wave U:** see docs/superpowers/plans/2026-10-07-unbranded-names.md, "Amendments", W10.7.

**Spec:** §12 (CLAUDE.md: services table, commands, invariants, guard successors, Transcoding paragraph, gotchas, status), R3 amendment (the MediaFile split per field manager)
> **Wave 4f note (NATS research 2026-10-07; split §12 as amended).** Also, each added to the check script's `fresh` list (`TestNoObjectLinks`, `Clustarr-Id`, `PurgeOrphanChunks`, `deliveryCount`, `objindex`):
>
> 1. The invariant "Artwork objects have two writers split by variant" ends: "…and of its metadata. Each `Put` sends the variant's complete header and metadata set (`artwork.ObjectMeta`), and `SetMeta` is the owner's alone, under its per-item lock. No code creates object links (`TestNoObjectLinks`). The ui watches the bucket read-only (`pkg/events/objindex`). The reaper is the only code that deletes both, and it also purges orphan chunks (`PurgeOrphanChunks`) and audits status against the bucket." Step 3's edit of "the renderer (`catalogarr --role artwork`," stands.
> 2. The gotcha "JetStream raises a pull consumer's MAX_DELIVERIES advisory only on its next delivery attempt…" gains its cause and loses its remedy: nats-server's `deliveryCount` returns redeliveries, so the ack-timer path (`checkPending`) catches a lapsed final delivery only for `MaxDeliver` 1, and for 2 or more `getNextMsg` raises it on the next waiting pull from any replica (`consumer.go:4841-4849, 2427-2457, 6187-6192`); a pull a stopping pod abandons is pruned by the next `CONSUMER.INFO` (the manager's QueueGauge, every 30 s) and is never relied on; a subscription fetches only for free slots and never parks (Wave 4c's parking spent an attempt per redelivery and dead-lettered healthy tasks it never ran, E11), so nothing keeps a pull open at saturation; membus's sweep dead-letters a lapsed final delivery in place.
> 3. New gotcha, **a fired schedule has no `Nats-Msg-Id`**: nats-server strips it and adds `Nats-Scheduler` and `Nats-Schedule-Next: purge` (`scheduler.go:214-231`); a copy published with those onto a stream without schedules is refused with 10188, which lost every scheduled task's dead letter until 2026-10-07. The envelope ID rides in `Clustarr-Id` too, and `EnvelopeFromHeaders` drops every transport header (`Nats-Schedule*`, `Nats-Expected-*`, `Nats-TTL`, `Nats-Rollup`).
> 4. New gotcha, **the broker keys `InProgress`, `Ack` and `Nak` by stream sequence, not by delivery**: a lapsed handler could keep its redelivered copy from timing out or move its deadline, so the bus mutes a lapsed delivery's `InProgress` and `Nak` (`Ack` and `Term` still go); double ack plus Msg-Id dedupe is not exactly-once after a lapse, the record fence is.
> 5. New gotcha, **object stores**: `Put` replaces an object's whole metadata (every `Put` is a complete declaration, like an SSA apply); two concurrent `Put`s of one name leak a full copy for good, which only `PurgeOrphanChunks` reclaims, since the meta-level `List` cannot see it; a reader whose object is overwritten mid-`Get` stalls until its deadline and fails with `i/o timeout`, never a digest mismatch, so `/art` reads whole objects under a deadline before it answers; a link fires no watch event when its target changes, and nats.go refuses a link over any name a regular object ever held; `ObjectStore.Watch` ignores `ResumeFromRevision` and `MetaOnly` (the bus refuses `WatchFromRevision`); a bucket re-created under a running watch is skipped silently, so `objindex` compares `Status().Created`.
> 6. Where step 1's text describes the agents' HPAs, it says they read JetStream `CONSUMER.INFO` pending + ack-pending per durable, never `/jsz` (only the consumer leader's `num_pending` is right) or a stream's message count (it counts schedule holds and retention).

     - The second par2 gotcha (`par2 r index.par2` alone…): "and `Par2Runner.Repair`
       now does too (`extraFiles`; `TestPar2RunnerRepairsASetWhoseFilesCarryOtherNames`
       runs real par2)" → "and `usenet.LibraryRepairer` does too (`par2Extras`,

       `TestLibraryRepairerRepairsASetWhoseFilesCarryOtherNames` runs real par2go)".
     - The `exec.CommandContext` gotcha's last sentence: "`Par2Runner.Repair` sets
       `Setpgid`, a `Cancel` that kills the process group, and `WaitDelay`; do the
       same for any subprocess given a deadline." → "The one subprocess left,
       `par2child.Exec`, sets `Setpgid`, cancels cooperatively by closing the
       child's stdin, kills after `WaitDelay`, and waits in its own goroutine so a
       child in uninterruptible I/O cannot hold `Run` past the grace."
     - New gotchas, appended:
       - "**ffgo maps FFmpeg at package init, and a stale shim is silently
         wrong.** Any binary or test that links ffgo has dlopened FFmpeg before
         `main`, through `LD_LIBRARY_PATH` and a fixed list of system paths, and
         ffgo's loader remembers a failure, so `t.Setenv` is too late: native tests
         run through `make test`, which sets the variables, and
         `nativetest.FFmpeg` fails when the mapped libavcodec is not the pinned
         build under `$CLUSTARR_NATIVE_ASSETS/lib` (a host's FFmpeg 9 cannot be told
         apart by version). A shim older than `ffruntime.MinShimAPI` reads FFmpeg 9's
         structs at FFmpeg 4-7 offsets; `ffruntime.Load` refuses it and
         `TestShimAPIMatchesTheFork` pins the two together."
       - "**par2's traps live in par2go, and the child protects the engine.**
         par2cmdline-turbo's `Process` ignores its `basepath` (T1; par2go sets it,
         `TestLibraryRepairerResolvesTargetsAgainstTheJobDir` holds it), its
         headers break inside a namespace (T2), it checks cancel only above quiet
         logging (T3), and its worker threads call `std::terminate` on an exception
         (T13): in the engine that would crash-loop it through re-attach, so repair
         runs in `agent par2-repair` (`pkg/par2child`). Tests that need the library
         call `nativetest.Require(t, \"par2go\", par2.Available())`, which skips
         naming `PAR2GO_LIB` and `make native-assets`, and fails under
