```go
// ffmpegNames are the CLIs no Go file may run (owner, 2026-10-06; U2).
var ffmpegNames = []string{"ffmpeg", "ffprobe"}

// cliLocators are the calls that run or locate a program by name.
var cliLocators = map[string]bool{"Command": true, "CommandContext": true, "LookPath": true, "Tool": true, "FindTool": true}

// scanForFFmpegCLI reports every place under root, in every .go file
// (tests, test/ and hack/ included), that runs or locates the ffmpeg or
// ffprobe CLI: a Command/CommandContext/LookPath/Tool/FindTool call given a
// string literal naming one (bare or as a path), an exec.Command* whose
// program argument is such a call, and the literal paths of the two
// programs under /usr/bin anywhere.
func scanForFFmpegCLI(root string) []string {
 var found []string
 usrBin := []string{"/usr/bin/" + "ffmpeg", "/usr/bin/" + "ffprobe"}
 _ = filepath.WalkDir(root, func(path string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
  if err != nil {
   return err
  }
  if d.IsDir() && (d.Name() == ".git" || d.Name() == "vendor" || d.Name() == "node_modules") {
   return filepath.SkipDir
  }
  if d.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(path, ".go") {
   return nil
  }
  rel, _ := filepath.Rel(root, path)
  f, err := parser.ParseFile(token.NewFileSet(), path, nil, parser.SkipObjectResolution)
  if err != nil {
   found = append(found, rel+": does not parse: "+err.Error())
   return nil
  }
  ast.Inspect(f, func(n ast.Node) bool {
   switch x := n.(type) {
   case *ast.BasicLit:
    if x.Kind == token.STRING {
     for _, p := range usrBin {
      if strings.Contains(x.Value, p) {
       found = append(found, rel+": names "+p)
      }
     }
    }
   case *ast.CallExpr:
    name := ""
    switch fn := x.Fun.(type) {
    case *ast.SelectorExpr:
     name = fn.Sel.Name
    case *ast.Ident:
     name = fn.Name
    }
    if !cliLocators[name] {
     return true
    }
    for _, a := range x.Args {
     if namesFFmpeg(a) {
      found = append(found, fmt.Sprintf("%s: %s(…) runs or locates an ffmpeg CLI", rel, name))
     }
    }
   }
   return true
  })
  return nil
 })
 return found
}

// namesFFmpeg reports whether e is a string literal naming ffmpeg or
// ffprobe (bare or as a path's last element), or a call whose arguments are.
func namesFFmpeg(e ast.Expr) bool {
 switch x := e.(type) {
 case *ast.BasicLit:
  if x.Kind != token.STRING {
   return false
  }
  v, err := strconv.Unquote(x.Value)
  return err == nil && slices.Contains(ffmpegNames, filepath.Base(v))
 case *ast.CallExpr:
  return slices.ContainsFunc(x.Args, namesFFmpeg)
 }
 return false
}

// No Go file runs the ffmpeg or ffprobe CLI: not production code (the exec
// guard), and not a test, a test helper or a hack/ program either (U2.4).
func TestNoGoFileRunsFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
 assert.Empty(t, scanForFFmpegCLI(installtest.RepoRoot(t)))
}

// The guard is falsified on a synthetic tree, each shape once.
func TestTheFFmpegGuardCatchesEachShape(t *testing.T) {
 root := t.TempDir()
 write := func(rel, body string) {
  p := filepath.Join(root, rel)
  require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755))
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body), 0o644))
 }
 write("a/a_test.go", "package a\nimport \"os/exec\"\nfunc f() { _ = exec.Command(\"ff"+"mpeg\", \"-v\") }\n")
 write("b/b.go", "package b\nimport \"os/exec\"\nfunc f() { _, _ = exec.LookPath(\"ff"+"probe\") }\n")
 write("test/c/c.go", "package c\nfunc f(t any) { _ = Tool(t, \"ff"+"mpeg\") }\nfunc Tool(any, string) string { return \"\" }\n")
 write("hack/d/main.go", "package main\nimport \"os/exec\"\nfunc main() { _ = exec.Command(Tool(nil, \"ff"+"probe\")) }\nfunc Tool(any, string) string { return \"\" }\n")
 write("e/e_test.go", "package e\nconst bin = \"/usr/bin/\" + \"x\"\nvar p = \"/usr/bin/ff"+"mpeg\"\n")
 write("f/f.go", "package f\nimport \"log/slog\"\nfunc f() { slog.Warn(\"ff"+"mpeg\", \"level\", 1) }\n") // a log message is not a program
 got := strings.Join(scanForFFmpegCLI(root), "\n")
 for _, want := range []string{"a/a_test.go", "b/b.go", "test/c/c.go", "hack/d/main.go", "e/e_test.go"} {
  assert.Contains(t, got, want)
 }
 assert.NotContains(t, got, "f/f.go")
}

// The indirect shapes today's tests used: a helper that forwards its
// program to exec.Command, called from another file of its package
// (pkg/transcode/engine's run), and a gate over a literal list.
func TestTheFFmpegGuardCatchesIndirectShapes(t *testing.T) {
 root := t.TempDir()
 write := func(rel, body string) {
  p := filepath.Join(root, rel)
  require.NoError(t, os.MkdirAll(filepath.Dir(p), 0o755))
  require.NoError(t, os.WriteFile(p, []byte(body), 0o644))
 }
 write("g/run_test.go", `package g
import "os/exec"
func run(t any, name string, a ...string) { _ = exec.Command(name, a...) }
`)
 write("g/use_test.go", `package g
func f() { run(nil, "ff`+`probe", "-v") }
`)
 write("h/h_test.go", `package h
import "os/exec"
func f() { for _, b := range []string{"ff`+`mpeg", "x"} { _, _ = exec.LookPath(b) } }
`)
 write("i/i_test.go", `package i
import "os"
func f() { for _, b := range []string{"ff`+`mpeg"} { _ = os.WriteFile(b, nil, 0o755) } }
`) // a fake written under the name is not a run
 got := strings.Join(scanForFFmpegCLI(root), " ")
 assert.Contains(t, got, "g/use_test.go")
 assert.Contains(t, got, "h/h_test.go")
 assert.NotContains(t, got, "i/i_test.go")
}

// Every test that needs FFmpeg's libraries gates through testmedia.Require
// or nativetest.FFmpeg, which fail under CLUSTARR_FFGO_REQUIRE=1 (CI): a
// gate of its own that only skips lets a missing library pass silently
// (upgrade guide U2.1).
func TestEveryFFgoGateHonoursTheRequirement(t *testing.T) {
 assert.Empty(t, scanForSilentFFgoGates(installtest.RepoRoot(t)))
}

// No shell script under hack/ or test/ runs the ffmpeg or ffprobe CLI
// either (hack/parity-clips.sh cut test/parity's clips with one).
func TestNoScriptRunsFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 run := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^\s*([^#\n]*[|;&(]\s*)?ff(mpeg|probe)\s`)
 for _, dir := range []string{"hack", "test"} {
  require.NoError(t, filepath.WalkDir(filepath.Join(root, dir), func(p string, d fs.DirEntry, err error) error {
   if err != nil || d.IsDir() || !strings.HasSuffix(p, ".sh") {
    return err
   }
   b, err := os.ReadFile(p)
   require.NoError(t, err)
   assert.NotRegexp(t, run, string(b), "%s runs an ffmpeg CLI", p)
   return nil
  }))
 }
}
```

```go
// The e2e fixtures image installs no ffmpeg and bakes its clips with
// test/fixtures/mkclips on the native image's pinned FFmpeg (U2.7).
func TestTheE2EFixturesImageRunsNoFFmpeg(t *testing.T) {
 root := installtest.RepoRoot(t)
 df := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures"))
 assert.NotRegexp(t, `(?m)^[^#\n]*apt-get install[^\n]*\bffmpeg\b`, df)
 assert.NotRegexp(t, `(?m)^\s*ffmpeg\s`, df, "a stage runs the ffmpeg CLI")
 assert.Contains(t, df, "./test/fixtures/mkclips")
 native := string(readRepoFile(t, root, "images/Dockerfile.native"))
 for _, arg := range []string{"FFMPEG_RELEASE", "FFMPEG_VERSION", "FFMPEG_BRANCH", "FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64", "FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64"} {
  re := regexp.MustCompile(`(?m)^ARG ` + arg + `=(\S+)$`)
  want := re.FindStringSubmatch(native)
  require.NotNil(t, want, "Dockerfile.native has no ARG %s", arg)
  got := re.FindStringSubmatch(df)
  require.NotNil(t, got, "Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures has no ARG %s", arg)
  assert.Equal(t, want[1], got[1], "%s: the fixtures' FFmpeg is the native image's", arg)
 }
}
```

```go
// Command mkclips writes the e2e fixture clips with internal/testmedia on
// ffgo, not the ffmpeg CLI (owner decision 2026-10-06; upgrade guide U2.7).
package main

func specs() map[string]testmedia.Spec {
 return map[string]testmedia.Spec{
  "tiny.mkv": {Shortest: true,
   Video: []testmedia.Video{{Source: "testsrc=duration=10:size=640x480:rate=25", Encoder: "libx264", PixFmt: "yuv420p",
    Options: map[string]string{"preset": "ultrafast", "x264-params": "nal-hrd=cbr:force-cfr=1",
     "b": "48M", "minrate": "48M", "maxrate": "48M", "bufsize": "48M"}}},
   Audio: []testmedia.Audio{{Source: "sine=frequency=1000:duration=10", Encoder: "aac"}}},
  "hdr10.mkv": {Video: []testmedia.Video{{Source: "testsrc2=duration=3:size=640x480:rate=25", Encoder: "libx265", PixFmt: "yuv420p10le",
   Options: map[string]string{"x265-params": "log-level=error"},
   Color:   testmedia.Color{Primaries: "bt2020", Transfer: "smpte2084", Matrix: "bt2020nc"},
   HDR10:   &testmedia.HDR10{MasteringDisplay: [10]uint32{13250, 34500, 7500, 3000, 34000, 16000, 15635, 16450, 10000000, 1}, MaxCLL: 1000, MaxFALL: 400}}}},
 }
}

func main() {
 out := flag.String("out", "/out", "where to write the clips")
 flag.Parse()
 // lavfi sources open only after avdevice.RegisterAll (W0.30); testmedia.Require
 // does this for tests, and testmedia.Write once per process (W6.18), but a
 // failure here names the cause before any clip is attempted.
 if err := avdevice.RegisterAll(); err != nil {
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mkclips: libavdevice:", err)
  os.Exit(1)
 }
 for name, s := range specs() {
  if err := testmedia.Write(filepath.Join(*out, name), s); err != nil {
   fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mkclips:", name, err)
   os.Exit(1)
  }
 }
 if st, err := os.Stat(filepath.Join(*out, "tiny.mkv")); err != nil || st.Size() < 50<<20 {
  fmt.Fprintln(os.Stderr, "mkclips: tiny.mkv must be at least 50 MiB (the import-size floor the e2e suite crosses)")
  os.Exit(1)
 }
}
```

  (Imports: `flag`, `fmt`, `os`, `path/filepath`, `github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo/avdevice` and
  `internal/testmedia`. `testmedia.Write` needs no `testing.T`, and `main` registers the lavfi devices
  itself, since `Require`, which does it for tests, is not called here; `Require`'s other checks are the
  image stage's environment. `TestTheE2EClipsAreTheOldRecipes` cannot catch a missing registration,
  because `testmedia.Make` calls `Require` first.) In `images/Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures`, replace the `clipgen` and `clipgen-hdr10` stages with:

```dockerfile
# clipgen: the e2e clips on ffgo (test/fixtures/mkclips), against the native
# image's pinned BtbN FFmpeg; no ffmpeg CLI is installed or run (U2.7).
FROM golang:${GO_VERSION} AS clipgen
ARG FFMPEG_RELEASE=autobuild-2026-09-30-13-08
ARG FFMPEG_VERSION=n9.0.2-17-g2a571b6068
ARG FFMPEG_BRANCH=9.0
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64=01a9764d0b5364b66cfeb4617557c64321b0e232e172ec73f0a701c5f7694326
ARG FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64=706ccdbc8b0537646345532713a9b6750c0a6258cc001ec1c0379754f0ae730a
ARG TARGETARCH
WORKDIR /src
COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/
COPY go.mod go.sum ./
RUN --mount=type=cache,target=/go/pkg/mod go mod download
COPY . .
# tar -xJ needs xz, which the golang image may not carry (every other stage that unpacks BtbN installs it).
RUN apt-get update && apt-get install -y --no-install-recommends xz-utils && rm -rf /var/lib/apt/lists/*
RUN set -eux; \
    case "${TARGETARCH}" in amd64) a=linux64 sha="${FFMPEG_SHA256_AMD64}" ;; arm64) a=linuxarm64 sha="${FFMPEG_SHA256_ARM64}" ;; esac; \
    curl -fsSL -o /tmp/ff.tar.xz "https://github.com/BtbN/FFmpeg-Builds/releases/download/${FFMPEG_RELEASE}/ffmpeg-${FFMPEG_VERSION}-${a}-gpl-shared-${FFMPEG_BRANCH}.tar.xz"; \
    echo "${sha}  /tmp/ff.tar.xz" | sha256sum -c -; \
    mkdir -p /opt/ffmpeg && tar -xJf /tmp/ff.tar.xz --strip-components=1 -C /opt/ffmpeg; \
    gcc -shared -fPIC -O2 -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVDEVICE=1 -DFFSHIM_HAVE_AVFILTER=1 -I/opt/ffmpeg/include \
      -o /opt/ffmpeg/lib/libffshim.so "$(go list -m -f '{{.Dir}}' github.com/obinnaokechukwu/ffgo)/shim/ffshim.c" \
      -L/opt/ffmpeg/lib -lavutil -lavcodec -lavformat -lavdevice -lavfilter; \
    mkdir -p /out; \
    LD_LIBRARY_PATH=/opt/ffmpeg/lib FFGO_SHIM_DIR=/opt/ffmpeg/lib CGO_ENABLED=0 go run ./test/fixtures/mkclips -out /out
```

  (The five values are W6.5's `images/Dockerfile.native` defaults; if a later task re-pinned FFmpeg there,
  copy the current ones: `TestTheE2EFixturesImageRunsNoFFmpeg` holds them equal.) The final stage's
  `COPY --from=clipgen /out/tiny.mkv …` and `COPY --from=clipgen-hdr10 /out/hdr10.mkv …` both read
  `--from=clipgen`. The header comments that say the image needs ffmpeg (the old lines 14-15, 47-75)
  say the clips are made by `test/fixtures/mkclips` on ffgo; the Dolby Vision note stays.

## Spec defects found while planning

Each wave's planner recorded where the spec was wrong, silent, out of date or
overtaken by main, and how its tasks resolve it. The spec itself is not edited, except OD19's resolution and the Adoption paragraph's go.mod sentence, which W0.26 records (upgrade guide U1), and the manager/agents ADR's renumbering to ADR-0018 (header, R11, §12), made with this plan because the branch's ADR-0016 took the number.
Waves 1, 4c, 4d, 5, 6 and 7 to 10 give the full notes their planners wrote;
the other waves give their planners' summaries. Waves 4e and 6b record none:
6b's decisions are the upgrade guide's U2, quoted in its own preamble, and 4e's
resolutions are in its tasks (W4.80-W4.88).

### Wave 0: the ffgo fork, par2go and go.mod (W0.1 to W0.30)

1. §6.4 TestWithInterruptAbortsAnOpenOnAStalledReader ('opens a FIFO nobody writes') would hang. open(2) on a FIFO with no writer blocks in the kernel inside FFmpeg's file protocol (avpriv_open), and the AVIOInterruptCB is never polled there. W0.21 uses an empty regular file opened with the file protocol's follow=1 instead: every read answers EAGAIN, and retry_transfer_wrapper polls the callback. Corollary: F16 cannot interrupt a read(2) blocked in the kernel (a hard NFS mount), so the probe's 45 s bound rests on ffruntime.Do's abandonment. §7.5 F16's 'for the probe's 45 s task bound' overstates what it does.
2. §7.6 item 3 and §10.1.6: make contexts refuses unless `git -C $(PAR2GO_DIR) rev-parse HEAD` resolves to $(PAR2GO_REF). par2go's HEAD is already 159eebd, one commit past 1bd94eb, so it would refuse permanently. git archive of the ref does not need HEAD to be there; the check should only be that the ref resolves to a commit.
3. Replace paths: the controller-chosen ../ffgo-unify, and ../par2go-1bd94eb (needed because ../par2go's working tree has moved past the 1bd94eb basis), differ from §7.6 items 1-2, §10.1.5 and §10.1.6. Inside the build stage they resolve to /ffgo-unify and /par2go-1bd94eb. The Dockerfiles must `COPY --from=ffgo / /ffgo-unify/` and `--from=par2go / /par2go-1bd94eb/` (not /ffgo/ and /par2go/). The Makefile needs FFGO_DIR ?= ../ffgo-unify, and the LOCAL_CONTEXTS grep patterns must match `=> \.\./ffgo-unify$` and `=> \.\./par2go-1bd94eb$`.
4. §7.5 asks for new layout entries with 'a layout.Offset Go fallback for FFmpeg 7.1, as the existing entries have'. But ffgo's existing AVCodecParameters fallbacks are FFmpeg 6.0's (format 28, width 56, sample_rate 116, ch_layout.nb_channels 148), not 7.1's or 9's (44, 72, ..., 132), despite the 'Verified with offsetof() on FFmpeg 7.1.1' comment. The AVFrame fallbacks are inconsistent too. W0 uses true 7.1 values; these equal FFmpeg 9's except AVStream.r_frame_rate (216 vs 204) and AVFrame.best_effort_timestamp (320 vs 304).
5. §7.5 F7 'buffer args colorspace=%d:range=%d': ColorSpace's zero value is AVCOL_SPC_RGB, so always appending them would tag every existing video graph as RGB, including clustarr's pkg/transcode/engine/video.go and pkg/transcode/selfcheck/trial.go. W0.10 appends them only when either field is non-zero.
6. The 'local' tag v0.0.0-clustarr.13 is repository-wide: the ffgo-unify worktree shares refs with ../ffgo, where other sessions work. A `git push --tags` there would publish it without OD18, and another session could claim .13 for its own fork work (.10, .11 and .12 were published today; main's MP4-standard work took .12 after this note was first written, so the fork is cut from .12 and tags .13). The spec does not cover the collision. W0.1 and W0.23 check locally and with ls-remote, and stop if the tag is taken.
7. Coordination: §8.10 says 'hack/deps gains no entry beyond it', while §12 schedules the hack/deps/deps.go:43-49 rewrite for the docs wave. Following the repo's pre-add convention (d779a014), W0.26 and W0.27 add hack/deps entries for par2go and component-helpers and do the §12 rewrite now. The tasks that first import those modules (pkg/par2child, app/autoscale/controller) must delete the entries, and the docs wave has nothing left to do in deps.go.

8. **Items 2 and 3 are overtaken by the upgrade guide's U1** (par2go published as `v0.1.0`, 2026-10-06): there is no par2go replace, export, context or local build any more (W0.24, W0.26 and the U1 amendments). Item 3 stands for ffgo alone.

   adds `AwaitTopology`, and §3.5.2 says it polls

### Wave 4a: the R3 probe queue (W4.1 to W4.15)

1. §6.5.3 verdict table: under 'first matching row wins', row 3 (older agent answered a current request: incorporate as is / wait) matches every probed skew record and shadows row 4 (request once now >= ProbedAt+probeSkewRetry), so an incorporated skewed file would wait forever. Plan limits row 3's wait to now < ProbedAt+30m (incorporate-as-is for a new file applies at any time).
2. §6.6/§6.2/§7.4: the probe worker must not import ffgo, yet abandonment is signalled only by ffruntime.ErrAbandoned (pkg/ffruntime imports ffgo); §7.4's code block also never declares ErrAbandoned though its text uses it. Plan adds an ffgo-free sentinel mediainfo.ErrProbeAbandoned for native to wrap.
3. §6.5.3 TranscodeJob gate is placed in plan() after the MediaInfo==nil check, but plan() runs only for Pending jobs and r.wait() resets to Pending; a job already Planned when its file's bytes change is admitted and dispatched without passing plan(). Plan also gates admission's candidate loop and dispatch.
4. §6.5.1 gives the probe consumers Slots: 4 / MaxAckPending 32, but ConsumerSpec.Slots arrives with the R5 bus wave (§11.1 step 6), after step 4; under today's Subscription() MaxAckPending is also per-pod handler count (32 per lane). Plan uses MaxAckPending 4 now; the R5 wave must switch to Slots 4 / MaxAckPending 32.
5. ProbeCurrent covers only ProbePending: a probe of changed bytes that then fails leaves Probed=False/ProbeFailed with status.probeHash and mediaInfo still describing the old bytes, so ProbeCurrent is true and squasharr/captionarr/segment results act on a stale summary for up to probeFailedRetry (1h), or forever after give-up. The window the gate closes reopens on failure; needs an owner ruling (implemented as specified).
6. AudioGraft drift: a naive ProbeCurrent gate in the AudioGraft controller's file() would call wait() during its own swap's re-probe and flip a Succeeded graft to Waiting, losing the Succeeded phase catalogarr's graft incorporation (unincorporatedGraft on main) keys on. Plan gates after file() and keeps Succeeded.
7. §6.5.3 path-only incorporation says a stale ProbeVersion is re-probed by 'the next reconcile', but a status-only write wakes no reconcile (For predicate is GenerationChanged || observed-fingerprint). Plan requeues after 1s.
8. §6.5.3 says a CAS miss returns Requeue: true; ctrl.Result.Requeue is deprecated in controller-runtime v0.25.1 (SA1019, lint). Plan uses RequeueAfter: probeConflictRetry (1s).
9. Spec is silent that a new dead-letterable payload (schema.ProbeTask) needs a DLQ resolver (TestEveryPayloadHasAResolver); plan adds resolveProbeTask. Also the DLQ projector's RBAC markers (dlq.go) grant no mediafiles patch, so in the split 'events' domain role a dead-lettered ProbeTask (and today's SegmentsResult/AnalyzeTask) cannot be annotated; masked today by catalogarr's merged role. The RBAC wave should add it.
10. §6.6 asks for a heartbeat before the audio probe, but FrozenFileQuality is called on the non-video import paths where no events.Message is in scope; plan bounds the probe at 15s (ack arithmetic holds without the beat) and leaves the heartbeat to the Prober injection, W4.86 (added by the plan review).

### Wave 4b: the indexarr split, R8 (W4.20 to W4.29)

1. §4.2.1 table gives app/indexer/agent `Register(ctx, Deps, Options) (io.Closer, error)`, while §3.5.2 step 9 says every domain's registration is `Register(ctx, mgr, bus, Options) (Registration, error)`. The signatures are inconsistent, so the plan avoids depending on either: its tests target the package-internal constructors newClientCache and genericFetcherFor.
2. §4.3 X3 says the hook is 'wired by run.go to `clients.Forget`'. Here `clients` is run.go's local ClientCache variable, not the new `app/indexer/clients` package from X2, which has no Forget. The name is ambiguous.
3. §4.3 Wave 5 step 5.6 moves app/indexer/facadekey.go to app/indexer/agent, but §4.2.1 (Wave 3) has agent Register own 'the facade and its key Secret (facadekey.go moves here)'. Wave 3 must do the move: app/indexer/agent cannot call the unexported ensureFacadeAPIKeys in the root package indexarr without an import cycle.
4. §5.12 gates only buildWireClientFor (the ClientCache.For rebuild path). The download verb's generic fetcher (download.NewFetcherFor) Waits on the host bucket without ever calling For. In an agent-only process, a grab from a generic Indexer not searched or polled since the agent started is therefore paced at the 2s default, not its spec.requestDelay; a 5s or 10s private tracker can be hit faster than it asked. The plan closes this with ClientCache.ApplyRateLimit and agent genericFetcherFor (W4.25).
5. §5.12 `ClientCache.Prune(now)` cannot tell a deleted Indexer from `now` alone, and pruning by TTL alone would also drop the applied generation and reopen the stale-revert window. The plan uses `Prune(ctx, now)`, which lists Indexers from the agent cache and keeps applied generations for live Indexers. Forget (a session change) must also keep the applied generation; the spec is silent on both.
6. §5.3.2 specifies `Drop(ctx, idx, failed)`, but the relogin hook today is `func(ctx)` and has no access to the failed session. The hook signature must change to carry `stale` (renewSession already holds it). The spec does not name this change; the plan adds `clients.ReloginFunc`.
7. §5.15 says its guards live 'in test/guards unless noted', yet `TestAgentClientCacheAppliesRateLimit`, `TestAgentForgetsClientOnSessionChange` and `TestBundleLoaderIsLeaderOnly` carry no package note, while §10.3.5 puts the first in app/indexer/agent. They need package-internal constructors, so the plan places them in their packages.
8. §5.15 `TestSessionDropDoesNotWipeANewerSave` needs an interleaving point between the agent's read and its apply, and the spec names no seam. The plan uses wrapping client.Client and events.KV types in the test, with no production seam.
9. §5.3.2 says '§2 and fieldmanager.go:222-239 only list the session and facade-key Secrets under indexarr-worker', but fieldmanager.go lists neither Secret today. This is a doc update to make (W4.20), not existing state; the design-of-record §2 text is left to the docs wave (§12).
10. §5.12 sessionsSource mirrors limitsSource, but on single-node NATS clustarr-indexer-sessions is memory-backed and a NATS restart ends the watch with nothing re-establishing it. The plan's agent WatchSessions re-watches; the manager's sessionsSource, like limitsSource, falls back to the 15-minute reprobe. The spec is silent.
11. §5.12's table makes indexSweeper an EveryReplica in the agent, but neither §4.3 Wave 3 nor the R8 step in §11.1 says which step flips it; §10.3.5 only moves the test. The plan does it conditionally in W4.28. Likewise the bundle loader's LeaderOnly conversion is assigned to Wave 3 in §4.3 but listed under R8/§5.12, so W4.27 is also conditional.

### Wave 4c: R5 bus changes (W4.40 to W4.47)

1. **§9.3's lapsed-cap start rule contradicts its own contract case.** §9.3
   starts a parked delivery only while `lapsed < slots` and says that once
   `lapsed == slots` "the loop starts no handler". With `MaxInFlight 1`, one
   lapsed handler makes `lapsed == slots`, so `LapsedHandlerFreesItsSlot`
   (MaxInFlight 1, the second task handled within 3× the deadline) can never
   pass. W4.44 uses: a lapse frees its slot only while fewer than `slots` are
   lapsed; a handler starts whenever `live < slots`; at `lapsed == slots` one
   `Fetch(1)` stays open and parks. That gives the same `2 × slots` bound and
   passes both lapse cases.
2. **`LapsedHandlerFreesItsSlot` as worded cannot pass with one slot either.**
   If the hung message hangs on every delivery, JetStream hands its redelivery
   the reclaimed slot first, and that delivery hangs too. W4.44's case hangs
   only on attempt 1.
3. **§5.9 names the wrong re-bind errors.** It re-binds on a `Fetch` returning
   `jetstream.ErrConsumerNotFound` or `ErrStreamNotFound`. nats.go v1.53.1
   reports a consumer deleted under a waiting pull as `ErrConsumerDeleted`
   (409), a pull on a missing consumer as `nats.ErrNoResponders` (503,
   `jetstream/message.go` `checkMsg`), and a restarted server as
   `ErrNoHeartbeat`. W4.44's `consumerGone` matches all of them.
4. **§5.9's no-op membus `WatchDeadLetters` fails §9.3's own backstop case.**
   The variant that stops the subscription and runs only `WatchDeadLetters`
   runs on both buses. A no-op on membus never copies. W4.45's membus
   implementation sweeps the durable instead.
5. **membus parity, as §9.3 lists it, breaks an existing case if landed
   piecemeal, and its cap is too strict.** On its own, "acquire a slot before
   `claimNext`" stops `WorkQueueHungHandlerSaturatedToDLQ` on membus: the hung
   handler holds the only slot, the final delivery is never made, and nothing
   lapses. It must land with lapse-frees-a-slot (W4.44). And "`claim` refuses a
   durable whose unsettled count reached its cap" must still allow a
   redelivery of an already ack-pending message, as JetStream does (W4.43).
6. **§11.1 orders step 4 before step 6, which it depends on.** Step 4 (the R3
   probe topology) needs the DiscardNew exemption in `Validate` and
   `ConsumerSpec.Slots` (`Slots: 4` in §6.5.1), and both are step 6's. W4.40
   must land before Wave 4a's topology task.
7. **The bind-only ripple is unlisted.** `contracttest.Topology()` strips
   every consumer, and every contract case subscribes its own durable. Nine
   sites in eight test files outside `pkg/events` subscribe ad-hoc durables
   too. All of them would hang under a bind-only `Subscribe`. They also have
   to set `MaxDeliver`, since `Topology.Validate` refuses the zero value
   (unlimited) for anything but a watcher. W4.42 handles all of this.
8. **§6.8 misses one test that breaks.** `TestEveryConsumerHasDeliveryHeadroom`
   iterates `Default().Consumers` and fails on the watchers' `MaxDeliver -1`.
   §6.8 names only `TestEveryWorkStreamHasAConsumer`.
9. **The contract suite cannot stage `SubscribeRebindsAVanishedDurable` as
   written.** The case says "delete the durable and its stream", but the suite
   has only `StreamAdmin`, which deletes durables, not streams. W4.44 splits it
   into a contract case built on `DeleteSubscription` and a natsbus-only test
   that deletes the stream.
10. **`ConsumerSpec.Subscription()` mapping `MaxInFlight` to `Slots` silently
    shrinks every transcode pool's cap from 64 to 1.** `natsbus.Pull` wrote
    `MaxAckPending: max(s.MaxInFlight, 1)`. §9.3 states Pull's new rule but
    not that it must land in the same change. W4.40 does both and pins the
    result with `TestPullWritesTheSubscriptionsCapNotItsSlots`.
11. **`LapsedHandlersDoNotMultiplyConcurrency`'s numbers do not fit the
    suite's 30 s `Timeout`.** 20 tasks of 5 s at no more than 4 at once take at
    least 25 s, before counting the duplicate deliveries of lapsed messages.
    W4.44 uses 8 tasks of 3 s under a 90 s `setupFor`, and asserts both bounds:
    at most `2 × slots`, and more than `slots` (a lapse did free a slot).

### Wave 4d: autoscaling, the manager side (W4.60 to W4.75)

1. **§9.9 `TestReconcilerBuildsTheHPA` contradicts OD46.** It expects a `caption` HPA with
   `maxReplicas 2` on two matching nodes, but caption's consumers are throttled
   (`MaxAckPending == Slots`, so `floor(MAP/slots) = 1`) and the HPA is 0..1. W4.66 runs the
   node-count case on `import` and asserts caption at 1 on two matching nodes.
2. **§9.5's `For(Deployment, has-label predicate)` would never see a label removal**, so "a
   Deployment that loses its domain label loses its HPA" could not happen. W4.66's update
   predicate passes when the old *or* the new object carries the label.
3. **§9.5's `c.SubResource("scale").Update` fails `make lint`:** forbidigo matches
   `client.SubResourceWriter.Update` everywhere but `pkg/k8s`. W4.62 adds `k8s.ScaleTo`. The
   Scale is read before it is written, so RBAC needs `deployments/scale` **get** as well as
   update (§9.5 lists update only).
4. **§9.5's RBAC list omits `configmaps get`**, but the Server reads
   `kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication` with `corev1.ConfigMap`, and
   `TestEveryBuiltinKindAControllerTouchesHasAnRBACMarker` requires a marker for it; the
   installer-rendered kube-system RoleBinding cannot satisfy that guard. No new grant results:
   importarr's role, which the manager's union already holds, grants `configmaps get`.
   `horizontalpodautoscalers` also gets `update` beside `create` and `patch`, the repo's
   convention for a server-side apply that creates.
5. **§9.4 records `ExternalMetricsAPIServiceForeign` "on the manager Deployment"**, but nothing
   tells the manager its own Deployment's name (no flag, no env). W4.71 records it on the TLS
   Secret.
6. **§10.2.4 accepts `TestEveryPackageWithRBACMarkersIsInARole` failing until the installers
   wave**, against the rule that every task leaves tests green. The plan puts
   `./app/autoscale/...` on `RBAC_PATHS_squasharr` until Wave 6 writes `RBAC_PATHS_manager`.
7. **§3.5.3 puts "`recyclesweep.Scheduler` in `app/import/manager`" and calls it "a
   `k8s.LeaderOnly`"**: a package `recyclesweep` cannot be the `manager` package, and §10.3.2's
   `TestLeaderOnlyRunnablesLiveInTheManager` finds it by runnable type. W4.61 makes it
   `app/import/controller/recyclesweep.Scheduler`, a typed runnable with
   `NeedLeaderElection() == true`, registered by `app/import/manager`.
8. **`RecycleSweepTask` is the first cluster-global payload**, and
   `app/catalog/history.TestEveryPayloadHasAResolver` fails without a resolver (the spec does
   not mention it). W4.60 adds one that returns the zero Target.
9. **§9.4's "servers reload it through the APIReader every 60 s" cannot be a background
   runnable** started before the caches (an `EveryReplica` is in controller-runtime's Others
   group, after the cache sync). W4.70 reloads lazily on the handshake that finds the material
   older than 60 s. Also: on a **first** install the TLS Secret comes from the leader-only
   CertManager, which starts after the cache sync, so "the API does not wait out a cache sync"
   holds for restarts, not for the first start.
10. **`QueueGauge` over "every consumer in `events.Default()`"** would, after Wave 4c, include the
    dead-letter watchers on `CLUSTARR_ADVISORIES`; W4.72 reports work consumers only.
11. **Unspecified cases** given Warnings: a domain label naming no autoscaled domain
    (`UnknownDomain`, any owned HPA deleted) and an unparseable `min-replicas` annotation
    (`InvalidMinReplicas`, the domain floor used). The reconciler also ignores labelled
    Deployments outside its namespace (§10.2.2 says it selects in `POD_NAMESPACE`; §9.5 does
    not).
12. **`TestTheServerAnswersBeforeTheCachesSync` needs a front-proxy CA** that envtest's
    kube-apiserver does not publish (no `--requestheader-*` flags), so `ServerOptions` gains
    `AuthConfigMap` (default `kube-system/extension-apiserver-authentication`) for the test to
    name its own.
13. **The `Slots x AutoscaleReplicaCeiling` raise has no owning step** in §11.1: step 6 (R5 bus)
    lists `Slots`, step 7 owns the `pkg/agentdomain` guard that requires the raise. W4.63 does
    the raise; Wave 4c must set `Slots` per §9.1.1 and leave `MaxAckPending` as it is.
14. **`NamespaceGuard` (an `EveryReplica`) is armed only after the caches sync**; a namespace
    deleted while a manager start is still syncing is not guarded, and `docs/autoscaling.md`'s
    manual `kubectl delete apiservice v1beta1.external.metrics.k8s.io` covers it.
15. **`test/e2e/zzz_observability_test.go:215-223`** reads `clustarr_work_queue_pending` from
    `importarr-worker`'s `/metrics`; after the cutover only the manager produces it (§10.4's e2e
    renames need to point there).

### Wave 5: binaries (W5.1 to W5.19)

1. **§11.1 step 8 deletes `cmd/clustarr` before step 9 switches the installers**, while §10.3.3
   moves the installer-argv guards into per-binary `manifest_test.go` files that parse installer
   argv through the new binaries. Between the two steps no binary can parse the installers' argv.
   Resolved: W5.16 keeps every such guard in transitional form, and the two that cannot survive
   are handed to the installers wave (table at the top). Running the installers wave
   immediately after W5 keeps the window to one wave.
2. **§4.3 step 5.6 recuts RBAC paths (§4.6) in Wave 5**, but §4.6's role names are installer-bound
   (chart sentinels, bindings) and §11.1 step 9 owns RBAC regeneration. Resolved: W5 drops only the
   deleted root from `RBAC_PATHS_grabarr`; start envtests bridge new identities to today's roles
   (`starttest.RolesFor`, W5.4).
3. **The agent `Register` shape is inconsistent**: §3.5.2 and §4.2.1 give
   `Register(ctx, mgr, bus, Options) (Registration, error)`, the indexer row
   `Register(ctx, Deps, Options) (io.Closer, error)`, and `Registration` lives in the catalog-specific
   leaf `app/catalog/agent` though all eight domains return it. W5 consumes the first shape for all
   eight (W5.1 checks it).

   set for the single `AddProbes` call. W3.1 adds `Checks.Merge` (W5.3 no longer does); W5.9 uses it.
5. **`downloadclient.EngineCommand(dc, EngineRuntime)`** cannot render the argv: it needs the
   data and scratch directories, and once `BusSingleNode` goes `EngineRuntime` contributes nothing
   to argv. W5.5 uses `EngineCommand(dc, dataDir, scratchDir)`.
6. **§3.2's "package-level run seam (`var runManager = Run`) which tests stub"** cannot be stubbed
   from `cmd/<bin>` tests, a different package. W5 exports `NewCommandWith(run)`.
7. **§4.5.4 denies `sigs.k8s.io/controller-runtime` (prefix) for markers** with no exception, but
   markers links `controller-runtime/pkg/scheme` through `api/catalog/v1alpha1` until §7.2.9

8. **Graft drift in the deps guards**: §4.5.5's transcode `AllowApp` misses `app/squash/grafttask`
   and `app/squash/worker/graft`; §4.5.1's manager `AllowApp` misses `app/squash/grafttask` (the
   AudioGraft controller's task type); and the AudioGraft controller imports `app/squash/worker`

10. **§4.5.6's exec-guard scope omits `internal/`**, the tree this wave creates. W5.14 adds it.
11. **§10.3.3 puts `TestBuildUIArtworkLogsAnUnconnectedBus` in `cmd/ui/bus_test.go`**, but its
    subject (`buildUIBus`, now `buildBus`) is unexported in `internal/cli/ui`. W5.11 tests it there.

### Wave 6: images, installers, RBAC, KEDA removal, e2e renames (W6.1 to W6.17)

1. **§10.1.3's single `native` stage sets `LIBVA_*` on both architectures**, the exact bug main's
   `142d0d4b` fixed in `Dockerfile.transcoder` after the spec's basis (arm64 stages no libva, so
   `LIBVA_DRIVERS_PATH` named amd64's multiarch directory there). W6.5 builds `native` as
   `native-${TARGETARCH}` over a FROM-scratch `native-base`, and `TestTheNativeImageCarriesTheIntelStack`
   holds it, as main's updated `TestTheOneTranscoderImageCarriesTheIntelStack` does.
2. **§10.1.2, §10.1.5 and §10.1.6 use `/ffgo/`, `/par2go/`, `FFGO_DIR ?= ../ffgo` and grep for
   `=> ../ffgo`**, but go.mod (W0.25, W0.26) replaces with `../ffgo-unify` and `../par2go-1bd94eb`.
   W6.3 derives the directories from go.mod; W6.4 and W6.5 copy to `/ffgo-unify/` and `/par2go-1bd94eb/`,
   and `TestEveryGoBuildingDockerfileCarriesTheReplaceStages` holds every Dockerfile to go.mod.
3. **§7.6 item 3 requires par2go's `HEAD` to be `PAR2GO_REF`**; par2go's `HEAD` has moved to `bc4c4f2`
   and must stay where another session left it. W6.3 checks only that the ref resolves (as
   Wave 0 rules) and exports it with `git archive`.
4. **§8.7's par2 stage repeats `FROM scratch AS par2go`**, which §10.1.3/§7.6 already declare at the top
   of `Dockerfile.native`; a Dockerfile cannot declare one stage name twice. Recorded in the hand-off

5. **§10.1.5 says every Dockerfile needs the replace stages, but `hack/e2e.sh` builds
   `Dockerfile.e2e-fixtures` with a bare `docker build`**, which cannot pass the named contexts. W6.6 adds

6. **§10.1.6/§10.1.7's check lists include `self-check:markers` and `self-check:par2-child`, and §10.1.4's
   `notices` list the par2 notices**, none of which exists at §11.1 step 9: markers' `--self-check` lands
   with step 10 (W5.12 keeps `--ffmpeg`), par2 with step 12. W6 lands the lists without them (W6.1 detects a

7. **§10.3.2's `TestEachRoleCoversTheMarkedPackagesItsHomeLinks` says "that identity's home" without
   defining it, and every agent identity's binary is the same `cmd/agent`**, which links every domain; a

   `internal/cli/manager`), built in its binary's cgo mode.
8. **§10.2.1 gives `markers` no `UMASK` (its `/data` is read-only) while §3.7's start order applies

9. **§10.4 maps e2e's `clustarr_download_bytes_total` check from `grabarr` to `manager`, but nothing in the
   tree increments `metrics.DownloadBytesTotal`** (`pkg/obs/metrics/domain.go:63` declares it; no producer).
   `TestObservabilityMetricsNonZero` cannot pass on any workload; W6.15 renames it as specified, and the

10. **§10.2.6 lists `config/e2e`'s patch retargeting under §10.4 (Phase H wording), but W6.11 cannot leave

11. **The `importarr-e2e-patch.yaml` §10.4 retargets at the manager also sets `CLUSTARR_PLEX_BASE_URL`**,

12. **§10.2.1's `GOMEMLIMIT` shares (60%, 50%) are computed by the chart as `× 0.8` today**, and a float

13. **Waves 1 and 4d were drafted calling this wave "Wave 9"** (after §11.1 step 9); the task numbers

### Waves 7 to 10: native media and the docs (W7.1 to W10.11)

1. **`pkg/ffruntime` is scheduled a step too late.** §11.1 puts `pkg/ffruntime`
   in step 11, but step 10's decoder runs every call under `ffruntime.Do`
   (§7.2.1, §7.2.8) and `cmd/markers` gates on `ffruntime.Load`/`Require`
   (§7.2.9). The plan creates `pkg/ffruntime` and `test/nativetest` in W7 (W7.2,
   W7.3); step 11 adopts them in transcode, import and caption.
2. **`ErrAbandoned` is used but not declared.** §7.4's API block lists
   `ErrUnavailable` and `ErrWedged`; `Do` "returns an error wrapping
   `ErrAbandoned`", and the probe wave's W4.1 already names
   `ffruntime.ErrAbandoned`. W7.2 declares it.
3. **atrim's end cannot be read from ffgo's filter graph.** §7.2.3 says to push
   frames "until `abuffersink` returns EOF", but `FilterGraph.Filter` folds
   `AVERROR_EOF` into "no more frames" (`ffgo filter_graph.go:517-518`) and F1-F17
   add no EOF signal. W7.7 stops instead once a frame starting at or after
   `first_pts + duration` has been pushed, which is when atrim has ended, so the
   output is the same; a fork addition (an EOF flag on `Filter`) would be the
   direct form.
4. **`self-check:markers` is not excluded from step 9.** §11.1 step 9 lists what
   the native image lands without until steps 11 and 12, but `markers
   --self-check` exists only from step 10 (§7.2.9). The installers wave noticed
   and handed it here (Wave 6 "Hand-offs"); W7.10 adds it.
5. **OD22's adoption contradicts §8.5.2 and §8.5.3.** The Adoption paragraph
   takes every OD at its recommendation, and OD22 recommends `ErrMemory` and a
   child that died without a result be local faults; §8.5.2 ("`ErrChildDied`
   becomes `ErrRepairFailed` (today's behaviour)") and §8.5.3's table were written
   before the decision. W9.4 implements the recommendation (`ErrPar2Crashed`,
   `writeError`).
6. **The repair child cannot be `os.Executable()` in a test binary without a
   dispatch.** §8.6 probes the library at engine start (`par2 library ready`),
   through `par2child.Exec{}`, whose child is `os.Executable()`. In any envtest
   that builds a usenet engine that is the test binary, which would run the
   package's tests again as its own child. W9.3 adds `par2child.RunIfChild()`,
   and W9.6 puts it first in the `TestMain` of every such package.
7. **par2go exports no loaded-library path.** §8.4's `Result.Library` and
   `par2-repair --self-check`'s "print `par2go <library path>`" need one;
   par2go keeps it in `internal/bindings.Path()`. W9.3 reads it from
   `/proc/self/maps` (`par2child.Library()`), as `ffruntime.Report` does for FFmpeg.
8. **Stream durations use `print_time`, not `print_duration_time`.** §6.3's
   "N/A rule (a duration of 0, or a non-duration at AV_NOPTS_VALUE, becomes 0)"
   reads as if a stream duration followed the duration rule. In FFmpeg n9's
   `ffprobe.c` (`show_stream`), stream and format durations are printed with
   `print_time` (`is_duration` 0), so `AV_NOPTS_VALUE` is N/A and 0 prints as
   `0.000000`. W8.4's `ffprobeTime` follows the source; the parity test is the
   arbiter.
9. **`inprocess.New` has no class to require.** §7.4 says it becomes "`Load()`
    plus `Require` of its class", but `New()` takes no class. W8.5 changes the
    signature to `New(class transcode.Hardware)` and maps the pool class onto
    `selfcheck.Needs`.
10. **Where the probe oracle's decoders live.** Wave 1's defect 8 left open
    whether `BuildRaw`/`MergeFrame` stay in `pkg/mediainfo` (§4.3 step 1.7) or go
    to the oracle (§6.2). The native probe does not need them; W8.7 moves them
    to `test/ffprobeoracle` per §6.2 and deletes `AudioProbeFrom(pd)` from
    `pkg/mediainfo` in favour of `AudioProbeFromRaw`.
11. **§4.5.4 and §4.5.5 do not deny `test/` for markers and transcode.** Once the
    oracle moves under `test/` (W8.7), the manager's and the agent's lists deny it
    (`…/test/`) but markers' and transcode's do not. W8.7 adds `mod+"test"` to both.
12. **markers' closure can now deny `os/exec`.** §7.7 says the markers closure
    has no `os/exec`; §4.5.4's deny list omits it. W7.9 adds it (the transcode
    closure keeps `os/exec` through go-ffprobe's package, a types-only
    dependency under OD12, so it cannot be denied there).

### Fold waves F0-F9: ADR-0016, the MediaFile remediation loop (F0.1 to F9.5)

The fold's planners recorded where the loop spec (`docs/superpowers/specs/2026-10-06-mediafile-remediation-loop-design.md`), and in a few places the split plan or the split spec, was wrong, silent or out of date, and how their tasks resolve it. The loop spec is not edited by the fold; F8.11 carries the split spec amendments. Waves F0-F1, F7 and F9 give their planners' full notes, moved here from their wave sections; the other waves give their planners' summaries, and their preambles' deviation lists say the same at more length.

#### Waves F0 and F1: prerequisites, and the records core (F0.1 to F1.5)

Each is a place where the loop spec (or a split-plan task it relies on) cannot be implemented as
written; the task named carries the resolution.

- **D1.** §4.5's `RecordHeader` tags `RequestedAt` as `json:"requestedAt"`; W4.3's `ProbeRecord` tags it
  `omitzero` and W4.3's test asserts a seed omits it, so the spec'd tag would change the probe
  record's JSON and fail `TestProbeRecordWireFormatIsUnchanged`. F1.1 keeps `omitzero`.
- **D2.** §4.12/§8.6 F1.1 embed `RecordHeader` flat and say W4.4's suite is the regression check with
  "no snippet in these tasks changes" (§8.3, Wave 4a row). Go forbids promoted fields in composite
  literals, so every `schema.ProbeRecord{State: …}`-style literal in W4.3, W4.4, W4.6, W4.11, W4.12
  and W4.13 stops compiling. F1.1 rewrites them mechanically (deviation 3).
- **D3.** §4.6/§4.12 change `Store.Request` to `NextSeq(rec.Seq, 0, now)`, whose time floor makes a first
  Seq the clock's millisecond. W4.4's `TestRequestSequencesAndCarriesTheAbandonedCount` (Seq 1, then 2),
  W4.6's `TestTheProbeWorkerAnswersOnlyTheCurrentRequest` (Seq 2) and W4.13's
  `TestAFailedProbeRetriesOnItsBackoff` (Seq 2) assert literal Seqs; F1.1 makes them relative.
- **D4.** §4.5's reading rule (a record whose `MediaFile.UID` is not the key's token reads as absent) makes
  W4.4's `TestAnswerRules` fixtures, which carry no `MediaFile`, read as absent; F1.1 adds the file to
  each fixture.
- **D5.** §4.9 types `recordsource.New` with `remediation.Key` and decodes `segments.Record` v2, neither of
  which exists until F3.1/F3.4, though F1.4 builds the waker and moves the probe onto it. F1.4 makes
  `New` generic in its key type with a `WithDecoder` option.
- **D6.** §4.9 opens with `WatchUpdatesOnly` (no replay), but §8.6 F1.4 says W4.12's tests keep passing;
  W4.12's first test asserts the replay of a pre-start record and its second drives internals
  `recordsource` replaces. F1.4 amends the first and replaces the second, by name (deviation 2).
- **D7.** §4.9 needs the bucket stream's last sequence and creation time, but §4.13/§4.15 add no `KV`
  method that reads them. F1.3 adds `KV.Status(ctx) (KVStatus, error)` on both buses.
- **D8.** §4.9 detects a recreated bucket only when the watch channel closes. nats.go's ordered consumer
  (the KV watch) resets onto a stream deleted and created again at its old sequence + 1 rather than
  always closing, so the source could wait forever on a recreated bucket (inferred from nats.go's
  ordered-consumer reset, not reproduced). F1.4 also checks `KV.Status` every 30 s.
- **D9.** §8.6 F1.2 has `Ensure` "returning each durable's lag in its report", but `Ensure` returns only
  `error` and has many callers and fakes. F1.2 adds `events.RetiredReporter` on both buses
  (deviation 4).
- **D10.** §4.3 caps the live `clustarr-segments` bucket at 128 MiB / 16 KiB per value without recording
  its current size (§7.1 lists none). A KV stream discards new, so a bucket already above the cap
  refuses every write after the update. The runbook (§7.5) should read its byte count first.
- **D11.** §4.15's `TestRecordsRequestersAreTheLoop` (Request and Withdraw only from `app/remediation`)
  conflicts with keeping `probestore.Request` (W4.4's API, §4.12) as a wrapper over
  `records.Requester.Request`; the guard needs a `pkg/probestore` exception, or F3.2 must call the
  requester from the loop. (Settled in F7.4: `recordsCaller` admits each store package's own
  wrapper, and the scan holds every other caller to `app/remediation`.)
- **D12.** §4.5 cannot count `clustarr_record_errors_total{op="decode"}` inside `pkg/records`, which may
  import only `pkg/events`, its schema and the standard library; F1.1 adds `Spec.Errors`, bound by
  the manager. Relatedly, "TestRecordsLinksNoKubernetes" cannot mean no `k8s.io` at all:
  `pkg/events/schema` links `k8s.io/apimachinery` through `api/common/v1alpha1`; F1.1 bans the
  client, controller-runtime, Prometheus and FFmpeg.
- **D13.** §3.20 extends `TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile` to allow exactly `ledger.profileWake` and
  `subtitleProfileWake` and fail on any other `source.Channel` fed from the loop's MediaFile
  handlers, but §8.6 F0.3 omits that half, neither channel exists before F5/F6, and the spec does not
  say how a source can be attributed to the loop's handlers syntactically. F0.3 implements the
  `For`/`Owns`/`Watches`/`source.Kind`/`GetInformer` half; F5.3 and F6.3 must add the channel half.
  (Done in the review of 2026-10-07: F5.3 adds `channelSources`, an allow-list of every raw channel
  source outside the loop keyed by package and channel expression, at most two of them
  MediaFile-driven; F6.3 adds `ledger.profileWake` and the admission wake; F6.6 drops the doomed
  `transcodejob` row.)
- **D14.** §4.15 names the buffer test twice ("`KVWatchDeliversPastTheBuffer` … the wave gate's
  `WatchDeliversEveryKeyPastTheBuffer`"); F1.3 uses the first only.
- **D15.** §8.6 F1.1 asks to rename `clustarr_probe_requests_total` "in amendment §A2.3", but W4.5 added it
  only to `wantSeries` and observability.md; F1.1 adds the record families (and
  `clustarr_probe_duration_seconds`, if absent) to §A2.3.
- **D16.** §8.6 assigns `RecordKey`, `RecordSubKey` and `ParseKVKeyToken` to F1.2, but §4.7's
  `Withdraw(key, rev, seq)` over an absent record must build its header from the key, so
  `pkg/records` (F1.1) needs them first (deviation 1).
- **D17** (split plan, not the loop spec). W4.2 adds the Durable `clustarr-probes` bucket but leaves
  `pkg/events/mediakey_test.go`'s `TestForSingleNodeKeepsDurableBucketsOnFile`, which lists Durable
  buckets by name, out of its Files; W4.2's own Step 4 (`go test ./pkg/events/...`) would fail on it.
  F1.2 rewrites that list with every Durable bucket.

#### Wave F2: API (F2.1 to F2.4)

1. §2.5: `TranscodeState.Phase` is `json:"phase"` (no `omitempty`) yet `+optional`. A typed marshal of a phase-less block (171 live legacy blocks, and the interim reconciler's own `TranscodeState` writes until F6) sends `phase: ""`, which the enum refuses, so under §3.7's JSON round-trip status apply (F3.1) every such file's status apply would be refused between F3.1 and F6. F2.1 makes it `json:"phase,omitempty"` in release N; F9.2 makes it `json:"phase"`, `+required`.
2. §2.11.2/§2.11.4: `TestMediaFileStringsAreBounded` cannot pass with the spec's cap table: `spec.mediaRef.name` (`commonv1.MediaRef.Name`) and `status.transcode.jobRef` (§2.5's code) have no MaxLength. F2.2 adds `MaxLength=253` to both.
3. §8.6 F2.4 says the CRD diff is limited to MediaFile, Movie and Episode, with the three legacy CRDs unchanged. It is not: §2.11.2 caps the shared `commonv1` types `MediaInfo`, `Quality.name` and `MediaRef`, so albums, audiobooks, issues, searches, downloads, transcodejobs (`status.result.mediaInfo`) and audiografts (`spec.itemRef`) change too, ten CRDs in all; only subtitlerequests is unchanged. F2.4 checks those ten and that the diff is additive.
4. §2.11.3: `MediaFileObjectBudgetBytes` = 768 KiB does not hold in release N. N's sidecars list is a map keyed by a 4096-byte path, so `catalogarr`'s managedFields entry repeats every key (32 × about 4.2 KB, about 131 KiB), which the 660 KiB estimate leaves out; the modelled worst case is about 778 KiB. F2.2 uses `832<<10` in N and F9.2 restores `768<<10`. The status budget (320 KiB, modelled 299 KiB) holds.
5. §2.11.3's budget arithmetic is in bytes at MaxLength, but CRD `maxLength` counts runes (kube-openapi `validate.MaxLength` uses `utf8.RuneCount`). A value the renderer does not clamp to bytes can reach four times its estimate: importarr's spec strings, or stored values carried forward. Only `Render`'s byte clamp makes the status bound provable.
6. §2.11.2 caps importarr's spec fields (`importedFrom.releaseTitle` 512, `indexerName` 253, `releaseGroup` and `edition` 256) but says nothing of importarr clamping them, and a Download's `ReleaseInfo` title, indexer name, group and edition are uncapped, so an import of a longer title would be refused at the MediaFile apply. F2.2 clamps in fileimport (`frozenRelease` and the indexer-name and non-video sites) to Go constants mirrored to the CRD.
7. §2.11.2 says only that the probe clamps stream titles. TranscodeJob's `status.result.mediaInfo` takes the same new caps (codec, profile, language, container and others) and has no renderer, so an over-long value would refuse squasharr's status write. F2.2 clamps every newly capped `MediaInfo` string in `pkg/mediainfo.toMediaInfo` (shared with the native prober through `FromRaw`), without a `ProbeVersion` raise.
8. §2.11.1 rule 3 sanitises every string, but a C1 control replaced inside a path or file name (`sidecars[].path`/`name`, `transcode.result.outputPath`, `naming.expectedPath`, `AudioDonor.path`) records a path that does not exist. F2.2 drops such an entry, as rule 1 drops an over-long one.
9. §2.11.1 rule 5 ("stored values are never re-clamped") must be judged per top-level status field, not per leaf: validation ratcheting correlates map-list entries by key but not the items of atomic lists (`mediaInfo.audio` and every new list), so a leaf-level carry inside a changed atomic list sends an over-cap value the apiserver refuses.
10. §2.9: "an invalid nonce ... is recorded", but the `handledNonces` fields are MaxLength 63. An over-long invalid value cannot be recorded as it is, and a clamped record never equals the annotation, so the nonce would be handled again (with a Warning Event) on every pass. F2.1 adds `catalogv1alpha1.HandledNonce(v)`: `v` when valid, else `invalid-` plus 16 hex digits of its sha256; F5 and F6 compare and record through it.
11. §2.4 puts `AnnotationSubtitleSearch` in `shared_types.go`, while §2.9 says the constants live in `mediafile_annotations.go`, and §2.9 names no Go constants for the five transcode annotations. F2.1 puts all six in `mediafile_annotations.go`: `AnnotationSubtitleSearch` and `AnnotationTranscode{Retry,Cancel,Suspend,Priority,Hardware}`.
12. §2.11.4 lists `TestSubtitleLanguageStateMirrorsTheFetchVerdicts` under F2.2, but the verdicts are `schema.SubtitleRecord`'s, created in F5.1, and the two sets differ (kept, throttled and dropped have no `SubtitleState`). It can only be a mapping check, written in F5.1.
13. §2.11.1 names `mediafilestatus.Render` without a package path or signature, and rule 5 needs the stored status as well as the draft; it does not name the Warning Event reason for a drop either. F2.2: `app/remediation/mediafilestatus.Render(stored, draft *MediaFileStatus) (MediaFileStatus, []Drop)`, Event reason `StatusEntryDropped`. It also dedupes duplicate map-list keys (sidecar path, condition type), which the apiserver refuses whole.
14. §2.6/§2.14: `AudioDonor.release` and `rejectedReleases` copy Download release titles into Movie and Episode status by server-side apply, and §2.11's sanitising covers MediaFile only, so one C1 control in a Download title would block the item's status apply. F2.3 bounds and sanitises in `rollup.AudioStateAC`, keeps the newest 16 rejected releases, and drops a donor whose path is over 4096 bytes or unprintable.
15. §2.11.4 step 1 says "every string at maxLength", yet §2.11.3's conditions figure (15,001 B) assumes realistic types and reasons; `metav1.Condition`'s `type` (316) and `reason` (1024) at their caps would add about 16 KB. The worst-case generator overrides conditions with the closed type set and 1 KiB messages (F2.2). The "`conditions[].message` is exempt" note is unnecessary: `metav1.Condition`'s message already carries `maxLength` 32768.

#### Wave F3: the remediation loop core, the probe, naming and markers planners, the rename and replay actuators (F3.1 to F3.6)

1. §8.6 F3.1/F3.3 cannot leave a working tree: F3.1 "dissolves the mediafile Reconciler / controller name mediafile", but the probe, naming and markers planners arrive only in F3.2-F3.4, and the old controller cannot run beside the loop (the same controller name, two writers of MediaFile status under `catalogarr`). F3.1-F3.3 build the loop unwired and F3.4 switches; the `--remediation-*` flags (§8.3's W5.7 row says F3.1) and the deletion of `app/import/controller/rename` (§8.6 F3.3) move to F3.4 with the switch.
2. §4.11, §4.13 and §8.6 F3.4 name `segmenting.Sweeper`, while F3.4 deletes `app/catalog/segmenting` in the same task; the sweeper lands as `segmentplan.Sweeper`, registered from `app/catalog/manager` so the registration guards see it wired.
3. §4.9's `recordsource.New` signature (`toKey` returning `remediation.Key`, a `source.TypedSource[remediation.Key]`) is impossible at F1.4 (`remediation.Key` is F3.1's) and would be an import cycle (`app/remediation` imports `recordsource`); it must be generic in the key (F1.4 builds `New[K comparable]` with `WithDecoder`).
4. §3.5's `View` and `Result` are incomplete for the planners §3.x describes: naming needs `spec.path` as of this pass (a swap the probe incorporates moves it), hence `View.Main`/`SpecPath()`; §3.7's limiter exemptions are "decided from the pass's own content" but only a planner knows its change is an answer or a first probe, hence `Result.Unpaced`; §4.15's incorporation and timeout counters cannot be incremented from a pure `Plan`, hence `Result.Records`. `RecordWrite` also needs request-counter labels and a pacer class (F5 asked for `Pace`), and `Publish` a schedule time (segment plans use `WithScheduleAt`).
5. §3.8 describes effects as data, `RecordWrite{Bucket, Key, Revision, Value}` executed by the loop, while §4.5/§4.7 say the loop writes through `Requester.Request` with `MaxValue` refusal and fact protection, and §4.15's `TestRecordsBucketsOpenOnlyThroughTheirStores` forbids raw bucket access; the two disagree. F3 follows §3.8 (and Wave F6) with revision-CAS raw writes; the store guard must exempt `app/remediation`'s executor, and per-bucket `MaxValue` is not enforced on the loop's writes. (F7.4's `TestRecordsBucketsOpenOnlyThroughTheirStores` exempts `app/remediation`.)
6. §3.5's structural gate (every planner after the probe keeps its last block while `!ProbeCurrent`) contradicts split §6.5.3/W4.13's pending path, which re-rendered naming as `NamingReasonProbePending`: a never-probed or pending file now keeps its previous naming (nil for a new file). The loop spec does not say so.
7. §4.7 meters the probe low lane at 600/min and requires the reservation check before "record reads of keys that are due but not in flight", but a version-only probe request changes no status, so the loop cannot know it is in flight without reading the record; F3.2 reserves after the `Get`. W4.13 and split §6.5 never paced the probe at all.
8. §3.9's rename gate ("`status.transcode.phase` and `status.graft.phase` terminal or absent") names blocks only F6 and F7 build, and an actuator that runs on every pass would retry a collision or a held rename on every wake (the old controller retried only on predicate changes); the spec is silent. F3.3 adds per-proposal memory and leaves an `inFlight` hook for F6.2 and F7.2.
9. §3.20 lists `TestAHungMountNeverStallsItemsOrGrants`, `TestAClaimArrivingBeforeTheCacheSeesQueuedIsIncorporated`, `TestAProbeThatChangesTheCodecPicksTheWinnerInTheSamePass` and `TestAMultiEpisodeFileWakesEveryEpisode` without owning tasks; they need item keys (F4), grants (F6) or profile selection (F5, F6), so F3 writes only their file-key halves, under other names. `TestBulkWritesArePaced`'s 1,000 files is impractical in envtest; F3 tests the rate with 20.
10. §3.3's S1' (status-only updates to item keys and `subtitleProfileWake`) has nothing to enqueue before F4.2 and F5.3; and §3.2's `KeyKind` block lists the item kinds that §8.6 gives to F4.1 ("`remediation.Key` and one index"), which Wave F4 reads as F3.1 defining `KindMediaFile` only (F3 follows F4).
11. §8.3's W2.9 row lists `segmentplan.{…, Due}` while §3.1 keeps `segments.Due` in `pkg/segments` (W7.4 moves it to `segmentplan`); and W5.14's committed `AllowApp` for `cmd/manager` listed `app/catalog/segmenting`, not `segmentplan`, which the inverted W2.9 makes the manager link (W5.14 now carries the fix).
12. §4.12 does not name the JSON key of `segments.Record` v2's file reference that the S21 waker decodes, nor require the loop's NotFound messages for queries it decides without asking (multi-episode, non-aired order) to stay byte-identical to the handler's (`status.markers` feeds cluster-plex's SeedKey). F3.4 picks `file` and pins the messages with a test.
13. §8.6 F3.4 retires `ManagerCatalogarrMarkers` into `RetiredFieldManagers`, but W5.19's `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome` iterates `FieldManagers()` only, so a retired manager could silently regain a writer; F3.4 adds "retired managers have no writer" to the guard.

#### Wave F4: item keys (F4.1 to F4.4)

1. §8.6 F4.1 says `episode.MediaFileByEpisodeIndex` should point at `remediation.mediafile.item` "so the segment planner keeps working". It would not: the new index's values are `<kind>/<name>`, and the planner passes a bare episode name (`segmenting/plan.go:162`, `segmentplan` after W2.9), so an alias compiles and silently finds no files. F4.1 deletes the alias and switches the planner and its fake-client test to `mfindex.Item` and `mfindex.ItemKey`.
2. §3.12 says the item path's MediaFile and AudioGraft watches "go" and graft state is read from MediaFile `status.graft`, but `status.graft` is written only from F7.2 and the donor only from F7.1, and §3.3 S23 keeps the AudioGraft watches "F3 to F7"; dropping the AudioGraft watch in F4 would freeze `status.audio.graft`. F4 keeps the AudioGraft watch and read in `Watches()` until F7.3; §3.12 and §8.6 F4.2 should say so.
3. §3.16 says every index is "registered once by `remediation.RegisterIndexes`", and its "Consolidated" paragraph has the loop use `series.EpisodeBySeriesRefIndex`, which the Series controller (not folded) registers, so the loop registering it is an indexer conflict at start. The loop reads it without registering it; F4.1 exports `series.RegisterIndexes` for the Series controller and the test harnesses.
4. §3.12 places `applyItemStatus` somewhere the item packages can call without importing `app/remediation`. It cannot be `rollup` (the catalog agent links `rollup` through `worker/search` and `worker/grab`, so a `catalogarr` write there makes W5.19's `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome` see `catalogarr` in the `catalog` home), nor `app/remediation` (an import cycle). F4.2 adds a manager-only leaf, `app/catalog/controller/itemstatus`, whose `Apply` is `PatchStatusCAS`'s single attempt over the planned view without the redundant read: it applies with the item's `resourceVersion`.
5. §3.3 S1 enqueues "the item keys of the old and new mediaRef" on every S1 update, annotation- and label-only updates included, but `spec.mediaRef` is immutable (CEL `self == oldSelf`) and §2.14 limits item wake-ups to rollup inputs. S1 should enqueue item keys on create, delete, generation change and `FileSignature` change (S1') only; F4.2 implements that narrower rule.
6. §2.14 says the new wake-ups fix "Album, Book, Audiobook and Issue missing probe-only verdict changes", but the Album, Book and Audiobook rollups read only MediaFile spec (`FilesByRecording`, quality and format), so S1' only adds wakes they do not need; only Issue (`rollup.FileState` to Transcoded) reads a status verdict.
7. Not addressed in the spec: folding six item controllers into one controller makes every item map function part of the loop's `HasSynced`. `albumsOf`, `booksOf`, `issuesOf` and the Artist, Author and Comic scans in `mapQualityProfile` list a whole namespace, with deep copies, per event during the initial sync (CLAUDE.md's map-function gotcha), and a slow one now delays every file pass. F4.3 adds `client.UnsafeDisableDeepCopy` to those Lists; §3.17 should cover it, and a follow-up should read the parents' existing indexes (`.spec.artistRef`, `.spec.authorRef`, `.spec.comicRef`).
8. A cross-wave guard gap: `TestControllerNamesAreUniqueAcrossTheBinary` (W5.15, from `cmd/clustarr`'s `runnable_registration_test.go`) counts only chains that start with `NewControllerManagedBy`, so the loop's `builder.TypedControllerManagedBy[Key]` chain is invisible to it, and the fold removes eleven counted chains against its floor of at least 30 (`mediafile` and `rename` in F3, six item controllers in F4, `subtitlerequest` in F5, `transcodejob` in F6, `audiograft` in F7). The guard must recognise typed builders, or the floor must drop (Cross-wave interface gaps, item 15).
9. §3.11's priority table does not say at what priority an item key's own requeue (an air date, availability, the 1 s conflict retry) is enqueued; F4.2 uses `PriorityTimed` (-50), and the spec should state it.
10. §3.2 and §8.6 are ambiguous about which task declares the item `KeyKind` constants (F3.1 lists "keys", F4.1 says "`remediation.Key`"), and the fold's planning files assumed differently; Wave F4 assumes F3.1 declares only `KindMediaFile`.
11. Citation drift: §2.14's Episode row cites the apply at `episode/reconciler.go:578`; on the current tree it is `:603`, which §3.12 cites correctly.

#### Wave F5: subtitles in MediaFile status (F5.1 to F5.5)

1. §8.6 puts the FetchTask v2 and SubtitleEvent v2 history resolvers in F5.4, but `app/catalog/history/target.go` decodes both structs and `TestEveryPayloadHasAResolver` demands a resolver for each payload's current schema, so F5.1 (FetchTask v2) and F5.2 (SubtitleEvent v2) neither compile nor pass unless the v2 resolvers move with the structs. F5.4 keeps only the namespace-only v1 resolvers and a test pinning the DLQ projector's `mediafiles` grant.
2. §8.3's W5.19 row and §8.6 F5.3 retire `ManagerCaptionarrWorker` in F5.3, but F5.2 removes the fetch worker's last write, so W5.19's `TestEveryFieldManagerHasItsHome` fails at F5.2 on `wantHomes[captionarr-worker]={caption}`. F5.2 sets that row to nil; the full retirement cannot move earlier, since `app/caption/status` tests still call `PatchRequest(captionarr-worker)` until F5.3.
3. §8.3's W5.7 row names only F5.3 among F5's amendments to `TestManagerFieldIndexes`, but F5.1 registers `remediation.mediafile.subtitles` (S14) and must amend it too.
4. §3.16 says every MediaFile index is registered by `remediation.RegisterIndexes`, but `remediation.mediafile.subtitleProfile`'s only reader is the slim SubtitleProfile reconciler registered by `app/caption/manager`, which must start without the loop (its own envtest); a second `IndexField` on the same name is an indexer conflict, so that reconciler registers it (`mfindex.RegisterSubtitleProfile`).
5. §6.4.3's five listing gates never re-list a file Blocked on `MediaDirUnreadable` or `MediaFileNotOnDisk`, so §6.4.1's 5-minute wake replans without reading the directory and the block can never lift; a sixth gate (the previous block is disk-Blocked) is needed.
6. §6.4's `Input` omits fields the planner needs: `Labels` (§3.3 requires `View.Labels()` for profile selection), `ProbeCurrent` (the hold reads the draft), the path and probe hash this process last listed (gates 3 and 4), the records-pacer slot (gate 1 checks it before listing, §4.7) and the `Admin.Subjects` reading (§6.4.6), which only `Gather` can do.
7. §6.6 gives the subtitle record schema as `captionarr.SubtitleRecord.v1`, while §4.5's `RecordHeader` says `Schema` is `records.<remediation>.v1` (`records.subtitle.v1`), which the generic `Get` checks against the `Spec`; F5 uses `records.subtitle.v1`.
8. §6.6 says every subtitle answer is a fact, its Answer rule list drops an answer over `withdrawn{S}`, and §4.8 says a `Spec.Fact` answer is written over `withdrawn{S}`: the three disagree. F5 sets `Fact` = verdict `downloaded` (the only answer that changed the disk).
9. §3.8's `Withdraw{UID, Seq}` effect names neither the subtitle `langKey` nor a revision, while §6.6 specifies `Withdraw(fileUID, langKey, seq, rev)`; subtitle withdrawals need a `Sub` field (F3.1 adds `Withdraw.Sub`, executed through the planner's `Withdrawer` with a fresh read).
10. §6.4.4/§6.4.6: on new bytes every outstanding request is withdrawn, but when the same pass redispatches that language, the withdrawal and the new requested-record write both compare-and-swap at the revision `Gather` read, so the second always misses. F5 skips the withdrawal and lets the higher Seq supersede the old task.
11. §6.4.6's `Admin.Subjects` check cannot tell the current dispatch's task from an older, superseded one on the same (`fileUID`, `langKey`) subject (subjects carry no Seq, and R7 forbids changing them), so an evicted current task is masked until the 26 h timeout.
12. §2.9 records an invalid one-shot nonce, but `handledNonces.subtitleSearch` is MaxLength 63 and the value may not fit or match the nonce format; F5.4 records a deterministic mark, `invalid-<fnv32 hex>`. (F2.1 already produces `ValidNonce` and `HandledNonce`, whose mark is `invalid-` plus 16 hex digits of a sha256; Cross-wave interface gaps item 16.)
13. §2.9 names Events only for transcode nonces with nothing to do (`NothingToRetry`, `NothingToCancel`); none is named for a subtitle search nonce with nothing to search (F5 uses `NothingToSearch`).
14. §2.4 declares the `SubtitleState` type and its enum but names no Go constants; F2.1 must produce them (F5 assumes `SubtitleStatePending` … `SubtitleStateFailed`).
15. §6.2 decision 7 and §6.7.2 delete the worker's upgrade margin and have the loop derive `upgradable`, yet §6.7.1 and §8.6 F5.2 say "the upgrade margin comes from the task": `UpgradeMarginPoints` has no decision left in the worker.
16. §6.4.5's wake ("the minimum of the scheduled `nextSearchAt` values") would requeue every 30 s for a past-due language waiting behind a closed backlog gate or a future pacer slot, and `schedule.go`'s `wantedDueAt` returns now for a never-searched language, so `nextSearchAt` is rewritten every pass (bulk status writes). F5 counts only future `nextSearchAt` values in the wake and keeps a stored `nextSearchAt` for a never-searched language.
17. §6.12's `TestAgentCaptionRoleHasNoWriteVerbs` presumes an agent-caption role, but until W6.9 the caption domain runs under the `captionarr` role it shares with manager-side caption controllers (SubtitleProfile and SubtitleProvider status patches); F5 checks the RBAC markers of the `app/caption` packages the domain links.
18. §4.7 says the pacer reservation is consumed when the request's apply lands, but §3.8's effect list cannot express it; F5 relies on `RecordWrite.Pace`.
19. §4.5/§4.8 do not say how `Answerer.Answer` reports a dropped answer, which the worker needs to count and publish only landed answers (§6.7.4); F1.1's `Answer` returns `records.Dropped` (or `DroppedFact`) with a nil error.
20. Split plan W5.10: `cmd/agent`'s start envtest runs no manager, so `verifyCaptionarrWorker` (moved verbatim) waits for a fetch task nothing publishes; F5.2 makes it seed the requested record and publish the v2 task itself.

#### Wave F6: transcode and admission (F6.1 to F6.7)

1. An import cycle: §3.5 types `View.Ledger` as `admission.Snapshot` (`remediation` imports `admission`), while §5.5 gives the ledger a `loopQueue priorityqueue.PriorityQueue[remediation.Key]` and §5.3's `LoopSource()` returns a source over the loop's `Key` (`admission` imports `remediation`). F6 resolves it with a generic `admission.LoopSource[K](l, toKey)` and `Snapshot` = `transcodeplan.Ledger`.
2. §5.3 says `transcodeplan` defines an `Admission` interface so it never imports `admission`, yet the planner's pure input is typed `admission.Snapshot`; the snapshot type must live in `transcodeplan` (aliased in `admission`).
3. §5.1/§5.3 say `Admit`, `admitsBefore`, `ChooseClass`, `assignClasses` and `unhealthyClasses` move "unchanged" into `admission`, but `assignClasses` and `unhealthyClasses` are `transcodejob.Reconciler` methods over TranscodeJob and TranscodeProfile; only `Admit`, `admitsBefore`, `ChooseClass` and `unhealthyMessage` can move verbatim.
4. §5.8 step 3 calls `jobspec.BuildTask`, but W2.30's `BuildTask` takes a `*TranscodeJob` and an `int32` attempt, and `jobspec.OutputPath` takes a `TranscodeJobSpec`; with D16 dropping `spec.outputPath` both must be re-signed (F6.2, F6.4), the old forms kept for the doomed controller.
5. §8.6 retires `squasharr-transcode-results` into `Topology.Retired` in F6.4 while `ResultsConsumer` (retired in F6.6) still subscribes; `Subscribe` binds only and waits for a missing durable (W4.42), which would stall the TranscodeJob envtests for two tasks. F6 moves the retirement to F6.6.
6. §8.6 F6.3 makes `transcodeprofile` slim with pool rendering from the ledger, but F6.6 still lists "TranscodeProfile's MediaFile and TranscodeJob watches", and the TranscodeJob admission pass that also renders pools under `squasharr-pool` survives until F6.6: two pool renderers in one manager unless registration is swapped at once. F6 builds in F6.3 and registers in F6.6.
7. §2.13 adds `TranscodeProfile.status.waitingFiles`, but F2.4's gate limits F2's API diff to MediaFile, Movie and Episode and no F task adds the field; F6.3 does.
8. "JobEvent v2" appears only in §8.6 F6.5, with no field definition, while §5.8 step 8 already publishes `clustarr.evt.transcode.job.<action>.<mfUID>` from the dispatch (F6.4). F6.4 defines it (`File`, `Seq` replacing `JobRef`) with its producer, sink case and resolver.
9. `records.FactWindow` is used as a constant (§2.3, §3.5, §5.9, §5.10), but §4.10 defines it per remediation as `Task.Deadline` + `deadlineGrace`, capped at 7 days; F1.1 makes it a function, and F6 calls `records.FactWindow(deadline, deadlineGrace)`.
10. §5.5/§5.17's `TestAClearedBlockFreesItsSlot` says new bytes clear a Queued block (`Queued(5)` to `none(5)`), contradicting §5.9's row (withdraw, then Pending or ProbePending, window place kept). F6 tests §5.9's behaviour, and a pure absent-block observation separately.
11. §5.17's falsification names `FuzzLedgerNeverOverAdmits` for the publish-before-Queued swap, but the ledger model has no publish and cannot observe effect order.
12. §5.9's DeadLettered row needs the DLQ projector to resolve a `transcode.Task.v2` dead letter to the MediaFile, but §8.6 leaves resolver retargeting to F8.6, so the row could not fire between F6 and F8; F6.5 adds the v2 task resolver.
13. Nothing in §5 or §8.6 says what audio-graft joins do between F6 and F7: before F7 there is no `status.graft` or `status.audio.donor`, and after F6.6 no TranscodeJob exists for `audiograft.JoinTask` to ride, so every AudioGraft runs standalone after its 6-hour wait until F7.3; `Eligible`'s "no standalone graft in flight" must read AudioGraft (`graftstate`) until F7.2.
14. §8.6 F6.3 says admission "uses catalogarr's `!finishedAt.After(probedAt)`", but that comparison belongs to the swap's incorporation (`transcodeplan`, F6.2), not to admission.
15. §3.4 step 8 and §3.5's `Result` have no channel for the transcode planner's per-pass eligibility that §5.5's `Observe(FileView)` needs (eligible, profile, effective priority); F6.3 adds `Result.Eligibility`.
16. §3.8 lists `Withdraw{UID, Seq}` as a generic effect, but the transcode withdrawal also needs the lease's cancel marker and the task-subject purge, and admission's sweep needs the same code; F6.5 puts it in `app/squash/task.Withdrawal` behind F3.1's `Withdrawer`.
17. §5.10 lists the withdrawal causes (Cancelled, Suspended, Rerouted, Unclaimed, SourceChanged, Orphaned, DeadlineExceeded) but omits DeadLettered and ProfileGone, which §5.9 also routes through withdrawal.
18. §2.9's "Retry clears a Failed or Skipped verdict and resets attempts" does not say what phase results; F6.5 clears the block so the file returns to the backlog and the window takes it again (`lastSeq` keeps the sequence floor).
19. §5.12/§2.13 do not say what TranscodeProfile Ready reads while counts are withheld before the ledger is rebuilt; F6.3 adds reason `WaitingForAdmission`, then Ready/Reconciled once counts are written (what W5.8's replacement verify waits on).
20. §5.17 names both `TestWorkerLostIsRetried` and §4.15's `TestLostWorkerIsRedispatched` for one scenario.
21. §3.7's applied-status memo makes any envtest that seeds MediaFile status from outside the loop read as a stale view for up to 30 s; §5.17's seeded-state envtests must seed before the manager starts (F6.4's harness does).
22. W5.8's `verifySquashController` asserted a rendered pool Job's command; after the fold a pool exists only for a dispatched file, which a manager-only start test cannot produce (no import agent probes a file current). The replacements are `pool.TestTemplateRunsTheTranscodeBinary` and F6.4's `TestDispatchPublishesOneTaskPerSeq`.
23. §5.9's deadline row uses `Task.Deadline`, which status does not keep; the planner re-derives it from the current profile (`jobspec.ActiveDeadline`), so a profile edit moves a running dispatch's deadline.

#### Wave F7: graft (F7.1 to F7.5)

1. §4.12 (Graft, "The donor is reduced at import") has fileimport run `graft.Reduce`
   (`app/squash/worker/graft`), but split spec §4.5.3 and W5.14's `TestAgentLinksNoManagerRegistration`
   deny `app/squash/worker` and everything under it in `cmd/agent`. F7.1 moves the reduction to
   `pkg/transcode/donoraudio`.
2. §4.12 and Appendix A item 16 say "the import agent already links ffgo"; at F7's position (after
   W5.19, before W6.1) it does not: split spec §4.5.3 says the agent "probes through `ffprobeexec`
   and links no ffgo" until step 11 (Wave 8). F7.1 makes the agent link ffgo three waves early, and
   §8.3 lists neither W8.6 nor W8.10 as changed.
3. §4.12 and §5.13 name the graft Job `k8s.ChildName(mf.Name, "graft", seq)` (253-character budget)
   and label it `squasharr.clustarr.io/graft-of: <mediafile name>`: a Job name over 63 characters is
   refused (it becomes the `batch.kubernetes.io/job-name` pod label) and a label value is capped at
   63, while MediaFile names are `ChildName`-built. F7.2 uses `k8s.LabelSafeName` and the UID. Today's
   AudioGraft Job has the same latent defect.
4. §3.8's effect list has no Job delete, but §4.12's "record answered" row deletes the Job with
   Background propagation; F7.2 adds `DeleteGraftJob`.
5. §3.3 S2'/S3' (`movieFileInputs`, `episodeNamingInputs` plus `originalLanguage`) omit the item's
   `status.audio.donor` and `status.audio.missing`, which the graft planner reads: a donor imported
   onto the item never wakes its file. F7.2 adds them.
6. §2.6's existence conditions would drop an in-flight block (`Queued`, `Running`, `Swapping`, or a
   withdrawn dispatch inside its fact window) when the donor is replaced, the profile edited or the
   language no longer missing, losing the Job's answer and a fact; F7.2 keeps such a block until it
   resolves.
7. `records.FactWindow` is listed as one name (§4.13, F1.1) but §4.10 defines it per remediation
   (the transcode task's deadline plus `deadlineGrace`; the graft Job's deadline plus
   `graftJobGrace`); it cannot be one constant. F7.2 defines `graftplan.FactWindow`.
8. §4.8's "absent record: `Claim` writes nothing, the worker naks with a 30 s delay" has no meaning
   for a graft Job pod (no message to nak); F7.2's pod waits `grafttask.ClaimWait` for the loop's owed

    AudioGraft the result is for; F7.3 drops it with `Task.Graft`, which §4.12 does drop.

    retires; it needs a change row (as do W5.12's `TestUMASKIsAppliedBeforeAGraft` and
    `TestPoolAndGraftArgsParse`).

    `mediafile/graft.go:33` (its `audiografts get;list;watch` grant) among the grants that "go in N

#### Wave F8: adoption, history, ui, e2e, release-N close (F8.1 to F8.12)

1. §8.6 F8.6 names `app/catalog/history/{target,replay,dlq}.go`, but W2.11 (kept by §8.3) moves `replay.go` to `app/catalog/history/replay/` and `dlq.go` to `app/catalog/worker/history/`; F8.6 edits the paths W2.11 leaves.

Following the plan's rule that RBAC markers move with the code that needs them, `rbac.go` lands in F8.3 and F8.8 only removes the rest. Likewise `ManagerLegacyFold` enters W5.4's `ManagersOf` and W5.19's `wantHomes` in F8.3, when it joins `k8s.FieldManagers()`.
