The guard keys on the role or roles whose `RBAC_PATHS` cover `app/catalog/legacyfold`.
5. §7.3.12's AST walk by selector name would flag QualityProfile's own `AudioGraft` bool (`pkg/decision/audiopolicy.go:159`, `pkg/quality/profile.go:398`); the guard resolves the selector through the file's import of `api/{subtitle,transcode}/v1alpha1`.
6. §7.2/§3.5 say release N "prepends `PlannerAdopt`" but not that its seeds must become `v.Prev` before any other planner's `Gather` (the probe planner needs a seeded swap's target; record reads key on the previous block), nor that seeds must never be written into `View.File` (the compare-and-swap render compares against it, so a seeded block would read as already applied and adoption would never land).
7. §7.3.8 step 1 loads the `catalogarr-markers` pending set once at start, but the informer's initial list reconciles every file before that paged List finishes, and without a wake source nothing re-enqueues them. F8.3 and F8.4 add a channel source inside `app/remediation`, so `TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile` still holds.
8. §7.3.8 says `TestOnlyLegacyFoldAppliesAsCatalogarrMarkers` holds the `catalogarr-markers` write to "one call site", but `restore-markers` (§7.3.11) also applies as `catalogarr-markers`; the guard can hold it only to one package.
9. §7.3.9/F1.2: the lag `Ensure` reads for `Topology.Retired` has no named type or route to the Migrator; F8.5 passes the start-up `Ensure`'s report through `remediationmanager.Options.RetiredLag` (F1.2's `events.RetiredReporter`).

11. §7.7 ("a file the profile skips or that wants no subtitles is complete") and §7.8 ("scenario 13's SubtitleDone leg can now pass") agree only if a video file with no transcode block is not complete, which the spec never states. F8.7 requires a terminal block (Succeeded, Skipped, a legacy `profileTag`) or `Transcoded()`.
12. §7.8 says `TestObservabilityMetricsNonZero` "waits for `status.transcode` to read Succeeded"; the test waits on no object (it scrapes metrics), so only its comment and message change.
13. §7.3.10 says `config/e2e` patches `--legacy-fold-retain=0s` and "W6 writes the installers after F8 and keeps these", but §8.3's W6.11 and W6.15 rows omit the patch, which `TestLegacyFoldAdoptsThenDeletes` depends on. (W6.11 now carries it: `config/e2e/manager-e2e-patch.yaml`.)

The live probe hashes (sha1 of path, size and mtime in ns) cannot be reproduced on another disk either, so the test re-keys the opaque hash consistently.

Rule 5 also needs the `hevc-mkv` TranscodeProfile, never dumped; its hash proves it is the all-default spec (`ProfileHashAt({}, 1)` = `c5a056785c…`). And the "19 copied_verdict" is reproducible only through a hash seam, since `standard.Version` 2 moved every hash.

22. §2.11.3 puts release N's worst-case status at about 306 KiB against `MediaFileStatusBudgetBytes` = 320 KiB without counting `legacyFold`, which adds about 8 KiB at its caps (16 entries); F8.1's budget re-check may fail.

#### Wave F9: kind removal, release N+1 (F9.1 to F9.5)

1. **§7.4 and §8.6 F9.4 drop builders the fold still uses.** They drop `TranscodeJobSubject` and
   "the job-keyed `WorkTranscodeTaskSubjectAnyPool`", but §5.16 publishes transcode history on
   `clustarr.evt.transcode.job.<action>.<mfUID>` (F6 builds it with
   `events.TranscodeJobSubject(action, mfUID)`), and §5.10 step 3 purges
   `clustarr.work.transcode.task.*.*.<mfUID>` (F6 uses `WorkTranscodeTaskSubjectAnyPool(mfUID)`);
   §4.12 keeps `TranscodeLeaseKey` re-keyed. After F6 these are MediaFile-keyed. F9.4 renames the
   event builder and re-documents the others (deviation 3).
2. **§8.6 lists `status.legacyFold` in F9.2,** but its only writer, the adopt planner, leaves in
   F9.1, and F3.1's `TestPlannerCopyPartitionsTheStatus` fails on a status field no planner names.
   F9.1 removes the field with its writer (deviation 1).
3. **§8.6 splits the flags (F9.1) from the installers (F9.3),** but W6.11's
   `TestInstallerArgsParseAsTheManager` parses both installers' manager args through the binary,
   so the flags cannot go while the installers pass them (deviation 2).
4. **§7.6's "N+1 → N: lossless … re-apply N's MediaFile CRD … then `helm rollback`" fails.**
   Release N's CRD keys `status.sidecars` by `path`; entries N+1 wrote have none. Server-side
   apply builds a typed live object (`k8s.io/apimachinery@v0.37.0`
   `pkg/util/managedfields/internal/structuredmerge.go:150-152`), and an element of a keyed list
   that omits every key field fails that conversion
   (`sigs.k8s.io/structured-merge-diff/v6@v6.4.2` `typed/helpers.go:226-228`), so N's first status
   apply on every file with an N+1-written sidecar is refused and that file's status never moves.
   Fix: clear `status.sidecars` (a JSON patch on the status subresource, which takes the Update
   path, `UpdateNoErrors`) under N+1's CRD before re-applying N's; N re-lists from disk. F9.2's
   transition envtest proves both the refusal and the fix; F9.5's runbook carries the step.
5. **No release N → N+1 transition test.** §7.3.12 tests N against the previous release, but
   nothing tests N+1's CRD against objects N wrote (the map list becoming atomic with
   `k:{"path":…}` managedFields entries; `legacyFold` pruning on read) or the N+1 → N row of §7.6.
   F9.2 adds one (deviation 5).
6. **`Sidecar.name` has no constraint against a separator or a dot-name,** while N+1's readers
   (librarydelete, the import list's removal, the rename) join it to `dir(spec.path)` and move or
   delete the result. F9.2 routes every reader through `Sidecar.PathBeside`, which refuses such a
   name (deviation 6); the spec should say so in §2.7.
7. **§7.4's gate "no non-history reference to the kinds" has no definition of "history".** Dated
   plans and specs, ADR bodies, research notes, CLAUDE.md's Status records, the chart's upgrade
   sections and the removal runbook (which must name the CRDs it deletes) all legitimately name
   them; this plan states the list in the guard. Relatedly, §7.9 has W10.4 remove §4.5/§4.6's
   kinds from the design of record while release N still serves them, and §8.6 F9.5 repeats it;
   F9.5 finishes whatever W10.4 left and pins it with a test.
8. **§7.4 deletes two release-N guards** (`TestOnlyLegacyFoldNamesTheFoldedKinds`,
   `TestOnlyLegacyFoldAppliesAsCatalogarrMarkers`) and retires `crdcheck` rows
   (`TestMaxTranscodeProfileLengthMatchesTheCRD`'s TranscodeJob row,
   `TestDownloadPurposeIsImmutableAndOptional`'s AudioGraft half) without naming replacements,
   against the split plan's guard rule ("each retired test with a named replacement" is asked but
   none is given). F9.1 and F9.2 name them.
9. **§7.4 says `Result` "moves to `app/squash/task`"** without naming the type or whether
   `MediaInfo` moves with it (§4.12 says it is always nil). F9.2 moves it as `task.Result` without
   `MediaInfo`, JSON names unchanged, held by a wire test.
10. **§7.5's N+1 step 2 applies only the MediaFile CRD.** F9.2 also changes the TranscodeProfile
    and SubtitleProfile CRDs' descriptions (comments that named the removed kinds); harmless, but
    the runbook should apply the whole directory after the deploy (F9.5 step 4 does).
11. **Unlisted leftovers:** `ProgressTranscodeSubject` (a job-keyed core-NATS subject with no
    caller since before the fold) and the fate of `Topology.Retired`'s two entries in N+1 are not
    mentioned; F9.4 deletes the first and keeps the second (deviation 4).

## Plan review notes

Recorded by the plan review of 2026-10-06, which applied the review's critical and important findings to the tasks above (see **Cross-wave interface gaps, and how this revision closes them** near the top for where each landed). What follows is what the review left open, merged, or decided differently from a finding's wording.

### Merged duplicates

- W5.7's `autoscale.Register` call (two findings, executability and ordering): one fix in W5.7 plus `TestRegisterWiresAutoscaleByTheFlag`.
- W5.17's `TestTheAgentIsTheOnlyIndexRegistrar` failing on the worker wrappers (two findings): one fix, option A of the finding (delete the wrappers and `catalogagent.RegisterIndexes`; the agent's `registerIndexes` is the one registrar; tests register through `test/starttest.RegisterIndexes`).
- W10.1's pathspec naming a file W5.17 deleted (two findings): one fix.

### Decided differently from the finding's wording

- **Rebase timing (2cbbb2c1).** The finding asked to re-verify W2.30, W8.3 and W8.5 against `2cbbb2c1` "after the R14 rebase". The plan now recommends a first rebase at W0.28 green (before Wave 1), so those moves apply to the code main has, and still rebases before hand-back; the three tasks carry conditional notes that hold either way. This relaxes the assembled plan's "only before handing back" rule for the controlling session only.
- **U3 lands in Wave 6, not at the end.** The guide orders U3 last, but restricting the `ffmpeg` stage to seven libraries and checking it depend on no exec deletion, so W6.5 and W6.6 carry it and the image is never built the old way.
- **No par2 verdict goldens.** The guide's U2.3 lists "`Par2Runner` → verdicts". No Wave 9 task compares `LibraryRepairer` with `Par2Runner` (they share `par2test.CreateSet` sets made by the par2 CLI, which U2 allows), so nothing would read them; W6.23 records probe, extraction and decode goldens only.
- **The recorder is deleted piecewise** (W7.7, W8.7, W8.9), with the implementation each piece calls, because a single `hack/record-goldens` that imported all three would stop compiling at W7.7. The guide's "delete the recorder with the last exec implementation" is met at W8.9.
- **`ffprobeexec` is deleted at W8.7, not moved to `test/ffprobeoracle`.** An oracle that runs `ffprobe` in a test is what U2 forbids; the probe goldens are its record.
- **W4.84 (OD13, `fileimport.applyMediaFile`).** The spec names no field of the MediaFile that a fresh read should change in the import's declaration. The task implements OD13 as stated (live read, resourceVersion, `RetryOnConflict`, an interleaved-writer test) and gives the read one behaviour of its own: it refuses to take over a MediaFile whose `spec.mediaRef` names another item. If the owner meant a specific race, it needs a sentence in the spec; the mechanism is in place either way.

### Left open (minor), with the reason

- **Per-package deps guards** (Wave 1's `pkg/obs`, `pkg/k8s/conditions`, `pkg/pipeline`, `pkg/busconn`, `pkg/overlay`, `pkg/subtitles`, and Wave 2b's five under `app/*`). The spec makes `test/guards` "the one home of every deps guard". Folding them needs each rule checked against W5.14's binary closures (a per-package rule can be stricter than any binary's: `pkg/subtitles` must not link astisub even through a binary that legitimately links `pkg/subtitles/postprocess`), so a mechanical deletion could lose a guard. They stay green and keep their meaning; a follow-up task after W5.14 should move each rule into `test/guards/deps_test.go` as a package-root `depguard.Load` and delete the per-package file, naming the replacement in its commit (the global guard rule).
- **The par2 CLI in the native test assets** (OD26). U2.5 allows it and suggests the cleaner option of committing the few PAR2 sets the usenet tests create, as par2go's `testdata/` does. This plan keeps the CLI; the owner may choose the committed sets.
- **`testmedia`'s bit-exactness.** W6.18 asserts that one FFmpeg build writes the same bytes twice. If an encoder in the BtbN build cannot be made bit-exact, the assertion should narrow to the clips the goldens use; the goldens themselves do not depend on it, because their clips are committed.
- **Library-corpus gates** (§11.2 gates 2-4) now read goldens the owner records with `hack/record-goldens -library` before W7.7, W8.7 and W8.9 delete the implementations. If the owner does not record them in that window, those gates can only compare against the stored `status.mediaInfo` dump (gate 2's second half).

### Found beyond the findings

- **AudioGraft field-index collision** (drift on main after the spec). The MediaFile reconciler and the AudioGraft controller both register AudioGraft `status.mediaFileRef`; in the one manager the second is an "indexer conflict" at start, and W5.7's `TestManagerFieldIndexes` listed no AudioGraft index. W5.7 now prefixes the AudioGraft controller's two names (`squasharr.audiograft.…`, §5.7's rule for squasharr) and lists all three.
- **W6.16 carries a U1 amendment** too (its CI comment named par2go as a local replace; its native-assets cache key now hashes `hack/par2go/SHA256SUMS`).
- **W4.9 and the Wave 4a defect note** pointed the audio-probe heartbeat at "the R2 wave"; both now name W4.86.

### Review of 2026-10-07 (the fold waves, F0-F9, and the split tasks they touch)

Applied in the tasks above: F3.2 and F3.4 drop `export_test.go`'s aliases with the code they name;
F5.3 settles the retired-manager rule (only `catalogarr-markers` validates in release N) and writes
its two `pkg/k8s` tests in the file's own package and style; F5.3 no longer re-deletes
`app/caption/itemindex` (F4.1's) and F5.1/F5.3/Wave F5's table follow F4.1; F5.2, F5.4 and F5.5 name
`app/catalog/worker/history/{sink.go,dlq.go}` and `app/catalog/history/replay/replay.go`; F5.3 adds
`TestOnlyTheLoopWatchesMediaFile`'s channel half (`channelSources`), F6.3 its two ledger rows and F6.6
drops the doomed `transcodejob` row; F3.4's `TestOnlyTheLoopWritesMediaFileStatus` calls W5.15's
`importAlias` with its arity and a new `chainRootedAt`; F8.4 admits `app/catalog/legacyfold` as the one
release-N `catalogarr-markers` writer and in the manager's `AllowApp`, and F9.1 takes all three
exceptions out; a new task F7.4 writes `TestRecordsRequestersAreTheLoop`,
`TestRecordsBucketsOpenOnlyThroughTheirStores` and `TestNoV1TaskProducers` (the gate is now F7.5) and
W6.9 writes `TestNoAgentRoleGrantsMediaFileStatus`; W6.23, W7.6 and W7.8 read F3.4's segments record;
W8.6 and W6.22 cover F8.12's `ffprobe` gate; F6.3's admission guard reads the real apply-configuration
path; W5.15's builder guards see `TypedControllerManagedBy[K]`; F2.1/F2.2/F6.2/F6.4 carry
`status.transcode.plan.dropped` (D44); F4.2/F4.3 share `rollup.DownloadPredicate` with S9's
`DownloadNonTerminal` edge; F7.2 writes `TestAGraftedOriginalKeepsItsSpecWhenTheGraftBlockGoes`;
F3.1's `isolate` opens the per-planner spans; W10.4 marks the transcode-worker design's §8 superseded;
F3.5 checks W4.3's `mediafiles` grant instead of re-adding it; and the minors (F1.1's step reference,
F3.4/F3.6's run lists, F6.2's grep, F6.6's line numbers, F8.1's package path, the Global
Constraints' ffgo sentence).

#### Decided differently from the finding's wording

- **Retired managers.** Of the two rules the finding offered, the plan takes the loop spec's (§3.14:
  "`Validate` still accepts `catalogarr-markers` in release N"): `captionarr-worker` is refused from
  F5.3, `Valid()` keeps a single `ManagerCatalogarrMarkers` arm until F9.4. F5.3's
  `TestCaptionarrWorkerIsRetired` was also written as package `k8s_test` with testify in a file that is
  `package k8s` with plain `testing`; both F5.3 tests now match the file.
- **The channel half lists every raw channel source outside the loop**, not only MediaFile-driven
  ones: the AST cannot tell what feeds a channel, so each row says what does, and at most two rows
  may be MediaFile-driven (§3.20). The admission pass's own `ledger.wake` is a row marked not
  MediaFile-driven, as loop spec §5.7 describes it ("a slot or window place frees or a pool state
  changes"); if the owner reads D3's "two channels the loop and the ledger signal" as counting it,
  the cap stays two and the row's flag is the only edit.
- **The records guards** are one new task (F7.4) rather than three edits spread over F3.4, F5.3 and
  F6.6, because the store guard must know all six stores and F7.2 adds the last. Two raw opens the
  stores still mediate are explicit `bucketOpeners` rows (`cmd/transcode`'s
  `ServeOptions.Records`, F6.4; `app/catalog/manager`'s segments sweeper, F3.4).
- **`TestNoAgentRoleGrantsMediaFileStatus` is W6.9's**, not a fold task's: the agent identities'
  roles first exist there, and before W6.11 the legacy per-service roles mix manager and agent code.
  F7.5's gate no longer names it.
- **`DownloadNonTerminal`'s edge** is one shared `rollup.DownloadPredicate` (F4.2) replacing the six
  identical copies, since S9 says the predicate is "the same in all six packages"; its tests set both
  forms of the held import (`991b7ced`'s message, `1b62902b`'s `heldSince`), so they hold before and
  after F0.2's rebase.
- **`plan.dropped`'s cap** lives in `mediafilestatus.Render` (F2.2), with the clamp, so every writer of
  the block is bounded; `StatusPlan` (F6.2) copies `standard.Result.Dropped` whole, and F6.4's
  dispatch test holds the re-plan's rewrite.

#### Left open (minor), with the reason

- **The markers planner's owed republish (loop spec §6.4.6 applied to §4.7).** F3.4's republish of a
  requested, unclaimed markers record reuses its Msg-Id without asking whether
  `CLUSTARR_WORK_SEGMENTARR` (DiscardOld) still stores the task, so an evicted TheIntroDB task is
  absorbed as a duplicate and waits out the 24 h timeout. The fix is F5.1's rule in the markers
  adapter: in `Gather`, for a requested record with `ClaimedAt == nil` inside
  `records.RepublishWindow`, `admin.Subjects(ctx, events.StreamWorkSegmentarr,
  events.WorkMarkersSubject(events.MediaKey("mediafile", ns, name)))` (a `Subjects` error is
  `remediation.Transient`), and in `Plan`'s effect loop the republish's Msg-Id becomes
  `<MsgIDForMarkers>/r<unix-minute>` when the subject is empty, tested by an evicted task on the
  embedded server. Not applied here because it adds an input to `catalogmarkers.Plan`'s adapter and
  an embedded-server envtest the review could not write against F3.4's still-unbuilt test env; F3.4's
  executor (or the controlling session before F3.6) should take it.
- **Three §3.20 behaviour envtests are still file-key stand-ins** (D-F3-7; spec defects item 9):
  `TestAHungMountNeverStallsItemsOrGrants` (extend F3.1's `TestAHungMountNeverStallsOtherFiles` with
  an item key in F4.2 and a granted file in F6.3 or F6.4),
  `TestAClaimArrivingBeforeTheCacheSeesQueuedIsIncorporated` (F6.4: a `claimed` record written during
  pass 1's apply with the informer delayed) and `TestAProbeThatChangesTheCodecPicksTheWinnerInTheSamePass`
  (F6.2: a probe whose `video-codec` label flips the winning TranscodeProfile in one pass). Each needs
  the envtest harness its owning task builds (item keys, the ledger, profile selection); writing them
  blind would guess at helpers. The controlling session assigns them when F4.2, F6.2 and F6.4 run.
- **Spans for the effect phase.** F3.1's `isolate` now opens a span for every isolated call, so the
  effect executor's calls are `remediation.<planner>.effect` spans beside §3.19's `gather` and `plan`.
  That is more than §3.19 lists, never less; no change asked of the spec.
- **`TestEachIsolatedPhaseIsAChildSpan` swaps the global tracer provider**, so F3.1's package must not
  use `t.Parallel()` in a test that runs `isolate`; none does as written.

#### Found beyond the findings

- **F6.2's transcode envtest suite imported the apply configurations from
  `api/catalog/v1alpha1/applyconfiguration/...`**, the same nonexistent path as F6.3's admission guard;
  it now reads `api/applyconfiguration/catalog/catalog/v1alpha1`, where controller-gen writes them.
- **F5.3's `pkg/k8s` tests** were written for package `k8s_test` with testify in a `package k8s` file
  that imports only `testing` (see the retired-managers entry above); fixed with the rule.
